POST requires `confirm_stop: true` only while the original writer is running; when it has exited, `false` is accepted. Takeover resumes the same thread and session ID in a new terminal tab. A separate continue option alone starts an independent session with context and attached to-do preserved. The `encrypted_context` failure permits continuation only.

`capabilities.rewind` permits `session.rewind` to before a user message. `capabilities.rewind_code` additionally permits
`code_and_conversation`. Absent values keep the Claude terminal heuristic. Codex advertises conversation rewind for a
shared app-server with persistent paginated history and a node able to materialize that history. Runtime rows report
`caps.rewind`, excluding sub-Agents. A runtime row may carry `capabilities` of its own for this: `rewind: false` takes
the rewind away from that session, and `rewind_code: true` offers file restoration with it (Paseo: what each agent's
provider can do); without it file restoration stays off. The web message menu reads both fields.

`capabilities.model` permits model changes through `POST …/modes`. Runtime rows explicitly report whether the runtime
advertised `caps.model`, excluding sub-Agent rows. Absent values preserve older clients' model-switch heuristics.
A runtime that advertises `caps.models` also handles `launchers.models` for live native model discovery.

`capabilities.modes` (#1843) says whether the composer's permission mode and effort chips can change the session through `POST …/modes`. A runtime row carries `true` when the runtime declared `caps.modes`, the row is not a sub-Agent's, and its `agent` is `claude` (Orca, Paseo's Claude providers) or the runtime's own (`agy`; not Paseo, whose bridge calls every agent other than Claude Code and Codex `paseo` and refuses a permission mode for them); otherwise `false`. `claude_bg` / `claude_desktop` / `claude_cli` rows always carry `false`: the peer inbox carries messages only, and a message never gives such a session a pane, so their mode and effort change on the computer. Other sources omit it for now. Clients show the chips from it when it is a boolean, whatever the agent; when it is absent (an older node, or a source that does not say) they keep deciding from `agent` and `source_kind` as before. The hub forwards it as the node sent it (a pointer in `proto.SessionCapabilities`, so an older node's row stays without it). An older hub, whose `proto.SessionCapabilities` has no `modes`, drops it on the way; clients then fall back to the `agent` / `source_kind` rule as for an older node. A change that reaches the node anyway is refused with `409 modes_on_computer` for such a Claude, or `409 modes_not_running` when nothing runs the session (Resume on its terminal page brings it back); both words come from the hub in the request's language (`rpc-errors.modes_*`), and the same refusals apply to `model` and `ultracode` on that endpoint. An older node answers both with its own fixed text and no code.
`capabilities.close` says whether the session can be closed independently of terminal access. Runtime rows report their declared `caps.close`. Web, iOS and Android use this value for the existing close action and confirmation (#6294). When it is absent, clients retain terminal-only closing for older nodes. An explicit false refuses closing even when terminal access is available.
`capabilities.rename` (#6294) says whether the session's title can be changed (`POST …/rename` with `title`) independently of terminal access. Runtime rows report their declared `caps.rename`, excluding sub-Agent rows (`is_subagent`, or a `<session>@<id>` id); a pointer in `proto.SessionCapabilities` like `close`, so the hub forwards it as the node sent it and an older node's row stays without it. Web, iOS and Android show Rename from it when it is a boolean, renaming the title alone (such a session has no tab); when it is absent they keep their earlier rule (the web: a row that can send and is the user's own Agent or a Persona conversation; iOS and Android: a terminal). An explicit false hides Rename even on a terminal session.
On iOS and Android, as on the web, `capabilities.model` true offers the model picker on a session without a terminal, listing its launcher's models (`GET /machines/{mid}/launchers/{name}/models`) and sending a pick through `POST …/modes {model}` (iOS never types `/model` for it, and offers no fixed Claude aliases before the list is read); `capabilities.rewind` true offers Rewind on such a session, whose item ids are its own (`<seq>#<n>`), with "code and conversation" only where `capabilities.rewind_code` is true.
Session also has the optional field `pane_index` (#2320): this pane's positional index within its tab (from 0, top-left is 0). The herdr node computes it from the split tree in the snapshot's `layouts` (`splits`; by rect on older herdr without it). It is omitted when the host gives no layout, on old nodes, or when the pane isn't in the layout; `0` is still sent, and only absence means unknown. A change in it alone also pushes `sessions.changed`. Clients group the Agents of one tab (`slot_id`) in this order, with 0 as the initiator; old clients ignore it (`docs/protocol/agent-states.md` "Several panes in one tab").
Session also has the optional field `space` (#2691): which assistant space an assistant chat belongs to. Chats in the health space are `"health"`; the assistant's own chats omit it. The hub fills it from the session's `cwd` (the health directory `~/.persona/health`), which for an assistant chat is the directory it started in, not where a `cd` in it went (#2368, see `cwd` below); it has nothing to do with herdr's `space_id` / `space_name`. Old clients ignore it (`docs/assistant/health.md`).
A Session's space also has the optional field `parent_space_id` (#2073): which space this space hangs under in the host, same machine, same `space_kind`; top-level spaces omit it. The Orca host fills it from `worktree.ps`'s `parentWorktreeId` (pointing at itself counts as none), and the hub forwards it as-is. Old clients ignore it and stay flat; the web client's **By Machine** and iOS / Mac's **By Repository** fold child spaces under their parent (`docs/web/web.md`, `docs/apple/ios.md`).

Reasoning effort (`docs/integrations/codex.md` "Thinking effort"): Codex sessions the phone drives through app-server (sendable ones in `codex_app_server`, and herdr panes attached to the shared daemon, which have no `source_kind`) and the Codex desktop App's chats (`agent_name` "Codex App", set through the App, #5575) carry `efforts`: the levels `effort` on `POST …/modes` can take, weakest to strongest (as reported by `model/list` for this thread's model; Codex's minimal … ultra when unavailable). `effort` is its current value, and `permission_mode` is omitted. For these sessions `/modes` accepts only `effort`; sending `permission_mode` is an error, a level not in `efforts` is an error, and failing to apply it (app-server disconnected, no timely response, Codex refused) is an error too, never a premature success. All other sessions omit `efforts`: Claude Code and the assistant keep the client's own set of levels, and the rest can't be changed. Clients show only reasoning effort when `efforts` is non-empty and sending is possible, without guessing from the Agent type; old clients ignore the field.

Context usage (#2430): sessions carry `context_tokens` (the tokens the model saw on the agent's latest reply: for Claude `input + cache_read + cache_creation`, for Codex the latest rollout `token_count`'s `last_token_usage.input_tokens`) and `context_window` (the model's window). The node computes these from the transcript tail that `readQuickMetaSince` already reads, without reading extra files; when the tail has no reply it keeps the last value read (`node/contextwindow.go`). Window: Codex uses the `model_context_window` recorded in its own rollout; Claude goes by model id: a `[1m]` suffix is 1 million, so is a model whose window is 1 million without it in Claude Code's own model list (Opus from 4.7, Sonnet and Haiku from 5, every Fable and Mythos; #5758), and a session that has already seen more than 200k tokens also counts as 1 million (ids in the transcript have no suffix); other `claude-*` (Opus and Sonnet 4.6 and earlier, Haiku 4.5, 3.x) are 200k. For non-Claude models (the gateway's own) the window is unknown and only `context_tokens` is sent. Unknown fields are omitted (`omitempty`): no reply yet, old node. Clients compute the percentage as `context_tokens / context_window` and draw nothing if either is missing.

`POST /api/v1/sessions/{mid}/{sid}/attach`: the user asks to attach live. The node requests resume only for a thread still loaded on its original instance with a unique owner, and without overriding run configuration. Discovery and ordinary history reads don't call resume. Attach permission is stored in settings per thread / stable instance; after a disconnect the owner is re-checked, with no automatic cold resume or instance switch. loaded/list and resume aren't atomic, so there's no promise against an unload race in between.

External sends also use `/messages`, must carry `client_msg_id`, and must successfully register a dedup record in Postgres; nothing is sent unprotected when storage is unavailable. An unknown send outcome (including a generic server error that may come after admission) returns `delivered: unknown`; it must not be resent automatically, and a failed steer must not be turned into a start. Send records don't expire after a day, so restoring a very old outbox can't execute twice; only records known not to have been sent may be forgotten.

Approval IDs contain machine / instance / connection generation / thread / the original typed request ID. Only an explicit answer from the phone replies on the original connection; unknown requests, cancels and disconnects don't automatically send error/decline. `serverRequest/resolved` only marks the card dismissed and takes it down; it never produces an approval. External interrupt doesn't clean up all background terminals; directly driving child threads from a parent isn't open yet.

## Claude Code ultracode (#3427)

ultracode is independent of reasoning effort and adds no level to `EffortLevels`. It applies only to the current Claude process, defaults to off, and does not remember the last choice or change launcher settings or the user's default effort.
This API is for ordinary Claude Code Agent sessions; Persona's headless assistant chats, including the main chat, do not support it. Client controls are tracked in web #3428, Android #3429 and Apple #3430.
The assistant's `agent_start` and `task_plan` take `ultracode` per Agent and pass `true` on to `session.start` (#12). A start refused for it (`ultracode_unsupported` or `node_outdated` below: a Codex or other non-Claude launcher the tier or default picked, an older Claude Code, a node too old for it) goes again without it, once, since both refusals come before anything starts. `agent_start`'s answer gives the reason. A task keeps it in the stored plan task's why, and the hub log has it: no client draws a started plan's why. Once the start went through, the stored plan keeps ultracode off, so a retry starts too; a start that failed after all keeps asking, so a task moved to a computer that can have it gets it (#3596). A refused start does not count against the launcher's health. The web and iOS / Mac show and change it on plan cards and to-dos ([web.md](../web/web.md), "Claude Code ultracode"; [ios.md](../apple/ios.md), "Claude Code ultracode"); Android is still to come in #12.

Optional Session fields:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `ultracode: bool` | The observed state; `false` is sent too. Omitted means unknown (no evidence yet, an old node, a non-Claude session, etc.), not off |
| `ultracode_note: string` | A node-provided reason, in Chinese, why the toggle is unavailable, was refused, could not be confirmed, or still waits (a draft or a dialog in the computer's terminal). A fixed text: it never quotes what was typed at the computer. Clients show the reason and do not treat request success as proof that ultracode is on |
| `ultracode_pending: bool` | A request is queued: the agent's turn is still running, or the terminal's input box or a dialog is in the way. Clients can show "Applies next turn"; this is a queue flag, not the requested toggle value |
| `ultracode_lost_at: time` | When a previously enabled session resumed with ultracode off. Clients can show a resume notice and offer to turn it back on; the server never re-enables it automatically |

`POST /api/v1/sessions/{mid}/{sid}/modes {"ultracode":true|false}`: the hub applies model, permission mode and effort changes through the existing path, then calls the node's separate `session.ultracode` method.
An ultracode-only request does not call `session.modes`. If an old node does not recognize the new method, the hub returns `409 {"code":"node_outdated","error":"…"}` rather than accepting a silently ignored field.
The same `/modes` endpoint accepts `{"ultracode_dismiss_lost":true}` to dismiss only the resume notice; the node parameter is `dismiss_lost`. Successfully turning ultracode back on also clears the notice. No confirmation dialog is required.
A request the session cannot take is refused with `409 {"code":"ultracode_unsupported"}` and nothing typed: the main chat, a non-Claude agent, a known CLI older than `2.1.284`, or a terminal the node cannot read or type into (botmux sessions, which only take messages).
A request that has to wait succeeds with `ultracode_pending` set; the node applies it later on its own. Right after a node restart, a request (a toggle or a dismissal) first waits for the node to load its session state from the hub (at most about 20 seconds), so the stored observation it changes is read in before it, not after it. Asking for the value the process already has while the opposite value is still queued takes the queued request back.

`POST /api/v1/sessions {"ultracode":true,…}` (also accepted by the node's `session.start`) types `/effort ultracode on` after Claude is ready and before the first prompt.
It is best effort: a refusal (model, dynamic workflows, `Invalid argument`), a verdict not read back in time, or a dialog the new Claude came up with never fails the start. The first prompt is typed as usual, and the reason is in `ultracode_note` (a dialog leaves the request queued). The one exception is a command that may still sit in the input box (typed, no verdict, and the box then shows a draft or a dialog, or cannot be read): the first prompt is not typed after it, and the session is listed as needing the user with the reason, as when a dialog holds the first prompt back.
Async creation still returns `starting:true` immediately; clients then read the actual result from the session fields. Omitting the parameter does not inherit the last choice or re-enable ultracode on resume.
`"ultracode":false` is the same as leaving it out: a new process is off anyway, so there is no agent or version check and no command. `true` is refused before anything starts (`ultracode_unsupported`) for a non-Claude agent, a known CLI older than `2.1.284`, or an engine that cannot read its terminals; a node without the `ultracode` capability gets `409 node_outdated` instead of starting without it.
Requests made while the foreground turn is working or blocked are queued until it ends and the input box is empty. A dynamic workflow that runs on after the turn ended does not hold the toggle back: the input box is free then.
A queued toggle never holds a message back. When a message arrives while Claude rests, the node types the pending toggle first, then the message; while the turn is still running, the message goes into Claude's own queue and the toggle waits for the next rest. Whatever the toggle's result (it lands in `ultracode_note`), the message is sent; only when the toggle's command may still sit in the input box (typed, its verdict not read back) does the send stop rather than type after it: with the usual `input_draft` / `dialog_open` refusal, or `not_delivered` when the terminal's screen cannot be read at that moment, since an unread screen says nothing about the box. Nothing of the message is typed in either case (`delivered: none`).
An existing terminal draft or dialog is left untouched: the slash command is never appended to a draft or used to answer a dialog. A queued toggle that waits for one is tried again with growing pauses (3 s, doubling up to 5 minutes). Refusals and mismatches between requested and observed state are recorded in `ultracode_note`.

Version gate: a running session uses the Claude version its transcript recorded since the current process started (a newer CLI resuming an old session has written nothing yet, so the old version says nothing about it and the command is tried); before starting, the node uses the machine's `claude_version`. Known versions older than `2.1.284` are rejected with an upgrade notice. Offline rows show no version notice.
The old `2.1.203–2.1.283` behavior, where ultracode was an effort level, is unsupported. An unknown version may be tried, but the command response decides the result: a launcher may run a different CLI from the login shell's default.
Dynamic workflows can be enabled through the existing **Claude Code Settings** boolean `enableWorkflows`. When unset, its default depends on the account's plan (`default:null` in the settings list); organization policy and other restrictions can still make Claude refuse.

State comes from the newest timestamped evidence within the same process: the screen response after a command, `/effort` output in `local-command-stdout`, or non-sidechain `ultra_effort_enter` / `ultra_effort_exit` attachments.
A recognized `/effort` status line ending in `· Ultracode on` means on; a recognized status line without that suffix means off. Ordinary assistant text is not state evidence.
Persona starts/resumes and `SessionStart` hooks with source `startup` or `resume` establish process boundaries; earlier evidence is invalid. `clear` and `compact` do not start a new process.
Toggle commands and their responses become notices in the chat. An `enter` attachment with `reminderType:full` and an `exit` attachment each produce a notice; `sparse` updates state without another notice.
Assistant snapshots and `agents_list` also carry the state. When on, they explain that each substantive task uses a multi-Agent workflow so background work is not mistaken for a stalled agent and rushed.

## Switching a running Agent to another provider (`launcher_switch`, #5035)

A running Claude Code Agent can move to another launcher (model provider) of the same engine. Claude Code reads its
gateway, key and model when it starts, so the node quits the agent and resumes the same conversation through the other
launcher in the same terminal; it does so with the user's next message from the chat, so a pick never interrupts the
agent. Node side and safety rules: `docs/integrations/claude-integration.md` ("Switching a running Agent to another
provider").

`POST /api/v1/sessions/{mid}/{sid}/modes {"launcher":"<name>","from"?,"model"?,"effort"?,"permission_mode"?}`:

- `launcher` other than the session's own (`launcher` on its row; plain `claude` when the row has none) records a
  pending switch after checking it, replacing one that waited, and answers `200 {}`; nothing is typed. `model` is a
  model id for that launcher (left out: what a new session of that launcher runs, refused as `switch_pick_model` when
  the computer cannot see it); `effort` the effort to start it with (left out: the one it runs with now).
  `permission_mode`, when given, is applied to the running agent after the switch is recorded; when that fails the
  request fails and the switch that waited before it is back. The hub remembers `model` as used with that launcher
  (`models.used`).
- `launcher` equal to the session's own drops a pending switch; `model`, `effort` and `permission_mode` then apply as
  without `launcher`. An empty `launcher` is the same as leaving it out.
- `from` is the launcher the client saw the session on. When it is given and the session runs on another one by then (a
  switch was carried out meanwhile), the request is refused as `switch_stale` and nothing is recorded or dropped; the
  same when, without `from`, the session moved while the request waited for a message in flight. Clients send it with
  every `launcher`.
- `launcher` or `from` that is not a string is `400`; any `launcher` to a computer whose node has not announced the
  `launcher_switch` capability, or that the manager has not reported yet (right after a hub restart), is
  `409 node_outdated`, nothing changed.

Optional Session field:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `pending_switch: {launcher, model?, effort?, at}` | The switch waiting for the user's next message: the launcher, the model and effort picked (absent: the launcher's default, the current effort) and when it was picked. Absent when none waits. `launcher` on the row stays the one the agent runs on until the switch is carried out; while it is carried out the row is listed as `starting` on the new launcher |

**Who carries it out.** Only a `POST …/messages` with `"apply_switch": true`: the user's own message from the chat of a
session that shows `pending_switch` (the web sends it then, and only then). Every other message (the assistant's, a
task's supervision, channels, older clients, the phone apps) goes on the launcher the agent runs on, and the switch
keeps waiting. An answer-only device's message never carries one. The exception is the assistant's `agent_switch`
(#5973), which the user asked for: node `session.send` with `"switch_now": true` (implies `apply_switch`) right after
its pick, carried out now or not at all (below), and its batch switch's `session.switch` (#6008), which carries a pick out with no message under the same rules. With `apply_switch`:

- The agent works, waits for the user, is starting, or has background work a quit would end (background commands and
  monitors of its claude process, running subagents or workflows, a `/loop`, or background work whose first read has not
  finished): the message goes on the launcher it runs on, as always, and the switch waits for a later one.
- A switch picked more than 24 hours ago, or naming the launcher the agent runs on by now, is dropped and the message
  goes as always. One picked more than 24 hours ago is not on the row any more meanwhile.
- Otherwise the switch is carried out before the text is typed. On success the row's `launcher` is the new one,
  `pending_switch` is gone and the message went to the new agent. After a switch the new agent may come up behind a
  dialog of its own; the message then gets the usual `dialog_open` and the switch is done.
- Any failure drops the switch (nothing tries it again by itself) and refuses the message: `409` with
  `delivered: "none"` (nothing typed, so the client keeps the words in the box), the summary in the request's language
  (`rpc-errors.<code>`) and the node's own words, with the launcher names, in `detail`. A draft or a dialog that came up
  while the switch was being prepared refuses the message as `input_draft` / `dialog_open` and leaves the switch waiting.
- With `switch_now` as well, nothing goes on the old launcher and no switch is left waiting: where the message would go
  on the launcher the agent runs on, it is refused with nothing typed (`switch_busy` for a busy agent; `input_draft` /
  `dialog_open`; `switch_stale` with no switch waiting; `switch_unsupported` for an agent that is not running in one of
  Persona's terminals, a runtime's session or another CLI; `switch_other_agent` for a switch to the other engine) and
  the switch is dropped. The hub refuses `switch_now` to a node without the `launcher_switch_now` capability
  (`node_outdated`).

**Time.** The node's checks before the quit take at most a minute; from the first Ctrl+C on, the switch runs on its own
clock (a client or connection that goes away does not leave the agent half switched; a resident node's next connection
lists it as starting, waits for it and writes what it wrote), at most 5 minutes: the quit
(about 8 seconds), the shell coming back (at most 10 seconds), the start on the new launcher (at most 90 seconds) and,
after a failed one, the pane cleared and the start on its own launcher (the same bounds). The hub waits 8 minutes for a
message with `apply_switch` (a switch to the other engine takes longer, "Switching a running Agent to another engine"), decided by the request (not the cached row), where it waits 90 seconds (5 minutes for a
session that is starting or offline) otherwise.

| Code | When | From |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `switch_stale` | `from` names another launcher than the session runs on, or a switch (or a start) of the session is being carried out right now | `POST …/modes` |
| `switch_under_way` | A switch of the session is being carried out right now: what would type into its pane or press its keys (`POST …/modes` with a model, mode or effort, a rewind, keys, an interrupt, a close) is refused with nothing done | the other requests |
| `switch_unsupported` | Not a Claude Code Agent in a terminal Persona can type into (another CLI, a runtime's session, an assistant conversation, botmux; a Codex, unless the launcher is Claude Code's: "Switching a running Agent to another engine"); a launcher Persona cannot tell (a session it did not start whose environment names none); a folder of the conversation it cannot tell; from a message to the other engine, photos with it (only text goes over; the switch waits); and, from a message, another failed check (a provider's secrets that could not be fetched…) | both |
| `switch_launcher_missing` | The launcher is not on that computer | both |
| `switch_other_agent` | The launcher runs another agent than Claude Code (or, for a switch to the other engine, than that engine) | both |
| `switch_model_locked` | `model` given, and the launcher fixes its own `--model` | both |
| `switch_pick_model` | No `model`, and what the launcher runs by default cannot be seen (a provider that names no model, a wrapper script): resumed without `--model`, the conversation would keep the old provider's model | both |
| `switch_config_dir` | The launcher runs Claude Code with another config directory than the one the conversation is in (`--resume` would not find it; the sign-in lives there too) | both |
| `modes_not_running` / `modes_on_computer` | Nothing runs the session, or a Claude outside Persona's terminals has it | `POST …/modes` |
| `switch_not_stopped` | The agent did not quit; it runs on as before | message |
| `switch_failed` | The agent did not come up on the new launcher; the node resumed it on its own launcher in the same terminal | message |
| `switch_failed_stopped` | The agent did not come up on the new launcher, nor again on its own: it has stopped (Resume on its terminal page brings it back on its own launcher) | message |
| `switch_busy` | With `switch_now` (the assistant's `agent_switch`): the agent works, waits for the user, is starting or has background work a quit would end. Nothing typed, the switch dropped | message |

A Persona-managed provider whose secrets the computer has not fetched is fetched first; one out of the computer's device
scope is refused with the manager's own code (`launcher_out_of_scope`, `launcher_own_service`) when picked. The user's
Resume of the session waits for a switch being carried out and then finds the agent running.

## Switching a running Agent to another engine (`engine_switch`, #5054)

A running terminal Agent can move between Claude Code and Codex in the same terminal: the launcher switch above, with a
launcher of the other engine. The conversation goes on in the other engine's session, which gets a handoff of what was
said so far in front of the user's message; when the conversation ran on that engine before, the session it ran in then
is resumed instead, with only what happened meanwhile in front. The conversation stays one row in the list. Node side:
`docs/integrations/claude-integration.md` ("Switching a running Agent to another engine"), the Codex side in
`docs/integrations/codex.md` ("Starting from the phone", "Resuming from the phone").

**Picking.** `POST …/modes {"launcher":"<the other engine's launcher>","from"?,"model"?,"effort"?}` as above: checked,
then kept as the session's pending switch with `agent` set to the engine it moves to (`"claude"` or `"codex"`); nothing is
quit or typed. The session's own launcher (one of its own engine) drops it. Checked: a Claude Code or Codex Agent running
in a terminal Persona drives (not an assistant conversation, a runtime's or botmux's session, a Codex thread an app-server
or another program runs, an agent in a terminal only); its own launcher known (one Persona started it with: it is brought
back on it after a failed switch); its conversation's folder known (Claude Code: the transcript's project folder; Codex:
its record's, else its rollout's `session_meta`); the launcher on that computer and running that engine; with `model`,
one the launcher takes. `effort` is the one picked only, since the engines' levels differ (Codex: one of `low`…`max`;
`auto` or none: the launcher's own). A Codex session picking another Codex launcher stays `switch_unsupported`. A node
without the `engine_switch` capability refuses such a pick in its own words (`switch_other_agent`, or `switch_unsupported`
for a Codex session); the hub answers `409 node_outdated` instead, "This computer's node can't switch a running agent
between Claude Code and Codex yet. Update the node" (`hub/ultracode.go` `oldEngineRefusal`).

**Carrying it out.** Only a message with `apply_switch`, as above; while the agent is busy (Claude Code as above; Codex:
working, waiting for the user, a turn running on its app-server, starting) the message goes to it and the switch waits.
A message with photos is refused as `switch_unsupported` and the switch waits: only text goes over. Otherwise, after the
usual draft and dialog checks (for a Codex too, before its app-server would take the message), the agent is quit, and
the other engine started in the same shell with the message behind the handoff as its first message: a fresh Claude Code
session (`--session-id`), a fresh Codex thread (`personad codex-start`, in the conversation's folder), or the
conversation's earlier session of that engine resumed (`claude --resume <id>`, `codex resume <id> -- <message>`). The
start takes the message: nothing is typed again, and the message counts as delivered. The permission mode goes where
the other engine has it (`plan` both ways, as Codex's read-only flags; `bypassPermissions` to Codex as its bypass flags;
any other: the launcher's own). The time bounds are the launcher switch's, with up to three starts (the earlier
session, a fresh one, the agent back on its own launcher) in at most 5½ minutes from the first Ctrl+C: with the checks
and the handoff built before it, still under the hub's 8 minutes.

**The handoff.** The new or resumed session's first message is a block, then the user's words:

```
<persona-context kind="engine-switch" title="Handoff" from="claude" to="codex" model="gpt-5.5" resumed="1">
…the handoff text…
</persona-context>

<the user's message>
```

`from` and `to` are the engines; `model` the model picked, else the one the launcher names for itself (absent when
neither says); `resumed="1"` only when the conversation's earlier session of `to` was resumed (its text then covers only
what happened since that session last ran it). Attribute values are HTML-escaped. The text is built by the node from
the conversation's transcripts, bounded and the same for the same transcripts. The transcripts keep the block as it
was sent; clients draw the switch divider from it instead of a context chip.

**One conversation, one row.** The session running the conversation carries its earlier stretches in `engine_history`,
oldest first: `{session_id, agent, until}`, `until` being when the conversation was switched away from that stretch
(stretch *i* covers the time after `until` of the one before it up to its own `until`, the first from its start; the
running session's own stretch is the time after the last `until`). A session may be named more than once (switched back
to and away again): after Claude Code A → Codex B → back to A the row is A with `[A until t1, B until t2]`. Only that
session's row carries the history (the node clears it on the session it switched away from), and the node leaves every
session named in another listed session's history, other than that session itself, out of its list while it is
parked: idle, done, offline or cut off by a restart, with no pane and no claude process that has it open (a Codex
thread an app-server keeps loaded after the switch included: a message to it would fork the conversation). Their
transcripts stay on the computer, and a switch back resumes the most recent one of that engine. A named session that
runs again (in a pane, resumed by hand, a claude in another terminal), works or waits for the user is listed as its own
row, and so is one used after the conversation left it (its activity more than two minutes after its stretch's
`until`: a Codex resumed in another terminal or the Codex App). A hidden earlier session still takes a message sent to
its id directly; clients open the conversation's row instead. The row shows the title of the
conversation's first stretch unless it has a manual title of its own. The history is kept in the session's state
record (the hub's Postgres), so a node restart keeps the row joined. While the switch is carried out, the session
switched away from is listed as `starting` with the new launcher and `agent`.

**Fallbacks.** An earlier session that cannot be resumed (its transcript gone, another config directory holds it, a
process has it open, its Codex home is not the launcher's, nothing tells its folder) is not a refusal: a fresh session
of that engine takes the conversation with the whole handoff. One that does not come up gives way to a fresh one once,
in the same shell. A fresh one that does not come up either rolls the switch back: the pane is cleared, the agent
resumed on its own launcher in the same shell (`switch_failed`), or stopped when that does not come up either
(`switch_failed_stopped`); an agent that does not quit runs on (`switch_not_stopped`). The terminal is never closed.
Every refusal is `409` with `delivered: "none"`, and a failed switch is dropped. Only a start that certainly never got
the message falls back like this. One that may have it (codex-start read its file and a Codex runs in the pane, or the
message was typed to a claude that did not take it in time) ends the switch where it is, so the message never runs
twice: nothing more is pressed or typed in the terminal, the switch is dropped, the message is answered with
`delivered: "unknown"` (look at the terminal before sending it again), and when the session that start was for is
known the conversation's history goes on it as after a switch carried out. A fresh Codex thread that did not show is
looked for five more minutes and given the conversation when it shows; meanwhile the pane no longer stands for the
session switched away from. codex-start claims its file by a
rename before it reads it and the node withdraws a file it gives up on the same way, so exactly one of them has the
message; what codex-start printed is not read for this.

**A first message held back.** When the new Claude Code session comes up behind a dialog of its own, its first message
is not typed: the switch is done and the row says the first message did not go in, as for any start. The handoff waits
on the session's record and goes in front of the next message sent to it, whoever sends it, once: it is cleared when
that message is known to be in, and dropped (not put in front) when the session got a message since or works. A first
message found lost only later by the node's background check does not keep it.

**The earlier session while it is resumed.** From just before the first Ctrl+C until the switch ends, the session
being resumed is held as switching (and one the user's Resume is starting right then is not resumed: a fresh session
takes the conversation): a message to it and the user's Resume of it wait for the switch and then find it running
(nothing starts a second writer of its conversation), and a stop, a pick or keys are refused as for the session
switching. It is looked at again as soon as it is held, before the first Ctrl+C, and right before the resume: one that
runs again by then is not resumed, and a fresh session takes the conversation.

**To-dos.** A pane linked to a to-do (`persona_todo_ref`) gets that link as `persona_from` before the other engine
starts, so the new session joins the same to-do as a spawned Agent would ([todos.md](../assistant/todos.md) "Following
spawned Agents").

## Model providers and per-purpose configuration

The original `/api/v1/launchers` stays compatible. Providers gain `kind` (`launcher` / `api`) and `api` (`messages` / `responses`). An API connection using the Messages protocol can also serve as a launcher for the main chat and Agents (the node starts claude with its URL and Key, #2455); Responses ones can't.

- `GET /api/v1/model-config` → `{purposes, providers}`. `purposes` are the five categories, the AI twin (`inbox.agent`), Lark /agent (`lark.agent`), the background supervisor (`assistant.supervise`, #5806: `kind` `launcher`, `launch` `headless`, `parent` and `category_id` `assistant`, its own `override`, `revision` and `fields`, the same object its single-item GET answers) and then the extensions' purposes, in that order. A hub before #5806 leaves `assistant.supervise` out and answers it by its ID only, so a client that reads it by ID must draw it once when the list has it; clients must take a purpose ID they do not know as a row named by `name` (`docs/assistant/model-config.md` “The background supervisor in the catalog”).
- `GET /api/v1/model-config/purposes/{id}` → `{purpose, providers}`. A built-in purpose carries `description` (#5086): what it is for, one sentence in the request's language; optional, absent from an older hub and for a task's, an extension's or a plugin's purpose.
- `PUT /api/v1/model-config/purposes/{id}` and compatible `PATCH` take `{revision, provider?, model?, effort?, runtime?}`; missing fields are unchanged, `null` clears the override, and a revision conflict returns 409. On success they return the same as the single-item GET. `inbox.agent` (the AI twin) and `lark.agent` are editable children of `agent.new`, each with its own revision and override; empty selections follow Agents. Their retired records are not consulted. Other legacy children with empty `fields` remain read-only (`docs/assistant/model-config.md`, “Lark /agent override”, “AI twin override”).
  `runtime` (`cli` / `agentsdk`) can only be written for `assistant`; other purposes sending it get 400. The `assistant` entry's `fields` has an extra `runtime`, plus `runtimes: ["cli","agentsdk"]`. Changing the provider does not clear runtime.
  The node's `assistant.send` / `assistant.start` / `assistant.warm` (params the manager fills in from the model configuration) carry `runtime: "agentsdk"`; CLI (empty or `cli`) omits it. `model_fingerprint` includes the runtime: when it changes, the node restarts the process and reattaches with `--resume`.
  Claude assistant creation also accepts `config_dir` (absolute / `~/…`, `"legacy"` or `"default"`); a nonempty selection requires the node capability `assistant_config_dir`. A resumed conversation retains its saved directory, or discovers its old transcript profile before falling back to the old launch resolution. A later `session.send` cannot relocate it. Details and downgrade procedure: `docs/assistant/assistant.md` ("Claude assistant profile compatibility (#3345)").
- `GET /api/v1/launchers/import?machine=<id>` → `{machine, providers:[{name, base_url, auth, has_key, has_headers, has_env, env_names?, skipped_env?, model, models, opus_model, sonnet_model, haiku_model, fable_model, small_model, subagent_model, subagent_force, custom_model?, custom_model_name?, custom_model_description?, effort, compact_window, max_context, proxy, no_proxy, timeout_ms, args, source, own_service, aliases, existing?, create_as?, sources, differs?, variants?}]}`:
  the manager calls that machine's `launchers.zshrc` and merges aliases that call claude into providers by `base_url + key` (the name is the first alias, with invalid characters replaced by `-`; `[1m]` is stripped from model names and the context window recorded as 1000000; the `ANTHROPIC_MODEL`s in one group are merged into `models`; the other settings are the first alias's).
  `existing` is the name of an already saved provider with the same `base_url + key`. `own_service` is `use`: what a created provider gets.
  `create_as` (a provider or variant without `existing`) is the name it will be saved under, present only when that is not `name`: a name Persona already lists (an rc-file launcher on any computer, the alias itself included, or a stored provider) gets `-2`, `-3`… Groups are named in this order; a group and its variants are each named against what earlier groups may take, and every name a group may take (its own and its variants') counts as taken for the groups after it. `name` stays what `POST` takes.
  `has_env`: the provider brings variables of the alias as its sealed `env`; `env_names` are their names, sorted; `skipped_env` `[{name, reason}]` the variables left out, sorted by name, `reason` `credential` / `shell` / `computer` / `limit` (rules in `docs/assistant/model-config.md`, “Importing providers from shell aliases”).
  `sources` `[{alias, file, hide, uses?, elsewhere?}]`, one per alias in `aliases` order: `file` the shell file (`~/.zshrc`, `~/.bashrc`, `~/.bash_aliases`), `hide` what hiding the alias after the import would do: `ok`, `in_use` (stays; `uses` are the plain names of what uses it), `elsewhere` (stays; `elsewhere` are the names of the computers the provider would not stand in on with the same account: out of its scope, a key of its own there that is not the alias's, or another computer whose own alias does not reach the same Base URL with the same key, asked of its node) or `none` (Persona does not list it, it is hidden already, or it is `claude` / a reserved name). When what the check reads cannot be read, the preview still answers, every alias `none`.
  A group of two or more aliases adds `variants` (each alias as its own provider, the same fields with its own `name`, settings, `models` its model, `existing` a stored provider with the same `base_url + key` imported from that alias, `sources` that alias only; no `variants` / `differs`) and, when they set more than the model differently, `differs` from `tiers`, `effort`, `args`, `limits`, `proxy`, `headers`, `env`, `auth`, `custom_model` in that order.
  Keys, request headers, env values and proxy credentials are never returned. Machine offline is 503 `code: "offline"`, node too old is 409 `code: "node_outdated"`, no such machine is 404.
- `POST /api/v1/launchers/import` `{machine, providers:[name…], split?:[name…], hide_aliases?}` → `{created:[…], updated:[…], hidden:[alias…], kept:[{alias, hide, uses?, elsewhere?}]}`: reads the aliases again; keys, request headers and env pass only through the manager and are saved encrypted, `source` is written as `zshrc:<alias>@<machine>` and a created provider is `own_service: use`.
  A group named in `split` (it must be in `providers`, or 400) is imported as its variants, one provider per alias with its own settings; a variant with an `existing` provider adds its model there. With `hide_aliases: true`, under the same lock and against the providers as saved, every imported alias whose `hide` is `ok` is added to `launchers.hidden` (shell files are not touched), written with the providers in one transaction; the aliases that stay are in `kept` with `hide` `in_use` or `elsewhere`. When the check cannot read what it needs, nothing is written and the import fails; a store that cannot write both at once saves the providers first and answers 500 with a message that they were imported but the aliases were not hidden. Without `split` / `hide_aliases` (older clients) every group is merged and nothing is hidden; `hidden` and `kept` are then empty.
  An existing provider only gets `models` filled in (new ids added, existing ones only get unknown context windows filled), other fields untouched; a new one whose name collides gets `-2`, `-3`. Unknown names are 400.
  If it would make `inbox.triage` unusable while a plugin that needs it is on, it returns 422 `{code: "triage_model_in_use", plugins: [names], error}` (`docs/extensions/extensions.md` "Shared Inbox rules").
  Both take an optional `alias` (`?alias=` on `GET`, a body field on `POST`; feature `launcher_import_parse`): only that alias of the machine is read, so the groups are that alias's alone; an alias the machine does not have previews `providers: []`. An older hub ignores it and previews every alias.
- `POST /api/v1/launchers/import/parse` `{text}` → `{format, drafts:[…], notes:[…]}` (feature `launcher_import_parse`, #5193): reads a pasted configuration into provider drafts without reading a computer or saving anything (rules in `docs/assistant/model-config.md`, "Starting a provider from a pasted configuration"). `format` is `shell`, `settings` (Claude Code's `settings.json`), `curl`, `cindy` (the cindy v1 provider import format), `link` (a provider import link, feature `launcher_import_link`, #5420: `cindy://provider/import?v=1&data=…` or the web's `<web address>/settings?tab=models#import=…`, checked as `docs/integrations/launchers.md` “Import links” says) or `""` when nothing was recognized.
  A draft is `{label?, aliases?, provider, env_names?, skipped_env?, skipped_headers?, matches?, notes?}`: `provider` is a `POST /api/v1/launchers` body with its empty fields left out (`kind`, `agent`, `api`, `name?` (a free startup ID, for an alias), `display_name?`, `base_url`, `auth`, `api_key?`, the model and tier fields, `models`, limits, proxy, `args`, `headers?` (`Name: value` lines), `env?` (`NAME=value` lines)); `skipped_env` is the alias import's; `skipped_headers` `[{name, reason}]` with `reason` `credential`, `protocol`, `unsupported` or `unsafe` (a value with a control character, a backslash or `$`); `matches` `[{name, display_name?, same_key}]` the stored providers on the same Base URL, those with the pasted key first.
  `notes` (top-level and per draft) `[{code, line?, name?}]`: `line` is 1-based in the pasted text, `name` an alias, variable, header, option, protocol, kind or sign-in method, never a value. Codes: `unrecognized`, `invalid_json`, `line_unused`, `not_claude`, `no_gateway`, `url_shell`, `url_user`, `url_query`, `key_shell`, `no_key`, `key_helper`, `args_left_out`, `header_unreadable`, `curl_option`, `curl_path`, `cindy_kind`, `cindy_auth`, `cindy_endpoint`, `cindy_request_path`, `link_invalid`, `link_version`, `link_too_long`, `link_field` (a refused link: the only note, no draft; `name` a field's path, or the version when it is a number), `too_many` (at most 200 notes and 100 `skipped_env` entries a draft); clients show an unknown code as a generic "not used" line.
  The pasted key comes back in `provider.api_key`; no other secret does (credential-like variables and headers are only named). At most 50 drafts. A body without `text`, or with only blanks, is 400; a body over 256 KiB is 413 `too_large`.
- `GET /api/v1/launchers/presets` → `{presets}`: built-in presets (`plugin: "builtin"`, id `builtin/<vendor>`, with extra `auth`, `signup_url`, `display_name`) plus plugin ones, sorted by request language; a plugin preset with the same id overrides the built-in one (`docs/integrations/launchers.md` "Built-in presets").
- `POST /api/v1/launchers` with `preset` may leave `name` empty (vendor slug, `-2` on collision); an empty `display_name` uses the preset's. With `assign: ["assistant","agent.new"]` it returns
  `{launcher, assigned: [purposes], kept: [{purpose, reason: "customized"|"incompatible"|"failed"}]}`, changing only purposes still at their defaults; other purposes are 400. `POST /api/v1/launchers/test` and `/discover` with `preset` use the preset's URL (and model) where not filled in. All of the above is registered in `features` as `builtin_presets`; clients use it only when they see it.
- `POST /api/v1/launchers` without `preset` may leave `name` empty too (feature `launcher_auto_name`): the startup ID is the slug of `display_name`, else of the base URL's host, else `provider`, with `-2`, `-3` while taken or reserved; with no `display_name` the host becomes it (`"gw.example.com 2"` for `gw-example-com-2`). A given `name` keeps its checks (400 invalid or reserved, 409 taken). `PUT /api/v1/launchers/{name}` changes `display_name` (left out or `null` keeps it, `""` clears it; over 64 characters or a control character 400); the ID in the path never changes ([launchers.md](../integrations/launchers.md) "Display names").
- A purpose's `fields` and `provider_ids` limit the editable parameters and compatible providers. `override` and `effective` are separate, `inherited_from` marks the source, and `status` is a status description in Chinese. Real tasks / plugins use `task.<id>` / `plugin.<id>`.

- Device scope (feature `launcher_scope`): a Persona-managed provider in `GET /api/v1/launchers` also has `share` (`all` / `selected` / `none`), `scope_machines`, `delivery` (`on_demand` / `push`), `own_service` (`skip` / `use`), `key_machines` (computers with their own key) and `legacy_scope: true` for one saved before scopes. `POST` / `PUT /api/v1/launchers` take the same plus `machine_keys: {"<machine id>": "<key>" or ""}`; a field left out is unchanged. Unknown values, `selected` without computers or an unknown machine id are 400. A start with a provider out of that computer's scope (`POST /api/v1/sessions`, the main chat, tasks, `…/check?machine=`) is 409 `launcher_out_of_scope`, or `launcher_own_service` when the provider skips computers with their own service and that one has it; `error` says what to change. `docs/integrations/launchers.md` "Device scope and on-demand delivery".
- Key references (feature `launcher_secret_references`): a Persona-managed provider's key may be a reference to a provider extension's secret. `POST` / `PUT /api/v1/launchers` take `api_key_reference` and `machine_key_references: {"<machine id>": "<reference>" or ""}` (with a key for the same at once: 400; one that is not a reference, has no enabled provider or does not resolve: 400). Its view answers `key_reference` and `machine_key_references` (`{provider, provider_name, reference, title}`), never the value; a refused `launchers.pull` says `launcher_key_unresolved`. `docs/extensions/secret-providers.md` "Launcher keys".

- Send through (#4775): a direct API connection (`kind: "api"`) in `GET /api/v1/launchers` has `via_machine`, the computer whose node sends its requests (left out: the manager itself). `POST` / `PUT /api/v1/launchers` take `via_machine` (left out keeps it, `""` clears it); on another kind, or naming a computer this manager doesn't have, it is 400. `POST /api/v1/launchers/test` and `/discover` take it too (left out: the stored one). `docs/assistant/model-config.md` "Sending through a computer".

`DELETE /api/v1/launchers/{name}` of a Persona-managed provider that a purpose of the catalog or a current extension purpose runs on answers 409 with a localized `error` naming those purposes, and deletes nothing; since #5806 the background supervisor's purpose is one of them (`docs/assistant/model-config.md` “Deleting a provider in use”).

Provider responses carry only the description and `has_key`, never secrets. Defaults, execution boundaries and compatibility rules are in `docs/assistant/model-config.md`.

## Data types

```jsonc
// Machine. kind: local | ssh | link; a link machine gains "link":{"version","address","since"} while persona-link is connected (docs/operations/link.md)
{"id":"laptop","name":"Laptop","kind":"ssh","ssh_host":"<SSH config alias>","online":true,"error":"",
 "hostname":"<machine hostname>","os":"darwin","arch":"arm64","herdr_version":"0.8.0","claude_version":"2.1.310",
 "last_seen":"...",
 // How it's connected (docs/server/server.md "tailcat hole punching"): transport is local | ssh | tailcat (absent when offline); tailcat: a tailcat address is configured;
 // tailcat_path only when going through tailcat: direct (hole punched, peer-to-peer) | relay (via DERP relay). Old hubs don't have these fields
 "transport":"ssh","tailcat":true,
 // Engine ("Engines" below): the terminal host the user chose for this machine (the saved choice, not what the node reports); the hub always sends it (herdr if never chosen); engines is what the node
 // found on this machine (empty array when offline). Old hubs don't have these two fields
 "engine":"herdr",
 "engines":[{"id":"herdr","name":"herdr","available":true,"version":"0.9.3"},
            {"id":"herdr-core","name":"Herdr App","available":false},
            {"id":"herdr-both","name":"herdr + Herdr App","available":false}],
 // System info (docs/server/machines.md): reported by the node the last time it connected, stored in the hub's database, present even when offline; old nodes don't have this field
 "system":{"os":"darwin","distro":"macos","like":"","name":"macOS 26.1","version":"26.1","build":"25B78",
           "kernel":"Darwin 25.1.0","arch":"arm64","model":"MacBook Pro","cpu":"Apple M4 Pro","cores":14,
           "memory":51539607552,"boot_time":1790000000},
 // How the primary reaches this one (docs/server/mesh.md "Multiple paths to one computer", plan-hub-center.md 5): hub_id / hub_name is the hub it currently goes through (direct means the primary itself,
 // through a member means that member); machine_uid is the computer's own uid (old nodes don't have it); route.via is local | service | link | ssh | tailcat (hops 0) or
 // hub (through a member, hops 1); rtt_ms is omitted when not measured. Present without linked hubs too (all this hub). id: the primary's id if the primary's hub.json has it; for ones configured only on a member, the member's
 // id, with @<member name> appended on collision. kind is the hub's: a computer configured only on a member. Old hubs don't have these fields
 "hub_id":"<hub UUID>","hub_name":"Home","machine_uid":"<UUID>","route":{"via":"service","hops":0,"rtt_ms":12},
 // Optional: when there is more than one path (or only through a member), one entry per path: method, which hub (the primary's own paths use the primary's hub_id), usable now, latest RTT, whether it's the active one
 "paths":[{"via":"service","hub_id":"<hub UUID>","ok":true,"rtt_ms":12,"active":true},{"via":"hub","hub_id":"<member hub UUID>","ok":true,"rtt_ms":40}],
 // Optional (feature machine_trust, onboarding plan #287 5.3): trust pending means this computer is waiting for the user to confirm ("Computer trust" below); omitted = confirmed;
 // error_code says which kind error is: node_service_down (link is up, resident node not running) | link_offline (connected before, disconnected now) | never_connected (a computer-connects /
 // hub-connects computer that has never connected) | node_outdated (online, the node is another version and too old to update remotely from here); the raw error is still sent, unknown codes show error
 "trust":"pending","error_code":"never_connected"}

// MetricSample: one reading (every 10 seconds). Unmeasured fields are absent (the first reading has no cpu / net_*), not 0; cores is Linux only
{"t":1790003600,"cpu":42.5,"cores":[40,45],"load":3.1,"mem_used":34359738368,"mem_total":68719476736,
 "swap_used":0,"swap_total":0,"net_rx":1024.5,"net_tx":512,"disk_used":10737418240,"disk_total":107374182400}

// MetricPoint: one step in history (average within the step); gap means a break here, don't draw a line across it. mem / swap / disk are bytes used
{"t":1790000000,"cpu":10.2,"load":1.25,"mem":34359738368,"swap":0,"rx":2048,"tx":512,"disk":10737418240}
{"t":1790000240,"gap":true}

// Launcher (from zsh: functions listed in _claude_launchers, plus aliases that call claude; docs/integrations/launchers.md). Each item from GET …/launchers also carries agent_type
// (claude / codex / traex / a runtime's agent; treated as Claude when an old hub lacks it): when unset it is inferred from agent, then from the name (codex, traex). hub.json's
// machines[].launchers can add wrapper functions or override the type, e.g. [{"name":"example_wrapper","agent_type":"codex"}]; same-name config keeps the model and gateway fields it doesn't override
// (sessionLaunchers in the manager's assistant/models_launchers_routes.go). Android filters launchers by type.
{"name":"example_launcher","base_url":"https://example.com","model":"<model name>","agent_type":"claude"}
// Codex launchers (codex on PATH, aliases that run codex) carry agent; starting one requires prompt and can't be async (docs/integrations/codex.md "Starting from the phone")
{"name":"codex","model":"Default","agent":"codex","agent_type":"codex"}
// A provider added in Settings › Model providers carries its display name in GET /machines/{mid}/launchers (launcher_auto_name); name stays the ID a start sends
{"name":"team-relay","display_name":"Team relay","base_url":"https://relay.example.com","model":"<model name>","agent_type":"claude"}
// GET /machines/{mid}/launchers adds health: that launcher's latest check or start on this computer (docs/server/launcher-health.md); absent when never checked,
// when a failure is older than 6 hours, and from older hubs. Clients gray out state "blocked" with a reason per kind and never hide it (#1643).
{"name":"example_gateway","model":"<model name>","agent_type":"claude","health":{"state":"blocked","kind":"not_in_terminal","error":"bash: example_gateway: command not found","checked_at":"2026-11-09T08:00:00Z"}}
// A start request may carry agent_type, and wrapper functions launch per the declared type: Claude keeps the original arguments, Codex / compatible forks don't get Claude-only arguments, and get the real session ID
// through the existing herdr / process detection; the first message is passed to the launcher as a single argument. Permission mode and reasoning effort apply only to Claude for now; Android's new-session form hides both when another type is chosen.

// Session: (machine_id, session_id) is unique. session_id is Claude Code's session uuid.
{"machine_id":"server","session_id":"uuid","title":"AI-generated title or directory name","cwd":"<project directory>",
 // cwd: an Agent's latest working directory (Claude Code records the shell's directory after each Bash `cd`), except that an Agent whose `cd` landed in an
 // assistant or health directory itself is listed where it started. For an assistant or health chat it is the directory the chat runs in, where it started,
 // never where its last `cd` left it (#2368): the node lists it there running, at rest and in session info. Only an updated node keeps to this: one from
 // before #2368 reports the latest directory for rows at rest (a chat drifts out of its directory, an Agent into an assistant one), and nothing tells the two apart
 "workspace_cwd":"<physical directory verified by the node>",   // optional; used for workspace association, falls back to cwd when missing, doesn't replace the original cwd
 "repo_root":"<main checkout of the repo cwd belongs to>",   // optional (#2840): named by the host (the Paseo bridge: its worktrees live under Paseo's own directory), else read by the node off git (#1805);
                   // "By Repository" groups by it: cwd inside it is the main checkout, otherwise one of its worktrees. When absent, clients infer from the cwd path as before
 "worktree":"<top of the git working tree cwd is in>",         // optional (#1805): the node reads it, and repo_root when no host names it, off git's files (node/gitplace.go): repo_root is the main checkout, a linked worktree resolves to its main repository
                   // both are physical directories (symbolic links resolved, #4492), whichever way cwd is written and whichever way a host wrote the repo_root it named: every session of a repository names the same repo_root, and worktree equals repo_root for the main checkout
 "branch":"<branch checked out in worktree>",                // optional (#1805): "" / absent when detached or not a git checkout; the apps group machine → project (repo_root) → worktree (labelled branch) → sessions
 "status":"idle|working|blocked|done|unknown|offline",   // offline = not running in herdr, only a transcript, can be resumed
 "pane_id":"w1:p2","tab_id":"w1:t2","workspace_id":"w1","agent_name":"j-3f2a",
 "pane_index":0,   // optional (#2320): this pane's positional index within its tab, from 0, top-left is 0 (the other panes were all split from it; with Agents, it's the group's initiator);
                   // the herdr node computes it from the snapshot's layouts; omitted when the host gives no layout, on old nodes, or when the pane isn't in the layout (0 is still sent; only absence means unknown). See docs/protocol/agent-states.md "Several panes in one tab"
 "agent":"claude","agent_label":"",   // agent_label only on Agents the App doesn't know: the runtime's name for it ("DSH", see "Runtime ↔ node")
 "agent_surface":"cli",   // optional (#6390): the client the agent runs in, "desktop" (Claude's or Codex's desktop app) or "cli" (its command line), read off its record
                          // (Claude Code's entrypoint, a Codex rollout's originator); omitted when it does not say (an SDK, a runtime, older nodes). The apps badge the command line's mark with </>
 "launcher":"cc_ds","model":"deepseek/v4.1-flash-chain","started_by_persona":true,"assistant":false,
 "ultracode":false,"ultracode_note":"…","ultracode_pending":true,"ultracode_lost_at":"...", // Optional; see "Claude Code ultracode". Omitted ultracode means unknown
 "pending_switch":{"launcher":"work","model":"opus","effort":"high","agent":"codex","at":"..."}, // Optional (#5035): a switch to another provider waiting for the next message; see "Switching a running Agent to another provider".
                   // agent (#5054): the engine ("claude" / "codex") a switch to the other engine moves the conversation to; absent for one within the engine
 "engine_history":[{"session_id":"<sid>","agent":"claude","until":"..."}], // Optional (#5054): the conversation's earlier stretches, oldest first, on the session running it now; see "Switching a running Agent to another engine"
 "origin":"inbox","origin_ref":"<Inbox item id>",   // only on assistant chats (assistant: true): who opened this chat, see "Origin of assistant chats" below; absent = user
 "opened_by":"<extension id>",   // only on assistant chats an extension's token opened, see "Origin of assistant chats" below; absent for any other
 "model_pick":{"launcher":"cx","model":"gpt-5","effort":"high"},   // only on assistant chats switched to a model in the app (PUT …/conversations/{id}/model, feature assistant_model_pick, #5033):
                   // what its next messages run on, model and effort optional; absent = it follows the default (Model configuration › Main chat for the main chat and a scheduled task's, otherwise what it runs). Summary rows carry it too
 "updated_at":"...","last_text":"first 200 characters of the last assistant text",
     "turn_error":"API Error: Connection lost mid-response… (only when stopped and this turn was interrupted by a model API error, otherwise absent; its task counts as \"interrupted\", #1516. Claude Code: the hub recognizes it from the start of the last line; Codex: the node reports it from task_complete.error / a failed turn/completed, #2185)",
     "turn_error_kind":"transient (optional: only when the agent itself states the error kind, Codex's codex_error_info: transient is worth a \"continue\", user needs the user to act, usage_limit is a subscription limit until it resets; otherwise judged from the turn_error text, docs/assistant/agent-work.md \"Triage\"; for Claude Code's \"Not logged in\", a wrong Key or a wrong model the hub fills in user)",
     "model_fallback":{"subtype":"model_refusal_fallback","original_model":"primary-model","fallback_model":"fallback-model","category":"synthetic-policy","scope":"session","explanation":"Upstream refused the request","text":"<the refusal's own words>"}, // optional: active refusal fallback; cleared by a confirmed model change. The public projection only (#2528), as in Item.model_refusal
     "model_restore":{"state":"next_start","to":"configured-model","at":"..."}, // optional: "back to the configured model" was asked for the active refusal fallback (#2528): the session's idle headless process was closed (or none ran), so its next start asks for `to`, the configured model as the node read it. Not proof it runs: it ends when a newer reply is written (from any model), the fallback record is replaced or gone, or the node restarts
     "turn_error_resets_at":"...",   // optional, with turn_error_kind usage_limit: when that subscription limit resets (RFC3339). Absent when the reset is not known
     "turn_error_resumes":true,   // optional: the CLI continues by itself once the limit resets. Absent or false: nothing of the CLI will, though the hub may still schedule a continuation (work.wake_at)
     "turn_error_code":"not_logged_in (optional: only when the hub recognizes the problem from turn_error: not_logged_in / auth_failed / model_route / rate_limited / model_fallback_unavailable; the last means an active refusal fallback is unavailable, not a wrong configured model; clients use it to draw a \"fix it\" card, see the new-user onboarding plan section 5.2)","pending_interactions":1,
 "work":{"phase":"blocked","on":"external","line":"Wait for the deploy to finish, then run the production tests","wait":"deploy finished","then":"run the production tests","every_minutes":5,
         "wake_at":"...","resets_at":"...","attempts":1,"max":6,"turn_at":"...","at":"...","by":"model"},
     // Work state (docs/assistant/agent-work.md): phase working | blocked | done; blocked's on is user (waiting for your decision; questions / link /
     // interaction_id are the card Persona opened for it) | agent (waiting for another Agent, agent:{machine_id,session_id,label}) | external (waiting for a deploy, CI, a point in time;
     // Persona wakes it at wake_at) | transient (the model service is temporarily failing; Persona sends "continue" at wake_at); done carries artifacts:[{kind:pr|commit|doc|build|url,ref}].
     // resets_at: when a subscription usage limit that stopped the turn resets (docs/assistant/agent-work.md "Usage limits").
     // "closeout":{"status":"done|not_done|blocked","merged":"yes|no","deployed":"yes|no","waiting":"…","missing":"…","did":["…"],"verified":"…","checked":{"merged":"yes|no","deployed":"yes|no"}}: the Agent's own record of the turn, with what the hub found when it looked at the pull request itself (checked), when it wrote one (docs/assistant/agent-work.md "Closeout"); lists omit did and verified.
     // Working is just {"phase":"working"}; absent after a turn stops and before triage (or when it can't tell). For finished ones and ones waiting for Persona to wake them, state is idle, not unread.
     // {"phase":"","line":"Not finished: …","closeout":{…}}: a turn that is not finished: its closeout says not_done (or blocked on nothing the triage could name), or the hub disproved its
     // merged / deployed claim, and the line then names that claim. state stays unread. The phase is empty and not a fourth value because clients draw a line under an unknown or empty phase as plain text,
     // and take only blocked for a wait and done for finished (docs/assistant/agent-work.md "Closeout").
     // Triage is done by the manager (the assistant process); the hub fills it in from what it reports in the snapshot (only for sessions still stopped on that turn), see "Agents" under "Bus" below
 "activity":"running tests","activity_at":"...",   // only when the latest step is a tool call with no new text since: what this step is doing (summarized by the node from the transcript, within 40 characters) and when it started; gone once new text is written or a new turn starts
 "queued":["messages typed while working, not yet picked up"],
 "queued_relayed":1,   // a Persona chat: the last this many of queued came from other conversations or the system, which its manager delivers when the turn has ended and the owner is not talking in it, by rank and not in this order (docs/assistant/assistant.md "Messages from the system wait for the owner"); an idle chat has them too; apps show them but take back, delete, move and send now only the others (#4342). Absent: none
 "subagents":[{"id":"a849e1f0…","session_id":"<id>@a849e1f0…","type":"Explore","description":"…","tool_use_id":"toolu_…",
                "parent_id":"c27d03b1…","fork":true,   // who started it: the id of the subagent that started it (absent when the main session did); fork = forked off. Treated as top-level when the parent isn't in the list
                "running":true,"background":true,"started_at":"...","updated_at":"...","last_text":"…",   // subagents are read as sessions
                "steps":7,"last_tool":{"id":"toolu_…","name":"Bash","summary":"running the tests"},   // #5602: tool calls made, the latest one (what it does now; summary in the request's language, like a workflow agent's latest_tool); updated_at is its last message's time, not the file's mtime
                "model":"claude-haiku-4-5-…","tokens":23456}],   // #5030: the model it ran on, its latest reply's in its own transcript (never <synthetic>), not the one its Agent call asked for; tokens is its latest reply's context + output tokens, as a workflow agent's. Each absent until it has replied; old nodes don't have them. sessions.changed goes out when its running, steps, last_tool or updated_at change; these ride along
 "loop":{"kind":"wakeup|cron","prompt":"/loop …","reason":"…","interval_seconds":1800,"next_at":"...","cron":"*/5 * * * *","ticks":12},
 "goal":{"objective":"…","status":"active|paused|blocked|usage_limited|budget_limited|complete","reason":"…",   // the goal it's working on (docs/integrations/agent-goal.md)
        "tokens_used":12345,"token_budget":500000,"seconds":600,"updated_at":"..."},                              // absent when there is no goal
 "plan":{"done":3,"total":5,"current":"Reproducing the crash in landscape","at":"..."},   // the agent's own task list (Claude Code's TodoWrite / TaskCreate / TaskUpdate; docs/integrations/agent-goal.md "Plan"): done of total items completed, current = the item in progress (its activeForm, else its subject; one line, at most 120 characters; absent when none is), at = when these last changed. Absent when it keeps no list, and for Codex and runtimes. Old nodes don't have this field
 // TCP ports the Agent's processes listen on that answer HTTP (docs/operations/ports.md): one entry per port; title is its home page's <title> (absent if none). Old nodes don't have this field
 "ports":[{"port":5173,"addr":"127.0.0.1","pid":4242,"process":"node","title":"Vite + React"}],
 // Linked unfinished to-do (docs/assistant/todos.md): only present while currently linked (not released) and the to-do is unfinished; filled in by the hub
 "todo":{"id":"todo_…","title":"Ship version 1.3 of the weather App"},
 "quiet":true,   // an Agent working (or that worked) on a quiet task (#1731, docs/assistant/unified-entry.md "Quiet tasks"): kept out of task notifications and the global badge, and stays set after the task is done
 "background":[{"id":"b85polnoj","kind":"shell|agent|monitor|workflow","description":"…","command":"…",   // background commands / subagents / Monitors / workflows that haven't reported back yet
                "output_file":"/private/tmp/…/b85polnoj.output","started_at":"...",
                "expires_at":"...",          // Monitor: stops by itself at this time (the "expires in 30m" in the result); absent if not stated
                "run_id":"wf_c1d9daf8-cd2"}], // workflow: which run in workflows it is; only running workflows are here (old clients still treat it as a background task)
 // Claude Code workflows (multi-agent scripts the Workflow tool runs in the background, #2935, docs/protocol/agent-states.md "Background workflows"): the last day's, newest first.
 // Running ones (running=true) count as background work: the hub computes state as working, doesn't push "done", doesn't judge the to-do complete or auto-close this Agent. Old nodes don't have this field
 // phase_stats follows phases order, including phases with no agents yet, then appends undeclared phases; title="" means unknown. done counts journal results only; failed counts the journal's failed lines (#5511, omitted when 0; older nodes counted them as done); agents stopped when the run ended are in none of done / failed / running.
 // A retried agent (Claude Code's workflow view starts the same call again: the journal's same key, a new agentId) counts once, as its latest attempt: the attempts it replaced are in no count, phase_stats or agents, only in tokens / calls (#2323; older nodes kept counting them as running until the run ended).
 // Each agent's tokens is the latest assistant usage's input_tokens + output_tokens + cache_read_input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens, not a cumulative total. Claude Code's own error replies (model <synthetic> / isApiErrorMessage, usage all zeros), usage whose input_tokens + cache_read_input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens is 0 (a gateway's on a turn's other replies, whatever its output_tokens) and a gateway's whole-turn sum (over transcript.PlausibleContext) are skipped: the last real one stands.
 // calls counts tool_use / server_tool_use, deduplicated by nonempty tool_use_id; latest_tool keeps the last tool even after the final reply. latest_tool.summary is a short line on what the call does, in the request's language (the node writes it in Chinese and the hub rewrites it, like activity). Clients retain their existing display when these fields are absent.
 // Pushes: sessions.changed goes out when a workflow's status, phase, any of its agent counts, or a listed agent's latest_tool name / calls change, at most as often as node rereads workflows (1.5 s); tokens, last_text and the rest ride along with those pushes.
 "workflows":[{"task_id":"wdp5zxh37","run_id":"wf_c1d9daf8-cd2","name":"parity-audit","summary":"…",
               "status":"running|completed|failed|killed|stalled","running":true,   // stalled: no end notification, but no activity for 30 minutes (its claude is gone); not counted as running
               "phases":["Audit","Verify"],"phase":"Verify","phase_index":2,"phase_count":2,   // phases from the script's meta; phase is the phase of the most recently started agent still running, phase_index counts from 1, 0 = unknown
               "phase_stats":[{"title":"Audit","started":180,"done":167,"failed":2,"running":11},{"title":"Verify","started":5,"done":0,"running":5}], // per-phase counts across all agents, unaffected by the 60-agent response limit
               "tool_use_id":"toolu_…",                                            // the Workflow call that started it
               "agents_started":185,"agents_done":167,"agents_failed":2,"agents_running":16, // the total is known only once finished (the script dispatches as it runs): show "done / started"; agents_failed only when > 0
               "tokens":123400,"calls":420,                                    // sums across all agents, before truncation; tokens is not cumulative consumption
               "started_at":"...","ended_at":"...","updated_at":"...",           // ended_at only once finished; duration = (ended_at or now) - started_at
               "error":"Error: Workflow aborted",                                 // first line for failed / killed
               "agents":[{"id":"a55ab0b9…","session_id":"<id>@a55ab0b9…","label":"audit:chat-rich","phase":"Audit",   // in start order, at most 60 (newest kept)
                          "running":false,"status":"running|done|failed|stopped",   // failed: the journal says it failed (an API error ended it; older nodes said done); stopped: it hadn't come back when the run ended
                          "started_at":"...","ended_at":"...","updated_at":"...","last_text":"…", // ended_at is absent while running; done and failed agents use the last exchange time (file mtime as fallback), stopped agents prefer the run's end time; omitted if unknown
                          "model":"claude-example","latest_tool":{"id":"toolu_…","name":"Read","summary":"Reading example.go"}, // summary in the request's language
                          "tokens":1234,"calls":8}]}],                   // each agent is read as a subagent: GET the content of session session_id
 "asks":"Push it to beta?",   // what the last reply asks the user, read by the node off the whole reply (last_text is only its start); absent when it asks nothing (#5096, docs/protocol/agent-states.md "Awaiting your reply")
 "asks_read":true,            // the node read asks off the reply (empty asks then means it asks nothing, was answered, or its closeout says done and needs nobody, #4110); without it the hub reads last_text when it is whole
 "awaits_reply":true,         // stopped (unread / idle) on a question nobody answered, with no card, error or background work. Computed by the hub; clients list an idle one as "Awaiting your reply", not folded with the idle ones
 // Session hierarchy (#5120, #5180, see "Session hierarchy" below), each omitted when empty:
 "started_at":"...",                    // when the session began (a Codex rollout's first line, a runtime's created time); set by the node where it knows it
 "asking_parent_session_id":"<sid>",    // a runtime child that waits for the user (status blocked, its parent fields cleared): the parent it asks for. Set by the node
 "folded_under":"<sid>",                // a child session: its topmost listed ancestor on the same machine, whose chat shows it; a tab's worker: its lead. Set by the manager
 "folded_as":"worker",                  // beside folded_under on a tab's worker (not on a child): it folds under its tab's lead ("Tab teams" below). Set by the manager
 "children":{"total":3,"working":1,"needs_you":1,"workers":2},   // on that ancestor: every session folded under it, by their own states (working / needs_you omitted when 0); workers: how many of them are its tab's workers (folded_as "worker", omitted when 0). Set by the manager
 "background_waiting":true,   // background_working, and all that background work only waits (#6045): its background commands sleep, loop on a check or watch something, using next to no CPU, and no subagent or workflow runs. Clients write "Waiting in the background", lighter than Working and not in its count; state stays working, so older apps show Working. Omitted when false
 "background_working":true,   // state is working only because of background work (this turn is over, workflows / background commands / Monitors / subagents are running, #2935): clients write "Working (Background)". Computed by the hub; omitted when false, so its absence means an old hub (before #3127) only when no run carries tool_use_id and no agent status: there, look for state=working with a running workflow
```
