 // The user's latest manual compaction (assistant chats only, present only after POST …/compact): running → done | failed (error is a human-readable reason); the node keeps it until the next one
 "compaction":{"state":"running|done|failed","error":"…","started_at":"...","finished_at":"..."}}

// Todo: a to-do item (docs/assistant/todos.md)
{"id":"todo_…","title":"Ship version 1.3 of the weather App","notes":"Notes","done_at":null,
 "created_at":"...","updated_at":"...",

                            "detail":"the report as the agent wrote it (Markdown)",   // #3181: at most 2000 characters, ending in … when cut; absent when it equals text

### Always allow

A permission card offers **Always allow** only where the answer is kept (#3590). The manager says so in
`always_honored`, a tri-state:

- `true`: it is kept. The manager sets it on a node's card in an assistant chat whose `always_keys` it remembers
  (a store, at most 32 keys, no `fields`), and on a card of its own that says in `always_label` what it keeps (the apps
  a computer may use, LCU's own scopes).
- `false`: nothing would keep it. The manager sets it on every other card it asks itself: the extensions' tools
  (`computer_*`, `browser_run`, `iphone_do`, connector writes, `extension.ui`), `persona_settings`, its to-do, agent
  and health confirmations; and on a node's card in an assistant chat it will not remember (keys but no store, more
  than 32 keys, `fields`, or a health conversation's card, confirmed each time). Clients show only Allow and Deny, and
  no scope line. An `always` answered on such a card anyway (an older client) is dropped: the card is allowed once.
- absent: clients keep their own rule, as before: on iOS a card with a session, on the web, Android and in Lark a card
  from Claude (no `agent`, or `claude`) or one with an `always_label`. Agents sessions' cards never carry the field: their
  agent keeps Always itself (Claude Code's session rule).

The field is a tri-state rather than a plain "kept" flag because absence cannot mean "not kept": an Agents session's
Claude card and a manager card look the same otherwise (a session, no `agent`, no `always_keys`), and an older
manager sends neither. So a new client hides the choice only on an explicit `false`, and keeps Always on every card
an older manager sends. An older client ignores the field and keeps offering Always on manager cards; answering it
allows once, as before, and is no longer recorded as an Always. The value is the manager's: whatever a node sends in
the field (or in `tool_title`) is dropped.

`tool_title` is the tool's name for people in the user's language (`assistant-tool_titles` in the hub's catalog,
"iPhone control" for `iphone_do`), set by the manager on its own tools' cards and on a node's card for one of
Persona's own MCP tools (`mcp__persona__…` under either namespace, #4966: "Report to supervisor · Done", the phone's
tools as "iPhone · contacts search", any other "Persona · agent read"). Clients title the card with it, and otherwise
with `tool_name` as before; Agents sessions' cards for any other tool never carry it. Where the title also says what
this call does (a report's kind), `tool_name_title` names the tool alone ("Report to supervisor"): a line about what
Always covers, every call of the tool, uses it, else `tool_title`, else the tool's name in words. Both are in the
hub's language (the manager's `lang`, from the hub's locale) like the rest of the text it writes, whatever language
the app is in. A node's value for either is dropped.

### Subagent deliveries as tool results

Claude Code subagent launch receipts, peer reports (including `SendMessage` to the parent), handbacks and task
notifications use the existing `tool_result` kind when the parser knows their launching `Agent` or `Task` call.
Both the item and its `task` carry that call's `tool_use_id`; `task.kind` is `agent`. The association comes from the
runtime's agent ID and launch record, or a notification's explicit call ID, never the sender's display name.
Unrelated cross-session messages retain their existing `user` text and `from` provenance. Unknown associations are
not invented.

- `task.status: running` marks a launch receipt or an interim report. `waiting` also remains nonterminal. These
  results do not end the running subagent or count as a user question. Completed, failed, killed and stopped results
  are terminal. Unknown statuses must not be inferred as completed.
- Each delivery retains its original item ID and sequence. There can be several results for one call: clients keep
  an ordered result list rather than replacing earlier reports with the latest item. Render them only under the
  original call, collapsed by default and manually expandable, not as independent messages in the parent chat.
  Running subagents keep their existing work/progress presentation.
- `text` is the report body, capped for pages with the normal `full_size` marker. `task.detail` is a bounded 4 KB
  compatibility preview. Use `text` first and the existing item full-text endpoint for manual full inspection.
  Launch receipts are not reports. A status-only notification, including the pointer after an already delivered
  handback, has no `text` or `task.detail`; its status still participates in the call's lifecycle.
- `wake` marks a task notification or associated peer report delivered as a user line while the parent was idle,
  including hidden `isMeta` peer lines. Queued-command attachments absorbed mid-turn do not carry it. It starts a
  new parent turn without becoming a user-authored message. Cold windows reconstruct earlier launch associations
  and delivery status before parsing their tail; incremental reads append results, never rewrite the old receipt.

Apple integration (#3377): decode `task` on `tool_result` as well as on legacy notices, accept `running`, retain all
results per call and use only terminal evidence to stop the work bar. Handle `wake` independently of item kind.
Keep the existing full-text reader for each result. Older nodes still send agent notices, so continue associating
those by their explicit call/task IDs without guessing from `from`. The Claude transcript history token includes
an opaque parser-version component; the existing history-change reset discards cached standalone peer cards when
an updated node is first read. Clients must not parse this token or require a new feature flag.

### Answering a question from its notification

A question notification may carry an optional top-level `ask` alongside `interaction_id`, `machine_id`, `session_id` and `hub_id`. This is an additive server protocol; clients that do not implement notification choices continue opening the card in the App.

```json
{
  "interaction_id": "ix_example",
  "machine_id": "computer_example",
  "session_id": "session_example",
  "hub_id": "hub_example",
  "ask": {
    "question": "Which library?",
    "options": ["pgx", "sqlc"],
    "multi_select": false,
    "rev": "<opaque rev from the hub>"
  }
}
```

The usual `aps` alert is omitted from this example. `ask` is present only for a `question` card with exactly one question, at least one option, no fields to fill in, and a non-health conversation. The question and ordered option labels are complete; the shortened display text in `aps.alert.body` is never an answer source. `rev` is an opaque 12-character hexadecimal SHA-256 prefix covering the question, option labels and their order, and `multi_select`. Clients echo the received value; they do not calculate it.

The hub first shortens the alert text to fit the push limit. If it still cannot fit, it drops the entire `ask`, restores the original alert text and fits that text again. It never truncates `ask.question`, truncates an option label, or removes individual options. Relay pushes seal `ask` with the rest of the payload; the relay receives no plaintext question or labels. The smaller encrypted-payload budget can omit `ask` even when the corresponding direct push would retain it.

Send the selected zero-based index back to the hub identified by the notification, using the same authentication as resolve:

```http
POST /api/v1/interactions/ix_example/choose
Authorization: Bearer <device token>
Content-Type: application/json
Accept-Language: en

{"option":1,"rev":"<rev from ask>","client_id":"<unique id for this tap>"}
```

For a card with `multi_select:true`, send `{"options":[1,0],"rev":"<rev from ask>","client_id":"<unique id for this submission>"}`. Send exactly one of `option` or `options`; `options` must be non-empty and have no repeated indexes. A single-select card accepts only one index. The hub validates the current card and revision, maps indexes to the complete labels in the card's order, and forwards a normal Resolution to the card's owning manager. For the example, index 1 becomes `{"answers":{"Which library?":"sqlc"}}`; multi-select indexes `[1,0]` become `{"answers":{"Which library?":"pgx, sqlc"}}`. Supplying a manager header does not override the card's owner.

On success the response is `200 {"ok":true}`. Keep the same `client_id`, target, revision and indexes when retrying a submission after a lost response. The body ID uses the existing `withClientOp` receipt mechanism; without `client_id`, an explicit `X-Persona-Op-Id` UUID is also supported. When both are present, `client_id` determines the receipt ID. A stored successful receipt replays success even after the card has disappeared. Reusing an ID with different parameters or another device returns `409 op_id_reused`. Without an operation ID there is no durable receipt. Full and answer-only device credentials may choose. Extension credentials require `agents.control` and remain limited to their own manager's cards.

Errors have `{code,error}`, with human-readable `error` localized in English, Simplified Chinese or Japanese. Branch on `code`:

| HTTP | Code | Meaning and client action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `bad_request` | Malformed JSON, a missing revision or missing / conflicting selection fields. Open the card in the App. |
| 400 | `invalid_choice` | An index is negative, beyond the options, or repeated, or an `options` entry is null. Open the card in the App. |
| 400 | `single_select` | More than one option was supplied for a single-select card. Ask for one selection. |
| 400 | `not_choosable` | The current card cannot be answered by notification choices (multiple questions, no options, fields, health conversation or another card kind). Open it in the App. |
| 409 | `ask_changed` | The revision no longer matches. Open and refresh the card; never apply the old index to new options. |
| 409 | `not_pending` | The card is absent from the hub's pending cards, or the manager reports it already ended. This includes unknown, answered, withdrawn and expired cards; do not submit another choice. Open the App to inspect the current state. |
| 409 | `op_id_reused` | The submission ID already names a different operation. Keep the original request when checking its result. |
| 413 | `too_large` | The request body exceeds 4 KiB. |
| 502 | `assistant_in_doubt` | The connection dropped or timed out after sending; the choice may already have been applied. Open the App to check the card. The receipt stays unknown and the same ID will not execute again. |
| 503 | `assistant_offline` | The owning manager did not receive the choice. Retry the unchanged submission when it reconnects. |

The shared authentication, scope, size-limit and operation-receipt errors still apply. A `202` receipt state of `pending` or `unknown` is not successful delivery: repeat the unchanged request to inspect its receipt, or open the App, retaining the original submission ID. An uncertain upstream outcome must not be resubmitted under a new ID. An `assistant_offline` refusal keeps no receipt when the store can release it, so the same ID can be tried again; an uncertain result stays recorded.

When `ask` is absent, cannot be decrypted, or cannot be rendered completely by the client, open the App. A hub that lacks this endpoint returns 404 / 405; open the App and use its existing card flow. Do not reconstruct answers from the clipped alert text. Native notification buttons and their UI are outside this server change.

### Closing a question without an answer

A question advertises `can_cancel:true` only when its runtime can discard that request and release its waiter without interrupting the task. Clients hide the close action when the field is absent or false. Send only `{"cancel":true}` to the existing resolve endpoint; mixing cancellation with answers, dismissal, approvals, keys, or other actions returns 400 and leaves the card pending. Approvals cannot be cancelled through this action. Folding a card remains local UI state.

The manager records `cancelled` with the cancellation resolution, removes the pending card, and releases its waiter once. Repeated HTTP cancellation returns the recorded result, and a reconnecting resumable hook receives the same cancellation instead of a new question. Claude `AskUserQuestion` hooks deny only that tool call without `updatedInput.answers`; Codex owned and joined app-server `item/tool/requestUserInput` requests receive `{"answers":{}}` on the original request, with no user message or `turn/interrupt`. The assistant's `ask_user` tool also releases its wait with an explicit no-answer result. Existing `dismiss` still hands control back to the computer.

Manager-owned `persona_triage` cards also advertise cancellation, including restored cards created by older versions. Their cancellation defers only that turn, removes its wakeup, and sends no Agent message. Triage option objects may carry `action:"defer"`; clients still submit the selected label in `answers`, and the owner interprets the action on that exact offered single-choice option. Existing clients can ignore the new optional field. Terminal outcomes are replayed to the owner without showing the same ID again.

Terminal-only Codex questions (including asynchronous rollout questions) do not advertise cancellation: sending Escape may fold a pane, clear notes, or stop a turn. Upgrade the hub, manager, and the node running the supported runtime before expecting the button; older components omit the capability. Existing runtime questions created before the upgrade keep their original capability; manager-owned triage cards are upgraded when restored.

### Decision fields

The assistant's `ask_user` card keeps what the assistant said of the decision, on the card itself and so in `GET /api/v1/interactions/history` (`assistant/decision_deadline.go`, `keepAskDecision`):

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `deadline` (card) | RFC 3339: when, unanswered, its recommended options are taken by default (reversible) or the user is reminded again (not). Absent without a deadline |
| `reversible` (card) | Whether going ahead can be undone, as the assistant said it. Absent when it did not say (it must with a deadline): never guessed |
| `questions[].recommend` | The label of the option the assistant recommends, always one of the question's options. Absent when it recommended none |

Cards from before this change, and every other card (Agents' questions, permissions, plans, screens), have none of them. They are optional keys on the `interaction` object; the apps read past them (`spec/fixtures/wire/interactions.json` `interaction_question_decision`). A card the assistant passed on to the user keeps its single recommendation in `delegate.recommend`, as before.

### Who answered a card

`resolution.answered_by` says who answered: absent for the user (in an app, a channel, or the to-do the question became), `assistant` for the assistant on the user's behalf (`reason` says why), `default` when nobody answered and the recommended options were taken at a reversible deadline (`reason` says so).

An `ask_user` card that expires unanswered becomes a to-do (`docs/assistant/todos.md`). Its history stays `expired`; what was answered after that is recorded on it with `resolution.late: true` (`assistant/late_answer.go`, `db.LateAnswer`): the user's own answers on the to-do (`answered_by` absent; one per question as each is given) or the default taken at the deadline (`answered_by: "default"`, with the deadline's `reason`), and `resolved_at` becomes when that happened. A question that cannot be undone is never taken by default, so its history keeps no answer until the user gives one. An expired card from before this change has no `late` answer. Only the manager writes `late` and `answered_by`: an app's answer has them dropped.

### MCP elicitation

`hello.features` adds `elicitation`. Clients must declare it explicitly in `client_hello.features`; Android and the web client declare it by default (the web client's `X-Persona-Client` gives platform web, version 1, matching the `platform` / `version` in its `client_hello`), and so does the iOS app (`ios-app` and its version, the two halves of its `X-Persona-Client`, `RequestClientMetadata`). The Mac and visionOS apps and the watch don't declare it. The `interaction` object in the existing `interaction` event gains the following optional fields; no keys are added at the envelope's top level:

```json
{
  "kind": "elicitation",
  "mcp_server_name": "example-mcp",
  "agent_id": "agent_example",
  "agent_type": "worker",
  "elicitation": {
    "mode": "form",
    "message": "Please choose",
    "requested_schema": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {"choice": {"type": "string", "enum": ["yes", "no"]}}
    }
  }
}
```

In URL mode `elicitation` is `{"mode":"url","message":"Open the link to confirm","url":"https://example.com/confirm","elicitation_id":"request_example"}`. `mcp_config_source`, `tool_name` and `tool_use_id` are all optional and present only when the source provides them; Claude Code 2.1.306's Elicitation input provides no tool association or config source, and nothing is inferred when they're missing.

Resolution gains optional `action` and `content`. `{"action":"accept","content":{"choice":"yes"}}` submits a form; accepting a URL sends only `{"action":"accept"}`; decline and cancel are `{"action":"decline"}` and `{"action":"cancel"}`. `{"dismiss":true}` still means giving up the phone takeover and handing it to the terminal. A reply without a valid action returns 400 and the request stays pending.

Delivery and fallback rules:

- Both broadcasts and connection initialization filter out connections that didn't declare the capability. After a connection first declares it, still-pending elicitations are resent; repeated hellos don't resend.
- The REST pending and history lists are filtered too. That kind is returned only if an active connection with the same credential and the same `X-Persona-Client` platform / version has declared the capability; an HTTP header can't declare a capability by itself.
- If there is no compatible connection at creation and no phone to push (next item), it is handed back to the terminal immediately, leaving no request waiting for a phone answer. The existing timeout, revocation and restart-recovery rules for interactions still apply.
- Pushes (#2433): a phone that shows these cards registers `elicitation` in `POST /api/v1/devices` `features` (only the iPhone app does; the Mac app doesn't). With no compatible connection, a request still waits when such a phone would be pushed the card: it has a push route (not `none`), "Needs you" is on, Phone Muted isn't holding pushes back for an open desktop app, and the card itself is pushed (its agent isn't muted, it isn't a quiet task's). It waits the usual card timeout, like a permission card, and can be handed back to the computer from the phone; meanwhile Claude Code shows nothing for it in the terminal, because the Elicitation hook runs before its own dialog. The push goes only to the devices that registered the feature, under the usual card rules (manager mutes, quiet hours, Phone Muted, the `withdraw` silent push when the card ends elsewhere or expires). Its category is `INTERACTION_ELICITATION` with no buttons: a tap opens the conversation (`interaction_id`, `machine_id`, `session_id`), and the app gets the still-pending card once it connects and declares the capability. The alert's title names the MCP server and its body is the message, with every link in it cut down to its host, plus "open Persona to fill in" for a form; it never carries the URL to open or a form's schema or values.
- WebSocket notifications for these cards go only to connections that declared both `ws_notify` and `elicitation`, with the same alert. The shared Fleet keeps using the existing terminal prompt and is not given the new kind.
- Compatibility of the pushes: an app that doesn't register the feature gets none and isn't waited for, so with only such apps a request is handed back as before; an older hub drops the unknown feature name, so nothing waits and nothing is pushed; `fleet.clients` keeps `elicitation` meaning a connected app and adds `elicitation_push`, which a manager from before it ignores (it hands such a request back as before) and an older hub never sends.

The new fields are stored in the existing interaction JSON payload; no database migration is needed. In-package protocol checks and items not yet signed off are in the [Claude integration doc](../integrations/claude-integration.md#mcp-elicitation-hooks).

## Saved Agent searches

The default manager owns reusable runtime-Agent query definitions in its Postgres setting `agents.saved_searches`.
The hub forwards these routes unchanged; explicit `X-Persona-Manager` pins a captured owner, otherwise the default
manager is used. The web deliberately uses the default rather than the sidebar's current Assistant. These routes
do not execute or interpret a search, start sessions, run commands or send messages. Applying a query remains a
client action through the existing palette. No new migration or browser-local persistence is required.

| Method and path | Body | Response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /api/v1/saved-agent-searches` | none | `SavedAgentSearches` |
| `POST /api/v1/saved-agent-searches` | `{revision: decimal string, action, ...fields}` | full confirmed `SavedAgentSearches` |

```text
SavedAgentSearches { revision: decimal string, searches: SavedAgentSearch[], can_write: bool }
SavedAgentSearch { id, name, query, created_at: RFC3339, updated_at: RFC3339 }
```

The revision is a canonical nonnegative int64 decimal string on the wire (no leading zeros except `"0"`), preserving
identity in JavaScript. It is stored as int64 in Settings. An absent key starts at revision `"0"` with `searches: []`;
a failed read is never an empty success. GET and POST require a real store with both `Setting` and `CompareSetting`.
Full-role connections may write; answer-role connections and extension tokens with `agents.read` may only read.
No extension write scope is granted. `can_write` reflects the request role, not a promise that the next write succeeds.

| Action | Fields beyond revision/action |
| --- | --- |
| `add` | `name`, `query`; server creates `search_` + 24 lowercase hex ID and UTC timestamps |
| `update` | `id`, `name`, `query`; preserves identity, creation time and position |
| `delete` | `id`; removes that entry without resetting collection revision |
| `move` | `id`, optional `before_id`; absent/empty appends, an existing different anchor inserts before it |
| `restore` | full captured `item`, optional `before_id`; restores a deleted identity only when ID/name are absent |

Every action has an exact field set; unknown, duplicate, differently cased or mixed-action members are rejected.
The body limit is 16 KiB. Names are trimmed, control-free, 1–64 Unicode code points, unique by Unicode case-fold.
Queries are trimmed, valid UTF-8, control-free and 1–1,024 bytes; a leading `>` is rejected because the palette treats
it as command mode. Relative-time expressions stay relative. At most 50 records are retained. Restored timestamps
must be valid, nonzero and ordered; restore preserves the captured metadata. IDs and anchors must use the generated
ID syntax. A missing anchor or self-move is invalid.

A mutation checks the supplied revision against the read document, then atomically replaces it using
`CompareSetting`. A successful mutation increments revision exactly once, including a valid no-op; int64 overflow
is refused. Only after success does the manager broadcast `saved_agent_searches` with `{revision: decimal string}`;
its normal manager stamp identifies the owner. No query text or names are included in the event. The client reloads
that owner while its view is open, and never retries a conflicting write automatically.

Errors: 400 `invalid_request` / `limit_reached`, 403 `forbidden`, 404 `search_not_found` for a missing entry,
409 `conflict` for stale/CAS revisions, 409 `duplicate_name` for conflicting names/restore IDs, 503 `not_supported`
when durable CAS is unavailable, and 503 `storage_unavailable` for read/write failure or corrupt stored data.
A missing route on an older manager is 404. Clients distinguish missing entries from an unsupported endpoint and
name validation from revision conflict. Failed actions emit no event and change no persisted collection.

Undo is a `restore` using the revision acknowledged by the delete, never a blind overwrite of the whole collection.
Another write invalidates that Undo. The visible entry order is the stored array order. Newer reads must not replace
a dirty editor's draft or retarget an in-flight request after credential/default-manager changes.

## Workspace board

Workflow, upgrades and persistence are covered in [Workspace board](../web/workspace-board.md). The APIs below belong to the manager (the hub forwards them unchanged over the bus `http.request`, see "Forwarding App requests"; `503 assistant_offline` when the manager isn't there), and the two events are sent by the manager via `ws.broadcast` and pushed unchanged by the hub. The APIs use the hub machine's Postgres as the only persistent state, with no fallback to in-memory or JSON file writes. `answer` may GET the board and the list; POST requires `full`. `can_write` says whether the current request's role can edit; it grants no extra file, Git or Agent permissions.

```text
BoardState { revision: int64, columns: Column[], cards: Card[], can_write: bool, batch_cards?: bool, activity?: bool }
Column { id, title }
Card { id, machine_id, workspace_id, title, cwd, source, source_id?, branch?,
       column_id, pinned: bool, archived: bool }
Workspace { id, machine_id, source, source_id, title, cwd, branch?,
            online: bool, available: bool, last_seen?: RFC3339 }
```

The default revision is 0 and the column IDs are `todo`, `doing`, `review`, `done`. Array order is the manual order; clients group by column, archived state and pinned, keeping the arrays' relative order. Card IDs are stable. Workspace IDs are scoped by the hub to machine, source and source ID; a host's local ID can't be matched directly against another machine.

POST must give `revision` explicitly; on success the database increments it atomically and returns the full state. Available actions and parameters:

| action | Parameters |
| --- | --- |
| `add_card` | `column_id,machine_id`, plus `workspace_id` or `cwd`, optional `title,pinned,archived`; the ID is generated by the hub |
| `update_card` | `id`; updates only the given `title,pinned,archived` |
| `move_card` | `id,column_id,before_id?`; omitting before puts it at the end of the target column |
| `add_column` | `title`; the ID is generated by the hub |
| `update_column` | `id,title` |
| `move_column` | `id,before_id?`; omitting before puts it at the end |
| `delete_column` | `id,move_to?`; another column is required when it has cards (archived included); the last column can't be deleted |
| `batch_cards` | `changes: CardChange[]`; atomically edits 1–1,000 distinct existing cards, as described below |

`batch_cards: true` in a GET or successful POST response advertises `batch_cards` support; absent or false means
clients must keep using single-card operations. A batch contains only `revision`, `action` and `changes`. Each
`CardChange` has `id` and at least one of `column_id`, `pinned`, `archived`; optional `before_id` requires `column_id`.
Omitted or empty `before_id` moves to the end; a nonempty anchor must be another card in the destination column at
that point in the supplied operation order. Duplicate IDs, missing cards, malformed references, empty changes,
unknown fields and batch fields on single actions are invalid. Batches cannot add/remove cards or columns, rename,
change workspace bindings or contain nested operations. The request limit is 4 MiB for a batch and 64 KiB for
single actions; the existing card, ID and state limits still apply.

Changes run in the supplied order against an independent candidate state. Validation failure discards the whole
candidate; success performs one compare-and-swap save, increments the revision once, and emits one `workspace_board`
event. No node RPC runs. Undo is another batch at the last acknowledged revision; clients must not rebase or retry
its inverse after a conflict. This preserves newer edits and the original binding authority.

The workspace in `add_card` must belong to the given machine. The hub re-enumerates or checks the session directories, then has the node verify and resolve the physical directory with `workspace.resolve`; clients can't write `source/source_id/branch`. Only one new binding is allowed per effective machine and canonical directory, with archived cards counted in the duplicate check. Paths are handled in the remote syntax (POSIX, Windows drive letters, UNC); remote paths are never resolved with the hub's own filesystem. When a machine alias is later absorbed, it is only projected onto the current routing identity in responses; the original card's column and order are not merged or rewritten, and the original state still takes part in edits and CAS.

Errors: invalid action, path, reference, duplicate binding etc. return 400; writes by non-full roles 403; a stale revision or a race at commit returns 409 `conflict`; storage unavailable returns 503 (code `not_supported` when the storage capability isn't implemented). On 409 clients should re-read first and never overwrite the latest state automatically; on other failures restore the last confirmed state. Old hubs may return 404.

The GET list merges host spaces, current session directories and bound directories. A host's unknown directory may be empty, and clients can't bind based on it. When a machine is offline or enumeration fails, the last snapshot is used with availability marked, and discovery errors go into `errors`. One host failing must not clear other hosts' results. Alias snapshots are grouped by the current effective machine, with the latest complete snapshot winning. Cards survive a workspace disappearing, a machine going offline and a hub restart.

Session gains optional `workspace_cwd`: the physical directory verified by the node with symlinks resolved, used only for workspace association; the original `cwd` stays unchanged. The field may be omitted for directories that don't exist, can't be resolved or can't be read. Old clients ignore it; new clients prefer it and fall back to `cwd` when it's missing. The value is cached briefly and is no guarantee of permission or existence for later file operations.

The board is off by default (#2475): `GET /api/v1/workspace-board/settings` returns `{enabled,can_write}`. The value lives in Postgres's `settings` table (key `workspace_board.settings`, `{"enabled":bool}`), one per hub, the same for all browsers and devices. If it was never set, it counts as on when `workspace_board`'s `revision > 0` (the board has been edited), otherwise off; the inferred value isn't written back, and only the first PUT stores it. PUT `{enabled}` requires `full`; on success WS pushes `{"type":"workspace_board_settings","enabled":bool}`. The toggle only decides whether clients show it: when off, the board and list APIs still work and no data is deleted. Old hubs without this API return 404; clients then treat it as on (the old version showed it to everyone) and hide the toggle.

Board edits such as move and archive don't trigger Agent or Git operations. On success WS pushes `{"type":"workspace_board","revision":<new version>}`, and clients re-read. While the board is visible the web client also refreshes discovery every 10 seconds, and immediately when it comes back to the foreground, to catch changes in directories and connection state.

### Board activity

The optional `activity: true` capability means the manager's store journals board saves. These routes are read-only
manager APIs relayed by the hub. Full and answer-role device tokens may read them; extension tokens need `agents.read`.
A manager without the store capability returns 503 `not_supported`. No new event type is introduced: the existing
`workspace_board` revision push can notify an open activity reader that newer history is available.

| Method and path | Query | Response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /api/v1/workspace-board/activity` | `limit` (1–50, default 20), optional positive decimal `before` revision (exclusive), optional `card_id` | `ActivityPage` |
| `GET /api/v1/workspace-board/activity/{revision}` | `offset` (default 0), `limit` (1–100, default 30) | `ActivityDetail`; 404 `activity_not_found` for a revision not retained |

```text
ActivitySummary { revision: decimal string, at: RFC3339, change_count, card_count, kinds: string[] }
ActivityPage { entries: ActivitySummary[], next_cursor?: decimal string, latest_revision: decimal string,
               oldest_revision?: decimal string, retention_limit: 500 }
ActivityDetail { revision: decimal string, at: RFC3339, changes: ActivityChange[], total, next_offset?: integer }
ActivityChange { kind, id?, title?, fields?: string[], before?: ActivityValue, after?: ActivityValue, card_ids?: string[] }
ActivityValue { title, column_id?, column_title?, pinned?: bool, archived?: bool }
```

Activity revision strings preserve int64 identity in JavaScript. `next_cursor` is the last returned revision, passed
as `before` for the next list page; absence ends pagination. New commits cannot duplicate older pages. Page rows,
latest board revision and oldest retained revision share a repeatable-read snapshot. Retention can advance between
pages, so a later page may be empty even when the earlier one had a cursor. `oldest_revision` describes all retained
history, not just the requested card. An empty history returns `entries: []`, no oldest revision and the board's
current revision (or `"0"` before it exists).

`card_id` filters revisions by affected card IDs, including deleted/archived cards and surviving cards whose relative
order changed. Summary counts and detail pages always describe the complete grouped revision, not only that card.
`change_count` counts change records; `card_count` counts distinct affected card IDs. Expanding a large update reads
only its requested detail page; `next_offset` is exclusive of changes already returned. Unknown future `kind` values
must have a generic display rather than crashing the client.

Kinds: `card_added`, `card_removed`, `card_updated`, `column_added`, `column_removed`, `column_renamed`,
`cards_reordered`, `columns_reordered`. A `card_updated` record's fields are any of `title`, `column`, `pinned`,
`archived`. Add/remove records omit the absent side. Reorder records are group-level facts, not actor attribution;
card reorder records carry the column ID/title and affected surviving `card_ids`. Full snapshots, paths, machine IDs
and transcripts are not journaled. A committed no-op has an empty change list but still advances revision once.

The migration starts recording future writes, with no backfill. Save, journal insert and retention run in the same
transaction under the board row lock. Keep the most recent 500 entries and at most 16 MiB encoded change details,
always retaining the newest complete entry. A conflict, failed validation, failed journal insertion or failed commit
leaves the prior board and history unchanged. Invalid query ranges, duplicate numeric query parameters and malformed
card IDs return 400; storage errors return 503. No POST/PUT/DELETE activity route exists.

## Main chat readiness (`assistant_readiness`, #3710)

Whether the main chat works right now and which step is missing is computed by the hub for all four clients (design: new-user onboarding plan sections 4.4, 5.1). The assistant service answers (via "Forwarding App requests"), for `full` devices only. When the assistant isn't connected it returns 503 `assistant_offline` like the other assistant APIs; old hubs return 404 and clients fall back to the current behavior.

```
GET  /api/v1/assistant/readiness            → Readiness
GET  /api/v1/assistant/readiness?probe=1    → Readiness, plus an actual one-word check (costs money; calls for the same computer and launcher within 30 seconds return the last result, and only one runs at a time; it runs to the end even if the client stops waiting, up to 100 s plus the 12 s self-check, so clients wait longer than that)
POST /api/v1/assistant/readiness/dismiss    {"dismissed": true}  →  {"ok": true} (an empty body equals true; false undoes it)
POST /api/v1/assistant/warm                 → {"ok": true, "readiness"?: Readiness} (same structure, no probe; if it can't finish within 2.5 seconds it returns the last recorded one, omitted if none was ever recorded)
```

```jsonc
{
  "version": 1,
  "mode": "setup",                 // full / setup; chat_only is reserved for P1 and not produced yet
  "ready": false,                  // mode == "full"
  "next": "model",                 // the first step that isn't ok / skipped; null when all are fine
  "machine": {"id": "mbp", "name": "Lin's MacBook"},   // the main chat's computer; null if none
  "launcher": "claude",            // the effective launcher (Model configuration › Main chat takes precedence)
  "steps": [
    {"id": "computer", "state": "ok", "machine": "mbp"},
    {"id": "claude", "state": "ok", "version": "2.1.308"},
    {"id": "model", "state": "problem", "code": "not_logged_in", "machine": "mbp", "launcher": "claude",
     "title": "Claude Code isn't signed in", "detail": "Sign in once on Lin's MacBook, or use an API key instead.",
     "action": {"id": "connect_model"}, "alt_actions": [{"id": "login_claude"}]},
    {"id": "first_message", "state": "todo", "code": "never_tried", "title": "Say hello", "detail": "…", "action": {"id": "test_assistant"}}
  ],
  "suggestions": [{"id": "what_can_you_do", "title": "What can you do for me?", "local": true}],
  "probe": {"ok": false, "agent": "claude", "millis": 2140, "error": "…"},   // only with ?probe=1 and the computer ok
  "dismissed": false,
  "checked_at": "2026-11-06T09:00:00Z"
}
```

- `steps` always has four entries in a fixed order: `computer`, `claude`, `model`, `first_message`. `state`: `ok` / `todo` / `problem` / `checking` / `unknown` / `skipped`. `todo` / `problem` always carry `code`, `title`, `detail` (per `Accept-Language`) and usually `action`; `model` in `unknown` carries them too (`model_unverified`).
- `computer`: no computer is `todo` + `no_machine` (`add_computer`); computer not online is `problem` + `node_unreachable` (`wake_computer`); node too old (doesn't know model configuration) is `problem` + `node_outdated` (no button). With no confirmed computer selected, a pending computer owned by the manager is `todo` + `machine_pending` (`confirm_computer`); the top-level `machine` has its ID and display name, and the computer step's `machine` has its ID. With several pending computers, choose the smallest ID. This is a confirmation target, not permission to run there: main-chat creation returns 409 `machine_pending`, `action: "confirm_computer"`, `delivered: "none"`, and `machine_name`. A selected confirmed computer keeps priority even when offline. When the computer isn't `ok`, the next three steps are all `unknown`.
- `claude`: the node self-check (`node.doctor`'s `claude-version`, cached per computer: 10 minutes when a version was read, 1 minute when not) reading a version is `ok` + `version`. The default launcher `claude` not found by the login shell is `problem` + `claude_missing` (`install_claude`, alternative `connect_model`); a check whose `claude --version` did not answer this time while the shell found claude (state `unanswered`: its 10 seconds ran out on a busy machine, or it printed no version) is `unknown`, never `claude_missing`. The last chat start being refused gives `claude_missing` / `launcher_missing` (no longer counted once a later self-check reads a version, or the launcher is back on this computer), and the same when the launcher health check's record says the command wasn't found. Your own launcher no longer existing on this computer is `launcher_missing` (`connect_model`; launchers added in Persona and direct API providers speaking Messages count as present on every computer in their device scope). A launcher running Codex or a runtime is `skipped`. An old node without the self-check, or your own launcher whose version can't be read, is `unknown`. A self-check that didn't finish answering this time is `checking` (GET waits at most 12 seconds, warm 2 seconds; the result is cached either way). Once the model has answered, it is always `ok`.
- `model`: takes the newest piece of evidence: the latest probe (same computer, same launcher), the main chat's latest turn (the session's `turn_error` / `turn_error_code`, or a normal answer), the launcher health check record (within 6 hours). If the newest is an answer, `ok`; if it's a failure with a recognized cause, `problem` + `not_logged_in` (`connect_model`, alternative `login_claude`) / `auth_failed` (`edit_provider`) / `model_route` / `rate_limited` (`connect_model`); with no evidence, or a failure of unrecognized cause, `unknown` + `model_unverified` (`test_assistant`), which doesn't count as a problem. For `rate_limited`, the optional `occurrence` identifies this failure occurrence: a main turn uses its `updated_at`; health-only evidence with a subscription `resets_at` uses that reset window; other evidence uses its timestamp. When newer health evidence has the same reset as the main turn, the turn's identity wins, so settlement and repeated checks do not revive a dismissed warning while another turn in the same reset window is still new. The response's `checked_at` is only the read time. Clients can use `occurrence` without treating another launcher's successful reply as recovery. For `auth_failed` and `model_route`, `alt_actions` includes `test_assistant` so the user can verify a repair even after `first_message` is `ok`, without replacing the current chat (#1894). On `not_logged_in`, when the machine's launcher list has any launcher besides the step's own (the machine's list, no probing of the others' sign-in state), `alt_actions` also includes `main_chat_model` — open the model configuration's Main chat purpose and switch to one of them (#4355) — and the step's `detail` says so instead of only pointing at an API key. It never spends tokens on its own. The evidence also includes the node's `claude.auth_status` (free, #4048; cached per computer per launcher: 10 minutes when signed in, 1 minute when not signed in or no answer (the call failed, `timeout`, `unreadable`), 10 minutes for an old node's `unknown method`): `not_logged_in` counts as a failure (`not_logged_in`). A `claude.ai` sign-in counts as an answer only when there's no other evidence or the newest is `not_logged_in`; it can't override a recognized `auth_failed` / `model_route` / `rate_limited`. Keys, gateway tokens and cloud providers (`api_key`, `api_key_helper`, `oauth_token`, `third_party`) don't count as evidence; with no other evidence, the `unknown` `detail` says "uses an account or key it was set up with, not tried yet". `unknown` doesn't count as evidence.
- `first_message`: `ok` once the main chat has answered (recorded, then always `ok`; a changed main chat counts too); if it never answered and the latest turn failed, `problem` + that turn's code; otherwise `todo` + `never_tried` (`test_assistant`). While `first_message` offers `test_assistant`, an unverified `model` step has no action: the try is one button, on `first_message`, where clients show its spinner and answer; the probe it runs verifies the model (#6317). It doesn't affect `mode`.
- `mode`: `setup` when any of `computer`, `claude`, `model` is `todo` or `problem`, except `rate_limited` (it recovers by itself, so `mode` stays `full`); `unknown` / `checking` don't block.
- `suggestions`: in `setup` only the two `local: true` ones (`what_can_you_do`, `how_to_connect_model`; the client opens local help, nothing goes to the model); in `full` also `largest_folders`, `today` (`needs: ["phone_calendar"]`), `connect_mail`, with `prompt` (the exact text sent when tapped).
- `probe` is `POST /api/v1/launchers/{name}/check`'s `{ok, agent, model, answer, millis, error}` on the main chat's computer. If the computer step is not `ok` (including `machine_pending`), `?probe=1` sends no probe and the response omits `probe`. When the computer didn't answer (offline, timeout) only `error` is present; such results are not recorded and not used as model evidence.
- Scheduled tasks (#4253): a run that comes due first computes readiness with the same rules (no probe). If a step this run needs is blocking, it isn't sent; the run record has `status: "skipped"`, `not_ready: true` (#1857), and `error` "Your computer or model isn’t set up yet, so this one was skipped", with no push. These skips, including temporary sleep / offline cases, neither count toward nor reset a failure streak. **Run Now** and one-off tasks don't check (a one-off closes when due, so a skip would lose it).
- Storage: the latest result, `dismissed`, the latest probe, chat start refusals, the main chat having answered once, and scheduled tasks waiting for readiness (`routines_waiting`, #4253) are stored in Postgres `settings` under `assistant.readiness`; nothing is written when the result is unchanged (ignoring `checked_at`, but retaining `occurrence` changes). The first version pushes no events; clients re-fetch when entering the Persona tab, after pairing succeeds, after adding / confirming a computer, after saving a provider, and on `machines` changes.

## Origin of assistant chats (`origin`, #3264)

Assistant chats (sessions with `assistant: true`) carry `origin`: who opened the chat. The hub records it when the chat is opened (the assistant's settings `assistant.origins`: session id → origin, `origin_ref`, start time),
and fills it into the session lists sent to the App through the snapshot (`SessionView.origin` / `origin_ref`) (`sessions` / `sessions_delta` pushes, `GET /api/v1/sessions`, `conversations` in `GET /api/v1/assistant`).
Once recorded, the origin never changes; Agent sessions (`assistant: false`) don't carry it. Hubs that know this field include `conversation_origin` in features.

| `origin` | Opened by | `origin_ref` | Sidebar (#5195) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `user` (or absent) | The user creating one in the App / web (including the main chat, and ones opened with **Hand to AI** in the Inbox or a Lark chat) | — | Recent, no mark (All Chats: Mine) |
| `channel` | The user sending `/new` in a channel such as the Lark bot or WeChat | Channel id (`feishu`, `wechat`…) | Recent, its channel's mark (All Chats: Mine) |
| `inbox` | The handling chat for an Inbox item (AI twin, `docs/assistant/inbox.md`) | Inbox item id | Recent, marked Inbox |
| `task` | Scheduled tasks and follow-ups (`schedule_followup`, including `new_conversation` ones and the own chats of `notify_user`-only `push: "asked"` tasks); also the built-in background supervisor's chat (#4927, `docs/assistant/unified-entry.md` "Background supervisor"), which has no `origin_ref` | Task id | Recent, marked Scheduled Tasks (not the background supervisor) |
| `spawned` | Opened by another chat with `conversation_new` | Session id of the chat that opened it | Recent, marked Spawned from Chats |
| `lark_agent` | Sending `/agent …` in Lark (the extension via `POST /api/v1/assistant/conversations`, `purpose: "lark.agent"`, `docs/extensions/lark-agent.md`) | Extension id | Recent, Lark's mark |
| `extension` | Opened by another extension via `POST /api/v1/assistant/conversations` | Extension id | Recent, marked Extensions |
| `meeting` | A recorded meeting's room conversation, a guest the hub opens for the meeting (#3862, "Meeting conversation (#3862)"), titled `MMDD \| 会议 \| <meeting title>` | Recording id | Recent, marked Other (apps that know it: one row per meeting) |
| `meeting_followup` | The follow-up conversation of a recorded meeting, made by the owner's first `POST /api/v1/recordings/{id}/followup` (#3862), titled like the room | Recording id | Recent, marked Other (apps that know it: one row per meeting) |

- **`opened_by`** (`SessionView.opened_by`, the session's `opened_by`): the extension whose token opened the chat (`POST /api/v1/assistant/conversations` with an extension's token, whatever its `purpose`), by id.
  The assistant notes it when the chat opens, from the extension the hub's auth found for the request (a client's own `X-Persona-*` headers are dropped on the way) and nothing else: not from `origin` or `origin_ref`, and never over the bus (`assistant.start` cannot set it).
  It is absent for every other chat, for the main chat even when an extension opened it, and for chats opened before it was noted: the backfill never sets it.
  A chat made main later (`PUT /api/v1/assistant {"main": …}`) loses it for good, and making another chat main does not bring it back. Only that extension's token may change the chat's permission mode (`agents.permission_mode`, `docs/extensions/extensions.md` "Hub API: scopes"); a chat without it is refused.
- Sending into an existing chat doesn't open a new one and isn't an origin: a task continuing in its own chat, quiet-task notifications (`task_notice`) going into the main chat, channel messages to the main chat, `conversation_send`.
- **How clients use it**: absent, empty, `user` and `channel` count as the user's own; everything else counts as an auto chat, including values added later that the client doesn't know (shown as **Other**). Old clients don't know the field and list everything as before.
- **Titles**: an auto chat's title is set from the start (no waiting for the first turn, no model call), following "MMDD | kind | topic": Inbox `MMDD | 收件箱 | <the item's title>`, scheduled tasks `MMDD | 定时 | <task name>` (the kind words are emitted in Chinese: 收件箱 = Inbox, 定时 = scheduled).
  `收件箱` is not among the kinds the model may pick (only the hub uses it). Other origins still get a title after the first turn (`docs/assistant/assistant.md` "Chat titles").
  A title an extension gives the chat it opened (`POST /api/v1/sessions/{mid}/{sid}/rename` with its token) is a hint the model reads, not the title (#3758).
- **Only a scoped token makes an extension the opener**: the hub tells the extension apart by its own token (`permissions.hub`, `docs/extensions/extensions.md` "Hub API: scopes").
  An extension that calls with the hub's full token (`hub_api`) is the user as far as the hub can tell: its chats are `user` and carry no source mark, and its renames are the user's.
- **Backfilling old chats**: when the hub sees the session list of the assistant's machine, it fills in assistant chats that have no origin yet (`by: "backfill"`): AI twin sessions recorded on Inbox items → `inbox` (filling the title too);
  chats recorded on tasks (`run_session_id`, sessions in run records) and titles started with `定时` (scheduled) → `task`; a first message starting with the Inbox AI twin / chat-forward / scheduled-task prompt → the matching origin;
  the rest → `user`. It can run repeatedly: already recorded ones are untouched. `POST /api/v1/assistant/origins/backfill` (full-permission devices only; with `{"redo":true}` it also re-judges `by: "backfill"` ones)
  → `{"checked","filled":{"inbox":3,…}}`.

### Sidebar (same on every client)

- **Recent** under **Persona Chats** lists every chat by last activity whoever opened it (#5195), except the main chat, the leaders (常驻, listed above it), the archived ones, the built-in background supervisor (#4927, in All Chats only) and the scheduled tasks' own chats (`origin == "task"`, #6228: they keep their Scheduled Tasks entry and All Chats). The heading folds the rows, with the folded / open state kept on the device (default open). iOS / iPadOS and Android list 5; the web lists its setting (5 by default) with Show more, and an explicitly chosen count is never reset.
- **A chat Persona opened carries its source's mark** beside the title in the channel mark's place: the icon and name of its All Chats filter where that filter exists (Inbox · Scheduled Tasks · Lark /agent with Lark's mark · Spawned from Chats · Extensions · Other), named for VoiceOver / TalkBack and in the tooltip. One source mapping decides the mark everywhere, and agrees with the All Chats filter on clients that have one; the same chat has the same mark in Recent, 常驻, the search results and All Chats.
- **All Chats** on iOS / iPadOS and the web has an origin filter at the top (All · Mine · Inbox · Scheduled Tasks · …) and opens on **All** every time: the last pick is not kept (on the web the pick is in the address, `/history/<origin>`, so Back returns to it). Android's All chats has no source filter. Search covers all chats whatever their origin.
- **Conversations an extension opened** (`lark_agent`, `extension`; #3758) say so, the same on iOS / iPadOS and the web (Android: #4203): their rows carry the source's mark as every chat Persona opened does (Lark's for Lark /agent, the extensions symbol otherwise, named "From Lark /agent" / "From an extension"; one mark per row, the origin's over the channel's), and the message that opened the chat gets the "From Lark /agent" / "From an extension" line a channel's message has, on that first message only. `channel` and `user` chats get no origin mark (a channel's chat keeps its channel's).

## Assistant chat search (#6282)

`GET /api/v1/assistant/search?q=<text>&limit=30` (the manager's, routed like the other `/api/v1/assistant…` routes: `X-Persona-Manager` names the current assistant; feature `assistant_search`). It finds the chats "All chats" lists (`origin` and `archived` included; never the health space) by their title, by the user's own words or by the assistant's replies, over the whole history. Thoughts, tools, system events, quoted contexts, hidden tags and messages Persona injected for the model are never searched: what a message counts as is the shared rule of `spec/fixtures/chat-search` (its `index`), the design in `docs/design/proposals/assistant-search.md`. A device that may only read gets 403.

- **Query**: trimmed, at most 200 characters, split on spaces into at most 8 words; every word must be in the same message (or the title). Matching is a substring match after NFKC and lower case.
- **Answer**: `{"results": [{"session_id", "machine_id", "title", "main"?, "archived"?, "origin"?, "updated_at", "title_match"?, "hits": [{"item_id", "seq", "role": "user"|"assistant", "ts", "snippet", "ranges": [[start, end]]}], "more_hits"?}], "partial": bool, "indexed": {"done", "total"}}`. `ranges` are UTF-16 `[start, end)` in `snippet` (about 40 characters before the first match and 80 after, on one line, `…` where cut). Up to 3 hits a chat, newest first; `more_hits` is how many more of its messages match. `limit` defaults to 30, at most 50.
- **Order**: chats whose title matches first (starting with the query, then holding every word; the latest updated first), then the others by their newest hit. The main chat is never matched by its title (the apps show it as Persona); a chat not named yet neither.
- **`partial`**: some chats are not read into the index yet (`indexed` says how many are), or the index could not be searched this time; the apps say the results may be incomplete.
- **Snippets** are cut from a reply as the chat shows it: without Markdown's markup (#7072), so neither `**` nor a link's address shows in one, and `ranges` count in that text.
- **The index** is the manager's own (`assistant_search_items`, `assistant_search_cursors`): kept current from the computers' session lists (a chat whose `rev` moved is read after its cursor with `session.items` `after_seq`, unfolded), read again from the start when a transcript's `history` changes. New messages can be found within seconds of a turn ending. The query is never logged.

## Extension install, upgrade and uninstall progress (`extension_operations`, #3277)

The hub records each install, upgrade and uninstall as an **operation**: split into named steps, each with a state; the download step carries byte counts, and on failure it records which step it stopped at and why. Whenever an operation changes, WebSocket pushes `extension_operation`; after closing the page and coming back, `GET /api/v1/extensions/-/operations` returns the ones in progress and just finished. These exist only when `hello.features` carries `extension_operations`; otherwise clients keep using the synchronous preview / install (the old APIs below are unchanged).

### Operation (`ExtensionOperation`)

```json
{
  "id": "3f9c…",                 // operation id
  "kind": "install",             // install | upgrade | uninstall
  "extension": "larkext",        // extension id (before preview only the market id is known)
  "name": "Lark",                // human-readable name, only once known
  "market": "c0bbc68b20",        // which market it comes from, optional
  "source": "market:c0bbc68b20/larkext", // install source (same as the extension's origin), optional
  "version": "0.11.1",           // version to install, only once known
  "from": "0.10.0",              // version before the upgrade, upgrade only
  "actor": "Web",                // who started it: device name, personad extension, hub (auto-upgrade)
  "state": "running",            // running | needs_consent | succeeded | failed | canceled
  "step": "download",            // the step id in progress (or stopped at)
  "steps": [
    {"id": "download", "state": "running", "bytes": 5242880, "total": 17302381, "started_at": "…"},
    {"id": "verify", "state": "pending"},
    {"id": "unpack", "state": "pending"}
  ],
  "error": "Download stalled: no data received for 30 seconds",  // on failure, in the language of the request that started it
  "error_code": "download_stalled", // on failure, optional, see below
  "preview_id": "…",             // when needs_consent: the preview the user must agree to
  "retryable": true,             // whether POST …/retry is possible after failure
  "warnings": ["…"],             // uninstall only, optional: what succeeded but needs a hand, e.g. files that could not be deleted (the same as the synchronous answer's `warnings`)
  "started_at": "…", "updated_at": "…", "ended_at": "…"
}
```

- Step `state`: `pending` (not reached yet), `running`, `done`, `failed`, `skipped` (not needed this time, e.g. no `download` when installing from a local directory). A `download` in `done` with `cached: true` means the package came from the local cache and wasn't downloaded again.
- `bytes` / `total` exist only on `download`: `total` is the size written in the index or the response's Content-Length, absent when unknown (draw an indeterminate progress bar). Other steps have no percentage.
- Step ids (in order; unused ones are `skipped`; clients show ids they don't know as-is, without erroring):

| kind | Steps |
| --- | --- |
| install / upgrade | `download` (download the package) → `verify` (check sha256 and the market index) → `unpack` (unpack) → `check` (manifest, permissions, dependencies, conflicts; bundles and missing dependencies are previewed together) → `consent` (wait for the user to agree) → `tools` (install the command-line programs in the manifest's `tools`, #4507) → `install` (put into installed/, write to the database) → `start` (start it and wait until it's up) → `nodes` (send its computer-side program to each computer, only for ones with a `node` section) |
| uninstall | `stop` (stop it) → `remove` (delete files and records) → `nodes` (stop and delete its program on each computer, only for ones with a `node` section) |

- While `consent` is `running`, the operation's `state` is `needs_consent`: it carries `preview_id`, and the client `GET …/operations/{id}` gets the full preview (same as the `catalog/preview` answer) to show the user. On agreement, `POST /-/install` (or `/{id}/-/upgrade`) with this `preview_id` as before, and the hub continues this operation; on refusal, `DELETE …/operations/{id}`. If the preview expires (`expires_at`) the operation becomes `canceled`. Upgrades that need no user consent (auto-upgrades, ones whose permissions didn't grow) have this step `skipped`.
- `start`: extensions with no program (declarations only) and on-demand ones (started on first call) are `done` immediately; otherwise it's `done` once `running`, and `failed` if it can't start (an upgrade rolls back to the original version, stated in `error`). It waits at most `host.ReadyWithin` plus 5 seconds.
- `tools`: `skipped` for extensions without `tools`; `done` immediately when everything is reused or the same spec was installed before. The step carries `tools: [{"name", "state", "reused"?}]` (`state`: `pending` / `running` / `done` / `failed`, in install order), and `bytes` / `total` are for the one being downloaded (`total` is often unknown). On failure nothing is installed, `error_code` is `tools_failed`, and `error` says which program and why; see [extensions.md](../extensions/extensions.md) ("Command-line programs (tools)").
- `next`: when the operation `succeeded` and the extension has `auth` but isn't signed in (`signed_out` / `expired`), the operation carries `"next": "auth"`: the client opens sign-in in the extension details ([extensions.md](../extensions/extensions.md) "Sign-in (auth)").
- `nodes`: waits for every online computer to finish syncing (offline ones aren't waited for; the hub sends to them when they come online, as before). The step carries `machines: {"done": 1, "total": 2}`; one computer failing doesn't fail the whole operation, and its reason is in `machines.errors` (`{"<machine id>": "…"}`).
- `error_code`: `download_stalled` (no data received for 30 seconds during download), `download_failed`, `checksum_mismatch`, `invalid_package`, `tools_failed`, `needs_consent` (what was agreed to isn't this preview), `start_failed`, `rolled_back`, `uninstall_failed`; unknown ones are shown via `error`.
- `download` (#3692): a package downloads once at a time (by its sha256). A preview of a package that is downloading waits for that download, its step showing the bytes so far, and a download goes on into the package cache after the preview that started it ended without it: a synchronous preview whose app stopped waiting fails with an `error` that says so (the next preview joins the download or takes the package from the cache). Only `DELETE …/operations/{id}` stops a download nobody else waits for. A download gives up after 30 seconds without data (`download_stalled`) or when its budget runs out (30 minutes, longer for a package too big to arrive at 16 KiB/s in that time; `download_failed`, and `error` says how much arrived).
- Operations live only in the memory of the manager running them: ones in progress and those finished within the last 10 minutes are listed (`GET …/operations` lists one manager's, chosen as in "Per-manager routing"), and they're gone after that manager restarts (an install unfinished before the restart is simply not installed; install again). A hub restart loses them only when it restarts the manager too (the built-in manager in child mode); in service mode the manager and its operations survive it. A manager that restarts sends no final `extension_operation`, and the hub only pushes `managers`: on that push (and on `hello`) the web and Android apps list every manager's operations again, and let go of one its manager no longer lists or answers `404 not_found` for, so the extension can be installed again. The Apple apps relist only when the market page opens.

### Endpoints

| Method | Path | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| POST | `/api/v1/extensions/-/catalog/preview`, `/api/v1/extensions/-/preview` | Unchanged; with `"async": true` in the body it returns 202 `{"operation": …}` right away, downloads and checks in the background, and the operation stops at `needs_consent` (or `failed`) when done. Without `async` the synchronous response is as before, plus an `operation_id` |
| POST | `/api/v1/extensions/-/install`, `/api/v1/extensions/{id}/-/upgrade` | Unchanged; with `"async": true` in the body it returns 202 `{"operation": …}` and runs `install` / `start` / `nodes` in the background. The synchronous form still returns the extension details once installed (plus an `operation_id`), without waiting for `start` and `nodes`. The first call with a `preview_id` takes over the operation waiting with it; another call with the same `preview_id` while that install runs (a double click, two clients) is 409 `installing_already` and changes nothing |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/extensions/{id}/-/` | Unchanged; with `async=1` in the query string it returns 202 `{"operation": …}` |
| GET | `/api/v1/extensions/-/operations` | `{"operations": [ExtensionOperation…]}`: in progress, waiting for consent, and finished within the last 10 minutes, newest first |
| GET | `/api/v1/extensions/-/operations/{id}` | One operation; in `needs_consent` it also has `preview` (the full preview). 404 if missing or expired |
| POST | `/api/v1/extensions/-/operations/{id}/retry` | Runs a failed operation again from the start and returns 202 `{"operation": new operation}`. A package already downloaded is in the cache, so `download` is `done` immediately (`cached`); if it failed after `consent` and the new preview's permission digest matches what the user agreed to, it does not ask again and goes straight on to install. A failed operation is retried once: afterwards its `retryable` is `false` (pushed to the apps) and the new operation carries on, so a second `POST` (a double tap, another app or the CLI) is 409 `not_retryable` and starts nothing |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/extensions/-/operations/{id}` | Cancel: a download or check in progress (started async) stops (the download goes on only for another preview waiting for it), one waiting for consent drops its preview, and the operation becomes `canceled`; a finished one is removed from the list; once `install` has started it cannot be canceled (409 `cannot_cancel`) |

Permissions follow the endpoint that started the operation: only a device that can preview / install can list, view, retry and cancel operations (a full-access device installs extensions from a market; every other source only accepts the main token over loopback).

### Events

`{"type": "extension_operation", "operation": ExtensionOperation}`: pushed whenever the step changes; at most one per second while downloading, without `preview`. Only pushed to connections that declared `extension_operations` in the WebSocket `?features=` or `client_hello.features`, and not written to the event log (`event_seq` resume cannot fill it in): after reconnecting, `GET …/operations` once more. Old clients don't receive it; those that only know `extension_upgrade` still get the result of automatic upgrades.

### How clients use it

0. When connecting the WebSocket, include `extension_operations` in `?features=` (or `client_hello.features`).
1. Tap **Install**: `POST …/catalog/preview {"market", "extension", "async": true}`, get the operation and draw the step list; from then on just listen to `extension_operation` (replace by `id`).
2. `needs_consent`: `GET …/operations/{id}` to get `preview`, show the existing permission confirmation; if the user agrees, `POST /-/install {"preview_id", "permissions_digest", "bundle", "async": true}`.
3. `succeeded`: refresh the extension list; `failed`: show `error` next to the step that failed, and when `retryable` offer **Retry** (`POST …/retry`).
4. When opening the extensions page (or reconnecting), `GET …/operations` and keep drawing the ones in progress.

## Error reports (feature `error_reports`, #5533)

Clients report their errors and crashes only while `features` has `error_reports` (an extension takes them, [extensions.md](../extensions/extensions.md) ("Error reports")). Without it they send nothing, and drop what they kept.

`POST /api/v1/error-reports` (full device credentials: the phone, the Mac, the web; not the watch, pairing tokens or extension tokens)

```json
{"reports": [{"id": "4f0c…", "source": "android", "kind": "crash", "level": "fatal", "time": "2026-11-06T09:00:00Z",
  "release": "1.4.0", "build": "512", "os": "android", "os_version": "16", "device_model": "Pixel 9",
  "message": "IllegalStateException in InboxViewModel",
  "exceptions": [{"type": "java.lang.IllegalStateException", "value": "…",
    "frames": [{"function": "load", "module": "persona.feature.inbox.InboxViewModel", "file": "InboxViewModel.kt", "line": 88, "in_app": true}]}],
  "breadcrumbs": [{"time": "…", "category": "navigation", "message": "inbox", "level": "info"}],
  "tags": {"screen": "inbox"}, "previous_launch": true}]}
```

- `ErrorReport` in `schema/extension/protocol.schema.json` is the format; `source` is the client's own (`web`, `android`, `ios`, `mac`, `vision`); `hub` and `manager` are refused. `fingerprint`, `count` and `received_at` are the manager's: what a client sends there is ignored.
- At most 20 reports and 256 KB a request (400 beyond). `202 {"enabled": true, "accepted": n, "dropped": m}`: dropped are invalid, repeated (same `id`), folded (the same problem within 10 minutes) or over the rate limit; none of them should be sent again. `200 {"enabled": false, "accepted": 0}`: the feature is off; nothing was kept.
- **What clients put in**: no user content (message text, mail, documents, prompts, notification bodies, file names the user chose), no device ids, account, hub address or machine names; breadcrumbs carry short code-chosen text (a screen's name, a route pattern). The manager scrubs again whatever slips through.
- **Keeping and retrying**: a client keeps reports locally until it gets a 2xx (a crash is written before the process dies and sent at the next start with `previous_launch`), at most 50 for at most 7 days, and makes each report's `id` once so a retry is recognized.

## REST (App → hub)

| Method | Path | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/api/v1/machines` | `{"machines":[Machine]}`. A Machine from a current manager has `clipboard: {supported, enabled, reason?, reason_code?}` (clipboard sharing, [clipboard.md](../operations/clipboard.md); `reason` in the reader's language when it can't share; an older manager leaves it out) |
| GET | `/api/v1/workspace-board` | `{revision,columns,cards,can_write}`, the full workflow board; readable by `answer`, see "Workspace board" |
| POST | `/api/v1/workspace-board` | `{revision,action,...}` → the full updated board; `full` only, a stale revision gets 409 `conflict` |
| GET | `/api/v1/workspace-board/settings` | `{enabled,can_write}`: the board switch (#2475), one per hub; when never set, inferred from whether the board has been changed, see "Workspace board" |
| PUT | `/api/v1/workspace-board/settings` | `{enabled}` → `{enabled,can_write}`; `full` only, missing `enabled` returns 400 |
| GET | `/api/v1/workspaces` | `{workspaces:[Workspace],errors?:[{machine_id,error}]}`; workspace discovery independent of Agents, keeps the last known info on failure, readable by `answer` |
| POST | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/reconnect` | Reconnect that machine's node |
| GET · POST | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/codex/{sid}/takeover` | Signed-in full-device route; generic device-call APIs are denied. GET → `{token,cwd,transcript_path,continuation_prompt}` with a single-use two-minute token. POST requires `{token,confirm_stop:true}` only while the original writer is running; `false` is accepted once it has exited. The manager verifies process identity and terminal instance, then sends one Ctrl+D only with empty composer and no modal or queued input. It waits for process exit, a complete stable transcript ending, and a fresh writer scan; any failed check or timeout refuses. No signals or forced termination. Takeover resumes the same thread/session ID in a new terminal tab. The separate continue option alone starts an independent session with context and attached to-do preserved. `encrypted_context` is continuation-only. |
| POST | `/api/v1/machines/{id}/confirm` · `…/reject` | Confirm / reject a computer waiting for confirmation (feature `machine_trust`, "Computer trust" below); only accepts a signed-in full device or the main token (a temporary identity from a pairing code gets 403) → `{"ok":true}`. confirm: confirming an already-confirmed one is also 200, unknown machine 404; reject only works on pending ones (already confirmed 409 `not_pending`, unknown 404) |
| GET | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/panes` | The terminal browser tree (feature `terminal_panes`, `full` only): `{hosts:[{kind, stream, control, new_tab, workspaces:[{id,label,number?,cwd?,branch?}], tabs:[{id,workspace_id,label,number?}], panes:[{pane, terminal, tab_id, workspace_id, agent?, status?, title?, cwd?, session_id?}]}]}`; includes shell panes with no Agent. `terminal` is the terminal-stream address `pane:<pane>`, `session_id` is the Agent session running in that pane (use it to open the terminal when present) |
| POST | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/panes` | `{workspace_id, kind?}`: open a new shell tab in this space (doesn't steal focus on the computer; the directory is the space's own, the request cannot set it) → `{pane, terminal, tab_id}`; `full` only, called only when the user taps |

Already reopening or already started is also 200 (returned as is, not started again); if it fails again, `done_at` + `start_error` are written back as usual and the plan's `error` is updated, without appending a second receipt. Target machine offline 409 `“{name}” is offline. Try again once it’s connected.` (to-do unchanged); not a task dispatched by the assistant, or not a start failure (e.g. completed manually) 409, missing 404, read-only device 403. **Unfinished tasks** are not restarted: if an Agent is stuck on a model API error (`turn_error`, #1516), it is sent "Continue" and the to-do is returned as is with 200; repeated taps on the same interruption send it only once; that computer offline 409; no interrupted Agent (working, waiting for you…) returns 200 as is and sends nothing |

The body gains `dismissed_at`, `dismissal_id`, `dismissal_updated_at`; task decision audit commits atomically. No send, Inbox filing, task completion or Agent closure. Without it (only for actions without confirm), the version the hub read when validating the binding is used. A version different from the saved one returns 409 `view_changed`: `{error,code,version,view?}` (`ViewChangedError`, `version` is the current version, `view` is the `AssistantView` envelope); the client keeps the draft, refreshes and has the user confirm again, and **must not resend automatically with the new version**. The submission locks the card inside a transaction before comparing versions, so concurrent with `view_update` it can only bind to the version still saved at submit time. Another submission 409 `already_answered`, with the existing action; retrying with the same client_msg_id / action / values / version returns the original record (older records without a version stay idempotent as before). The submission is stored together with the text to send; pending / sent / failed are synced via events and the feed. Optional `X-Persona-Op-Id` hooks into the persistent `start` receipt. `model` is optional: the model picked in the new-Agent sheet (the `id` from `…/launchers/{name}/models` above, or a model ID the user typed: letters, digits and `. _ - / : @ [ ]`, starting with a letter or digit or with `~` and then one (a gateway's `~vendor/model-latest`), at most 256 characters, `proto.ValidModelID`; anything else 400 in the request's language), for this one time only, overriding **Model Settings › Agents** (the manager's `agents.start_params`, see "Agents" under "Bus"; when the manager isn't connected the hub waits for it a while, and if it doesn't come, applies **Model Settings › Agents** itself and doesn't generate a tab name). `todo_id` is optional: attached within the same request after a successful start (missing 404, done 409, read-only device 403); with `prompt`, the background of the project the directory belongs to and the to-do's decisions are prepended to it; without `prompt` (`async`), they're prepended to the session's first message (`docs/assistant/todos.md` ("Record the conclusion when done")). `tab_name` is the herdr tab name; if not given, the manager uses the small-task model to make a short English name from `prompt` (`assistant/agents_start.go`, about 2 seconds; if it fails or the manager isn't connected, no name), and the node falls back to `agent-<n>`, adding `-2`, `-3` for duplicates in the same space (`node.tabLabel`). When a new space is created, its first tab also gets this name. The assistant's `agent_start` names tabs automatically the same way. `"async": true` (all Apps send it): returns the session right away (new session id, directory, launcher, `starting: true`) and opens the tab and waits for Claude to be ready in the background, see "New session" below; in this case the hub doesn't wait for naming, the tab is called `agent-<n>` first and `session.rename` follows once the name is ready. `name_hint`: when the App sends the first message as a normal message (so it shows up immediately), it's used for naming and not put into `prompt` The answer has `launcher_note` when the Agents default (or a profile tier) is a launcher the computer lacks and another one starts it instead (#4661). |
| POST | `/api/v1/tabs/autoname` | `{"dry_run"?,"all"?}` → `{"tabs":[{machine_id,session_id,space,title,from,to,error?}]}`: renames tabs of running Agents that "nobody has named" (`persona`, `persona-N`, herdr's numbers, `agent-N`) to short English names based on the session title, same rules as new sessions; `dry_run` only lists what they'd become, `all` also renames tabs the user named. The model occasionally returns nothing, so it asks once more, and if still nothing keeps the old name (`error`). Run once on 2026-10-31 on two machines: of 61 tabs, 39 were renamed and the user's own 21 were untouched. Answered by the manager (forwarded by the hub); 503 `assistant_offline` when it isn't connected |
