The page starts with a user question (at most 2000 items; when one turn is very long and going back would mean parsing tens of MB, the page is shorter with `has_more: true`, and paging back continues from there; but as long as there is earlier content, a page contains at least one item, since an empty page with `has_more: true` would leave the App with no seq to page back from); old clients' `limit` still counts items. With `lazy_images=1`, images carry no data (`image: {mime, lazy:true, size, width, height}`) and are fetched when displayed. With `after_seq=N`, returns new content with seq > N (for background sync, about 500 items per page, never splitting the items of one line; `more_after: true` means there's more, fetch again from the last item's seq, or fetch the latest page instead). With `fold_work=1`, pages going back from the end fold the work; with `from_seq=&through_seq=`, returns the items of those lines (for expanding a fold, about 1000 items per page, `more: true` means `through_seq` isn't reached yet). No bodies, previews, image bytes or model calls. The hub relays the node's position-only `session.items` mode; runtimes use their existing item pages. The richer #2071 API supersedes this temporary query mode once merged; it is not implemented or taken over here. |

| GET | `/api/v1/sessions/{mid}/{sid}/items/{item id}/full` | An item's full text (`Item`, without images and without `full_size`; at most 1 MB): fetched when the App taps "show full text". The node re-reads and parses that line |
| POST | `/api/v1/sessions/{mid}/{sid}/messages` | `{"text":"…","images":[{"mime","data"}]?,"client_msg_id"?,"clear_draft"?,"todo_id"?,"via"?}` (`via`: as on a new assistant conversation, below); `todo_id` is optional: attached after a successful send (missing 404, done 409, read-only device 403), and the to-do's decisions are prepended to `text`; for rejections see "Sending messages" below. → `{"ok":true}`; to a Claude outside Persona's terminals that took it while a permission prompt or another dialog only the computer can answer holds it, also `"waits_on_computer":true` (#5890; a reply to a question the session asked answers that question instead, #5961): delivered into its queue, read once that is answered at the computer, which the iOS and web apps say on sending (an older node never sends it, an older app ignores it; a retry answered from the hub's send record leaves it out); to a Codex waiting for its first message (`awaiting_first_message`) also `session`, the thread that message began (left out when it could not be told apart), where the conversation goes on: its row replaces the waiting one in the same pane (`docs/integrations/codex.md` "Starting without a first message"). | GET | `/api/v1/sessions/{mid}/{sid}/info` | Session info: `{session_id,transcript_path,cwd,model,launcher,git_branch,version,permission_mode,effort,context_tokens,output_tokens,compactions,turns,started_at,last_activity}`. `cwd` is as on the Session: an Agent's latest directory, an assistant or health chat's own directory where it started (#2368) |
| POST | `/api/v1/sessions/{mid}/{sid}/queue` | `{keep:[indexes]}`: takes back the queued input and keeps only the given items, in the order given, returns `{queue}`; used for editing, deleting and reordering (a permutation of the indexes, #6088); doesn't go through client_ops. In a Persona chat (#4342) `keep` indexes the user's own queued messages (the first `len(queued) - queued_relayed`). The node takes them out of its headless Claude with `cancel_async_message` (only the ones that have to move or go) and writes the kept ones again in the new order, and answers `{queue, images}` (`proto.QueueEdit`, samples in `spec/fixtures/wire/queue.json`): `images[i]` are message i's photos (`{mime, data}`, base64) for the composer, null for a message without any, and the key is left out when none has. 409 `queue_taken` (a message to take out went in meanwhile; nothing is written twice), `queue_changed` (an index past the queue), `queue_unsupported` (a Codex chat: nothing waits), `assistant_control_failed` (a Claude Code without the request, or a chat on the Agent SDK bridge) |
| POST | `/api/v1/sessions/{mid}/{sid}/queue/send-now` | Gives the agent what waits in Claude Code's queue now (#6088, node `session.queue.send_now`): Claude Code's own send-now, so a command it runs moves to the background and goes on, and a reply it is writing is asked again with the message (Esc would stop the command). The node presses it only while the screen offers it, with the keys the hint beside a queued message names: `ctrl+enter to send now` → ctrl+enter (Claude Code 2.1.311 to 2.1.321 in a terminal with extended keys, such as a herdr pane, the hint on the line under the message), `ctrl+x ctrl+s to send now` → ctrl+x ctrl+s (2.1.319, and 2.1.311 to 2.1.321 inside tmux or screen or a terminal without extended keys; measured in `docs/integrations/claude-integration.md`, "Queued messages"). The hint is read by its shape (#4537): the keys of any binding, an optional separator, `send now`. A fullscreen Claude Code scrolled up has the hint off screen; the node first presses the scroll-to-bottom key its "Jump to bottom" pill names (else ctrl+End), which sends nothing, then looks again. That is the queue at that moment, which the transcript reports about a second late. → `{sent:true}` once the queue is gone from the screen. 409 `nothing_queued` (nothing queued on the screen), `send_now_unsupported` (not a Claude in a terminal), `send_now_unrecognized` (#2467: something is queued but the screen shows no send-now hint the node knows, even at the end of a scrolled-up transcript, or one naming keys a terminal can't send (cmd, fn, a click), which the node's message quotes; nothing was pressed; a node from before #2467 answers this case `send_now_unsupported`), `send_now_in_doubt` (`delivered: "unknown"`: the key went in, the queue is still shown); an older node: `node_outdated`. It sends the whole queue. In a Persona chat (#4342) it is Claude Code's `interrupt` with `send_now` over stream-json: the waiting messages start the next request at once, and the step it was on stops or, when it can, goes on in the background; 409 `nothing_queued` when nothing waits, `assistant_control_failed` when that Claude Code refuses |
| POST | `/api/v1/sessions/{mid}/{sid}/seen` | Mark the session as seen, returns `{ok:true}`; `seen` can also be sent over WS |
| POST | `/api/v1/sessions/{mid}/{sid}/interrupt` | Send Esc |
| POST | `/api/v1/sessions/{mid}/{sid}/keys` | `{"keys":["esc"],"text":""}` |
| GET | `/api/v1/sessions/{mid}/{sid}/screen?lines=60&source=visible` | `{"text":"…","status":"working"}` (`lines=40` with `source=visible` is a screen card's read: on a pane herdr can't send 40 plain rows of, fewer, see "screen card"); `source=recent` also reads the pane's scrollback (lines up to 20000; fewer lines returned than requested means it reached the top); `format=ansi` includes colors (SGR, lines end in `\r\n`; old nodes don't understand it and return plain text as before) |
| POST | `/api/v1/sessions/{mid}/{sid}/screen/before` | `{"anchor":["the top few lines on screen"],"lines":200,"format"?:"ansi"}` → `{"text","has_more","at_limit"}`: a stretch of scrollback before the anchor (located by content, the anchor compared as plain text; herdr keeps only about 1000 lines, `at_limit` means it reached the top) |
| POST | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/spaces/{wid}/rename` | `{"name"}` → `{ok, name}`: `herdr workspace rename` (a Paseo space, by its id or one of its workspaces' as Android names it: the Paseo project's name, #6297, runtime ↔ node `workspace.rename`), and updates "machine/old name" in pins / mutes to the new name: the one the node's `space.rename` answers it shows now (a named herdr session's space has `<session> · ` in front, #2196), else the one given. The old name is the space's sessions', or a runtime session's whose `workspace_id` is `wid`. A space no engine of the computer lists any more (the default engine Paseo, no terminal host listing it) is refused with 409 `space_gone` |
| (node RPC) | `session.start` `plan_then` | For a start with `permission_mode: "plan"`: the mode the session goes on in once its plan is approved, wherever that happens (`docs/integrations/claude-integration.md`, "The mode after the plan"). The manager fills it in; a start that names it keeps its own. Ignored for any other mode, and by nodes older than #3784. |
| (node RPC) | `session.start` `session_id` | A manager-started Claude session may carry the id it wants the new session to use (a v4 UUID). The node starts Claude with `--session-id <id>` and answers that session, so when the start's answer never comes back the manager reconciles it by this exact id instead of guessing from launcher and directory (#6908). Optional and backward compatible: a node that does not honor it generates its own id, and the manager falls back to the pre-start snapshot heuristic. |
| POST | `/api/v1/sessions/{mid}/{sid}/modes` | `{"permission_mode"?, "effort"?, "model"?, "launcher"?, "ultracode"?, "ultracode_dismiss_lost"?}` or a separate `{"service_tier":"<advertised id>"}` request: change a running session's permission mode / reasoning effort (`effort` is `auto` / `low` / `medium` / `high` / `xhigh` / `max`, `auto` being the model's own default, see `docs/apple/ios.md` ("Reasoning effort and permission mode")); `model` (#2434) is only for Claude Code terminal sessions: the node types `/model <id>` into its input box (with the same checks as sending a message: `dialog_open` / `input_draft` reject, Agent working rejects, and the screen is read afterwards to confirm), the id comes from `GET /machines/{mid}/launchers/{name}/models` or is one the user typed (the same rule as a start's `model`, `proto.ValidModelID`; the node refuses anything else), and within one request the model is switched first, then the rest; the session list's `model` shows this choice until a new model appears in the transcript; `permission_mode` and `effort` in the session list are the current values. A Claude Code agent's `bypass_available: true` says it can switch to `bypassPermissions` while it runs (its claude was started with `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, `--allow-dangerously-skip-permissions` or `--permission-mode bypassPermissions`, read off the process by the node, #1379); without it, a terminal Claude Code the node can restart (one in a pane of a terminal host that can start an agent there, on a launcher and in a folder Persona can tell) takes the pick anyway: the node restarts it in that mode once its turn is over, resuming the same conversation (`bypass_pending: true` on its row until then, #6476, `docs/integrations/claude-integration.md` "Full access by a restart"); any other mode picked meanwhile drops the restart. Elsewhere (or from an older node) only a new start or the assistant can pick that mode. Sessions with `efforts` (Codex via app-server or the Codex App) accept `effort` from `efforts` and separate speed requests when `service_tiers` are advertised ("Codex sources and capabilities"). `POST /api/v1/sessions` and `POST /api/v1/assistant/conversations` also accept these two fields, as the starting values. `ultracode` calls the separate `session.ultracode` method after model and effort changes; `ultracode_dismiss_lost:true` only dismisses the resume notice. See "Claude Code ultracode". `launcher` (feature `launcher_switch`, #5035) other than the session's own records a switch to that launcher that the user's next message (`apply_switch`) carries out, with `model` and `effort` for it; its own launcher drops one; `from` is the launcher the client saw. See "Switching a running Agent to another provider" |
| POST | `/api/v1/sessions/{mid}/{sid}/rename` | `{"tab_name"?, "title"?}`: the tab uses `herdr tab rename`; the session name sends `/rename <name>` to the running claude (it writes `custom-title`), and if it isn't running, appends the same `custom-title` line to the transcript directly. For assistant chats, `title` is also recorded as the user-given title (the hub's `assistant.titles`, no longer overwritten by automatic titles, `docs/assistant/assistant.md` ("Chat titles")); Codex assistant chats are only recorded on the hub. With an extension's token the title is only a hint: the hub still names a chat it started after its first turn (#3758) |
| POST | `/api/v1/sessions/{mid}/{sid}/autoname` | #7432, hub feature `agent_autoname`, full devices only: the model names this Agent session now → `{"ok", "title", "title_source": "auto", "changed"}`, the list update sent before the answer. Asked by the user, so the automatic naming's limits and a hand-written name do not hold it back; Persona's own conversations are refused (400 `assistant_session`). Request, answer and error codes: "Naming an Agent on request". Answered by the manager (relayed by the hub to the computer's owner) |
| GET / PUT | `/api/v1/mutes` | Mutes, same structure as pins, plus `allowed` (Agents with notifications turned on individually while their space is muted). Rule: the Agent itself in sessions → muted; in allowed → not muted; otherwise go by its space. Muted Agents / spaces get no notifications at all (done, needs you) and are shown dimmed on the phone; cached in hub memory, updated on PUT. GET returns the cached list when available; a failed initial read returns 500 (`code: internal`) without a mute list and is retried on the next read. Clients keep their previous copy on failure; only a successful read may replace it |
| GET | `/api/v1/hub/update` | The hub's version and update state (`docs/operations/hub-update.md`): `{version, build, channel, can_update, why_not?, latest?{version, build, released, notes, newer, bad, held?}, state, progress?, busy:[{machine_id, machine, session_id?, title}], error?, auto, auto_notice, last_check?, confirmed}`; `state`: `idle` / `checking` / `available` / `downloading` / `waiting_idle` / `restarting` / `confirming` / `updated` / `rolled_back` / `failed`; `busy` lists what a restart would interrupt (chats working or waiting for an answer, machines being redeployed); `auto_notice`: the user hasn't been told "automatic updates are on" yet; `latest.held`: why automatic update won't install this newer version (its code may not include the commit this hub is running, `docs/operations/hub-update.md` ("No going backwards")), though a manual update still can; a Docker hub also has `image{name, tag, pinned}` (the image it runs; `pinned`: the tag is a version number, so `.env` must be changed first), `latest` is the newest release on the registry (`build` is 0, no `released`), and `POST …/check` asks the registry; all `/api/v1/hub/update` endpoints return 503 `internal` with a localized unavailable message when persisted update settings cannot be read. Failed reads are retried, and no settings/history write or automatic update proceeds from unread settings |
| POST | `/api/v1/hub/update/check` | Check now, returns the same as above |
| POST | `/api/v1/hub/update` | `{"now"?: true}` start updating: download, verify, wait until the assistant and Agents are idle, replace, restart; `now` is "update now" after a second confirmation and doesn't wait for idle. Not a release build (`dev` / `docker`), or no newer version 409 (`error` explains; for Docker it gives the `docker compose pull` command) |
| PUT | `/api/v1/hub/update/settings` | `{"auto"?: bool, "auto_notice_seen"?: bool}`: the automatic update switch (on by default); changing the switch also counts as having told the user; a failed save returns 503 `internal`. Retrying after storage recovery preserves update history and the bad-build list |
| GET | `/api/v1/hub/update/history` | `{"history":[{from_version, to_version, to_build, started, ended, result: updated\|rolled_back\|failed\|held, reason?, auto}]}`, newest first, keeps 50; `held`: the newer version wasn't installed automatically (`reason` says why), recorded once per version |
| GET | `/api/v1/sessions/{mid}/{sid}/skills` | Full-access-only ordinary Agent skill catalog, routed to the machine manager. No client execution overrides. Requires node capability `session_skills_v1` and returns `{catalog_version:1,skills:[{id,name,description?,source}],complete}`. References bind manager, machine, session and actual execution environment; unavailable environments fail explicitly. |
| GET | `/api/v1/assistant/skills` | Web assistant mention catalog (#5357), per-manager routing. Optional `machine_id`, `session_id`, `launcher`; the manager owns cwd/profile/identity. Returns `{catalog_version:1,skills:[{id,name,description?,source}],complete}`; instruction-file paths stay on the node, while human-readable source labels can identify roots. Unsupported, unavailable or old environments fail explicitly; ordinary chat remains independent. Selected references are revalidated on send. See "Explicit skill mentions" in `docs/assistant/assistant.md`. |
| GET | `/api/v1/skills` | Skills on the machine running the assistant (read-only): `{"machine_id","machine","skills":[{"name","description","source":"user\|builtin"}]}`; the user's are in that machine's `~/.persona/skills/` (`docs/operations/hub-update.md`). Uses the shared localized node-proxy error mapping: offline computer 503 `node_unreachable`, unavailable manager 503 `assistant_offline`, a node reporting `node_outdated` 409; transport/RPC failures retain `timeout` / `node_unreachable` (usually 502) |
| POST | `/api/v1/skills/import` | Manager-relayed, full-access-only Web skill ZIP flow. JSON `{op:"preview"\|"install"\|"cancel"\|"undo",archive?:base64,reference?,environment?}` (strict fields, body ≤6 MiB). Preview returns `{name,description,destination,machine,files,bytes,reference,environment,expires_at}`; install resends the exact ZIP plus preview reference/environment and returns a new Undo receipt. Cancel drops a preview; Undo returns `{name,recovery}`. The manager derives/authorizes current assistant and execution machine; browser paths/machines are refused. Stable `skill_*` codes explain archive/layout/metadata/limit/conflict, expired/changed environment, busy/I/O and changed-Undo failures; existing node-proxy codes cover offline/outdated nodes. No overwrite, general delete or model invocation. Limits, atomic publication, recovery and session boundaries: `docs/operations/hub-update.md` "Web skill ZIP installation". |
| GET / PUT | `/api/v1/pins` | Pins in the dev list: `{"spaces":["server/app"],"sessions":["server/<session id>"]}`; spaces use "machine/space name" (herdr workspace ids change after a herdr restart); stored in Postgres settings |
| GET | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/file?path=&cwd=&offset=` | Read a file (file viewer, `docs/apple/ios.md` ("File viewer")): `{"path","name","size","mime","text"\|"data","truncated","offset","next","is_dir","entries"?}`. Text files at most 2 MB per call, read from `offset`; if not finished, it stops at the end of the last complete line, and `next` is where the next page starts (0 when done); binary files are given whole (up to 2 MB) and can't be read from the middle; directories give the first 500 entries. `~` is home, relative paths are inside `cwd`; iCloud is refused. With `stream=1` (hub feature `file_stream`), binary files return only a descriptor `{"stream":true,"revision",...}` without `data`, and the content goes through `/file/download`; `mime` comes from a fixed extension table, then sniffing the leading bytes (see "File preview" below) |
| GET | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/file/download?path=&cwd=&inline=` | The raw bytes of the complete file, authenticated by the App with the same Bearer; the web's `<video>` / `<audio>` / `<img>` can't send headers, so they use `?token=` (the hub never logs query strings); the hub reads via the node's `file.chunk` at most 1 MiB at a time, and a single request never holds the whole file in memory. Supports HTTP Range / Content-Range (including suffix ranges), with Content-Length, ETag and an attachment file name; empty path 400, old node 409 `node_outdated`, non-regular files, iCloud and read errors are refused. Later chunks must match the size and version from the first read; if the file changes midway or the request is canceled, the download stops. The old `/file` 2 MiB binary preview is unchanged. `inline=1` only applies to images, audio/video and PDF (`Content-Disposition: inline`); everything else is still an attachment; everything except PDF carries `Content-Security-Policy: sandbox` |
| GET | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/file/thumb?path=&cwd=&size=` | A file's thumbnail (hub feature `file_thumb`, node `file.thumb`): long side at most `size` pixels (default 256, 32–1024), JPEG when opaque, PNG when transparent; JPEGs are turned to their EXIF orientation first (#1303); `ETag` is "processing version-file version-size" (a node that draws differently answers a new one), `If-None-Match` gets 304, `Cache-Control: private, max-age=86400`. Can't render 404 `no_thumbnail` (the client shows an icon), old node 409 `node_outdated` |
| GET | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/file/convert?path=&cwd=&to=pdf` | Convert a document to PDF with that computer's LibreOffice (hub feature `file_convert`, node `file.convert`, the web's Office fallback, #1345): returns `{"path","size","mime"}`, where `path` is the PDF in the node's cache, then read with `/file/download?path=<it>&inline=1`. Cached per file version, cleared 7 days after its last use; one conversion at a time, 90-second timeout; the input is first copied to a fixed file name and a temporary profile directory is used, so it doesn't fight with a LibreOffice the user has open. Not installed 404 `no_converter`, old node 409 `node_outdated` |
| POST / GET / DELETE | `/api/v1/files/transfer`, `/api/v1/files/transfer/{id}` | Copy a file from one computer into another's receive folder (feature `file_transfer`; the manager does it, the hub relays), follow it, cancel it; see "Sending files between computers" |
| GET / PUT | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/file-transfer/settings` | The computer's file transfer switch, off by default (the manager's, settings key `machine_file_transfer`): `{"enabled": bool}` → `{enabled, inbox?}`; full devices only; see "Sending files between computers" |
| GET | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/git/blob?cwd=&path=&rev=` | A file's content at some revision (hub feature `git_blob`, node `git.blob`, for the web's diff, #1437): `rev` is `HEAD`, `INDEX` (the staging area), a commit hash or "hash^" (its parent), `path` is relative to the repo root. Returns `{"path","size"}`, where `path` is a file in the node's cache named by blob id (with the original extension), then read with `/file/download`; if the file doesn't exist at that revision, `{"missing":true}`. Up to 200 MB, cleaned 7 days after its last use |
| GET / POST / DELETE | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/browser/cookies` | Sign-ins in ego lite (plugin ego, #1304, `docs/plans/plan-ego-browser.md` ("What cookie import did")): GET lists sites `{"sites":[{"domain","count","expires"?}]}` (no names or values); POST `{"cookies":[{name,value,domain,path?,expires?,secure?,http_only?,same_site?,host_only?}]}` imports and returns `imported`, `skipped`; DELETE `?site=a&site=b` or `?all=1` clears and returns `removed`. Only accepts the user's own device tokens (pairing tokens etc. 403); the hub stores nothing; target Mac offline 409 |
| GET | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/stat?paths=&cwd=` | Whether paths mentioned in a session exist on this machine: `paths` one per line (also accepts `path=a&path=b`), at most 200 → `{"stats":[{"path"(as given),"kind":"file"\|"dir"\|"denied"\|"missing","size"?}]}`. `denied` is a folder macOS won't let personad read (opening it explains how to grant access); relative paths without `cwd`, paths in iCloud, and sensitive files (see below) are always `missing`; waits at most 3 seconds per call, and anything not answered by then (a hung network drive) is also `missing`. The phone only turns file / dir / denied paths into tappable file blocks; the web inlines them as links |
| GET | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/fs?path=&cwd=` | File tree: `{"path","entries":[{"name","dir","symlink","size","mtime","ignored"}],"truncated"}`, directories first, at most 2000 entries; iCloud is refused; `ignored` (#2439): Git ignores it (the node runs `git check-ignore` once over the names on this page; outside a repo or without git nothing is marked and the field doesn't appear) |
| GET | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/fs/find?cwd=&limit=` | All files under a directory (#2438, node `fs.find`, for the web's ⌘K file search): `{"cwd","files":[relative paths, "/"-separated],"truncated","source":"git"\|"walk"}`. Inside a git repo (including subdirectories) it uses `git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard` (ignored files and files deleted on disk aren't listed); otherwise it walks breadth-first from `cwd` (skips `.git`, `node_modules` and various cache directories, doesn't follow symlinks into directories, capped at 5 seconds), so when over the limit the shallowest files are kept. At most `limit` files (default and maximum 50,000); sensitive paths are not listed (same as `fs`: ssh keys, the hub's token, etc.), and iCloud and sensitive directories are refused entirely. The node reuses the result for the same directory within 10 seconds. Same permissions as `fs`: full role only, answer-only devices (the watch) can't |
| GET | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/git/status?cwd=` | `{"is_repo","root","branch","head","upstream","gone","ahead","behind","files":[{"path","orig_path","index","worktree","added","deleted","binary"}],"stashes","commits":[latest 30]}` (read-only, `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`; `gone`: the upstream is configured but its ref is missing, e.g. deleted on the remote and pruned, so `ahead` / `behind` are 0 and mean nothing; left out otherwise) |
| POST | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/git/pull` | `{"cwd"}` → `{"status": GitStatus, "updated": bool}`; only allowed on a normal branch with an upstream and a clean worktree, runs `git pull --ff-only --no-rebase --no-autostash --no-recurse-submodules`. Divergence, uncommitted changes, no upstream, auth failure or timeout all report an error; it never stashes / merges / rebases automatically; the pull command gets at most 60 seconds, the node 75 seconds total, the hub 90 seconds. Full role only |
| GET | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/git/diff?cwd=&path=&staged=0\|1` | `{"path","diff","truncated"}`; untracked files are diffed against /dev/null, at most 512 KB: the node stops reading there, and a longer diff ends after its last whole line within it, with `truncated` |
| GET | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/git/show?cwd=&hash=` | `{"commit","files","diff","truncated"}`; the diff is capped like `git/diff`'s |
| GET | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/git/log?cwd=&skip=&limit=` | `{"commits":[…]}` paged |
| GET | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/git/review?cwd=&scope=&base=&path=` | #151, hub feature `git_review`, node `git.review`: every file a scope changed, with its hunks, for the web's Review panel ([review](../web/review.md)). `scope` is `uncommitted` (the working tree against HEAD), `branch` (against where the branch left the default branch, or the branch named in `base`) or `commit` (against the commit in `base`); new files Git does not track yet count as added. → `{"root","scope","base":{"hash","short","subject","ref","empty"},"head":{"hash","short","branch"},"files":[{"path","old_path","status","untracked","added","deleted","binary","generated","refused","big","revision","hunks":[{"header","old_start","new_start","lines"}]}],"truncated"}`. `path` (repeatable) asks for only those files (a `big` one, which came without its hunks; a rename with both paths). Refusals are 409 with `code`: `not_git`, `bad_scope`, `bad_base`, `no_default_branch`, `no_merge_base`; an older node is 409 `node_outdated` |
| GET | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/git/branches?cwd=` | #6121: `{"branches":[{"name","remote","current","upstream","hash","subject","date"}],"default"}`: local branches, then remote ones without a local branch of the same name, newest first, at most 300; `default` (#7014) is the remote's default branch as git knows it (`origin/HEAD`, without the remote's name), left out when git doesn't know it (and by an older node). Full role only |
| GET | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/git/pr?cwd=` | #6121, through `gh` on that machine as it is signed in: the current branch's pull request `{"branch","pr":{"number","url","title","state","draft","base","head","mergeable","merge_state","review","auto_merge","checks":[{"name","state":"pass\|fail\|pending\|skipped","url"}],"checks_state":"passing\|failing\|pending","threads":[{"path","line","outdated","comments":[{"author","body","url","at"}]}]}}` (`threads`: the unresolved review threads only); `"pr":null` when the branch has none. Full role only |
| POST | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/git/stage` · `…/git/commit` · `…/git/push` · `…/git/switch` · `…/git/stash` | #6121, the Git panel's writes, each a click the client confirmed; answer `{"status": GitStatus, …}`. `stage {cwd, paths, unstage?}` (`git add` / `git restore --staged`; paths `file.read` refuses are refused); `commit {cwd, message}` commits what is staged (nothing staged is refused, never `-a`; hooks run, the hub waits up to 5 minutes) → `+ commit`; `push {cwd, set_upstream?}` pushes the branch to its own upstream branch by an explicit refspec with no `+` (a forcing refspec in the config does not apply), a branch without one only with `set_upstream` (to `origin`, same name) → `+ output`; `switch {cwd, branch, create?, from?}`: uncommitted files the target has differently are listed and nothing is switched, other uncommitted changes go along; a remote-only branch gets a local branch tracking it; `stash {cwd, op: push\|list\|apply\|pop\|drop, index?, oid?, message?, untracked?}` → `+ stashes:[{index,oid,message,date}]`. Nothing forces, resets, stashes on its own or skips a hook; one write at a time per repository. A refusal is a 409 with `code`: `git_not_repo`, `git_detached`, `git_nothing_staged`, `git_hook_failed` (its output is `error`), `git_identity`, `git_no_upstream`, `git_no_remote`, `git_push_rejected` (pull first), `git_auth`, `git_conflict` (`files`), `git_busy` (another git holds the lock), `git_no_branch`, `git_no_stash`, `git_stash_stale`, `git_stash_unsupported`, `git_stash_conflicted` (`files`: an apply / pop stopped on merge conflicts, so the stash's content is in the tree with those files unmerged and the entry is kept; #1885), `git_failed`. Full role only |
| POST | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/git/pr` · `…/git/pr/merge` | #6121: `{cwd, title, body, base?, draft?}` opens a pull request for the current branch (pushed, nothing left to push, else `git_not_pushed`); `{cwd, number, method: squash\|merge\|rebase, auto?}` merges it now or sets it to merge when ready, `{cwd, number, auto_off: true}` takes that back; the branch is never deleted (gh would switch the checkout). Both answer as `GET git/pr`. `gh` missing: `no_gh`; not signed in: `not_signed_in`; no pull request: `git_no_pr`; no GitHub remote: `git_not_github`. Full role only |
| POST | `/api/v1/sessions/{mid}/{sid}/fork` | Branch into a new chat (#2137): body `{at_item_id}` (the item id of a reply; empty means the whole thing) → `{session_id}`. The node copies Claude's transcript up to the end of the turn that reply is in, under a new session id, leaving the original session untouched; the new session is an offline session, and the next message `--resume`s it as usual. Only supported when the session has `can_fork: true` (Claude Code, with a transcript, not an external source / Codex; a runtime's session only when its runtime names a Claude transcript on that computer, Paseo's agents running Claude Code, #6298: the copy is of that transcript, named after the session, and the machine's engine continues it), otherwise returns `code: fork_unsupported`; branching from the turn still being written returns `fork_turn_running`. Limits: only the conversation itself is copied; the file snapshots `/rewind` uses (`~/.claude/file-history/<id>/`) and subagent records are not, so `/rewind` in the branch can't go back to changes made before the branch |
| POST | `/api/v1/sessions/{mid}/{sid}/restore-model` | Back to the configured model after a refusal fallback (#2528): no body; a relay of the session id to the node's `session.restore_model` (see "Going back to the configured model"). Full role only |
| POST | `/api/v1/sessions/{mid}/{sid}/close` | Quit claude and close the tab (any Agent in herdr, including manually started ones; for a split tab only its own pane is closed) |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/sessions/{mid}/{sid}` | Delete a chat: only removes it from the session lists everywhere (the hub records the time in settings `sessions.deleted`, and neither the `sessions` push nor `GET /api/v1/sessions` includes it anymore); the transcript on the computer is untouched; this holds for finished sessions still open on their computer (`idle`, `done`, a Codex App thread the App keeps listing) too, whatever their status reads next; if the session is used again later (`updated_at` later than the deletion, it runs again, or it waits on a card for the user), it reappears. The note is kept (it does not expire). Sessions that failed to start (`start_error`) can also be deleted and disappear immediately. → `{"ok":true}`; running or still starting 409, assistant chats 400 (use archive), no such session 404, read-only device 403 |
| GET | `/api/v1/assistant` | `{"machine_id","launcher","cwd","timezone","timezone_picked"?,"notes"?,"notes_effective","main"?,"main_tasks_quiet","recording_days","minutes_days","kb_topics","main_background_folded","meeting_attendance_default","idle_close_hours","archive_closed_days","interject_background","agent_tasks","inbox_signals","next_suggestions","main_supervises_own_tasks","background_supervisor"?,"conversations":[Session]}`: `main_supervises_own_tasks` is the effective "the main chat supervises its own tasks" switch (`false` if never changed: the background supervisor follows up the tasks no leader supervises, #4927, `docs/assistant/unified-entry.md` "Background supervisor"), and `background_supervisor` is that conversation's session id once it has been made (on the assistant's computer; read-only, with `background_supervisor_machine_id` and `background_supervisor_at`); `next_suggestions` is the effective "suggest the next message" switch for chats without a suggestion of their own (`false` if never changed, #4644, `docs/assistant/assistant.md` "Next-message suggestions"); `agent_tasks` is the effective "every Agent Persona starts is a supervised task" switch (`false` if never changed, #3617, `docs/assistant/unified-entry.md` "Agent tasks"); `inbox_signals` is the effective "tell a task's supervisor about new Inbox messages on it" switch (`false` if never changed, #4293, `docs/assistant/unified-entry.md` "Supervision (#3124)"); `interject_background` is the effective "move running work to the background when I interject" switch (`false` if never changed, #3278, `docs/assistant/assistant.md` "Interjecting while it answers"); `notes` is present only if saved in the App; `timezone_picked` is present once a client said whether the user picked `timezone` by hand (#1855, below); `main_tasks_quiet` is the effective value of "notify tasks dispatched by the main chat only in the main chat" (`true` if never changed, #1731); `idle_close_hours` is the effective number of hours an idle Agent Persona started stays open before the hub closes it (default 12, 0 is off, #2784, `docs/assistant/todos.md`); `archive_closed_days` is the effective number of days a closed session stays listed before the manager archives it by itself (default 3, 0 is off, #3618, `docs/assistant/todos.md` "Closed sessions archive themselves"); `recording_days` is the effective number of days recordings stay in the knowledge base (default 14, #3235); `kb_topics` is the effective "organize knowledge points by topic" switch (`true` if never changed, #3783, [knowledge.md](../assistant/knowledge.md) "Topics"); `main_background_folded` is the effective "fold background rounds" switch: the apps fold the main chat's rounds that another chat, a scheduled task or a follow-up started into one line (`true` if never changed, #4314, `docs/assistant/assistant.md` "Background rounds"); `minutes_days` is the effective number of days a meeting's minutes stay after its transcript went (forever by default: unset or `0`; otherwise the larger of it and `recording_days`, #3780 / #3862, [meeting-minutes.md](../assistant/meeting-minutes.md) "Privacy"); `meeting_attendance_default` is the role a meeting recording pre-selects (`off` until changed, `listener`, `participant`; present only with the `meeting_attendance` feature, #2981, [meeting-minutes.md](../assistant/meeting-minutes.md) "Attending a meeting"); `main` is the main chat's session id (on the `machine_id` machine); archived chats are not listed by default, `?archived=1` includes them (`archived: true`). `?space=health` lists chats in the health space, with `cwd` being the health directory; without `space` only the assistant's own are listed, not the health chats; any other `space` returns 400 (`docs/assistant/health.md`) |
| GET | `/api/v1/assistant/search?q=&limit=` | The assistant's chats found by their title, the user's words or the replies (`assistant_search`); see "Assistant chat search (#6282)" |
| PUT | `/api/v1/assistant` | `{"machine_id"?,"launcher"?,"timezone"?,"timezone_picked"?,"notes"?,"main"?,"main_tasks_quiet"?,"recording_days"?,"minutes_days"?,"kb_topics"?,"main_background_folded"?,"meeting_attendance_default"?,"idle_close_hours"?,"archive_closed_days"?,"interject_background"?,"agent_tasks"?,"inbox_signals"?,"next_suggestions"?,"main_supervises_own_tasks"?}`, stored in Postgres settings (`docs/assistant/assistant.md`); only the fields present are changed; `recording_days` is 1–365; `minutes_days` is `0` (forever, the default) or 1–3650 (`400` otherwise; a positive value below `recording_days` is saved but `recording_days` stays in effect); `meeting_attendance_default` is `off`, `listener` or `participant` (full credentials only); `idle_close_hours` is 0–8760; `archive_closed_days` is 0–3650; an empty string for `notes` also counts as a change; `main` of `"-"` clears the main chat (the App sends it together when switching machines); `timezone_picked` (#1855): `true` with a `timezone` the user picked by hand (without one, the zone in effect becomes the picked one), `false` to follow the devices again; while the saved value is `true`, a `timezone` sent without `timezone_picked` (a device syncing its own zone, as apps from before do) is left out and the answer still has the picked zone |
| POST | `/api/v1/assistant/conversations` | `{"prompt","images"?,"launcher"?,"model"?,"effort"?,"service_tier"?,"purpose"?,"machine_id"?,"main"?,"space"?,"report_tasks"?,"via"?}` → `{"session"}`: writes CLAUDE.md, then starts a new session in the assistant directory. `via` says how the app sent the prompt when it was not typed in the app itself: `"intent"` (Siri, Shortcuts, an App Intent), `"share"` (the share sheet) or `"card"` (a card's button that wrote it, as the Today card's Prep does from a calendar event); any value marks it, and such a message never counts as the user's own words for a secret hand-off's Always rule (`docs/extensions/secret-providers.md` "Always rules"), and the same field on a message to an assistant conversation (`…/messages`) does the same. `launcher` / `model` / `effort` are the first message's, as a message's pick (#5033): `service_tier` (feature `assistant_start_service_tier`, #6240) is the native speed ID advertised by the selected Codex model's `service_tiers`, currently `priority` for Fast; it is independent of `effort` and is acknowledged through `thread/settings/update` before the first `turn/start`, including when a warm thread is adopted. Omitting it makes no per-request speed override, so Codex's configured default remains effective; later messages omit it and the native thread retains its acknowledged setting. An existing-session send gets 409 `assistant_service_tier_start_only`, a non-Codex start 409 `assistant_service_tier_unsupported`, and a native refusal 409 `assistant_service_tier_refused`, all with `delivered: "none"` and no turn. A native refusal stops the cold or warm-adopted process before conversation, mode or recovery state is saved. These coded summaries are localized in en, zh-Hans and ja, without exposing the native English diagnostic as person-facing detail. A nonempty value requires the node capability `assistant_service_tier` and returns 409 `node_outdated` before starting on an older node. A manager without `assistant_start_service_tier` in its hello gets no relay and the app gets 501 `assistant_service_tier_manager_outdated`; an older hub ignores the unknown field, so capable web clients neither offer nor send it without the hub feature and default manager. `model` is any model ID (`proto.ValidModelID`, else 400; a typed one the list lacks is kept), for `launcher` or else the purpose's launcher; 400 when that launcher sets its own model (`locked`) or its agent takes none, before anything starts; a `launcher` that isn't on the computer falls back to the purpose's, its `model` dropped. Without `purpose` or `guest`, a named `launcher` or `model` (with `effort`) is kept as the new chat's `model_pick` (in the answer's `session` too) so its later messages keep it (feature `assistant_model_pick`); an `effort` alone, nothing named, or a fallback keeps nothing. A `main: true` start after `/clear` starts on the cleared main chat's pick unless it names a launcher or model (its `effort` is then the first message's only); when it names neither, the manager discards an explicit `service_tier` rather than applying it to that carried pick, so a client choosing Fast must name the launcher or model whose displayed setup it belongs to; a carried pick that can't run any more refuses that start once (409 `launcher_out_of_scope` / `launcher_own_service` / `launcher_missing`, or 400) and is dropped, so the next start runs on the default. `space: "health"` starts it in the health space's directory (the health CLAUDE.md, `docs/assistant/health.md`); together with `main: true` it's 400, and any other `space` is 400. `purpose`: which model purpose to use (one the hub knows, e.g. `lark.agent`; unknown 400; empty means `assistant`); `machine_id`: which of the hub's machines to run on (empty means the assistant's; unknown machine 400). The plugin's /agent uses these two (#1484). `report_tasks: true`: tasks dispatched by this chat (`task_plan`, `agent_start`) are, like the main chat's "quiet tasks", not pushed separately; their status changes are sent into this chat as task notifications (#3192, `docs/extensions/lark-agent.md` ("Dispatched tasks")); the plugin's /agent sets it. `guest: {"tools": [...]}`: starts a guest conversation (`docs/assistant/assistant.md` ("Guest conversations")): it can use only these 1–8 connector tools, runs in its own directory with no built-in tools and no live snapshot, can't be combined with `main` / `space`; 400 when the node is too old The answer has `launcher_note` when the configured launcher can't run there and one of the same kind runs it instead (#4659). |
| GET / PUT | `/api/v1/assistant` (Agent naming) | `agent_auto_naming` (effective default `true`), `agent_auto_naming_max` (effective default `1`, integer 1–1000), `agent_auto_naming_interval_hours` (effective default `0`: periodic updates off; integer 0–8760). A sparse PUT requires full credentials and an explicit assistant in `X-Persona-Manager` or `?manager=`; conflicting or missing targets are rejected. The success response includes the owner and effective values. The count is successful automatic name changes per session, including periodic refreshes; refresh requires new output tokens and never overrides manual titles. iOS and Android can add controls against this same API later; this change adds web controls only. Older managers omit these fields, so clients must not infer support. |
| GET | `/api/v1/assistant/leaders` | Every direction (leader conversation): `{"leaders":[{"id","title","name"?,"project"?,"ended"?,"progress"?,"by","at","ended_at"?}]}`, current ones first, then ended ones, each by `at` then `id`; `name` is what the direction is called (the owner's or the secretary's name, else the project's name, else the title without its date and kind), `progress` the leader's latest own summary `{reached?,doing?,needs_you?,links?,at}`; titles or directions not readable 503 (`docs/assistant/unified-entry.md` "Leader conversations") |
| GET | `/api/v1/assistant/dispatch-policy` | The assistant's dispatch policy: `{"dispatch_policy":{"rules":[{"conversation_class","deny":["task_plan"|"agent_start"|"start_conversation"|"send_to_main"|"send_to_leader"],"message"?}],"expires_at"?}}`. A conversation class is `main`, `leader`, `background_supervisor`, `scheduled` (a scheduled task's own conversation) or `other`; with no policy in force the answer is `{"dispatch_policy":{"rules":[]}}`. Full credentials, or an extension token granted `assistant.dispatch_policy`. See "Dispatch policy" below |
| PUT | `/api/v1/assistant/dispatch-policy` | Replace the dispatch policy with `{"dispatch_policy":{…}}`; empty `rules` clears it (`{"rules":[]}`). A full-credential write may omit `expires_at`; an extension write must name an `expires_at` no more than one hour ahead (a past or later one is 400), so a stopped or uninstalled extension leaves nothing in force. An unknown class or action, a repeated class, an empty `deny` or an over-long `message` is 400; read-only devices are 403. The same field may be written with `PUT /api/v1/assistant` (full credentials, expiry optional). Full credentials, or an extension token granted `assistant.dispatch_policy`; see "Dispatch policy" below |
| GET | `/api/v1/assistant/directions/tree` | The direction tree (#4352) every client's sidebar, To-dos grouping and Agents grouping read: `{"directions":[{"id","name","secretary"?,"counts":{"working","needs_you","stuck","review","planned"},"running","tasks":[{"id","title","state","agents":[{"machine_id","session_id","title","agent","state","children"?}]}]}]}`. Current directions in the order `GET /api/v1/assistant/leaders` lists them, then the secretary group last (`secretary: true`, `id` the main conversation's, `name` `""`, always present). `tasks` are the open to-dos (the To-dos page's open count) whose supervisor is that direction; the main conversation's, no supervisor's, an ended or unknown conversation's go to the secretary group; a worker of a task leader is not listed or counted, its Agents are `children` of the leader's Agent. `state` is `needs_you`, `review`, `planned` (no Agent has worked on it yet, #5846; `counts.planned` absent or 0 from an older hub), `stuck` or `working` (first match), tasks listed needs_you, review, stuck, working, planned, newest activity first; `counts` counts the listed tasks per state. `running` (#6626, always sent): an Agent of the direction's listed tasks, or one under it, has a `working` session, whatever the task's state — the one rule for a direction row's spinner on every client (a client reading a tree without it, from an older hub, uses `counts.working > 0`). An Agent's `state` is its session's as on session rows (`""`: not found); `children` are the Agents it spawned, its workers' Agents, its running sub-agents (`session_id` `"<parent>@<id>"`, `title` the description) and its Codex sub-agent sessions still going. Answered by the default manager alone (not merged over managers like `GET /api/v1/todos`). Read-only devices may read it; to-dos not loaded 503; an older hub 404 (clients keep the flat direction rows). Rules: `docs/assistant/unified-entry.md` "The direction tree" |
| GET | `/api/v1/assistant/directions/offers` | The directions offered for New chats and not yet answered, newest first: `{"offers":[{"conversation","machine_id","title","project"?,"new_project"?,"closest"?,"at"}]}` (`docs/assistant/unified-entry.md` "New chat opens a direction") |

| POST | `/api/v1/assistant/directions/{id}/make` | Make it a direction: the same without an offer. The clients' **设为常驻** (en **Pin**, #4331) |
| POST | `/api/v1/assistant/directions/{id}/end` | End direction → `{"ended"}` (false: it was no direction); the tasks it supervised keep their `supervisor`. The clients' **取消常驻** (en **Unpin**) |

| DELETE | `/api/v1/assistant/conversations/{id}/always/{hash}` | Full-access clients only: remove one grant, then reset the running assistant's permissions (stops its current response). Other conversations and grants remain unchanged |

| POST | `/api/v1/assistant/main/new` | `{"carry":"summary"\|"none","expect"?}`: start a new main chat. `carry` (default `summary`) brings along the old main chat's latest compaction summary and the few messages after it; `expect` is the main chat id the App sees, and a mismatch returns 409 `main_changed`; the old main chat answering / compacting 409 `busy`. On success the main chat is cleared (`main` disappears from `GET /api/v1/assistant`), and the old one is renamed "旧主对话 · 至 M月D日" ("Old main chat · until <month/day>") and archived → `{"ok","archived":"<old id, empty if there was no main chat>","carried":bool}`. The next `POST /api/v1/assistant/conversations` with `main:true` (and messages to the main chat from the Lark bot or channels) starts the new main chat, with the carried background placed before the first message as `<persona-context kind="context" title="接上旧主对话">` ("Continuing the old main chat"), used once. When it starts, the old main chat's open tasks move to it, `origin` and `supervision.supervisor` together (`docs/assistant/assistant.md` ("New main chat")) |
| POST | `/api/v1/assistant/main/clear` | `{"expect"?}`: clear the main chat's context in place (the apps' **Clear context** and `/clear`, #5095; hub feature `assistant_main_clear`). `expect` as for `main/new` (409 `main_changed`); a turn it is on is no refusal: Persona's own process for it is closed (`session.close`, not for a conversation the user resumed in a terminal) and a question it waits on is withdrawn; the tasks it handed out keep running. The old main chat is put away as `main/new` puts it (renamed, archived, listed in `former`), nothing is carried over, and a background an earlier `main/new` left waiting is dropped, so the next main-chat message starts a new chat with that message alone → `{"ok","archived":"<old id, empty if there was no main chat>"}` (`docs/assistant/assistant.md` ("Clear context")) |
| POST | `/api/v1/assistant/warm` | `{"launcher"?}`: start a spare claude process in advance for new chats to use → `{"ok":true,"readiness"?}` (`readiness` see "Main chat readiness" above, without probe; if it can't be computed in time, returns the last recorded value or omits it) |
| GET | `/api/v1/assistant/availability` | Availability metrics (#4924, `docs/assistant/assistant.md` "Availability metrics"): `?hours=` (default 168, at most 720) → `{"hours","reply_wait":{"all":{"<state>":WaitN},"main":{"<state>":WaitN},"main_days":[{"day","open_tasks"?,…WaitN}]},"background_share":[{"day","conversation","main","seconds":{"<source>":n},"rounds":{"<source>":n},"background_share"}],"queue_wait":{"by_kind":{"<kind>":QueueN},"main_by_kind":{"<kind>":QueueN},"queued_now":[{"conversation","main","depth","oldest_seconds"}]},"supervision":{"by_model":[{"model","effort","accepted","settled","reopened","rework_rounds","rework_rounds_per_task"}],"days":[{"day","conversation","role","model","effort","accepted","output_tokens"}]},"ask_outcome":{"<card kind>":{"<who>":{"n","median_seconds","p90_seconds"}}}}`. `WaitN` = `{"n","median_seconds","p90_seconds","unanswered"}`; `QueueN` = `{"n","median_seconds","p90_seconds","max_seconds","max_depth"}`, `main_by_kind` being the main chat's alone; `open_tasks` is the most tasks open when one of that day's messages came (omitted when not known); a day's `background_share` leaves `other` rounds out; `<state>` is `idle`, `owner_round`, `background_round` or `unknown_round`; `<source>` and `<kind>` are `owner`, `supervision`, `followup`, `patrol`, `conversation`, `notice` or `other` (a queue has no `owner` or `other`); `<card kind>` is `question`, `permission`, `plan`, `screen`, `elicitation`, `ask_user`, `decision`, `conclusion` or `verify`; `<who>` is `owner`, `supervisor`, `delegate`, `standing_authorization`, `default`, `remembered`, `dismissed` or `expired`. `supervision` (#5086, `docs/assistant/assistant.md` "Supervision by model"; absent from a hub before it): `by_model` is, per model and effort the reviewer ran on (`""` when not known; a conversation or a task leader's agent), the acceptances its `task_review` closed a task with, how many of them are `settled` (at least 24 hours old at the read), how many of the settled ones were `reopened` within 24 hours of the acceptance, and the rework rounds each took since the task's previous acceptance, most accepted first; `days` is, per day and conversation that reviewed in the window (a task leader's agent has none), its `role` (`main`, `background`, `leader` or `conversation`), the tasks it accepted and the output tokens it generated that day (all of its output, input and cache not counted: not attributed to the tasks). Days are the assistant's time zone, newest first. Read-only: computed from `session_work_events` (kept 30 days). Full role only (others 403); no database 503; an older hub 404 |
| GET | `/api/v1/assistant/readiness` | Main chat readiness (`?probe=1` actually runs a one-word check, reused within 30 seconds), see "Main chat readiness" above |
| POST | `/api/v1/assistant/readiness/dismiss` | `{"dismissed":bool}`: remember "Later" → `{"ok":true}` |
| GET | `/api/v1/assistant/tasks` | Scheduled tasks (one table, `docs/assistant/assistant.md` ("Scheduled tasks")): `{"tasks":[Task]}`; one-off follow-ups that have already run aren't listed. `Task` = `{id,title,prompt,repeat:"once"\|"daily"\|"interval"\|"cron",at,time:"HH:MM",weekdays:[1..7],every_minutes,cron,cron_text,next_runs,enabled,machine_id,session_id,launcher,permission_mode,effort,created_by,created_at,last_run,last_session_id,last_status,last_error,next_run,run_machine_id,run_session_id,run_launcher,push,inbox,facts,until}`: `once` uses `at`, `daily` uses `time` + `weekdays` (empty = every day), `interval` runs every `every_minutes` (5 minutes to 7 days) with `at` being the next run, `cron` runs on the 5-field cron expression `cron` (`minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week` or `@hourly` / `@daily` / `@weekly` / `@monthly` / `@yearly`, read in the user's time zone, runs at least 5 minutes apart) and the list adds `cron_text` (the expression in words in the request's language, omitted when there are none) and `next_runs` (its next 5 runs, omitted when it is off); when `session_id` is set it posts into that chat, empty = the task's own chat (`run_session_id`, recorded by the hub: created on the first run and reused after; empty = created on the next run); `launcher` / `permission_mode` (`default` / `acceptEdits` / `plan` / `auto` / `bypassPermissions`) / `effort` (`low`…`max`) empty = the assistant's default, changeable only in the App; `created_by: "assistant"` means the assistant created it in a chat; `facts`: the run's fixed part (what waits for the owner, the last 12 hours, what is to be verified) is computed by Persona and sent as one Lark card, the model writing only a summary on top (`docs/extensions/bots.md` ("Morning and evening briefings")); on for the default morning and evening routines, `false` or absent otherwise; `push`: `""` pushes every run's answer (default), `"asked"` only pushes what the run itself sends with `notify_user`: such a task runs in its own chat, or, with a `session_id` other than main chat, posts into that chat without pushing or mirroring the run's normal answer (a `session_id` that is main chat is cleared) (`docs/assistant/assistant.md` ("Push after running")); a hub that understands this field includes `task_push` in features, and clients show the switch based on that. `until`, omitted when unset, is an optional RFC 3339 end time, ignored for `once`; PUT omits it to keep the stored time and `null` clears it; when that time is reached the task is disabled and a skipped run is stored |
| POST | `/api/v1/assistant/tasks` | Create a `Task` (`session_id` ignored; the task's own chat is used) → `{"task"}`; invalid 400, with a user-facing message (in Chinese) |
| PUT | `/api/v1/assistant/tasks/{id}` | Save the user-editable fields (`title,prompt,repeat,at,time,weekdays,every_minutes,cron,enabled,launcher,permission_mode,effort,push,facts,until`, `""` = default; when the body has no `push` (or no `facts`) the existing value is kept, `null` or an unknown value returns 400; omitting `until` keeps it and `null` clears it) → `{"task"}`; `session_id` can only be cleared (switching to the task's own chat); `run_*` is written only by the hub; for `interval`, the next run is counted from now when the interval or rule changes, or when it's re-enabled; a body without `cron` on a `cron` task keeps its rule (`repeat`, `cron`) and saves the rest, since older apps read the task as another repeat |
| GET | `/api/v1/assistant/tasks/cron?cron=<expression>` | Check a cron expression before saving it → `{"cron","text","timezone","next_runs"}`: the expression as it would be stored, in words in the request's language (`""` when there are none), the user's time zone (IANA name) and its next 5 runs; invalid 400 with what is wrong in the request's language |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/assistant/tasks/{id}` | Delete |

| POST | `/api/v1/assistant/places` | Add a place `{name,address?,latitude,longitude,radius_meters?}` → `{"place"}`: the name and address are trimmed, one line, at most 40 / 200 characters; the coordinates are required and on Earth; the radius defaults to 150 and is clamped to 100–2000; a name another place has (case aside) 409; at most 50 places; a device without full credentials 403 |
| PUT | `/api/v1/assistant/places/{id}` | Change a place (the same body and rules) → `{"place"}`; not there 404 |

A hub or manager from before them answers 404, which clients show as "not available on this assistant" |
| POST | `/api/v1/assistant/saved-prompts` | Add one at the end `{name,text}` → `{"prompt"}`: the name is the word after `/` (a `/` typed before it is dropped), trimmed, at most 32 letters (any script), digits, combining marks, `-`, `_` or `.`, unique ignoring case (else 409); the text is trimmed, its line ends made `\n`, 1–8000 characters, no control characters but newline and tab; at most 100 prompts (400); read-only devices 403. | PUT | `/api/v1/assistant/saved-prompts/{id}` | Change one's name and text (the same rules), keeping its place → `{"prompt"}`; not there 404 |
| PUT | `/api/v1/assistant/saved-prompts/order` | `{"ids":[…]}`: every saved prompt's id once, in the new order → `{"prompts"}`; a list that changed since it was read (one added, deleted, missing or named twice) is 409 and nothing moves |

PUT `{"on":bool}` → 200 `{"on"}`; GET also returns `{"on"}`. Stored per machine in the hub's settings table (key `claude_live_replies/<machine id>`); on when never set; works while offline, and a PUT sends `node.configure {"claude_live_replies", "claude_dirs"}` right away (`claude_dirs` so the node keeps its directories). Missing `on` 400; an older hub 404, and clients hide the switch (`docs/integrations/claude-integration.md` "Live replies (MessageDisplay)") |

The hub records which device credential registered it, and revoking that credential deletes the device too, so it no longer gets pushes. while only a compatibility Persona Link desktop is active (a computer whose parent reports presence through persona-link, [link.md](../operations/link.md) "Presence"), it doesn't get the "Needs You" cards whose notifications that parent confirmed (`notify.request`'s `link_covered`; Focus on the Mac may still hold them back there), and still gets the cards it did not ring for, "Agent finished", reply reminders, decisions, `POST /api/v1/notify` alerts and the Live Activity's start alert; reminders the assistant sends at your request are still pushed); `look` (which avatar this phone's Live Activity draws: `{"design","light","dark","package"?}`, PUT separately when the App switches avatars; the hub puts it as is into the content-state pushed to this device, see `docs/apple/live-activity.md` ("Avatar"); a design over 32 bytes or package over 160 bytes is not stored); `quiet` (quiet hours, #5806: `{"enabled","start":"HH:MM","end":"HH:MM","tz"?}`, all empty until set; the window may cross midnight, start = end is no window, an empty `tz` is the user's time zone the hub knows; inside it this device gets no "Agent finished", and "Needs you" (cards, reply reminders) arrives without sound and with `interruption-level: passive`; a Live Activity push-to-start leaves out its alert; the assistant's reminders, `POST /api/v1/notify` and the hub's own notices are unchanged; bad times or an unknown zone return 400); `muted_managers` (Settings › Managers › one › Notifications: the ids of the managers whose pushes this device doesn't want, default `[]`, always a list in answers (an app offers the switch only when it is there), trimmed and without repeats, only managers of the roster (a write drops the others, so a removed manager's id takes no place; checked against one read of the roster, and when the roster can't answer every id is kept), at most 64 ids of at most 64 bytes; what a manager asks for skips this device: `notify.request` (its assistant's reminders, finished turns, reply reminders and cards), its extensions' `hub.push_localized` and `POST /api/v1/notify` with their token, `POST /api/v1/notify` with another credential that names one of its computers (one naming no computer of this hub is the hub's own), and `personad notify` on one of its computers, on APNs and as `notify` WebSocket events alike; PUT may carry only the fields to change (PUTs of one device apply one after the other, so partial ones sent at once all take effect); the response also has the hub's `long_turn_seconds` and `done_delay_seconds` (read-only). Can be set before the device has registered for push |
| PUT | `/api/v1/devices/{id}/widgets` | Which extension widgets are on this device's screen `{"widgets":[{extension,id,family}]}` (replaced wholesale, at most 64): when an extension sends `ui.invalidate`, the hub sends the background push `extension_widget` to devices with that widget (at most one per device per widget every 15 minutes), see `docs/extensions/extensions.md` ("System-level placements") |
| POST | `/api/v1/notify` | Send a reminder to the devices (for extensions, see `docs/extensions/extensions.md` ("Sending notifications")): `{"title","body","machine_id"?,"session_id"?,"level"?:"active\|time-sensitive","push_level"?:"P0\|P1\|P2","id"?,"silent"?,"actions"?,"ui"?,"state"?}` (`push_level` is the low-distraction urgency, default `P1`, see "Low-distraction mode" in `docs/server/server.md`), at least one of title and body (title at most 120 characters, body 1000), `machine_id` and `session_id` both given or neither, `level` defaults to `active`, the same `id` replaces the previous one on the phone (apns-collapse-id; `id` at most 56 bytes), `silent: true` has no sound. Extension credentials may carry up to 3 `actions`, `ui` and `state` (notification button spec in `docs/extensions/extensions.md` ("Notification buttons")). With a session, tapping opens that session; a muted session returns `{"sent":false,"reason":"muted"}` and nothing is sent. Respects the device's `input` switch (turn off "Needs You" and it's not received), and the "Phone Muted" and desktop-online rules; on the persistent connection it's a `notify` event with `kind` `alert` and the caller's `id` (without a session, `machine_id` and `session_id` are empty strings); the push collapse id is `notify:<id>`, so it never collides with the hub's own pushes. An extension credential's `id` goes out as its own instead: on the persistent connection `ext:` and the sha256 of its manager, the extension and the `id` (64 hex digits, longer than any caller's `id` may be), on the push `notify-ext:` and the first 32 of them. It replaces only that extension's earlier alert, and no other extension's, manager's or caller's `id` replaces it. An encoded payload over 3500 bytes, or `machine_id` / `session_id` over 128 bytes, returns 400. Callable with full-access credentials and extension credentials with the `notify` scope; a non-extension credential sending `actions`/`ui`/`state` gets 400. If no recipient is selected on either channel, returns `{"sent":false,"reason":"no_device"}` when no device has a usable push route and no capable WebSocket connection is online, or `{"sent":false,"reason":"filtered"}` when all reachable recipients are excluded by notification preferences (including manager switches) or desktop suppression. `{"sent":true}` only means it was handed to push or a capable WebSocket connection, not that it was delivered; asynchronous APNs or relay failures do not change this reply |

Tiered avatars (such as `nwverse`) only expose the current tier: `manifest` is that tier's own persona.json (files under `tiers/<tier>/`), `rev` is a hash of that tier's files, and changing tier means rev changes. An empty list when there are no packages |
| GET | `/api/v1/personas/{id}/{file…}` | One file from the package (PNG / SVG / persona.json); only regular files inside the package directory (no following symlinks, no dotfiles); extension avatars only serve files named in the manifest, and SVGs are sanitized (with CSP); when `?rev=` is the current rev, `Cache-Control: immutable` is set |
| GET | `/api/v1/looks` | All avatars (#3200, `docs/extensions/extensions.md` ("Avatars")): `{"looks":[{"id","source":"builtin\|hub\|extension","name","names?","subtitle?","subtitles?","app_icon","extension?","extension_name?","rev?","bytes?","manifest?","uploaded?"}],"current":{"id":the chosen one or null,"effective":the one to show,"updated_at?"}}`; built-in avatars first, then avatar packages and extension avatars (`/api/v1/personas` lists them too); a database read failure returns 500 `internal` without reporting a default choice |
| PUT | `/api/v1/looks/current` | `{"id", "if_unset?"}` choose an avatar (stored on the hub, synced across clients), returns the new `current`; not in the list 404; with `if_unset`, if the hub already has a choice it's returned unchanged (clients use this to migrate their old local choice up). A change broadcasts `look`; with `if_unset`, a database read failure returns 500 `internal` without saving or broadcasting a choice |
| POST | `/api/v1/looks/uploads` | `{"name", "subtitle?", "image", "choose?"}` makes an avatar from an image (#2404, `docs/apple/persona.md` "Uploading an image"): `image` is base64 (or a `data:` URL) of a PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF, at most 8 MB and 40 million pixels, at least 64 px a side; the apps send it cropped square and upright, and the hub crops a non-square one to its centered square. The hub writes a format-1 package `personas/u-<hex>/` (avatar at 64 / 128 / 256 / 512 px, a still dot frame per state, `source.kind: "upload"`) and returns `{"look": <as GET /looks lists it, "uploaded": true>, "current?"}`; with `choose` it is chosen too (`current`, broadcast `look`). Broadcasts `personas`. Refusals carry `code`: 400 `no_name` / `bad_name` (1–40 characters, no control or bidi formatting characters) / `bad_subtitle` (≤ 80) / `no_image` / `not_image` / `too_small`, 413 `too_large` / `too_many_pixels`, 409 `too_many` (50 uploaded avatars). Full credentials only |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/looks/uploads/{id}` | Deletes an avatar made from an upload and returns `{"current"}`; when it was the chosen one, the default is chosen (broadcast `look`). Broadcasts `personas`. 404 `not_found`; 409 `not_uploaded` for any other package (placed by hand, built in, an extension's). Full credentials only |
| GET | `/api/v1/plugins` | The hub's plugins: `{"plugins":[{"id","name","kind","status","error"?, "version", "source", "enabled", "contributes", "needs_setup"?, "nodes"?, "node_status"? …}], "can_install"}`; `status` is `disabled / needs_setup / incompatible / stopped / starting / running / error` — for an extension whose program runs on computers, while the hub runs no process of its own, `status` is aggregated from its machines and `node_status` carries the counts (see `docs/extensions/extensions.md` ("Programs running on computers")); only present when `features` has `plugins` |
| GET / PUT / DELETE | `/api/v1/plugins/{id}/-/…`, `/api/v1/plugins/-/…` | Plugin details, switch, config and secrets (full-access devices), preview / install / upgrade / rollback / uninstall (main token over loopback only); only present when `features` has `plugin_manager`, see `docs/extensions/extensions.md` ("The hub's API") |
| GET | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/ports/{port}` | Port probe (`docs/operations/ports.md`): `{"port","listening","http","title"?}`, only looks, doesn't allow |
| POST | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/ports/{port}/open` | The user taps a port in the App that doesn't belong to any Agent: if something is listening it's allowed for 24 hours and returns the same as above; nothing there 404; read-only device 403 |
| GET | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/ports/{port}/connect` | Port forwarding: upgrades to a WebSocket whose binary messages are the bytes of one TCP connection (the phone listens locally and connects once for each connection the browser opens). The port must be in `ports` of some session on this machine or have been opened, otherwise 403; not listening 404; read-only device 403; machine offline 503; more than 64 concurrent per machine 429. For the live screen (5900 with `pair`) a phone may offer the subprotocol `persona-screen-link.1`, and `attach=1` to rejoin a live session; the hub selects it only when the node answers with a screen session, and a session to rejoin that is gone is 410 ([computer-use.md](../extensions/computer-use.md) "Live screen routes (#6398)") |
| GET | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/preview/servers?cwd=` | Dev servers of a session's folder (feature `preview`, [preview](../web/preview.md)): `{file?, servers: [{name, port?, url?, command?, env?, cwd?, listening, title?, problem?}], error?, browser?}` from its `.claude/launch.json`; a node without previews 409 `node_outdated` |
| POST | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/preview/start` | `{cwd, name, workspace, kind?}`: runs that `launch.json` entry in a new terminal tab of the workspace → `{pane, terminal, port}`; read-only device 403. A runtime's workspace (a Paseo session's `workspace_id`, which has no terminal) runs it in the terminal engine's workspace holding the entry's folder, else in a new workspace there; a computer whose engines open no tabs answers 409 `preview_no_terminal` |
| GET | `/api/v1/machines/{mid}/preview/connect?port=&path=&w=&h=&dpr=&mobile=1` | A dev server preview: upgrades to a WebSocket of JSON text messages and binary pictures ([preview](../web/preview.md) "Messages"). Same port rules as `…/ports/{port}/connect` (403, 503, 429) and 409 `node_outdated`, before the upgrade; when the node cannot open it, after the upgrade one message `{t: "error", code, error}` and the close (`port_gone`, `no_browser`: no Chrome / Chromium / Edge / Brave on that computer, `browser_failed`, `offline`, `failed`), since a browser cannot read why a WebSocket was refused |
| GET | `/api/v1/agents/sessions/{id}/messages?cursor=&limit=` | Messages of one personal-Agent session (`id` is `<source>:<sessionKey>`, percent-encoded in the path) → `{session?, messages, hasMore, nextCursor?}`; to page back, pass the previous `nextCursor` (see "Personal Agent source state" below) |
| POST | `/api/v1/agents/sessions/{id}/messages` | Send a message `{"clientId"?,"text","origin"?}` → `{outbox, duplicate, upstream?}`; if `clientId` isn't given the hub generates one, and resending the same one won't send twice (`duplicate: true`); `origin` defaults to `app`; empty text or a `clientId` that isn't a UUID 400, over 20000 (counted in UTF-16) 413; `clientId` already used on another session, or the session can't send right now (`canSend=false`) 409 |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/agents/sessions/{id}/messages/{clientId}` | Delete one outbox entry (by `clientId`) → `{"ok":true}` |
| POST | `/api/v1/agents/sessions/{id}/read` | Mark this session as read → `{"ok":true}` |
| GET | `/api/v1/agents/sessions/{id}/avatar` | The session's avatar image as is, with `ETag`; a matching `If-None-Match` returns 304; cached for a day |
| GET | `/api/v1/agents/outbox?session_id=&limit=` | The personal Agents' outbox `{"outbox":[{clientId, sessionId, preview, length, origin?, status, error?, attempts, createdAt, updatedAt}]}`; `status` is `sending` / `sent` / `failed` / `deleted` (resending a `failed` one with the same `clientId` is safe) |
| POST | `/api/v1/channels/{id}/test` | Send a test message to the owner bound to the channel → `{"ok":true}`; couldn't send 502; no such channel 404 `not_found`, read-only ones or ones from a market not installed yet 409 `read_only`, read-only device 403 ([channels.md](../extensions/channels.md) "6. Endpoints") |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/channels/{id}/binding` | Unbind: for a plugin channel the connector signs out, for the Lark bot it unpairs; returns the channel details after unbinding; unbind failed 502, other errors as in the row above |
| POST | `/api/v1/phone/runtime-cli` | `{cmd, args, timeout}`: have the DEBUG build on the phone run one Runtime CLI command (`docs/operations/runtime-cli.md` ("Connecting to a real device via the hub")), returns the App's response as is `{"ok": …}`. Full device credentials only (read-only device 403); no App online that registered `phone_runtime_cli` 503 `phone_offline` (doesn't wake it); no answer within `timeout` seconds (at most 120) 504; the App says the call failed 502. The hub logs one line per call (command, caller device id, status, duration), without arguments or responses |
| Any | `/api/v1/plugins/{id}/-/machines/{mid}/{path…}` | HTTP to the plugin's program on computer `mid` (`node.http`, `docs/extensions/extensions.md` ("Programs that run on computers")), WebSocket too: the hub opens a stream via `plugin.node.dial` and forwards, stripping `Authorization` and `token`; full-access devices only; plugin not enabled on this machine 404, machine offline 409, program not responding 502 |
| Any | `/api/v1/plugins/{id}/{path…}` | Forwarded as is to the plugin's `/{path…}` (except paths starting with `/-/`) (WebSocket too), stripping `Authorization` and `token`; read-only device 403. The voice plugin's contract is in `docs/extensions/extensions.md` ("Voice") |

**Limits on reading files by path** (`file`, `file/download`, `file/thumb`, `file/convert`, `stat`, `fs`; the node's `pathguard.go`): only for authenticated clients (device tokens). Symlinks are resolved one segment at a time and **each segment is checked before it is looked at**, so anything reached through a link is blocked too, and the target is never touched:
- **iCloud** (any segment containing `Library/Mobile Documents`, case-insensitive): touching it on a locked Mac hangs, so `stat` treats it as nonexistent and reads are refused.
- **Sensitive files**: the whole directories `.ssh`, `.gnupg`, `.aws`, `.azure`, `.kube`, `.docker`, `.password-store`, `Library/Keychains`, `.local/share/keyrings`, `.config/gcloud`, `.config/gh` under home,
  `.netrc`, `.git-credentials`, `.npmrc`, `.pypirc`, `.pgpass`, `.credentials.json`, `settings.json` and `settings.local.json` in every Claude Code config directory the node knows (`~/.claude`, `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, those seen in running claudes or listed by the hub), `auth.json` in every Codex home it knows (`~/.codex`, `$CODEX_HOME` of the configured and discovered homes), private keys named `id_rsa` / `id_ed25519` etc. anywhere, and the data folder's credentials where they are written, in any `.persona` / `.persona` folder and in the folder `PERSONA_HOME` names: directly in it or in a manager's folder (`managers/<id>/`), the files whose names start with `hub.json` (including backups `hub.json.*`), `link.json`, `tailcat.json`, `tailcat-hub.json`, `daemons.json`, `manager.json`, `apns`, `relay.json`, `relay.secret`, `devices.json`, `mail_accounts.json`, and the `.key` / `.p8` / `.pem` / `.crt` files; and `launcher-settings/`, `tls/`, `link-tls/`, `extensions/data/` (the extensions' own data, their sign-ins and tokens among it), `extensions/staging/` (what an uninstall or an upgrade sets aside of it), `plugins/` (the extensions' folder of a hub from before #1844, or the link to `extensions/` it left: paths through it are refused, use `extensions/`) and `node-plugins/` (the programs extensions run on a computer and their data), whole, the folders themselves included; a link standing where one of these, or a folder on the way to one, is named is not followed. The rest of the folder (the knowledge base `data/`, a `.pem` deeper in it) stays readable, and so does a project's file of the same name elsewhere (with `PERSONA_HOME=~`, a project's `link.json` or `certs/dev.pem`). `stat` treats them as nonexistent; reading, listing and downloading are all refused.
- The Git panel reads the same files' content: `git/diff` and `git/blob` refuse these paths; `git/review` lists them with `refused` and without their hunks or line counts (both sides of a rename that has one); `git/show` still lists every file of the commit but leaves the refused ones (both sides of a rename or copy that has one) out of `diff` (with no working tree to check the names against, a bare repository or a `cwd` inside `.git`, `diff` is empty).
- **A manager's folder anywhere** (`personad manager join/run --dir`, #5877): a folder holding a manager's `manager.json` (one naming its hub and token, or one that doesn't read but may hold a token) has the same credentials refused as a data folder's (`manager.json` and its copies, `secret.key` and the other keys, the same folders), also when they are not in the working tree any more. The folder is only looked at for such names, once the links up to it are followed; a link named `manager.json`, or a placeholder of one that is not downloaded, counts as a manager's without being opened.
- Links are followed at most 40 levels deep (a loop stops it). This is basic protection, not a sandbox: a device token can already have an Agent read these files.

For mail, see "Mail API" below. For the HTTP error format and optional fields, see "Error body" above.

### Computer trust (feature `machine_trust`, #3347)

From the onboarding plan (#287) 4.2 and 5.3: a signed-in device can add a computer itself (feature `machines_add`); an added computer starts out **pending** (`trust: "pending"`) and is confirmed only when the user taps **It's mine**.
Trust is stored in the Postgres table `machine_trust`, and **no record = confirmed**: machines from before the upgrade, ones added via `/admin`, and ones added via `hub pair --machine` are all confirmed directly, with unchanged behavior. A pending computer:

- Doesn't receive Persona-managed providers (the assistant's `pushManaged` and `launchers.catalog` / `launchers.managed` on new connections all skip it, and `launchers.pull` is refused); all its requests to the manager (`assistant.context`, MCP tools) are refused;
- Isn't an assistant machine (`defaultAssistantMachine` and hello's `assistant.machines` exclude it), isn't in the assistant's `devices.list` (dispatch, starting Agents and to-dos don't see it), and the hub doesn't forward the assistant's `device.call` to it;
