- `POST /api/v1/sessions` starting an Agent on it returns 409 `machine_pending` (old Apps still list it in the new-Agent list);
- Is still listed in the machine list (the App needs to show the confirmation), with `error` set to "Waiting for you to confirm this computer is yours in the latest app or on the web", followed by the original `error` in parentheses;
- Is deleted automatically if not confirmed within 24 hours (the hub.json entry and the record; its Persona Link credential and unused pairing codes are revoked), the same as `reject`.

After rejection or timeout deletion the record is gone (so it looks confirmed), but until the manager disconnects it (config changes take a moment), the hub still keeps it out as pending, and the machine list no longer lists it, so hello won't treat it as a just-confirmed computer and push keys to it.
When the hub can't read pending computers (database unreachable), every computer is kept out as pending (the machine list doesn't mark `trust`), re-read every 5 seconds until it succeeds; no timeout deletion happens during that time. When the manager can't read them, requests from computers are refused with the error "the hub's database isn't responding", without saying the computer is waiting for confirmation.
`error` for `confirm` / `reject` is localized by `Accept-Language` (403 `forbidden`, 404 `not_found`, 409 `not_pending`).

Once confirmed, hello's machine list includes it, and the assistant then pushes keys to it. Issuing a code, redeeming, confirming, rejecting, timeout deletion and deleting it in the admin console (`remove`) are all written to the `machine_audit` table (who, when, what was done, no credentials).
How a device adds a pending computer: see "Computer pairing codes" under "Temporary pairing" above.

### Renaming a computer (feature `machine_rename`)

`PUT /api/v1/machines/{id}/name` `{"name"}` → `{"ok": true, "name"}`: a signed-in full device (as for `confirm`) gives the computer another name; `""` is its id again. The admin page does the same with
`PUT /api/v1/admin/machines/{id}` `{"name"}`, and the computer's own Persona Link with `rename` on its link ([link.md](../operations/link.md) "The computer's name"). Only the name changes: the id, and everything kept by it
(pins, mutes, trust, credentials), stays.

- The hub writes `name` into the hub.json entry (or, for a computer its manager keeps in its own list, into that list through
  `devices.machines.put`) and takes it at once: no restart (the admin page's restart list doesn't count it), no reconnect (the manager keeps the machine and its connection when only the name
  changed). Every client gets a `machines` event with the new name; the computer's Persona Link gets `endpoints` with `machine_name`; the hub's own texts (notifications, errors, the assistant's `devices.list`) use it.
- Names are one line, at most 40 characters: 400 `invalid_name` otherwise; 404 `not_found` for an id hub.json doesn't have (a linked hub's computer is renamed on its own hub, and the center follows its record);
  403 `forbidden` for a device that isn't a full one. `error` is localized by `Accept-Language`.
- The manager's `devices.rename` `{machine_id, name}` → `{name}` carries a Persona Link's request: only for a machine of its own, refused with code `pending` while the user hasn't confirmed the computer.
- Each rename is written to `machine_audit` (action `rename`, detail `{from, to, via}`; `via`: `admin` / `device` / `link` / `system`).
- A computer that pairs while its name is still its id is named once after its system (`system_name` in the pairing request, `POST /api/v1/auth/tokens`, via `system`).
- Clients show a rename entry only when hello's `features` has `machine_rename`.

### Dispatch policy

The assistant can run under an optional dispatch policy: an organization rule for which conversations may hand out
work, so a conversation that is meant to only read and report cannot open tasks or push work into the main or a
leader conversation. With no policy stored, or one past its expiry, every conversation behaves exactly as without
the feature.

A policy is one setting on the assistant (`dispatch_policy` in `GET`/`PUT /api/v1/assistant`, full credentials) and
also has its own route, `GET`/`PUT /api/v1/assistant/dispatch-policy`, open to full credentials and to an extension
token granted the `assistant.dispatch_policy` hub scope. Its shape:

```json
{
  "rules": [
    {
      "conversation_class": "scheduled",
      "deny": ["task_plan", "agent_start", "start_conversation", "send_to_main", "send_to_leader"],
      "message": "where the model should leave findings instead"
    }
  ],
  "expires_at": "RFC 3339, optional"
}
```

- `conversation_class` is one of `main`, `leader`, `background_supervisor`, `scheduled` (a scheduled task's own
  conversation) or `other`. Classes are resolved most specific first, so a conversation a scheduled task runs in
  that is later made the main or a leader conversation keeps that higher class.
- `deny` names what the class may not do: hand out work (`task_plan`, `agent_start`), start another conversation
  (`start_conversation`, so the limit cannot be bypassed by opening one), or relay work with `conversation_send` to
  the main conversation (`send_to_main`) or a leader conversation (`send_to_leader`). A send to any other
  conversation is not limited.
  A limited conversation also cannot cancel or delete its own scheduled task (`cancel_followup`,
  `delete_routine`): removing the task would take away the conversation's own class mid-turn.
- `message` is an optional short note (at most 300 runes) appended to the localized refusal that starts with
  "The current organization policy requires…".
- `expires_at` is optional for a full-credential write, which may also set one further than an hour ahead. An
  extension write must set it to no more than one hour ahead; an expired policy is treated as absent, so a stopped or
  uninstalled extension leaves nothing in force. Empty `rules` clears the policy.
- The owner's own words are never blocked: when a limited conversation relays something to the **main**
  conversation, the send is allowed if the current turn started with the owner's own message (a user text item with
  a client message id and no source marking it as a scheduled run, a supervision message, a relay or a system
  notice), or if the sent text starts with one of the owner's messages verbatim. If the conversation's transcript
  cannot be read, the send stays refused.

The checks run on the model's tool-call entry only: the hub's own internal starts are not affected, and the main
conversation, leader conversations and the background supervisor keep working unless a rule explicitly names their
class.

## WebSocket `/api/v1/ws`

Envelope `{"type":"…", ...}`.

Server → client:

| type | Fields |
| --- | --- |
| `hub_restarting` | `back_in_ms`: the hub is about to restart (deploy, `systemctl restart`, update), followed by 1001 "hub restarting". The client reconnects immediately and keeps the UI as is ([hub-restart.md](../operations/hub-restart.md)). No `event_seq`, not replayed |
| `hub_update` | `update` (same as `GET /api/v1/hub/update`): checking, downloading, waiting for idle, restarting, confirming, rolling back; pushed whenever the state changes; after `restarting` the connection drops for a while, which is expected |
| `hello` | `server_version`, `client_id`, `features`, `hub_id`, `hub_name`, `endpoints`, `tls_port`, `fp`, `mesh`, `channel`, `build`, `protocol`, `min_app_build` (the last four same as `/api/v1/health`), `event_stream`, `event_seq`, `resumed` (see "Event resume" below), `locale` (the user's language, feature `locale`); the first message on every WS, not yet including the negotiated heartbeat. `mesh`: `{"hubs":[{hub_id,name,online,self,center,endpoints,tls_port,fp}]}`, every hub in the linked-hub group (including itself, `self: true`; paired but currently unreachable ones `online: false`; `center: true` is the group's primary hub, which clients prefer among those in the same group); without linking, only itself. When connected to a member, hello comes from the primary (`hub_id` is the primary's) ([mesh.md](../server/mesh.md)) |
| `endpoints` | `endpoints` (the full candidate list, only sent to connections that declared the capability of the same name) |
| `client_hello_ack` | `heartbeat: {interval, pong_timeout}` (the seconds actually used after this negotiation) |
| `machines` | `machines` (also after a rename: the whole list, with the new `name`) |
| `file_transfer` | `transfer` (`FileTransfer`): a computer-to-computer transfer started, progressed (at most once a second) or ended; `manager` identifies a non-default manager. Only full devices that declared `file_transfer` receive it; not in the event log, so clients `GET` the current transfers after reconnecting ([file-transfer.md](file-transfer.md)) |
| `managers` | No payload: the manager roster changed (created, renamed, connected, disconnected, deleted, new reported bot identities); clients re-read `GET /api/v1/managers` ("Bus" below, [managers.md](../assistant/managers.md) "Clients"). Only sent to connections that asked for feature `managers` (`?features=` or `client_hello.features`), not in the event log |
| `saved_agent_searches` | `revision` (decimal string): the default manager committed a saved-query mutation; re-read the collection while its view is open, respecting the message's manager stamp. No query/name payload; see "Saved Agent searches" |
| `workspace_board` | `revision`: a board change was saved; the client re-reads the full state; doesn't indicate an Agent state change |
| `workspace_board_settings` | `enabled`: the board switch changed (`PUT /api/v1/workspace-board/settings`); clients show or hide the entry accordingly |
| `kb_selection` | —: the knowledge base's selection was saved (`PUT /api/v1/kb/selection`, or a per-item change from the assistant); clients re-read `GET /api/v1/kb/selection` |
| `todos` | —: pushed whenever to-dos or links change; clients re-fetch `GET /api/v1/todos` |
| `extension_operation` | `operation` (`ExtensionOperation`): an extension install, upgrade or uninstall moved to the next step, or the download progressed (at most one per second); only sent to connections that declared `extension_operations`, not in the event log; see "Extension install, upgrade and uninstall progress" above |
| `extension_auth` | `extension`, `auth` (`ExtensionAuth`): an extension's sign-in state changed (sign-in finished, signed out, expired, the extension sent `auth.changed`), see [extensions.md](../extensions/extensions.md) "Sign-in (auth)" |
| `extension_upgrade` / `plugin_upgrade` | `extension` / `plugin`, `note` (`ExtensionUpgradeNote`: `kind` `upgraded` / `rolled_back` / `needs_permission` / `failed`, `from`, `to`, `detail?`, `at`, the same as `ExtensionView.upgrade_note`): an automatic upgrade of a market extension went in, was rolled back, waits for the user to confirm more permissions, or failed. Both are sent, the old `plugin_upgrade` first ([extensions.md](../extensions/extensions.md) "Auto-upgrade", "Naming and compatibility") |
| `subscription` | `id`, `connector`, `revision`, `state`, `removed`: a source subscription was saved, ran or was deleted; clients showing it re-read `GET /api/v1/subscriptions/{id}` or the list ([subscriptions.md](../extensions/subscriptions.md) "API") |
| `extension_ui` | `extension`, then either `id`, `badge` (a badge change, as `plugin_ui`, which is sent first with `plugin` for old apps) or `id?`, `invalidate: true` (the extension's `ui.invalidate`, gathered for one second; no `id` means all its UIs; only this name is sent): clients redraw the pages they show ([extensions.md](../extensions/extensions.md) "`ui.invalidate`", "Naming and compatibility") |
| `plugin_ui` | `plugin`, `id`, `badge` (`{text, tone}`, `null` clears it): a plugin changed the badge on its main navigation entry (`nav_page`), [extensions.md](../extensions/extensions.md) "UI slots" |
| `extension_ui_stream` | `kind` (`snapshot` / `delta` / `receipt` / `error` / `closed` / `suspended`), the payload under the name of its kind (`session` for `closed` / `suspended`), `request_id?`, `manager` (set by the hub: the manager that sent it): a frame of a native extension page stream, sent only to the one connection that opened it (feature `extension_ui_stream_v1` and `context.stream`); never broadcast, not in the event log. The hub itself only sends `kind: error` with `error.code` `manager_unavailable` when the manager does not answer the request; every other frame is the manager's ([extensions.md](../extensions/extensions.md) "Source runtime (#5956)", [schema/extension/README.md](../../schema/extension/README.md) "Canonical main-app WebSocket envelopes") |
| `assistant_feed` | `conversation`, `item` (`FeedItem`): a new entry in the chat feed; kind `view` is a live card's original position, and body.view is the AssistantView |
| `assistant_view` | `conversation`, `view` (the schema's AssistantView: id, conversation, version, view, created_at, updated_at): an update to a live card already stored in the database; at most once per second per card, old updates ignored by version; no separate notification |
| `assistant_view_block` | `conversation`, `key`: a body card has been validated from a trusted assistant text item and stored in the database, so its single reply can be enabled; replaying the same source doesn't broadcast again; goes into the existing event resume, and if missed is filled in by the feed.view_blocks snapshot |
| `assistant_view_action` | `conversation`, `action` (ViewAction: key, action, page?, values, client_msg_id, status, revision, error?, at, updated_at, kind?, version?, text?): card submission and send status; `kind` absent or `action` means a declarative action, `html` is an HTML bridge reply (`action` is the component key, `text` is the confirmed text); `version` is the card version the user saw when submitting (older records don't have it); old states ignored by revision; goes into the existing event resume |
| `task_plan` | `plan` (`TaskPlan`): a plan handed to the user, started, dismissed, or one of its tasks failed to start (`tasks[i].error`) |
| `directions` | No payload: the direction tree changed (a to-do, an Agent's session, a direction or its name; gathered for one second, sent only when the tree's content differs); clients re-read `GET /api/v1/assistant/directions/tree`, and also on (re)connect |
| `direction_offer` | `conversation`, `offer` (`{machine_id, title, project?, new_project?, closest?, at}`, or null once it was answered): a New chat was offered as a direction, or its offer went (`docs/assistant/unified-entry.md` "New chat opens a direction") |
| `assistant_schedule` | No payload: the assistant's scheduled tasks changed; clients re-read `GET /api/v1/assistant/tasks`. From another manager it carries `manager`, and only the shown manager's counts ("Messages to the App" below, [managers.md](../assistant/managers.md) "Clients") |
| `assistant_saved_prompts` | No payload: the user's saved prompts changed (#7329); clients re-read `GET /api/v1/assistant/saved-prompts`. From another manager it carries `manager`, and only the shown manager's counts, as `assistant_schedule` |
| `agents.triage` | `triage` (the switches as `GET /api/v1/agents/triage` returns them: `enabled`, `auto_continue`, `wake`, `decide`, `tool_loop`, `closeout`, `closeout_ask`, `reply_reminder?`, `reply_reminder_minutes?`, `transient_retry?`): the session triage switches were saved, and what they turned off has stopped ([agent-work.md](../assistant/agent-work.md) "Switches") |
| `launcher_health` | `record` (one record as `GET /api/v1/launchers/health` lists it: `machine`, `launcher`, `state`, `kind`, `error`, `checked_at`, `source`, `fails`, `repair?`, `blocked_reason?`, `resets_at?`): a launcher's health state changed; only to connected clients, not a push ([launcher-health.md](../server/launcher-health.md) "API for the board") |
| `meeting_live` | `recording_id`, `changed` (an open set: `room`, `asks`, `private`, `followup`, from phase 2 `lines` and `topics`, from phase 2b `highlights`, from phase 3 `photos`; later phases add more) and `revs` (each changed part's revision, numbers only; for `lines` the live log's length): a meeting's parts changed, at most one a second per recording, content-free; clients read only the newer parts with `GET /api/v1/recordings/{id}/live?parts=…` ([meeting-minutes.md](../assistant/meeting-minutes.md) "The `meeting_live` event", #3862) |
| `model_profile` | `active` (the id of the profile now in use, empty when none is): a model profile was applied, rolled back, saved or deleted; clients re-read `GET /api/v1/model-profiles` ([model-profiles.md](../assistant/model-profiles.md)) |
| `sessions` | `machine_id`, `sessions` (the full set for that machine, pushed on change, not pushed if identical to the last one; each session carries `rev` = transcript byte count, and a change means new content; optional `suggestion`: the gray "next message" suggestion Claude puts in the input box after a turn, see `docs/integrations/claude-integration.md`, or the one the manager's `suggest.next` model made for any other chat (`docs/assistant/assistant.md` "Next-message suggestions"); optional `suggestion_risky`: the suggestion names a command, a path, a link, a secret-looking string or a risky action, so clients fill it in but offer no one-tap send; optional `attention_reason`: when the session is in "Needs you", the reason the host gave (botmux's attention reason); optional `external_url`: where to open it outside Persona (the Lark thread of a botmux session), see `docs/integrations/engines.md` ("botmux")) |
| `revs` | `machine_id`, `revs` (`{session_id: rev}`, changed ones only; sent when the fields visible in the list haven't changed but the transcript grew, pushed to all clients, and the App fetches the increment in the background; an open web chat takes it as its session's rev moving, "The page's own fallback") |
| `sessions_delta` | `machine_id`, `upsert` (`[Session…]`, new or changed sessions, whole objects), `remove` (`[session_id…]`): only to connections that asked for `sessions_delta`, after one full `sessions` snapshot per machine on connect; not in the event log; see "Session deltas" below |
| `sessions_list` | `revision` (an opaque checkpoint): only to connections that asked for `sessions_list`, which get no `sessions` or `sessions_delta`; sent once on connect and again when the indexed session list changes. A hint to read the HTTP `since` page from the saved checkpoint, not a baseline itself; not in the event log; see "Bounded Agents lists" ("Lightweight WebSocket negotiation") below |
| `lark` | `feed_ids` (chats with new Lark messages / changes); `settings_changed` (optional boolean, default false; this batch includes a change to message display settings, independent of the chat IDs; the client also re-reads settings); `account` (the Lark gateway account number these chats belong to); `ol_account` (only present when not the default account, equal to `account`: the parameter needed to read these chats, `docs/extensions/feishu.md` ("Multiple accounts")). The hub follows the live events `/agent/v1/events` of every signed-in account on the Lark gateway, sends at most once every 400 ms per account, and pushes to all clients. |
| `messaging` | `source` (message source id), `conversations` (ids of changed chats), `account` (optional, which account), `settings_changed` (optional): an extension's `messaging.changed`, coalesced for one second, then pushed to all clients (`docs/extensions/extension-messaging.md` ("9")) |
| `agents` | `session_ids` (personal Agent session ids, `<source>:<sessionKey>`, whose content changed; `[]` means the list itself changed): an extension's source reported changes (`agentsrc.updated`), a send went out, a source was removed, or a conversation was removed from or restored to the list; clients re-fetch `GET /api/v1/agents/sessions` (a bounded reader from that collection's own `since` checkpoint) ([extensions.md](../extensions/extensions.md) "Personal Agent sources", "Removing a personal Agent from the list" below) |
| `agents.prefs` | No payload: the personal Agent list preferences changed (`PUT /api/v1/agents/prefs`, a conversation hidden or unhidden); clients re-read `GET /api/v1/agents/prefs` ("Personal Agent list preferences" below) |
| `items` | `machine_id`, `session_id`, `items`, plus this batch's position in the transcript (see "Continuity of items" below): `history`, `to_seq`, `from_seq` (only on continuation batches). Only pushed to clients subscribed to that session; lines with no item (ai-title and the like) also get an empty `items`, so the App knows those lines have been seen |
| `message_send_state` | `machine_id`, `session_id`, `client_msg_id`, `state` (`processing` / `delivered` / `failed` / `unknown`), `at` (UTC RFC3339Nano): a transport receipt for `/sessions/{mid}/{sid}/messages`, only to that session's subscribers. Processing precedes manager preparation and node delivery; it is not a durable queue or execution state. Final HTTP remains authoritative. Not in the event log; reconnect/retry the original operation ID to reconcile. Trust only when the current authenticated `hello` has top-level `message_send_state: 1`, fixed by the hub, not the extension-merged feature array. No client feature negotiation; older clients ignore the unknown type. See "Message feedback (#5258)" below. |
| `delta` | `machine_id`, `session_id`, `text` (the whole text the headless assistant is generating; an empty string means the turn is over. A Claude session Persona started sends it too: the message Claude is showing in its terminal, as far as the transcript does not have it yet, "" once it does; whole lines every 0.1–1 s; see `docs/integrations/claude-integration.md` "Live replies (MessageDisplay)". The live text is never the source: the transcript's items replace it). At most one every 80 ms, and what came after the last one goes out 80 ms after it, so the end of a burst of model output never waits for the next burst (#6651). The App draws each chat at most 5 times a second, the first one after a pause immediately and then the latest; an empty string is drawn immediately; anything not yet drawn is dropped when the message lands in the transcript or on reconnect (`DeltaPacer`). The streaming view reveals what was drawn a few characters a frame (`StreamReveal`); the web staggers new words at the stream's pace (`web/src/ui/stream/wordFade.ts`) |
| `live` | `machine_id`, `session_id`, `live` (`SessionLive` or `null`): the status line of a working Claude, only sent to connections subscribed to that session that declared `session_live`; see "Live status" below |
| `screen` | `machine_id`, `session_id`, `text`, `status`, `ts` (the node no longer samples the screen per subscription: the terminal page reads `/screen` itself on demand, and old Apps not receiving this doesn't matter) |
| `fs_changed` | #2439: `machine_id`, `cwd`, `dirs` (folders in this page's `fs_watch` that changed), `git` (the Git status of `cwd` changed). Only sent to pages that did `fs_watch`; not in the event log and not replayed on reconnect (the page refreshes itself once after reconnecting) |
| `terminal_control` | `machine_id`, `session_id`, `state`: `active` (took control, with `cols`, `rows`), `busy` (another program on the computer holds it; ask the user whether to `takeover`; mirror in the meantime), `taken` (grabbed by another device or program), `lost` (the node let go itself), `unsupported` (old node / herdr, mirror only); `error` is a human-readable reason |
| `terminal` | `machine_id`, `session_id`, plus a frame `epoch`, `seq`, `full`, `cols`, `rows`, `data` (base64 VT bytes), or `error` (the stream stopped: computer offline, session not running…) + `unsupported` (old node / herdr can't stream; poll `/screen` instead). See "Terminal stream" below |
| `herdr_state` / `herdr_data` / `herdr_end` | `id` plus `state: "open"`, `cols`, `rows` / `data` (base64, ≤ 32 KB each) / `error?`, `code?` (`forbidden` `too_many` `bad_request` `offline`), `unsupported?`: a view of the full herdr interface (the response to `herdr_open`). The hub ends the view when un-acked bytes exceed 1 MiB |
| `herdr_focus` | `id` (the view), `machine_id`, `workspace_id`, `tab_id`, `pane_id`, `session_id?` (the Agent session in that pane), `source` (`client`: some full client on this computer was just typed into / `persona`: requested by a `herdr_focus` / `other`: anything else), `mine` (done by this view itself): herdr's focus changed, pushed to every view on this computer. The web only follows ones that are `mine` and `client`; `persona` + `mine` is an echo; the rest only show a hint. Feature `herdr_focus`. `docs/integrations/terminal.md` section 28 |
| `interaction` | `interaction` (a new pending one, pushed to all clients). When a question is first answered by the assistant on the user's behalf (#3029), the same card comes twice: first with `delegating: true` (the assistant is looking; not pushed yet), then again when the assistant hands it to the user, without `delegating` and possibly with `delegate` (`what` / `why_now` / `recommend` / `cost` / `reason` / `deadline`, the context the assistant filled in); a question a supervisor passed up may carry `suggestion` (`RuleSuggestion`, "Tasks and the chat feed", #4929), and the card comes again without it once the suggestion was answered with Always or Not now; overwrite by `id` |
| `interaction_resolved` | `id`; when the assistant answered on the user's behalf, also `answered_by: "assistant"` (#1602), plus `reason` (why it answered that way) and `answers` (what it answered; re-answering starts from here, #3029) |
| `interaction_reanswered` | `id`, `resolution` (`{answers}`): the user changed the assistant's answer, and the new answer has been sent to that Agent (#3029) |
| `fleet` | `fleet` (the Live Activity summary, matching the content of HTTP `/api/v1/fleet`) |
| `hook_event` | The node hook event's original fields; the hub adds `machine_id` and sets `type: hook_event`; used to refresh session run state; `Stop` carries `stop_sig` (a reply signature the hub uses to dedupe "done" pushes, see `agent-states.md` ("Hook turn signals")); global report-only hooks (`../integrations/claude-integration.md` ("Global report-only hooks")) carry `report_only: true`, so the hub doesn't take them to mean the session has Persona's hooks; `UserPromptSubmit` carries `prompt_source`, who the prompt is from (its message source's kind, such as `meeting` or `conversation`; `notification` for a background task's report; else `user`), never the prompt itself; otherwise as before |
| `tool_call` | `call_id`, `name`, `args` (only sent to phones that did `register_phone` and provide that tool) |
| `desktops` | `desktops`: connected desktop clients (the Mac App), `[{"device","name","since"}]`; `device` is its device credential id (empty for those connected with a pairing credential, which can't be signed out individually). Sent once on connect, then pushed to all clients whenever a desktop client connects / disconnects (feature `desktops`). The iPhone uses it to show "Persona is signed in on a Mac"; it declares `desktops_link` for Persona Link entries ([ios.md](../apple/ios.md) "Mac signed in"). A client that lists `desktops_link` (feature `desktops_link`) also gets the active Persona Link desktops, `{"kind":"link","machine_id","device":"","name","since"}`: `machine_id` the computer, `name` what the hub calls it, `since` when this run of presence began (RFC 3339); entries without `kind` are the desktop App. Such a client gets the list again when one starts, ends or lapses, and once more when its `client_hello` adds `desktops_link`; a client that doesn't list it gets the list as before |
| `notify` | `kind: interaction / done / assistant / alert`, `machine_id`, `session_id`, `title`, `subtitle`, `body`; a decision's push (an `assistant` notify) also carries `todo: {id, asked_at, recommend, manager}` ([todos.md](../assistant/todos.md) "Waiting for the owner"), a meeting's minutes push `recording_id` (the push payload too; "Recording sync"); interactions also carry `interaction_id`, alerts the caller's `id` when it gave one, an extension's as `ext:` and a hash (`POST /api/v1/notify`; Android replaces the earlier alert with the same `id`, #5614); a manager push may also carry `level` (`P0`/`P1`/`P2`) and `related_key` for the hub's low-distraction filter (the WebSocket event is never filtered even when the APNs alert is held back); `quiet: true` when the device is inside its quiet hours (post it without sound); only sent to connections that declared `ws_notify`; one selected while a device without push was offline comes after its next `client_hello`, see below |
| `lock_test` | `lock_test_id`, `lock_test_due_at`, `lock_test_sent_at`, `lock_test_title`, `lock_test_body`; only sent to the selected connection on this device that declared `lock_test`, see "Lock screen test" |
| `inbox` | No payload; a list-change hint, the client re-fetches the Inbox |
| `mail_accounts` | No payload: the assistant added or removed a mail account (`persona_settings`, confirmed on the phone); clients re-read `GET /api/v1/mail/accounts` ("Mail API" below). The HTTP account endpoints don't send it |
| `look` | `{"id","effective"}`: the selected avatar changed (chosen on another device, or back to the default after an extension was uninstalled); every client switches to `effective` (#3200) |
| `personas` | No payload; the avatar list changed (a tiered avatar changed tier, an extension with avatars was installed / uninstalled / disabled); clients re-fetch `GET /api/v1/personas` and switch once the new package has fully downloaded (`docs/apple/persona.md` ("Tiered avatars")) |
| `error` | `machine_id`, `session_id`, `error`; e.g. a subscription replay failed, and the client checks the session against it |
| `pong` | `id` (a string, echoing the client's application-level ping) |

Client → server:

| type | Fields |
| --- | --- |
| `subscribe` | `machine_id`, `session_id`, `since_seq` (optional; the App passes its local `covered`; if present, all items after it are replayed, one `items` per page (`backlog: true`), at most 8 pages / 4000 items, and beyond that the last one carries `more_after: true`; otherwise the last two turns are replayed), `lazy_images` (optional; when true, items received on this connection carry no image data), `fold_work` (optional; when true, the last two turns replayed from the end on this connection fold their work; `since_seq` replays are not folded) |
| `seen` | `machine_id`, `session_id`; same as HTTP `/seen` |
| `unsubscribe` | `machine_id`, `session_id` |
| `terminal_subscribe` | `machine_id`, `session_id`, `epoch` (optional), `after_seq` (optional): start receiving live frames of this session's terminal (only sent when the hub's `features` has `terminal_stream`); `control: {cols, rows}` (optional, `terminal_control`): the phone takes control of the terminal at this size, and `takeover: true` grabs it even when another program holds it |
| `terminal_input` | `machine_id`, `session_id`, `text` (terminal bytes, written as is), `control: {cols, rows}` (optional, new size), `scroll` (optional, wheel lines, > 0 goes back, < 0 goes newer, feature `terminal_scroll`), `at` (optional, `[column, row]` from 0, which cell of the screen the wheel lands on: where the finger went down; without it the node uses the center of the screen), `click` (optional, `[column, row]` from 0, a left click on that cell, feature `terminal_click`), `mouse` (optional, `{action: down|up|drag|move, button: left|middle|right, at: [column, row], mods}`, `mods` bits: shift 1, ctrl 2, alt 4; one mouse event, feature `terminal_mouse`, docs/integrations/terminal.md section 23): only forwarded to the node when sent by the connection currently in control |
| `terminal_unsubscribe` | `machine_id`, `session_id` |
| `fs_watch` | #2439 (automatic refresh of files and Git, "Automatic file refresh" below): `machine_id`, `cwd` (the session directory), `paths` (folders open on this page, absolute paths, at most 32), `git` (whether the Git status of `cwd` is shown). Replaces this page's whole set for this machine and this `cwd`; empty `paths` with `git` false releases it (so does disconnecting). Only full-access devices can send it; answer devices (the watch) are ignored |
| `herdr_open` | `id` (chosen by the browser, ≤ 64 characters), `machine_id`, `session_id` (optional, a session id or a `pane:` address, whose tab is focused first), `cols`, `rows`, `focus`: have the node run herdr's own client in a PTY and stream the bytes back (feature `herdr_client`, `full` devices only). `docs/integrations/terminal.md` section 24 |
| `herdr_input` / `herdr_resize` / `herdr_ack` / `herdr_close` | `id` plus `data` or `b64` (≤ 1 MiB) / `cols`, `rows` / `bytes` (cumulative bytes parsed) / —: only the connection that opened the view can use it |
| `herdr_focus` | `id` (the view's id), `session_id` (a session id or a `pane:` address, ≤ 256 characters): the page now shows this pane, so move herdr's focus there (feature `herdr_focus`, `full` devices only, only the connection that opened the view; it changes state on the computer, since focus is shared by the whole herdr session). No reply; if focus actually changes, it comes back as `herdr_focus` (`source: "persona"`). `docs/integrations/terminal.md` section 28 |
| `register_phone` | `device_name`, `tools` (`[{"name","description","input_schema"}]`, i.e. MCP tool definitions), `simulator` (a simulator only takes tool calls when no real device is connected); optional `device_id`, `platform`. Registration is replaced per device; an empty tool list only clears that device's tools; without `device_id`, the authenticated device ID is used, falling back to `legacy`. A call first filters online phones that provide the tool, then prefers real devices and the most recently active connection. The iPhone's `device_id` is the device id used for push (same as `POST /api/v1/devices`): while it's connected, the hub doesn't send APNs pushes for this device's Live Activity and the App draws it itself, `docs/apple/live-activity.md` ("Push cadence"); old Apps don't send it. `phone_runtime_cli` in `tools` (a DEBUG build with Runtime CLI via the hub turned on) doesn't count as a phone tool: the hub takes it out, so it's not in the Agents' tool list and Agents can't call it; it's only for `POST /api/v1/phone/runtime-cli`; a connection that registers only that one (a script-driven simulator) doesn't count as a phone. |
| `register_desktop` | `device_name`: a desktop client registers as a desktop client, not a phone: it doesn't take `phone_*` and doesn't stop the hub from sending pushes that wake the iPhone (`hub/desktops.go`); `device_id` (the device id used for push, same as `POST /api/v1/devices`: while it's connected, the hub doesn't push "Needs You" or "Agent finished" to this desktop, and it posts local notifications itself; old Apps don't send it). Signing it out means revoking its device credential (`DELETE /api/v1/auth/tokens/{id}`; the hub then drops its connection and deletes the push registration it made) |
| `unregister_desktop` | No fields: withdraw this connection's desktop registration while the app is locked, idle or unable to notify, so Phone Muted doesn't suppress phone alerts it cannot show. The socket and the app's other work stay connected; an active desktop may register again on the next authenticated hello. Older hubs ignore the message, leaving socket-close withdrawal as the compatibility path |
| `tool_result` | `call_id`, `content` (`[{"type":"text","text"}|{"type":"image","data","mime_type"}]`), `is_error` |
| `client_hello` | `device_id`, `platform`, `version`, `build`, `os: {name, version, sdk}`, `features`, `heartbeat: {interval?, pong_timeout?}`, `locale` (`zh-Hans` / `en` / `ja`, the UI language), all optional, see below |
| `extension_ui_stream` | `manager?` (the manager to route it to; default the default manager), `request` (`UIStreamRequest`: `request` is `open` / `close` / `suspend` / `resume` / `event` / `snapshot`, with `request_id` and the fields that request needs): a native extension page stream request. The hub forwards it with this connection's authenticated identity to that manager, whose frames come back to this connection only (`extension_ui_stream` above). Only from full devices on a connection that declared `extension_ui_stream_v1`, at most 64 KiB and at most 16 managers per connection; anything else is dropped without a reply, and a ninth request while eight still wait for their manager closes the connection ([schema/extension/README.md](../../schema/extension/README.md) "Native UI stream protocol 1") |
| `ping` | Must carry a string `id`; an empty string is allowed; no reply if it's missing, null or not a string |

### Event resume (`event_seq`, 2026-11-04)

Broadcasts the hub sends to all clients (everything in this table except `hello`, connection snapshots, `sessions_delta`, `sessions_list`, `managers`, `extension_operation`, `extension_ui_stream`, `items`, `delta`, `terminal*`, `tool_call`, `notify`, `lock_test`, `pong`, `error`,
`client_hello_ack`, `hub_restarting`) carry `event_seq`: it increments by one per event within a stream (`hello.event_stream`), and numbering continues after a hub restart.

- The client remembers `event_stream` and the highest `event_seq` it received, and passes them when reconnecting: `/api/v1/ws?event_stream=<stream>&event_seq=<n>` (both are required).
- `hello.resumed: true`: right after hello, broadcasts with `event_seq > n` are replayed (in order, no duplicates), then live ones follow; the client doesn't need a full re-fetch. Connection snapshots are sent as usual (full state, applied silently).
- `resumed: false` (the stream changed: the hub crashed; what was missed is no longer in the last 2000 events / 15 minutes the hub keeps; more than 400 events) or an old hub without these fields: do a full refresh as before.
  `hello.event_seq` is the last event at this moment; after the full refresh, keep counting from it.
- Permission cards that need filling in (elicitation `interaction`s) are not replayed; they come from the pending-interaction snapshot after connecting.
- After a subscription (`subscribe`) replay, a headless assistant session that is still generating is followed immediately by one current `delta`.

### Notifications over the persistent connection (ws_notify)

`notify` is the event name; `ws_notify` is the capability name both sides declare. The hub reuses the APNs decisions for questions and completions, mute rules and device preferences, and sends it to a connection only when `c.has("ws_notify")`. It's received even without an APNs token or key; old iOS versions don't declare it and so don't get the new event.

`interaction` means an interaction that needs handling, `done` means an Agent finished, `assistant` means the assistant finished, and `alert` is a reminder an extension sent via `POST /api/v1/notify` (or a script's `personad notify`, `../integrations/script-cli.md`) (clients ignore unknown kinds). Preferences are read from `/api/v1/devices/{id}/prefs` by the authenticated device ID: interactions follow `input`, completions follow the existing completion policy; quiet hours (`quiet`) drop completions and mark interactions and reply reminders `quiet: true`; machine and space mutes use the existing checks. Completion events are decided by the hub, and Android should not generate another one from session state changes. The raw `interaction` and `interaction_resolved` events are still sent, for request cards and withdrawing notifications; don't treat both as new reminders.

**Kept while offline** (#4043): APNs stores an iPhone's alert until the phone is back, but a device with no push route (an Android phone, a browser, a phone whose token is missing or was rejected) hears of a question or a finished turn only on this connection. So, for each device that has no push route (no reachable APNs or relay registration under its credential), the hub keeps the `notify` events it selected for that device while the device had no `ws_notify` connection, and sends them right after the `client_hello` of its next connection that declares `ws_notify`, oldest first (not ordered against `client_hello_ack`):

- They are the same events a connected socket would have got, with no new fields. The device's settings (`input`, the completion policy, manager mutes, Phone Muted, quiet hours) were applied when each event was selected and are not applied again, so one selected inside quiet hours still carries `quiet: true`. They are written in the language of the device's last `client_hello`.
- An `interaction` notify whose card was resolved in the meantime is skipped. Other kinds are sent as kept; clients collapse them with their usual notification tags (the interaction id, the session, an alert's `id`), so one already shown is replaced rather than repeated.
- Bounds: at most 50 events per device for at most 30 minutes (the oldest go first), for the 32 devices whose last `client_hello` declared `ws_notify` most recently. A `client_hello` without `ws_notify`, or revoking the device's credential, forgets the device and its events.
- Memory only: a hub restart loses them, and a device is known only after it has said `client_hello` with `ws_notify` to the running hub. An event sent to a socket that was already dead but not yet detected (before its heartbeat times out) is not kept. Kept events don't count as selected in `POST /api/v1/notify`'s answer.

Events don't prove a notification was actually shown; after a disconnect the client must still fetch interactions and sessions to reconcile. Notification reliability, lock screen display and battery use have not been measured.

### Web Push (browsers, #7459)

A browser that turned on **Settings › Notifications › When Persona is closed** ([web.md](../web/web.md) "Web Push") gets, while no page of it is connected, the `notify` events a socket would get, as a Web Push (RFC 8030) encrypted to it (RFC 8291 `aes128gcm`) and signed with the hub's VAPID key (RFC 8292). `server/internal/webpush` encrypts and signs with the standard library only; `server/internal/hub/webpush.go` decides and delivers. Push delivery is the hub's own: full devices only (an extension's token, an answer-only device and Persona Link are refused).

| Method | Path | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/api/v1/push/ln-mode` | Push grading switch state: `{"enabled": bool}` (default false). Full credentials and an extension token with the `notify` scope may read it |
| PUT | `/api/v1/push/ln-mode` | `{"enabled": bool}` → the same shape; full credentials only (extension tokens get 403, even with `notify`); stored in `hub_settings` |
| GET | `/api/v1/push/intercepts` | `{"intercepts": [{"at","level","reason","title"?,"body"?,"related_key"?,"manager"?,"also"?}]}` newest first, at most 200, the pushes the grading filter held back (`reason`: `ln_p1_held` / `ln_p2_silent` / `ln_dedup_12h`; `also`: titles merged into one same-minute P1 entry). Full credentials read every manager's. An extension token needs the `notify` scope **and** its extension ID in `hub.json` `intercept_readers`; any other extension token gets 403, and a listed extension still reads its own manager's only (the manager filter runs **before** the 200 limit, so other managers' bursts cannot push its entries out). `body` is a stored summary, not the full text: title plus at most 140 runes with an ellipsis when cut, because bodies can contain the owner's decision questions, agent replies or notify_user text |
| GET | `/api/v1/push/stats/daily[?days=N\|&since=RFC3339]` | `{"since": RFC3339, "days": [{"date","manager","sent","intercepted","by_reason"?}]}` per UTC calendar day and manager: `sent` counts logical alert pushes allowed through to delivery (one entry however many devices were targeted, regardless of per-device mute/quiet filtering or APNs acceptance; counted with the switch off as well as on, including the hub's own pairing / joining receipts with `manager` empty; silent background and Live Activity pushes are not counted), `intercepted` with `by_reason` counts held pushes. Counts read the hub's full in-memory records (up to 500 held / 2000 delivered, 14 days), so they stay exact past the intercepts' 200-entry limit. `days` is 1 (today) to 14; `since` takes an RFC3339 timestamp and wins over `days`; windows older than 14 days are clamped; bad params get 400. Full credentials read every manager's; an extension token with the `notify` scope reads its own manager's only. There is no "opened / handled" count: the app has no push-open callback, and card-resolution events are not stored per push |
| GET | `/api/v1/push/web` | `{key}`: the VAPID public key (uncompressed P-256, base64url), the browser's `applicationServerKey`. Made the first time it is asked for and kept in the hub's settings (`hub.web_push.vapid`); 503 when it can't be read or stored |
| GET | `/api/v1/push/web/{device}` | `{subscribed, service?, host?, browser?, current?, endpoint?, created_at?, updated_at?, last_ok_at?, failed_at?, status?, error?}`. `{device}` is the browser's notification device id (`web-<uuid>`, the id its prefs go by). `service` is `FCM` / `Mozilla` / `Apple` / `Windows`; `current` false: made with a key the hub no longer has (the page subscribes again); the last delivery (`last_ok_at`, or `failed_at` with the push service's `status` and `error`) is kept in memory |
| PUT | `/api/v1/push/web/{device}` | `{endpoint, keys:{p256dh, auth}, key, locale?, features?, browser?}` (`PushSubscription.toJSON()`, the key it subscribed with, the page's language, its `client_hello` features, "Chrome · macOS") → the status above. 400 `bad_device`; 400 `unknown_push_service`: the endpoint must be https on 443, without credentials, at FCM (`fcm.googleapis.com`), Mozilla (`*.push.services.mozilla.com`), Apple (`*.push.apple.com`) or Windows (`*.notify.windows.com`), so a device can't make the hub post to an address of its choosing; 400 `bad_endpoint`, `bad_keys`; 409 `key_changed` with `key` (subscribe again with it); 403 `owned`: another device credential made it, and the request doesn't present its endpoint (the same browser signed in again does); 503 when it can't be stored. `features` keeps only `elicitation`. At most 32 browsers, kept whole in `hub.web_push.subscriptions`: one more drops the one renewed longest ago; the same endpoint under another device id replaces that row |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/push/web/{device}[?endpoint=]` | `{ok, removed}`; 403 `owned` as for PUT |
| POST | `/api/v1/push/web/{device}/test` | A test push now, page open or not: `{ok, push_status}`, or 502 `push_failed` with `push_status` (`-1` for a request that could not be made) and `gone`; 404 `not_subscribed`; 403 `owned` |

**What is pushed, and when.** `notifyWSFrom`, after the sockets and the notify ring, picks each subscribed browser that has no connection whose `client_hello` named its device id (for a page from before that, no connection with the credential that subscribed), that has the capability the event requires, and whose prefs take the event: the decision a socket gets (`input`, the completion policy, manager mutes, Phone Muted, quiet hours). So cards, finished turns, reply reminders, decisions and `POST /api/v1/notify` alerts; not an extension's own `hub.push_localized`, pairing receipts, hub updates, Live Activities or withdrawals (the page takes back what is over when it opens). The browser's service worker gets:

```json
{"v":1,"kind":"interaction","title":"Needs your permission","subtitle":"Fix the login · Laptop","body":"Bash: npm test","machine_id":"laptop","session_id":"<id>","interaction_id":"<id>","quiet":true}
```

with `id` (an alert's), `todo_id` (a decision's) and `recording_id` when the event has them, written in the language it subscribed in, the texts shortened until it fits 3,993 bytes (one 4,096-byte record). `TTL: 1800` (what the notify ring keeps); `Urgency: high` for `interaction`, `reply` and `assistant`, else `normal`; `Topic` a hash of the notification's tag (`<machine>/<session>#needs` or `#finished`, `card:<id>#needs`, `todo:<id>`, `alert:<id>`), so pushes waiting at the push service replace each other as the notifications do. The VAPID `sub` claim names the project, never the user. A 429, 5xx or network error is tried again after 1 s and 4 s; 404 or 410 drops the subscription, and so does revoking the credential that made it. The push service sees ciphertext, its size and timing only.

### Client capabilities and heartbeat

Once the client sees that the server supports `client_hello`, it may send:

```json
{"type":"client_hello","device_id":"<device id>","platform":"android","version":"<version>","build":1,"os":{"name":"Android","version":"<OS version>","sdk":36},"features":["endpoints"],"locale":"en","heartbeat":{"interval":240,"pong_timeout":15}}
```

`locale` is the resolved UI language (`zh-Hans` / `en` / `ja`, [i18n.md](i18n.md)), not "Match System". The hub uses it for the text of `notify`, `error` and the like on this connection. A `full`-role connection's value also decides the **user language** (Postgres `settings.user_locale`), used for assistant answers, injected messages, task notifications, bot replies, and pushes to devices without their own `locale`: the first device to report one sets it, and after that only a device reporting a different language than it did before changes it; another device connecting in its own language does not ([i18n.md](i18n.md), "Protocol: telling hub the language"). If no client has ever reported one, it's `zh-Hans`. Omitting `locale` changes neither. When the user changes the language (or the system language changes under Match System), send `client_hello` again right away (with the other fields as before; omitting `features` clears the capability set).

The web client's `device_id` is its notification device id (`web-<uuid>`, #7459): while a connection that named it is open, the hub pushes nothing to that browser's Web Push subscription ("Web Push (browsers)" above). This metadata is only recorded on the current connection and doesn't change the authenticated device identity or permissions. `build` currently accepts any JSON.

**App version.** The hub also keeps, per device credential, the app version each client last reported, so the assistant can say which build is installed while the app is in the background or offline (Postgres hub setting `hub.client_apps`; `devices.list` gives the manager `apps`, `assistantwire.ClientApp`; `server/internal/hub/client_apps.go`). It reads the fields above: the Apple apps send the two halves of their `X-Persona-Client` header (`"platform":"ios-app"`, `"version":"1.4.0+52"`: the version, then the build after `+`) and `os` (`{"name":"iOS"|"iPadOS"|"watchOS"|"macOS"|"visionOS","version":"26.1"}`); Android sends `"platform":"android"`, its `versionName` and its `versionCode` in `build`. HarmonyOS sends `"platform":"harmony"`, its bundle version and build, and the reported HarmonyOS version in `os`. Only `ios`, `macos`, `watchos`, `visionos`, `android` and `harmony` (an Apple `-app` suffix is dropped) with a short version-like `version` are kept; the web is not (the hub serves it, so its version is the hub's), nor a pairing token or the hub's main token (no credential: a simulator on it could never be marked as one). A credential that registers as a simulator (`register_phone`'s `simulator`) is marked so, and the assistant prefers a real device over it. Entries unseen for 180 days are dropped, and at most 32 are kept; an unchanged report is saved again at most hourly. Another client reports its version by sending these fields; nothing else is needed. Each `client_hello` replaces the client's capability set, and omitting `features` clears it; don't substitute the server's capability list for the capabilities the client itself supports.

The seconds below are all negotiation bounds and timer settings in the code; **network latency, actual packet frequency, battery use and carrier idle timeouts have not been measured**.

- Without negotiation, the old behavior holds: the hub sends WebSocket protocol pings every 20 seconds and waits 15 seconds for the protocol pong; TCP keepalive settings on old connections are unchanged.
- `heartbeat.interval` is in whole seconds, first clamped to 10–900, then jittered downward only: a random integer in `0..min(interval-10, floor(interval/10))` is subtracted. It's drawn once per negotiation, and `client_hello_ack` returns the value actually used.
- `heartbeat.pong_timeout` is in whole seconds, clamped to 5–60; an omitted item keeps the previous or default value. An empty `heartbeat` object also marks it as negotiated; omitting the whole field keeps the previous negotiation state.
- The web client sends `heartbeat: {"pong_timeout": 45}` (no `interval`): the 15 s default is too tight for high-latency public links whose outbound path changes, and 45 s still sits under the page's own 70 s quiet limit.
- After the writer goroutine applies the new settings, it returns `{"type":"client_hello_ack","heartbeat":{"interval":<actual>,"pong_timeout":<actual>}}`. The client can send it again to renegotiate; even sending only metadata without heartbeat gets an ack with the current values.
- After negotiation it also tries to adjust TCP keepalive: Idle uses interval, Interval uses pong_timeout, Count is 3; this depends on whether the underlying connection supports it. A protocol pong timeout closes the connection. Only one protocol ping is outstanding at a time, and it doesn't block application-level replies.

Application-level probes use separate client-initiated JSON messages:

```json
{"type":"ping","id":"probe-1"}
{"type":"pong","id":"probe-1"}
```

The first is sent by the client, the second is the hub's reply, with `id` echoed as is. Check the server's `app_ping` capability first; it's independent of WebSocket protocol control-frame ping / pong, and neither replaces the other. The hub never sends JSON `ping` on its own and doesn't handle client JSON `pong`. Old clients that don't send `client_hello` don't receive the new `endpoints` event or the negotiation ack.

New fields must be optional and must not use a type that conflicts with a same-named key in the existing iOS `Envelope`; for example, `id` stays a string and can't become an object for the new protocol.

### Codex questions and approvals

Codex / compatible forks have no hooks in the terminal, so the node reads questions from the rollout itself (`request_user_input_async` / `request_user_input`) and approvals from the screen, turning them into ordinary
`question` / `permission` interactions with `agent: "codex" | "traex"`; permission cards also carry `reason` (the reason Codex gave) and `always_label` (what **Always Approve** would allow;
without this field there's no **Always Approve**). The answer format is the same as Claude's: `{"answers":…}`, `{"allow":true,"always":…}`, `{"allow":false,"message":"…"}`
(with `message`, the turn stops and the message is sent in as the next message). Answers are synchronous: the hub hands it to the node (`codex.answer`), and the node checks that the computer still shows this question / this approval
and that the TUI is back in a state where it can be answered, types the input, then confirms Codex accepted it before returning success; otherwise it returns 409 `input_draft` / `dialog_open` / `prompt_changed` (nothing typed),
and the card stays (except for `prompt_changed`). Details in `docs/integrations/codex.md` ("Questions and approvals").

### Permission cards that need filling in

A `permission` interaction can carry `fields: [{key,label,placeholder?,secret?,optional?}]`; the App fills in passwords with a secure input field and on approval sends
`{"allow":true,"values":{"password":"…"}}`. If a required field is missing, the hub rejects this approval and keeps the card; secret fields in the interaction history are recorded only as `<redacted>`,
and the raw values only go to the waiting tool. The notification category for these cards is `INTERACTION_INPUT` (no quick allow button), and the list, the watch and Siri don't approve them directly.
Values for keys the card does not declare are dropped when it is answered. Everyone else told of the answer gets the redacted copy: the `interaction.resolved` / `interaction.ended`
events (the channels, the task feeds), and a second answer's `{"already":true,"resolution":…}`. Such an answer is never held for redelivery, and the hub's operation receipt for `resolve`
(`client_ops.digest`) covers the answer as the hub reads it (`proto.Resolution`, field names in any case) with each value replaced by its key, and one fixed body for a body that
is not an answer. Lark and plugin channels can only decline such a card. The assistant's `secret_run` card (`tool_name: "secret_run"`, one secret `password` field,
`docs/assistant/assistant.md` "Password card") is one of these: the iPhone, Mac, Vision Pro, Android and web apps fill it in on the card itself, and the watch (an answer-only device) offers only Decline. Only the assistant's tool
makes it: a card with `tool_name: "secret_run"` from a node (`interaction.create`, a Codex list) or from `fleet.ask` is refused.

### Secret hand-off cards (`secret_handoff`, #3962)

A `permission` interaction with `tool_name: "secret_handoff"` asks to hand secret values to one Agent run as environment variables
(`docs/extensions/secret-providers.md` "Who may approve a hand-off"). Its `tool_input` is `{"variables":[{"name","provider","provider_name"?,"title"?}],"agent"?,"machine_name"?,"cwd"?,"prompt"?}`
(the item as its provider describes it, its detail on one line of at most 40 characters; never a reference or a value). Its `summary` (also the push's text and the "Needs you" row's title) leads with the Agent and how many secrets it asks for, and says "an Agent" when the Agent has no name yet; the items are on the card only. Only the manager's Agent start makes it: a card with that tool
name from a node or from `fleet.ask` is refused. Only a `full` device approves it, by a `resolve` request that itself carries
`X-Persona-Features: secret_handoff`; a client sends that header on the card's own approve request only (not from a notification, a
widget, the Live Activity, the watch or Siri), and the feature in `client_hello` does not count. Any other approval of such a card
(an answer-only device, an extension's token, the hub's own token, a request without the feature) gets 403
`{"code":"secret_handoff_elsewhere"}` with "Approve on iPhone or the web", the card stays pending, and the refusal is recorded in each
provider's audit log. A plain no (`{"allow":false}`, with or without `message`; `{"dismiss":true}`; `{"cancel":true}`; nothing else set)
goes through from any client. Its notification category is `INTERACTION_INPUT` (no quick allow button), its Live Activity row has no
`interaction`, and `…/choose` answers 400 `not_choosable`.

### Terminal dialogs (screen interactions)

When an Agent is blocked without a hook interaction, the hub reads the screen once (`session.screen`, 40 lines) and builds a `screen` card:

- The node reads those 40 plain rows the same way for the card and for its answer (`node/hosts.go` `dialogScreen`). When herdr can't send them whole (a wide pane full of CJK text is past 8 KB in 30 plain rows),
  both take the most bottom rows that fit (30, 24, 16, 12), and a dialog is read from them only when they show it whole, from the rule that opens it (`screen.DialogWhole`).
  Then it is the dialog a whole screen shows, with the same `rev` whatever rows fit at the card and at the answer. A dialog taller than those rows stays unreadable as before:
  no card, and an answer presses nothing, since part of it (a permission's command) would be neither shown nor in `rev` (#6318).

- When it's built: for Claude Code without Persona hooks (started from the user's own profile), it reads the screen and builds the card as soon as it's blocked; for sessions with hooks (that sent a hook event since this hub started,
  or that Persona started), it first waits 1.5 s so the hook's own card arrives first (3 s for Codex / compatible forks). If the hook's card arrives late, it still replaces the screen card.
  A hook card answered with an allow that Claude doesn't take (its own safety checks, #3752) leaves the dialog on screen: node then lists the
  session as blocked by it (`docs/protocol/agent-states.md`, "An allow Claude did not take"), and the screen card follows the same way.
- After a screen card is answered, the hub looks at the screen again every 250 ms for up to 2 s: when the Agent asks again right away (the next AskUserQuestion question, the next permission), herdr may stay blocked
  with no state change, and this check is what builds a card for the new dialog; if it still sees the one just answered (the keys haven't landed yet) or no dialog, it keeps looking, and stops once the Agent is no longer blocked or another card exists.
- Measurements of the whole path and the no-rate-limit convention are in `docs/server/server.md` ("Card fast lane (#751)").

- The hub parses the dialog with `server/internal/screen` and puts it into `interaction.dialog`: `header`, `question`, `detail`,
  `options[{key,label,detail,kind,keys}]` (`kind`: `type_something` / `chat` / empty), `rev` (a hash of the question and options, excluding the cursor and spinner).
  Numbered options are chosen by number; unnumbered lists like Claude 2.1.312's trust-folder prompt are computed as `up/down` + `enter` from the cursor. The card id includes `rev`: a changed dialog is a new card,
  and what was selected on the previous card doesn't carry over.
- The App's answer carries `option` (plus `text` for `type_something`) instead of guessing keys itself; the hub passes `rev` and `option` to the node's `session.keys`,
  and the node **re-reads the screen, re-parses and compares `rev` before pressing any key**; if they differ it presses nothing and returns 409 `{"code":"prompt_changed"}`, and the hub then builds a new card from the current screen.
  The keys are also computed on the node from the screen at that moment (so it won't pick the wrong thing if the cursor was moved on the computer).
- Compatibility: old Apps don't know `dialog` and keep parsing `screen` and sending `keys` themselves; the hub adds `rev` to those too and checks it the same way; old nodes don't know `rev` / `option`,
  so the hub also passes the computed `keys`, behaving as before. Cards where no dialog was parsed (only the terminal and the key bar) aren't checked.
- Screen card answers are synchronous: the hub waits until the node has pressed the keys before replying to the App (it used to reply success first and press in the background).
- `rev` hashes the header, what is asked and each option's label and detail with all white space and ANSI escapes left out, so the same dialog redrawn at another pane width (a phone or the web viewing the pane resizes it) keeps its `rev` (#5538).
  The card takes the `rev` the node will check: `session.screen` with `lines` 40 (plain, visible) also returns `dialog_rev`, the node's own parse of that screen, so a hub and a node of different builds still agree.
  A node that returns no `dialog_rev` (older than #5538) gets the old formula (`LegacyRev`, which kept the wrapped rows), and a node also accepts that one from an older hub.
  A `prompt_changed` refusal's data carries `rev` (the card's) and, when a dialog is on screen, `seen_rev`, `seen_question` and `seen_options`. The node logs the same with the pane the answer read and the agent's pane (the one `session.screen` reads for the card), and the hub logs the refusal's data.
  The card the hub makes after a `prompt_changed` is named by the node's `dialog_rev` too, so a dialog the node reads differently gets a new card rather than the old id again.
- **A permission prompt for a shell command** (Claude Code's "Bash command", its description, the command between dashed rules `╌╌╌`, a boxed warning, a countdown): `dialog` also carries
  `command` (the command, its wrapped rows joined back where the screen shows they were wrapped), `description` (the agent's words for it), `warning` (the boxed note as Claude Code words it),
  `risk` (what the warning is about, for the apps to say in plain words: `delete` for "Dangerous rm operation …"; empty for any other warning, shown as it is),
  `deadline` (the countdown sentence as on screen), `deadline_action` (`deny` when it blocks the request, `allow` when it lets it through) and `deadline_at` (RFC 3339, when it runs out by the hub's clock at the read).
  `detail` still holds "Bash command", the description and the command, for older apps. The command is in `rev`; the warning and the countdown are not, so the card stays answerable while the clock runs.
  The countdown is read as one sentence across the two or three rows a narrow pane wraps it onto (#5265: read as question rows, its seconds changed `rev` every second once the phone's terminal view had narrowed the pane, and every answer was refused).
  Claude Code 2.1.322 draws a `│` before each row of the command, as before the warning; the rows between the dashed rules are the command whatever they start with (#5265: read as the warning, the command was neither shown nor in `rev`).
- The watch also answers with `option` when there's a `dialog` (Siri's **Approve First Pending** doesn't handle screen cards).
- **Multi-select** (AskUserQuestion `multiSelect` in Claude Code 2.1.316, `docs/integrations/claude-integration.md` ("Screen cards for multiselect questions")): `dialog` also carries
  `multi: true`, `submit` (`Submit`, or `Next` when more questions follow), and options also carry `checked` (already checked on the computer) and `text` (what's already typed in the free-answer box);
  with several questions, `steps[{label,done}]` is the tab bar at the top; the confirmation page before submitting is `review: true` (`incomplete: true`: some questions unanswered), with options "Submit answers / Cancel".
  `checked`, the cursor, typed text and tab checkmarks don't go into `rev`.
  The App's answer carries `options` (the keys of options to check; unlisted ones get unchecked) and `text` (the free answer; empty means don't check it). The hub passes it to the node's `session.keys`
  (`multi: true`, `options`, `free_text`), and the node presses one key at a time, re-reading the screen after each, and finally presses Submit / Next; on the confirmation page, if all questions are answered it presses "Submit answers" too.
  Old Apps send only one `option` for a multi-select card: treated as checking just that one.
- **Several questions on iPhone and iPad** (#2970, `ScreenStepsLogic`): the card shows `steps` with the question it is on, **Previous** / **Next** and a review before
  the answers go. Nothing new is asked of the hub or the node:
  - Previous and Next are answers with `keys: ["left"]` / `["right"]` and no `option`: the node checks `rev` and presses the key, and the hub's look after an answer
    makes the card of the question that shows next. The terminal marks the current tab by color only, which the screen reading drops, so the app tracks it from
    its own keys and answers (`ScreenTrail`, in memory) and highlights nothing when it can't tell.
  - A question gone back to has the `rev`, and so the card id, it had: once this device answers in the dialog, the session's other screen cards it had ended may
    come again. The terminal marks the answer it had (`checked`); words already in a "Type something" field are cleared (`ctrl+e`, `ctrl+u` in `pre_keys`) before
    the new ones.
  - The node presses "Submit answers" after an answer that names its `option` once every question has one. So the answer that may complete them goes as keys
    (a choice's number, or `pre_keys` + `text` + `enter`), and the review tab comes as a card of its own: a row per question from its `detail`, Submit (its first
    option) or, with a question left, a button that goes back to it with ← one card at a time. A multi-select last question is held for a review the app draws
    from what it answered, then sent as before. The Mac app keeps the old card.
- Passwords: when the last line on the screen is a password prompt (`[sudo] password for …:`, `Password:`, an ssh passphrase, the passwd, mysql/psql, ssh-keygen, ansible-vault and openssl/keytool prompts…; the rules are deliberately narrow, and the word password in body text doesn't count), the card carries
  `secret: true` and the App uses a password field (not saved to drafts). Password or not, `text` in terminal card answers is always stored as `<redacted>` in the database;
  the terminal panel's key endpoint (`/keys`) isn't stored at all, and the hub's request log only records the path and status code.

### Session deltas (`sessions_delta`, 2026-11-02)

A machine's session list has hundreds of sessions at about 1 KB each, and a push usually changes just one; pushing the whole list made the phone download and decode about 2.6 MB a minute (`docs/server/server.md` ("Traffic pushed to the app")).

- When connecting the WebSocket, the App adds `?features=sessions_delta` to the URL. If the hub has the capability (`sessions_delta` in `hello.features`), it:
  1. On connect, sends one full `sessions` list per machine as a snapshot, **without Codex history sessions** (`source_kind: codex_history`; the App gets them from `GET /api/v1/sessions`);
  2. After that only sends `{"type":"sessions_delta","machine_id","upsert":[Session…],"remove":[session_id…]}`: new or changed sessions (the whole object, not half of it) and the ids that are gone;
     nothing is sent if nothing changed. Codex history sessions only appear in deltas if the App already has them (a live Codex session ends and the same id becomes history).
- The hub tracks, per connection, every session of every machine each App holds (`client.have`); snapshots and deltas are computed and queued under the same lock, so a delta is always computed against what the App really has.
- Reconnecting after a disconnect means a new snapshot, which fills in any missed changes.
- App (`SessionPatch`, `AppModel.applySessions`): a snapshot replaces this machine's list but keeps the existing Codex history; a delta replaces changed ones in place, appends new ones and removes the ones that are gone;
  while the socket is connected, the `GET /api/v1/sessions` response is older than the pushes, so only Codex history is taken from it (history no longer in it is removed, and existing entries are replaced with the copies in the response: pushes don't carry history, so seen / went offline can only be updated from here, #2463), and it doesn't overwrite pushed sessions.
  Known issue (#2425): history the App already has keeps the old copy, so seen / went offline aren't updated in the list; the web has switched to using the copies in the response, the App is still to do.
- Compatibility: old Apps don't send `features` and keep getting full lists (identical ones not sent); old hubs don't know `features` and keep sending full lists, and the App, seeing no `sessions_delta` in `hello.features`, handles them as full lists.
  The mock (`scripts/mock/mock_hub.py`) supports it too, and `MOCK_WHOLE_LISTS=1` makes it act as an old hub.
- Replay (19 minutes recorded from a real hub): session pushes 2605 KB → 79 KB per minute, the snapshot on connect 602 KB → 227 KB (`docs/operations/testing.md` ("Push replay")).
- The web uses it too (`web/src/lib/sessions-delta.ts`, the same rules as `SessionPatch`): `wsQuery` adds `features=sessions_delta` on every connection, `store.ts` merges by `upsert` / `remove`, and `refresh()`, while connected to a delta-capable hub, only takes Codex history from `GET /api/v1/sessions`, replacing existing history with the copies in the response (pushes don't carry history, so seen / went offline can only be updated from here, #2425). Before this the web didn't send `features`, and each connection was measured receiving about 3 MB of full lists per second, slowing down the small events behind them (#1707).

### Bounded Agents lists (`sessions_list`, #5929)

**Choose the right collection.** Claude Code, Codex (including history), terminal-host and contributed-runtime sessions use **`GET /api/v1/sessions`** and snake_case `Session` rows, identified by `(machine_id, session_id)`. **`GET /api/v1/agents` is source/setup status**, not those sessions. Extension personal-agent conversations use **`GET /api/v1/agents/sessions`**, camelCase rows and the opaque `id` (`<source>:<sessionKey>`). The two collections are not combined or renamed.

#### Opt-in parameters (both session collections)

Any of `limit`, `cursor`, `since`, `summary`, `state`, `project`, `group`, or `counts` opts into the bounded API. `pane_source`, `roots`, `parent_session_id`, `place`, `space`, `catalog`, `todo`, `waiting` and `exclude_pane_source` also opt in, but are supported only by the runtime collection (see below). Without them, legacy requests and response shapes remain unchanged: runtime `machine_id` filtering still returns the complete list; personal-agent `source`/`provider` filtering still returns the complete list; personal-agent `q` alone still searches messages and returns `items`.

| Parameter | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `limit` | Integer 1–200, default **50**. Full and delta pages both use it. A delta removal consumes one slot, just like an upsert. |
| `cursor` | Opaque `next_cursor` from a preceding page. URL-encode it and repeat all original filters, `summary` and `since`; `limit` may change. Empty/invalid cursor is rejected, not treated as a first page. |
| `summary` | `1`/`true` for list-row summaries, `0`/`false` for complete rows; default false. Does not change row identity or filter membership. |
| `state` | Exact unified state: `needs_you`, `working`, `unread`, `idle`, `offline`, or `unknown`. Omit for all states. No user-specific mute/pin ordering is implied. |
| `machine_id` | Exact runtime machine id. Personal-agent sources do not expose a machine, so this filter matches no personal-agent rows. |
| `project` | Exact runtime `repo_root`, falling back to `workspace_cwd`, then `cwd`. This is the node's supplied path, **not** a guessed repository or a knowledge-base project id. Personal-agent rows have no project. |
| `group` | Runtime `space_id`, falling back to `workspace_id`; personal-agent `accountId`. Machine-local space ids can overlap: use `machine_id` with `group` when expanding a particular computer's group. This does not represent personal-agent custom preference sections or to-do group ids. |
| `source` | Runtime `source_kind` or personal-agent contribution id; unchanged transport/source semantics, never a pane origin. |
| `pane_source` | Runtime only: exactly `terminal`, `feishu`, `desktop`, or `unknown`. Requires the independently advertised `sessions_pane_source` capability. See pane/host origins below. |
| `roots` | Runtime only: `1`/`true` leaves the child sessions folded under a listed parent out of the rows, `total` and every count, and filters and counts the others by their folded state; `0`/`false` is the same as no key. Requires the independently advertised `sessions_hierarchy` capability. See "Session hierarchy" below. |
| `parent_session_id` | Runtime only: a session id, with `machine_id` (400 `invalid_query` without it, when empty, or with `roots=1`): only the sessions folded under that session, all depths. Requires `sessions_hierarchy`. See "Session hierarchy" below. |
| `place` | Runtime only, repeatable (1 to 64 values): each value is a JSON array `["<machine_id>","<project>"]`, and the sessions at any of those directories are selected: one project's checkouts across computers; an empty project selects that computer's sessions in no directory. Requires the independently advertised `sessions_catalog` capability. See "Projects and spaces" below. |
| `space` | Runtime only, repeatable (1 to 64 values): each value is a JSON array `["<machine_id>","<group>"]`, and the sessions in any of those computers' spaces are selected; an empty group selects that computer's sessions in no space. Requires `sessions_catalog`. See "Projects and spaces" below. |
| `catalog` | Runtime only: `1`/`true` returns the filtered list's projects and spaces instead of rows; `0`/`false` selects a normal page. Requires `sessions_catalog`. See "Projects and spaces" below. |
| `todo` | Runtime only: a to-do id selects the sessions on that open to-do (`Session.todo.id`); `none` selects the sessions on no open to-do (a done to-do's included). Empty or repeated: 400 `invalid_query`. Requires the independently advertised `sessions_todo` capability. See "Sessions by to-do" below. |
| `waiting` | `1`/`true`: only the sessions that only wait in the background (`Session.background_waiting`, by the folded state with `roots=1`); `0`/`false`: the others. With `state=working`, the two halves of the working sessions. Requires `sessions_quick_filters`. See "Quick filters" below. |
| `exclude_pane_source` | Runtime only: one of the `pane_source` origins; the sessions of that origin are left out of the rows, `total` and every count. Empty, repeated or unknown: 400 `invalid_query`. Requires `sessions_quick_filters`. See "Quick filters" below. |
| `manager` | Runtime only: a manager's id; only the sessions on its computers. Requires the independently advertised `sessions_manager` capability, and does not opt into the bounded API by itself. See "One manager's sessions" below. |
| `provider` | Runtime `agent` or personal-agent `provider`. Empty values on older runtime nodes stay empty; no agent name is guessed. |
| `q` | Case-insensitive substring, at most 256 Unicode characters. Runtime title, cwd, repository, branch, space/slot/agent names and last preview; personal-agent title/provider/account id. With an opt-in parameter this is **row search**, never remote transcript/message search. |
| `search` | Runtime only, opt-in ranked search, 1–1,024 UTF-8 bytes. Requires `sessions_search`; separate from legacy `q`. See "Ranked runtime search" below. |
| `counts` | `1`/`true` returns aggregates instead of rows. `0`/`false` selects a normal page. The same filters apply. |
| `since` | Opaque `revision` from the completed baseline/previous delta. Returns only changed rows and removals, including state/title-only changes when `updated_at` did not advance. Keep the same filters; changing a filter requires a new first-page baseline. |

Repeated recognized parameters, malformed booleans/page sizes/states and malformed tokens return HTTP **400** with `code: "invalid_query"`. Unknown parameters are ignored for compatibility. Responses retain the usual localized `error` field.

#### Page and ordering

```http
GET /api/v1/sessions?summary=1&limit=50
GET /api/v1/agents/sessions?summary=1&limit=50&source=demo
```

```json
{
  "sessions": [],
  "remove": [],
  "has_more": true,
  "next_cursor": "<opaque cursor>",
  "revision": "<opaque checkpoint>",
  "total": 8000
}
```

`total` is the number of matching sessions in the **whole collection**, not the page length or number of changes. Empty arrays are `[]`, not null. `next_cursor` is absent on the final page.

- Order: newest `updated_at` first for runtime rows, newest `rankTimeMs` first for personal-agent rows, then composite identity ascending for ties. This is a latest-update timeline, not the clients' state-rank/pin sort.
