The ctx a handler receives **ends once the reply is sent** (same as being cancelled): work that continues after replying (`session.watch`'s transcript pushes, anything streaming) must not hang off it; use `rpc.ConnContext(ctx)` (the connection's ctx, which ends only when the connection drops). After #2645 every request's ctx was cancelled as soon as it replied, while `session.watch` still hung off the request ctx, so transcript pushes for every session (main session, sub-Agents) stopped the moment after the watch reply. Pages only got `sessions_delta` and needed a refresh to see new content (#3139).

hub → node requests:

| method | params → result |
| --- | --- |
| `node.info` | → `{hostname, os, arch, home, herdr_version, claude_version, version, system, engine, engines}` (`system`: see Machine, read once at node start; `engine` is the engine the node currently uses, `engines` are those it found, see "Engines"; old nodes lack these two). If `claude_version` is empty on connect (the `claude --version` run failed), the hub asks again after 1, 2, 5, 10, 30 minutes and then hourly; once it gets a value it updates the machine and pushes it to the App, and stops when the connection drops (#542) |
| `engine.use` | `{engine, hosts?, default?}` → `{engine}`: switch to this engine, or to the set in `hosts` / `default` for a node that takes sets ("Engines", "Host sets"; unknown ones error). If it equals the current one, nothing happens; otherwise it swaps the host, drops the old engine's Agents (refresh results started before the switch and returning after it are discarded), ends all terminal streams (each pushes `terminal.end` with an error saying the engine changed), swaps the event stream, and pushes one `sessions.changed`. Multiple `engine.use` calls run in order |
| `launchers.list` | → `{launchers}`; a Codex launcher has `agent: "codex"`, `prompt_optional: true` when the node starts it with no first message too (`node/codex_waiting.go`), and `run_here: true` when the node starts it in a shell pane the user picked and keeps that pane when the start fails (`panes.agent`, #5504); `source: "claude_desktop"` is the launcher `claude-desktop`, which starts the session in Claude's desktop app (`docs/integrations/claude-integration.md`, "New sessions in the desktop app"), and `source: "codex_app"` the launcher `codex-app`, which starts the chat in the Codex App (`docs/integrations/codex.md`, "New chats in the Codex App") |
| `launchers.zshrc` | `{}` → `{aliases:[{alias, env:{K:V}, args, command, file}]}`: lines of the form `alias x="K=V … claude [args]"` in this machine's `~/.zshrc` (`$ZDOTDIR` first), `~/.bashrc` and `~/.bash_aliases`, the login shell's file first (zsh: `~/.zshrc`, `~/.bashrc`, `~/.bash_aliases`; bash: `~/.bashrc`, `~/.bash_aliases`, `~/.zshrc`); only those whose `command` is claude. `file` is that file's label (`~/.zshrc` for `$ZDOTDIR`'s too); inside a file the last definition of a name counts, across files the first file that defines it. A missing file has none; the login shell's own file there but unreadable is an error naming it, another unreadable one is skipped. `env` carries keys, which are handed to the manager only over this RPC (import, over the hub-to-node connection) and never logged; old nodes return `unknown method`, and nodes from before `file` read only `~/.zshrc` (the manager takes their aliases as `~/.zshrc`) |
| `launchers.repair` | `{name, action: "upgrade_cli"}` → `{ok, unsupported?, output?}`: auto-repair from the launcher health check (`docs/server/launcher-health.md`). The node only applies fixed repairs (for Claude, it runs `claude update`) and accepts no commands; old nodes return `unknown method` |
| `launchers.catalog` | `{launchers: [ManagedLauncher]}` → `{ok}`: the Persona-managed providers in this computer's device scope (`docs/integrations/launchers.md` "Device scope and on-demand delivery"), on every connection and after every change. An entry with `withheld: true` has no `api_key`, `headers` or `env`; the node asks `launchers.pull` for them when it needs them, and right away for one with `delivery: push`. `rev` changes on every save: what was pulled at another rev is dropped. Old nodes return `unknown method`, and the manager sends `launchers.managed` with this computer's providers instead |
| `launchers.managed` | `{launchers: [ManagedLauncher]}` → `{ok}`: the same with every secret, for nodes from before `launchers.catalog` (and from managers from before it) |
| `launchers.own_service` | `{agent}` → `{agent, known, own, via?}`: whether the harness (`claude`, `codex`) already has a usable service of its own on this computer (`via`: `login`, `api_key`, `launcher`); others are `known: false`. Cached ten minutes; old nodes return `unknown method`, read as not known |
| `launchers.models` | `{name, agent_type?, refresh?}` → `{agent, models, locked?}`: same as REST `…/launchers/{name}/models`; `agent_type` is this launcher's type in the hub config (if omitted, whatever the node detects itself) |
| `session.skills` | Manager-owned `{session_id,skill_owner}` → the versioned ordinary Agent catalog above. Derives live Claude terminal launcher/cwd/profile, or the uniquely owning Codex app-server and its actual home/cwd/connection. Reads do not join or resume threads. `session.send` validates explicit leading skill contexts before delivery; Claude receives exact-file instructions, Codex native typed skill input. Plain text requires no catalog. Unsupported nodes must not receive selected references as literal text. |
| `skills.list` | `{cwd?}` → `{skills: [{name, description, source}]}`: the legacy prepared inventory, unchanged. Optional manager-owned catalog mode `{catalog:true,skill_owner,machine_id,cwd,session_id?,launcher?,runtime?,config_dir?}` → `{catalog_version:1,skills:[{id,name,description?,source}],complete}` resolves the actual supported execution environment; paths stay on the node. The new manager requires `catalog_version:1` so an old node's legacy inventory is not mistaken for a complete runtime catalog. See `docs/assistant/assistant.md` ("Explicit skill mentions"). |
| `skills.import` | Manager-only `{dir,scope,op,archive?:base64,reference?}` → skill import result (REST above). `dir` is the server-derived assistant state directory; `scope` binds assistant and machine. Strict fields and directory/scope agreement are required. The node resolves the existing user skills directory, validates/stages in isolation and atomically adds a new safe name; preview/cancel/install/unchanged-new-only Undo use bounded ten-minute in-memory receipts. No arbitrary-path management, script execution or runtime/model call. |
| `dirs.list` | `{path}` → same as REST |
| `workspaces.list` | `{}` → `{workspaces:[Workspace],errors?:[{source,error}]}`; Workspace is the same as in "Workspace board"; the node omits machine_id, and id/source_id are host-local IDs. Includes spaces with no running Agent. Each source reports errors separately; if all fail it returns an RPC error and must not pretend to be an empty success. Sources not running on this computer (`host.ErrNotRunning`: Orca not open, botmux has no daemon or is too old to have `observe`) count as having no workspaces, not an error; if only non-running sources exist, it returns an empty list. An engine runtime that keeps workspaces (Paseo, `caps.workspaces`, #6295) is a source too: its `runtime.workspaces` rows, with the runtime id as `source`, `project_id` / `project_name` its space, `project_path` the repository's main checkout, `is_main` true for a main checkout, `workspace_kind` `git` or `folder`, and `owned` true on a worktree the runtime made (the only rows Delete worktree is offered for, #6297); while it is not connected it lists none |
| `workspace.resolve` | `{path}` → `Workspace`; validates a real directory and resolves symlinks. On success source is `directory`, id/source_id/cwd are the physical path, available is true. Accepts local absolute paths or `~/`; rejects missing paths, non-directories and protected iCloud paths. Performs no host, Agent or Git operations |
| `sessions.list` | → `{sessions, update_busy?}`: `update_busy` (with `node_update_idle`) is whether `node.update.commit` would refuse now, the node's own check; older nodes leave it out |
| `session.start` | `{cwd, launcher, agent_type?, prompt?, resume_session_id?, workspace_id?, permission_mode?, effort?, ultracode?, tab_name?, async?, in_pane?, secret_ticket?}` → `{session}`; `secret_ticket` (capability `secret_env`) is a `secret.stage` ticket: only a new Claude Code start in a terminal with a Persona-managed provider or plain `claude` takes one (`secret_env_agent` otherwise, `secret_env_gone` when the ticket is unknown, used, expired or another start's: the first start that names it takes it), and the Agent then starts through `personad launch --ticket` (`docs/extensions/secret-providers.md`); `in_pane` starts in a failed start's kept tab (`shell_waiting` / `agent_start_stalled` data `pane`) instead of a new one while the node still keeps it, else opens a new tab (#2570); `async` returns immediately and starts in the background (`node/starting.go`); Codex launchers are synchronous, and without `prompt` answer with a row waiting for the first message (`node/codex_waiting.go`). `ultracode:true` is best effort once Claude is up (never a failed start); `false` is the same as leaving it out. With `resume_session_id` for a Claude session that isn't running, whatever the start leaves out (launcher, the model picked for that launcher, directory, permission mode, effort, tab name) is what the session ran with, as a message that resumes it gets (`fillResume`, `node/retire.go`; the apps' Resume Session, #4328). An older node runs a left-out launcher as `claude` and the launcher's default model  With `resume_session_id` (the user's Resume, the one way a stopped Agent runs again, #4754) the resume runs in the shell the Agent left when that shell is at rest in the session's directory, else in a new tab. |
| `session.modes` | `{session_id, permission_mode?, effort?, model?, launcher?, from?}`: a running session's permission mode, effort and (Claude Code in a terminal) model, the model first. `launcher` (capability `launcher_switch`) other than the session's own records a pending switch to it (`pending_switch` on its row, kept in its state record so a node restart keeps it; a session Persona did not start keeps it in memory only), checked first (`switch_*` refusals); its own launcher drops one; `from` other than the session's launcher is `switch_stale`. See "Switching a running Agent to another provider". A launcher of the other engine (capability `engine_switch`) records a switch to that engine, `pending_switch.agent` naming it: see "Switching a running Agent to another engine" |
| `session.ultracode` | `{session_id, ultracode?:bool, dismiss_lost?:bool}`: the independent toggle for ordinary Claude Code Agent sessions; queued while busy or while a draft / dialog is in the way (success, `ultracode_pending`); refused with `ultracode_unsupported` where it cannot be made (botmux, main chat, old CLI). `dismiss_lost:true` dismisses the resume notice. An old node's `unknown method` becomes `409 node_outdated` at HTTP `/modes`; see "Claude Code ultracode" |
| `session.send` | `{session_id, text, images?, client_msg_id?}` (`client_msg_id`: see "Matching pending messages"). A stopped Agent of a terminal engine is read-only (#4754): refused `agent_stopped` (`delivered: none`), nothing typed; only a branch nothing has started yet is started by its first message. `apply_switch:true` (the user's message from the chat) carries a pending switch (`session.modes` `launcher`) out first: the agent quit in its terminal and resumed through the new launcher there, or the switch dropped and the message refused with a `switch_*` code and nothing typed; while the agent is busy the message goes as always and the switch waits. `switch_now:true` (the assistant's `agent_switch`, capability `launcher_switch_now`) implies `apply_switch` and carries the switch out now or not at all: where the message would go on the old launcher or leave the switch waiting it is refused (`switch_busy`, `input_draft`, `dialog_open`, `switch_stale`, `switch_unsupported`, `switch_other_agent`) with nothing typed and the switch dropped. A switch to the other engine (`pending_switch.agent`, `engine_switch`) starts that engine in the same terminal with the message behind its handoff, or resumes the conversation's earlier session of it; the message is consumed by that start |
| `session.switch` | `{session_id, launcher?, from?, model?}` → `{}`: the switch `session.modes` just picked (`pending_switch`), carried out now with no message (the assistant's batch switch, #6008, capability `launcher_switch_idle`): the agent is quit and resumed on the new launcher in the same terminal and waits there, idle. Refused with nothing done and the switch dropped as `switch_now` is (`switch_busy`, `input_draft`, `dialog_open`, `switch_stale`, `switch_unsupported`, `switch_other_agent`); a failed switch as for a message (`switch_failed`, `switch_failed_stopped`, `switch_not_stopped`). For a session that is not running, with `launcher`: nothing starts; Persona's record of it is pointed at that launcher and `model` (else the launcher's default), so its next Resume, or the message that resumes it, comes up there. The same launcher checks as a switch (`switch_launcher_missing`, `switch_other_agent`, `switch_config_dir`, `switch_model_locked`, `switch_pick_model`); `from` must name the launcher it is on (`switch_stale`); a session Persona keeps no record of is `switch_unsupported` |
| `session.echoes` | `{echoes: [{session_id, client_msg_id, text, images, sent_at, after_seq, line?}]}` → `{ok}`: the hub hands back sends recorded for this machine within the last day (every time the node connects, before `sessions.list`); the node skips ones it already knows. Old nodes return unknown method and the hub ignores it |
| `session.keys` | `{session_id, keys, text}` |
| `start.keys` | `{pane, text?, keys?}` → `{ok}`: types `text` as is (no enter, at most 32 characters), then presses `keys` (at most 8, Persona's key names) in a failed start's kept tab while no agent runs there (#2570, `node/startremedy.go`); any other pane is refused with `start_tab_gone`, too much with `too_large` |
| `session.rewind` | `{session_id, prompt, occurrence, prompts_after?, restore}` → `{prompt, restore, code_restored, input_cleared}`: uses the owning tool's native rewind ("Rewind to a message"); refusals carry `code` |
| `session.restore_model` | `{session_id}` → `{restore: "next_start", restore_to, closed}`: closes a Persona conversation's idle headless process so its next start uses the configured model; sends nothing ("Going back to the configured model"); refusals carry `code` |
| `session.interrupt` | `{session_id}` |
| `session.screen` | `{session_id, lines, source, format?}` → `{text, status}` (`format: "ansi"` includes colors) |
| `panes.list` | `{}` → `{hosts:[…]}`, same as REST `/machines/{mid}/panes`: the node answers with spaces / tabs / all panes from its latest host snapshot (taking a new one only if older than 3 seconds), without starting its own polling |
| `panes.new` | `{workspace_id, kind?}` → `{pane, terminal, tab_id}`: the host's `CreateSlot` opens a shell tab (directory is the space's own); errors if the space is gone or the host can't open tabs. With `cwd` and no `workspace_id`, the first workspace of a host that opens tabs; when that host has none, its `CreateSpace` opens a new workspace in `cwd` (home for `~`; capability `pane_new_space`, which clients ask for with `new_space`) |
| `panes.close` / `panes.split` / `panes.agent` / `panes.git` / `tabs.close` / `tabs.rename` | node menu actions, params as in the REST above. The pane / tab must be one the host lists (if not, take a snapshot first and check again); the directory is the pane's own. Closing an Agent's pane goes through `session.close` (asks it to exit first). `panes.agent` reuses the whole new-Agent launch flow (same launcher command, wait for the session to be ready, bind); on failure the pane is not closed |
| `panes.close_finished` | `{panes?, preview?}`: "Close finished terminals", as the REST above (`node/stopped.go`) |
| `claude.auth_status` | `{name}` (launcher; empty means `claude`) → `{state: logged_in\|not_logged_in\|unknown, auth_method?, api_provider?, key_source?, version?, reason?}` (#4048): runs `claude auth status --json` with the same command and the same `--settings` used to open a chat; sends no model request. `auth_method` is Claude Code's `authMethod` (`claude.ai`, `api_key`, `api_key_helper`, `oauth_token`, `third_party`, `none`); `key_source` is only the variable name (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`); email, organization and keys are never returned. `reason` for `unknown`: `old_claude` (before 2.1.41 there's no `claude auth`; not run), `not_claude` (the launcher runs Codex / a runtime), `unreadable` (status can't be read: claude not found, the launcher swallowed the arguments), `timeout` (20 seconds). A name that isn't a launcher on this computer errors without running; old nodes return `unknown method` |
| `node.doctor` / `node.doctor.fix` | `{fix?: bool, preflight?: bool}` / `{}` → the same `DoctorReport` as `personad node doctor --json` (#2429): checks run inside the node process. `node.doctor` without `fix` writes nothing; `fix` (or `node.doctor.fix`) only rewrites files Persona itself generated (`writeGeneratedConfig`) and then checks again; never the LaunchAgent (#5944). `preflight: false` leaves the `path-access` check out (the assistant's readiness passes it: it only reads `claude-version`; older nodes ignore it). The hub's GET never passes `fix` |
| `secret.run` | `{check: true}` → `{ok: true}`: nothing runs, the password card's pre-flight; refused on Windows. `{commands, password, timeout_ms}` → `{results: [{command, exit_code, timed_out, output, truncated, output_withheld}]}`: the commands the user approved on the password card (`docs/assistant/assistant.md` "Password card", capability `secret_run`), 1 to 5 one-line commands of printable ASCII, each with `/bin/sh -c` in the home directory with `PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin`, in its own session and process group. `password` is base64 of its bytes, without control characters; a command that runs one `sudo -S` (not after a pipe) gets it and a newline on stdin, any other command an empty stdin. It stops at the first command that exits non-zero, cannot start or runs out of `timeout_ms` (the whole run, at most 30 minutes; the group gets SIGTERM, 5 seconds, then SIGKILL until it is empty; `timed_out: true`, `exit_code: -1`, and a root command sudo started may still run). A command whose shell exited while a background child still holds its output runs out of time the same way; a command whose turn comes after the time is used up does not run and gets no result. `output` is stdout and stderr together, the last 16 KiB; a command whose output held the password returns none of it (`output: ""`, `output_withheld: true`). The node zeroes the password when the run ends and logs neither params nor output; it is not told when the caller stops waiting. A node without the capability gets `node_outdated` from the manager |
| `secret.stage` | `{check: true}` → `{key, key_id}`: a one-time key for one hand-off (base64 of an uncompressed P-256 point), good for 2 minutes; also the hand-off's pre-flight (refused on Windows). `{key_id, sealed}` → `{ticket, expires_at}`: values a provider extension resolved for one Agent start after the user approved the hand-off card (`docs/extensions/secret-providers.md` "The hand-off to one Agent run", capability `secret_env`), sealed to that key (HPKE: DHKEM(P-256, HKDF-SHA256), HKDF-SHA256, AES-256-GCM, info `persona secret stage v1` NUL `key_id`; the plaintext is the JSON array `[{name, value}]`, `value` base64), so whatever relays the connection sees none. The key works once. 1 to 8 variables; `name` an environment variable name that is not the computer's, Persona's, the Agent's own or one that changes how programs load, run or connect (`PATH`, `HOME`, `LD_*`, `DYLD_*`, `PERSONA_*`, `ANTHROPIC_*`, `CLAUDE_*`, `GIT_*`, proxies, CA bundles, editors and the like); `value` 16 bytes to 16 KiB without NUL. The node keeps them in memory only, under a random one-time `ticket` (64 hex characters) good for 2 minutes that `session.start`'s `secret_ticket` names; it logs neither params nor values. Only the manager that connects the computer sends it: a `device.call` of it from the hub or another manager is refused with `handoff_refused`, as is a `session.start` with `secret_ticket` (in any letter case). From staging on, the node process hides each value in everything it sends (`docs/extensions/secret-providers.md`). A node without the capability gets `node_outdated` from the manager |
| `worktree.snapshot` | #2173 a reviewer's own copy of an agent's change: `{cwd, name_hint?, kind?}` → `{path, root, head, skipped?}`. `git worktree add --detach` of the HEAD of the repository `cwd` is in, at `<checkouts>/review-<slug of name_hint>` (made unique), with the folder's staged, unstaged (`git diff --binary HEAD` applied) and untracked, not ignored files (at most 2000 files / 64 MiB; `skipped` counts the rest). Nothing is written in `cwd`'s tree. `worktree.remove` with `force` takes the copy away. Refusals: `not_a_repository`, `no_commit`, `worktree_failed` |
| `worktree.prepare` / `worktree.create` | #2431, same as the REST above (`workspace_id`, `kind?`; create also has `branch`, `path`): the workspace must be one the host lists, and the directory is the workspace's own. Instead of `workspace_id`, `cwd` names it (#5325, the assistant's `agent_start` with `worktree`; the REST routes do not pass it): the host's space whose directory holds `cwd`, the deepest one; none holding it is an error. herdr with `worktree` uses `worktree.create`; older herdr falls back to `git worktree add` + `workspace.create`; Orca uses its runtime's `worktree.create` (#5325), after refusing a branch checked out in another worktree, which Orca would rename instead of failing. On failure it returns git's `fatal:` line; Paseo, while its bridge is connected (`caps.workspaces`, #6295), makes the worktree itself as a Paseo workspace in Paseo's worktrees folder (runtime ↔ node `workspace.create`), after the same checks: `path` must be in the folder prepare returns (only its last element can be chosen, and it is taken as Paseo names a folder: `[a-z0-9]` runs joined by single hyphens, at most 50 characters; a name with nothing left, or one whose folder exists at all, an empty one too, is refused, since Paseo would put the worktree beside it), `auto_name` lets Paseo name the branch and the folder, and a parent other than the source is refused; with Paseo not connected it fails with a sentence saying so, without `worktree_unsupported`. Only while Paseo is one of the computer's enabled engines: a bridge that is connected but not enabled makes, lists and deletes no workspaces. A whole create (prepare, the checks and Paseo's work) has one deadline, 145 s, inside the hub's 150 s; running out of it says so rather than the hub timing out. An engine with no checkouts (Cindy, a runtime without `caps.workspaces`, or a host without checkout support) fails with code `worktree_unsupported` (message `unsupported: <kind> cannot do this`), which the assistant reads as "run an inferred task in its own directory"; a repository with no commit on any ref (an unborn HEAD and nothing fetched) fails both with code `worktree_no_commits` and a sentence in the request's `locale` instead of git's "invalid reference" (#5548) |
| `terminal.watch` / `terminal.unwatch` | `{session_id, control?: {cols, rows, takeover}}`; watch → `{cols, rows, control}`, after which the node pushes `terminal.frame`. A watch while already pushing reopens a stream (new epoch, starting from a full frame). If herdr has no observe it reports `unsupported: …`. With `control` the node takes over via `herdr terminal session control` (reply has `control: true`; old nodes lack this field); if the slot is taken and there's no `takeover`, it errors with `code: attach_busy` |
| `git.pull` | `{cwd}` → `{status, updated}`, same safe pull as REST |
| `git.branches` / `git.pr` / `git.stage` / `git.commit` / `git.push` / `git.switch` / `git.stash` / `git.pr_create` / `git.pr_merge` | #6121, params and answers as the REST above |
| `fs.list` / `git.status` / `git.diff` / `git.show` / `git.log` | same as REST (same param names) |
| `git.review` | #151: `{cwd, scope, base?, paths?}` → the same answer as REST `git/review`; refusals are `rpc.Error` codes (`not_git`, `bad_scope`, `bad_base`, `no_default_branch`, `no_merge_base`) |
| `fs.watch` | #2439: `{dirs: [{path, cwd}], git: [cwd]}` → `{ok}`, **replaces the whole set** of folders and Git directories the node watches (at most 32 folders and 8 Git directories; an empty set stops the watch loop). Old nodes report unknown method; the hub logs a line and the page keeps refreshing manually |
| `file.read` | `{path, cwd, offset}` → same as REST `file` (old nodes don't know `offset`, and their reply has no `offset` / `next`) |
| `fs.stat` | `{paths, cwd}` → `{stats}`, same as REST `stat` (old nodes report unknown method, and the phone links no paths) |
| `session.items` | `{session_id, user_inputs?, before_seq, limit, turns, after_seq, lazy_images, fold_work, from_seq, through_seq}` → `{items, has_more, more_after, history, to_seq, from_seq}` (with `through_seq` it is the folded rows: `{items, more}`) (`from_seq` is only present in `after_seq` requests; without `lazy_images: true` the node reads image data back, for compatibility with old hubs). With `user_inputs:true`, returns only `{total, inputs:[{id,seq}], history}` for the full conversation (#2338), with no body/image data; runtime sessions use their existing item pages server-side. The richer #2071 contract remains independent. |
| `session.image` | `{session_id, item_id}` → `Image{mime, data}` (the node's items don't keep image data in memory; it rereads that line at the recorded line offset) |
| `session.item` | `{session_id, item_id}` → `Item` (full text, no images) |
| `session.watch` / `session.unwatch` | `{session_id, since_seq?}`; after watch the node reads new lines every 250ms and pushes `session.items` (with `history` / `from_seq` / `to_seq`); with `since_seq` it first resends everything after it, 500 items per page. The hub sends only one watch / unwatch at a time per session, and when its turn comes decides which to send, or whether to send at all, by the subscriber count at that moment (the node does nothing on a watch for a session already watched, so the two arriving out of order would leave the last subscriber without live content); a failed one is retried next time. An App's connection only counts the subscription when it reads `subscribe` / `unsubscribe` (and when it ends); the call itself is made off its read loop, so a node slow to answer does not keep the App's other messages unread, and a subscribe's backlog still follows its watch (#5915) |
| `session.close` | `{session_id, force?: bool}`: `force: true` is the confirmation-only close used above; refuses a session no longer blocked, and never approves its dialog |
| `session.archive` / `session.unarchive` | `{session_id}` → `{native, already?, via?, reason?}`: archive (restore) the session in the tool that owns it, with the tool's own reversible archive; the manager calls them after the user archives or restores it in Persona ("Agent session archives"). `native: "done"` (now in the asked state; `already: true` when it was before, with no call to the tool; `via`: `app_server`, `cli` or `runtime`) or `"unsupported"` (no archive of its own: Claude Code, Orca, opencode, pi, a runtime without `caps.archive`, an older Codex with no `archive` command; `reason` says why). Codex: `thread/archive` / `thread/unarchive` on a connected app-server of the thread's `CODEX_HOME`, else `codex archive|unarchive <thread>` with that `CODEX_HOME` (`docs/integrations/codex.md`, "Archive"). Refused, to be tried again later: `code: native_archive_busy` (working), `native_archive_live` (a Codex process still has the thread open and no app-server can close it), `native_archive_failed` (the tool refused or failed; what Codex did is read back from where the rollout is). A runtime's session whose runtime is away is refused like `session.close`. Old nodes report unknown method (the manager treats it as unsupported). Nothing is deleted, and the node moves no file itself |
| `session.fork` | `{session_id, at_item_id}` → `{session_id}`: see HTTP `/fork`; old nodes report unknown method |
| `session.stop` | `{session_id, retire?: bool}` → `{stopped}`: quits the Agent (Ctrl+C twice, up to three rounds, until the engine no longer shows it in its pane) and **keeps its terminal**, the tab with the shell it ran in (#4754); `stopped: false` when it isn't running. With `retire` only a still Agent: working, waiting on the user, starting, or another tool's returns `code: not_retirable`. Without it (a cancelled task) a working Agent is stopped too; a session with no terminal (another tool's, an engine that runs Agents itself) returns `code: no_terminal`, which the assistant then closes with `session.close`. An Agent that does not quit returns `not_stopped`; its pane is never closed to make it go. Old nodes report unknown method (the assistant treats it as refused: nothing closed). See `docs/assistant/todos.md` ("Stop Agents of completed tasks") |
| `session.retire` | `{session_id, close_terminal?: bool}` → `{closed}`: what hubs before #4754 ask for a finished task's Agent; a node since #4754 answers like `session.stop` with `retire` (the Agent stops, its terminal stays). With `close_terminal` (the user's **Archive and close**) it closes the pane after the same checks, as `session.close` does; an older node closes it either way. Refusals: `code: not_retirable` |
| `file.upload.begin` | `{name, size, dest?, dir?, cwd?, conflict?, health_dir?}` → `{upload_id, chunk_bytes, dest?, health_dir?}` (over the limit reports `too_large`; `dest` `dir` / `inbox` is echoed, see "Sending files") |
| `file.upload.chunk` | `{upload_id, offset, data}` (data is base64; offset must continue from what was received) → `{received}`; any error voids the whole upload |
| `file.upload.end` / `file.upload.abort` | `{upload_id}`; end checks the size and renames → `{path, name, size}` |
| `interaction.resolve` | `{id, resolution}` |
| `port.probe` | `{port}` → `{port, listening, http, title?}`: one GET / (Host is `localhost:<port>`) |
| `model.http` | `{method?, url, header?, body?, timeout_ms?}` → `{status, header?, body?}`: one request of a direct API connection that sends through this computer (`docs/assistant/model-config.md` "Sending through a computer", capability `model_http`). `method` is `GET` or `POST` (left out: `POST`), `url` http(s) without user info; `body` is base64. The node sends it with its own network and proxy settings, never follows a redirect, reads the answer (a whole event stream) to its end, at most 16 MB, and returns it with `body` base64. `header` carries the key for this call only: the node never logs, keeps or repeats it, and errors name the URL at most. `timeout_ms` bounds the whole request (60 s when left out, at most 10 minutes); the manager's `rpc.cancel` ends it sooner. A node without the capability gets `node_outdated` from the manager |

The node runs the launcher once, headless, as a start does (its environment, settings and default model; `model` / `effort` override them), in a temporary directory removed afterwards, with no tools, no MCP servers, no hooks and no session kept; Claude Code gets `system` as its system prompt and `prompt` on stdin. `launcher` must be one this computer offers or the manager vouches for (`configured`), and only Claude Code launchers answer (`codex exec` can't be kept from its tools). At most two runs at a time on a computer, a run waiting for its slot within its time; `timeout_ms` bounds it (2 minutes when left out, at most 10) and `rpc.cancel` ends it sooner. Errors: code `model_run_timeout` (no answer in time), `model_run_logged_out` (the CLI is not logged in there), otherwise the end of what the CLI printed without keys, URLs or addresses. The prompt and the answer are never logged. A node without the capability gets `node_outdated` from the manager |
| `clipboard.get` | `{}` → `{kind, text?, image?:{mime, data}}` (see `GET /api/v1/machines/{mid}/clipboard`): the clipboard of the session the node runs in; text first, else an image as PNG. Errors carry a code: `clipboard_unsupported` (message: a reason code, `no_display` / `no_tool` / `no_session` / `os`), `too_large`, `clipboard_failed` (message: what failed, never the content). Capability `clipboard` ([clipboard.md](../operations/clipboard.md)) |
| `clipboard.set` | `{text}` or `{image:{mime:"image/png"\|"image/jpeg", data}}` → `{}`; also `clipboard_bad_image` when the bytes are not the image type named. Whether the user allowed it is the manager's to check, not the node's |
| `preview.servers` | `{cwd}` → the `…/preview/servers` answer: the nearest `.claude/launch.json` from `cwd` up to the repository's root, each entry probed (capability `preview`, [preview](../web/preview.md)) |
| `preview.start` | `{cwd, name, workspace, kind?}` → `{pane, terminal, port}`: a new tab in the workspace named after the entry, in its folder, typing its command (each word quoted, `env K=V` in front for its `env`). For a runtime's workspace (a Paseo session's, #6295), the terminal engine's workspace whose folder holds the entry's, the deepest (one in the home folder or at the root holds everything and does not count), else a new workspace in the entry's folder with the tab named after it; never one that only happens to be first. With no host that opens tabs: refusal `preview_no_terminal` |
| `preview.open` | `{id, port, path, w, h, dpr, mobile}` → `{browser}`: a tab of the node's headless browser at `http://localhost:<port><path>`, on stream `id` whose bytes are length-prefixed frames (`internal/preview`); `port_gone`, `no_browser`, `browser_failed` |
| `computer.status` | `{}` → `Computer` (`enabled` filled in by the hub): probes the local cua-driver (path, version, daemon, `permissions status --json`) and the desktop session (IOConsoleUsers from `ioreg`: active / locked / away). | `computer.call` | `{session, tool, args, call_id?}` → `{output?, text?, image?}`: `cua-driver call --screenshot-out-file … <tool>`, args via stdin, `session` filled into the args (element_token stays valid across calls); screenshots go separately in `image` (`{mime, data, width, height}`, converted to JPEG when smaller than PNG). Only reads and `run_script` / `run_steps` are accepted; if the daemon isn't running it first runs `open -g -b com.trycua.driver`. Not installed: error code `not_installed`. `call_id` is a canonical UUID present only for an opted-in MCP call and correlates a nested LCU elicitation with it. No originating-machine field is sent; older nodes ignore the optional id |

| `browser.status` / `browser.install` / `browser.open` / `browser.cancel` | `{}` → `Browser`: whether ego lite is installed, first-time setup, stats, read-only probes. Install downloads the official DMG, verifies its signature (Team `JGQLC6YQYJ`) and notarization, then ditto's it into Applications, keeping quarantine. Open runs `open` on it on that Mac |
| `browser.call` | `{session, script?, look?, full?, screenshot?, timeout_ms?}` → `{output, image?}`: `ego-browser nodejs` (script via stdin) runs the assistant's script in the task space named `session` (`task` and `page` are ready-made), or takes a snapshot for look. The last result line is marked with `@@persona-browser@@` (NUL can't be used: ego drops the whole output); screenshots go separately in `image` |
| `plugin.node.have` / `plugin.node.put.begin` / `.chunk` / `.commit` | the plugin's package on this computer (`docs/extensions/extensions.md` ("Programs running on computers")): `{id, version, digest}` → `{have}`; `begin {id, version, digest, size}` → `{upload_id}`, `chunk {upload_id, offset, data}` (in order, 1 MB), `commit {upload_id}`: verifies sha256 and unpacks into `~/.persona/plugins/<id>/<version>/` |
| `plugin.node.start` / `plugin.node.stop` | `start {id, name, version, command, args?, env?, rpc, http?, keep, lease_seconds, init}` → `{id, version, state, error?}`: starts it (if identical to what is running, leaves it alone and just renews the lease; if a new version doesn't come up within 30 seconds, rolls back to the previous version and reports an error). `init` is the program's `initialize` (config, secrets sent to the computer, never written to disk). `stop {id}` |
| `plugin.node.sync` / `plugin.node.renew` / `plugin.node.status` | `sync {programs: [{id, version, digest}], installed: [id]}` → `{programs: [state]}`: those not in `programs` are stopped and their packages deleted; those not in `installed` are deleted along with their data. `renew {ids, lease_seconds}`; `status` → `{programs}` |
| `plugin.node.dial` | `{id, plugin}` → `{}`: connects to this plugin program's HTTP socket and opens a stream `id` (after that, bytes flow over `stream.*` events, same as `port.dial`); if the program isn't running or doesn't serve HTTP it returns `code: not_running` |
| `plugin.node.call` | `{id, method, params?}` → the program's answer: a plugin protocol method (programs on the hub call it via `nodes.call`); if the program isn't running it returns `code: not_running` |
| `port.dial` | `{id, port, keep_awake?, pair?, link?, attach?}` → `{}`, or `{link: 1}` when it opened a screen session for 5900 with `pair` (`link`; `attach` rejoins a live one without dialing, else `session_gone`; [computer-use.md](../extensions/computer-use.md) "Live screen routes (#6398)"): connects to this local port (the address it was bound to at scan time, otherwise 127.0.0.1 then ::1; local only) and opens a stream `id`; if nothing is listening it errors with `code: port_gone`. After that both sides pass bytes over the `stream.*` events below. On a Mac a paired 5900 stream is also read for the phone's pixel scroll records (RFB client message type 200), which never reach Screen Sharing ([computer-use.md](../extensions/computer-use.md) "Pixel scrolling (#7775)") |
| events `plugin.node.state` / `plugin.node.event` | node → hub: `{id, version, state, error?}` (came up, stopped on lease expiry), `{id, event, params}` (events the program sends; the hub forwards them to programs on the hub) |
| `credential.gh_token` | `{host}` → `{token}`: runs `gh auth token --hostname <host>` non-interactively on this machine, for the GitHub connector (`github.auth.from_machine`). Only the hub can call it (the hook / MCP `node.sock` doesn't accept it); the token is never logged. gh not installed reports `code: no_gh`; not signed in (or signed in via the keychain, unreadable over ssh) reports `code: not_signed_in`; old nodes report unknown method |
| `connector.list` | → `{connectors:[{id, status, error?, guide?, via}]}`: connectors this computer itself can provide (currently only `imessage` on Mac; other systems return an empty list). `status` is `ok` / `not_configured` (no Messages data) / `no_permission` (no Full Disk Access; `guide` gives step-by-step instructions to enable it on this Mac, worded two ways depending on whether `via` is `ssh` or a resident `launchd` node) / `error` |
| `connector.chats` | `{id, limit?, before?, keep?}` → `{chats:[{id, name, group?, members:[{handle, name?}], services, last, preview?, from_me?, unread?}], more?, before?}`: chats, newest first. One person's chats across iMessage / SMS / RCS count as one; each group counts separately. `id` is a hash (`imessage-<12 chars>`) and contains no phone number. Read-only. `keep: contacts` (used by the Inbox and assistant) lists only chats handed to Persona (see `connector.changes`); the App's own browsing doesn't pass it |
| `connector.older` | `{id, chat, limit?, before?, keep?}` → `{chat, messages:[{id, at, kind: message\|event, from_me?, sender?, text?, service?, attachments?:[{kind, name, mime, size}], reply_to?, edited?, unsent?, unread?, undecoded?}], more?, before?}`: a chat's latest page or the page before `before`, oldest first. Tapbacks don't count as messages; attachments are descriptions only. No permission reports `code: no_permission`; no such chat (or, with `keep: contacts`, it isn't handed to Persona) reports `code: no_chat`. Only the hub can call it; nothing is logged (no numbers or bodies); old nodes report unknown method |
| `connector.changes` | `{id, cursor?, limit?, days?, keep?}` → `{batches:[{chat, messages}], next, more?}`: messages that came in after `cursor` (message ROWID), batched per chat, oldest first, for the hub's knowledge base and Inbox (when "Hand to Persona" is on). The first time (no `cursor`) it starts `days` (default 30) days back. `keep` defaults to `contacts`: only chats with someone from the address book among the members, or chats I've spoken in; `all` gives everything. Verification codes are masked; `next` moves past everything read (including what wasn't returned) |
| `connector.search` | `{id, query, limit?, days?, keep?}` → `{hits:[{chat, message}]}`: messages from the last `days` (default 365) days whose text contains `query`, newest first (the assistant's `imessage_search`); `keep` and masking as above. Matching only; `query` is never spliced into SQL |
| `codex.answer` | `{session_id, id, resolution}`: answers a Codex card the node listed (`docs/integrations/codex.md` ("Questions and approvals")); a refusal is an error with `code`, and nothing is typed |

`git.status` also accepts `{cwd, identity_only: true}` for manager authorization matching. It reads local metadata only and returns `{version: 1, path_resolved?, is_repo, cwd, root?, common_dir?, origin?, head_oid?}`. `path_resolved: true` certifies physical path resolution before cleaning parent segments; managers require it for paths named by standing-authorization cards. Older nodes omit it and those cards remain manual. `cwd` and Git paths are resolved on the node; `origin` is a credential-free canonical repository identifier. Linked worktrees share `common_dir`, the only cross-directory repository authorization evidence. Clones can share `origin`, but a copied URL proves no identity; independent clones require separate standing grants. Other status requests keep their existing response.

Stash selections (#1480) carry the full lowercase object ID (`oid`, SHA-1 or SHA-256) from the list.
`apply`, `pop` and `drop` require both `index` and `oid`; missing identities and moved, removed or mismatched
entries return `git_stash_stale` before applying or deleting anything. Refresh and explicitly reselect; never
retry a mutation automatically. Apply uses the OID, so a later stack change cannot substitute other content.
Pop holds the removal boundary across OID application and deletion; conflicts retain the stash. An apply or pop that
stopped on merge conflicts (git printed `CONFLICT` and paths are unmerged) is `git_stash_conflicted` with those `files`, not
`git_conflict`, whose files are ones the apply would overwrite and so left alone (#1885). Removal uses
Git's files-backend common-directory reference/reflog locks (also shared by terminal Git and linked worktrees),
rewrites the reflog chain and updates the reference, including a packed final reference. Reftable, symbolic or
redirected stash storage, and installed reference-transaction hooks return `git_stash_unsupported` before pop/drop;
OID-only apply remains available. Publication failures are errors and may require inspection after content was applied.
Older clients sending only an index are refused by new nodes. New clients disable apply/pop/drop on older-node rows
without a valid `oid` and show an update notice; push/list remain available. The hub forwards these fields unchanged.

Streams (`internal/streams`, both directions): `stream.data {id, data}` (data is base64, at most 32 KB at a time), `stream.ack {id, n}` (n bytes were written out;
at most 512 KB unacknowledged per direction, and the sender stops and waits when it reaches that), `stream.close {id, error?}` (this end's connection dropped; the other side finishes writing what it received, then closes). The hub registers the stream before sending `port.dial`, and the node replies only after it has connected and registered, so bytes never arrive before the stream does. A `stream.close` can still arrive before the stream does (the hub gave up on a slow `port.dial` or `preview.open`): each side remembers for 2 minutes (at most 1024) the ids it heard closed without holding them, and refuses to register such an id, so the node answers that call with an error and closes its connection. The first `stream.data` for an id a side does not hold (it ended there, or that side restarted since) gets `stream.close {id, error}` back. Stream ids are therefore never reused between the same two ends: the hub's carry a token of its process, since a node's streams outlive a hub restart.

hub → node events (handled in the order sent): `terminal.input {session_id, text}`, `terminal.resize {session_id, cols, rows}`, `terminal.scroll {session_id, lines, up, column?, row?}` (scroll wheel: herdr hands it to programs that take the mouse, such as Claude Code's full-screen rendering and Codex; otherwise it scrolls herdr's own history.
The node splits it into `lines` one-line events, landing on the `column` / `row` cell, or the center of the screen if not given; `docs/integrations/terminal.md` section 16), `terminal.click {session_id, column, row}` (left button down + up), `terminal.keepalive {session_ids}` (every 20 s, for terminals under takeover; the node lets go after hearing nothing for 75 s).

Full herdr interface (feature `herdr_client`, `docs/integrations/terminal.md` section 24): hub → node RPC `herdr.client.open {client_id, cols, rows, session_id?, focus?}` (`session attach` starts a herdr client inside a PTY; at most 4 per computer, the 5th gets `code: too_many`; unsupported returns `unsupported: …`),
events `herdr.client.input {client_id, data | b64}`, `.resize {client_id, cols, rows}`, `.ack {client_id, bytes}` (cumulative), `.close {client_id}`, `.keepalive {client_ids}` (every 20 s; the node closes after hearing nothing for 75 s); node → hub events `herdr.client.data {client_id, data}` (base64; the node stops reading the PTY when the browser is 256 KB behind), `herdr.client.end {client_id, error}` (client exited, lease expired, browser not reading; not sent for closes the hub requested).

Focus sync (feature `herdr_focus`, `docs/integrations/terminal.md` section 28): hub → node event `herdr.client.focus {client_id, session_id}` (the page is showing another pane: the node has herdr focus it; requests for the same view replace each other; if the pane isn't one the host lists or the view is gone, nothing happens); node → hub event `herdr.focus.changed {workspace_id, tab_id, pane_id, session_id?, source, client_id?}` (herdr's focus changed: `persona` = just requested on behalf of `client_id`'s view, `client` = that client was actually typed in / clicked within 1.5 s, `other` = anything else; herdr's event itself doesn't say who changed it).

node → hub events: `fs.changed {dirs?, git?}` (#2439: the listing of a folder in `fs.watch` changed (names, sizes, times), or a Git directory's `git status` changed; the hub turns it into `fs_changed` for the relevant pages), `terminal.frame {session_id, epoch, seq, full, cols, rows, data}` (frames less than 30 ms apart are merged by the node into one: diff bytes are concatenated, and a full frame drops the diffs before it), `terminal.end {session_id, error, control?, taken?}` (the stream stopped and can't restart: the session isn't running, herdr keeps refusing; with `control`, the takeover ended: `taken` means someone else grabbed it, otherwise the lease expired),
`session.items {session_id, items, history, from_seq, to_seq}`, `session.delta {session_id, text}` (the message being written as one text, "" when there is none: the headless assistant's from its stream, a Claude session Persona started from its MessageDisplay hook while the session is watched, a runtime's as it sends it; `docs/integrations/claude-integration.md` "Live replies (MessageDisplay)"), `session.live {session_id, live}` (status line of a watched, working Claude (on hosts that can read the screen: herdr, herdr-core, Orca), sent only on change, with a trailing `null` when it ends; see "Live status"), `session.echo {session_id, client_msg_id, text, images, sent_at, after_seq, line?}` (pushed once when the node records a send and once when it recognizes its line; the hub stores it in `sent_messages.echo`; an already-recognized one is never overwritten by a late "still waiting"), `sessions.changed {sessions}` (a list byte-identical to the last one written on this connection is not written again; after a `sessions.revs`, an answer to `sessions.list`, an engine switch or a reconnect the next list goes even when it is the same, #2439),
`sessions.revs {revs}` (checked every second, only changed revs are sent; when the list itself changes, revs go with `sessions.changed`),
`usage {buckets:[{minute, model, in, cache_write, cache_read, out, req}], full, load, cpus}` (every 10 seconds, only changed minutes, with full per-minute values;
the first one after connecting is `full: true` with the whole last 26 hours; `docs/apple/live-activity.md` ("Usage")),
`metrics {sample: MetricSample}` (every 10 seconds, aligned to whole 10 seconds; the manager stores it in `machine_metrics`, `docs/server/machines.md`),
`codex.interactions {interactions}` (all open Codex / compatible forks questions and approvals on this machine, sent in full on any change; the manager adds and removes cards; old versions that don't know it keep using screen cards).
(All of these first reach the manager connected to this computer; interactions, status, usage and monitoring belong to it, and it forwards what the App needs to the hub; see "Computer events" below.)

node → manager / hub requests (`interaction.create`, `computer.elicit`, `mcp.*`, `assistant.lark`, `lark.sent`, `mail.attachment` answered by the manager; `notify` answered by the hub):
- `interaction.create {interaction}` → `{resolution}` (blocks until handled / expired; on expiry returns `{"dismiss":true}`). When the manager answers from an "Always allow in this session" it kept (or one a card answered meanwhile covers) rather than from an answer to this card, the resolution has `"remembered":true` next to `allow` and `always`; only the manager sets it, an App's answer never carries it (the sent-as-user ledger records such a write as `conversation_always`)
- `mcp.tools {}` → `{tools}`; `mcp.call {name, args, session_id, wait_updates?, call_id?}` → `{content, is_error, error_kind?, retry_after?}` (`error_kind` is the failure category: `declined` the user or `connector_gate` didn't agree, `unavailable` the connector isn't signed in / can't connect, `rate_limited` rate limited; `retry_after` is how many seconds of rate limiting remain. Included only when the hub knows; `personad tool` sets its exit code from it, #3779). `wait_updates` and the node's canonical UUID `call_id` are present together only for an opted-in call on a capable hub. A malformed or oversized id disables wait reporting without failing the tool call or publishing an event
- `computer.elicit {conversation, params, call_id?}` → the MCP elicitation result: LCU's nested permission or question, shown through the existing cards. An opted-in outer `computer.call` carries the same canonical UUID `call_id`, which the node includes here. The manager resolves only a live id in its own registry, joining the originating machine's existing reporter and card state; the eliciting node cannot choose a destination machine. It reports `approval` or `answer` and then restores the newest still-open card or the call's base state. An unknown, malformed, oversized or completed id gets no reporter and no event, without failing the elicitation
- `lark.sent {command?, method, path, text?, session_id?, message_ref?, let_through}` → `{}`: the node's gate proxy forwarded a write and the API answered with a 2xx; the manager keeps it in the sent-as-user ledger (`docs/extensions/connectors.md` "Sent as the user"). `let_through` is `{kind: "rule", rule: {method, path, body?, action}}`, `{kind: "conversation_always"}`, `{kind: "permission_mode"}` (a classified ordinary write allowed by assistant bypass), or `{kind: "card", interaction_id, answered_by?}`; `text` is at most 4000 characters; `message_ref` is the id the API's answer gave for the message the write made (absent when there was none, the answer could not be read or the id was longer than 200 characters: it is not cut), which the manager keeps only for a route that creates one message in a conversation (`docs/extensions/connectors.md` "Sent as the user"). The computer is the connection's, never a field; `permission_denied` for a computer the manager does not know, `invalid_params` for a read or a `let_through` that is not one of these, `no_database` without a ledger; an older manager reports an unknown method, which the node only logs
- `mail.attachment {account_id, uid, mailbox?, attachment_id, session_id?, assistant?, guest?}` → `{filename, mime, size, data}` (`data` base64): the bytes of a mail attachment for `mail_save_attachment`, which the node answers itself and writes on its machine (`docs/extensions/mail.md` "Saving attachments"). The manager checks the caller as for `mcp.call` (work machine, assistant conversation, guest given the tool), then answers only while the mail connector offers `mail_save_attachment` to it; at most 25 MB (`attachment too large` otherwise). `filename` is the sender's, uncleaned. The computer is the connection's, never a field; an older manager reports an unknown method, which the node returns as the tool's error
- `agents.closeout.check {session_id}` → `{reason?}`: an Agent is about to stop after a turn that did work, without a closeout; the manager answers with the reason to hold the stop with while its `closeout` triage switch is on, and with nothing otherwise (`docs/assistant/agent-work.md` "Closeout"). The node holds a stop at most once per turn (`stop_hook_active`).
- `agents.closeout.brief {session_id, cwd?}` → `{context?}`: an Agent's session is starting (Claude Code's SessionStart hook, in a session with Persona's own hooks); the manager answers with the closeout's form to hand it as the hook's additional context while its `closeout` triage switch is on, and with nothing otherwise or for a review's reviewer (`docs/assistant/agent-work.md` "Closeout"). The node waits 1.5 seconds and asks once per session.
- `assistant.view.check {session_id, message}` → `{reason?}`: the persona-view check on the trusted assistant's Stop; the devices manager passes it through to the hub. The hub decides whether to check based on the session's identity. When reason is non-empty, the node returns decision=block the first time, and stops asking when stop_hook_active=true. Replies up to 1 MB, 4 errors of 2000 characters each; the node waits at most 5 seconds. Not applicable, an old hub, or a disconnect keep the original Stop behavior. This is not a public App / extension action interface, and it accepts no machine identity supplied by the client.
- `launchers.pull {name, own_service?: {agent, known, own, via?}}` → `{launcher: ManagedLauncher}`: a withheld provider's secrets for this connection's computer (that computer's own key when it has one). The manager checks the connection's machine, never params, against the scope and refuses with `launcher_out_of_scope`, or `launcher_own_service` when the provider says `own_service: skip` and the node reports a service of its own (sent only for such a provider), or `launcher_key_unresolved` when the key is a reference that did not resolve; the message is in the user's language. A pending computer is refused like every other request of its
- `notify {title, body?, level?, silent?, id?, session_id?}` → `{sent, reason?}` (`personad notify`: `machine_id` is this connection's machine; extension `actions` / `ui` / `state` are not accepted; otherwise the same as `POST /api/v1/notify`, with mute and "Needs you" preferences applied the same way; old hubs report unknown method)

### Computer link (persona-link, kind link)

Computers the hub can't connect into (laptops) have persona-link connect out to the hub's TLS port and open streams on that link; inside a stream is the RPC above (bytes forwarded as is to that machine's resident node).
Since 2026-11-04, once the hub has checked the credential it hands the link and its streams as is to the manager (`devices.accept` + `GET /api/v1/bus/relay`, "Computers (devices.*)" below); the messages "the hub" sends below are sent by the manager, and close codes are passed through.
When the manager isn't connected, `GET /api/v1/link` returns `503 assistant_offline`. Details in [link.md](../operations/link.md); only what's on the wire is listed here:

- `GET /api/v1/link` (WebSocket, a credential with `role: link`, TLS only, loopback excepted). Text messages, one JSON each:
  - persona-link → hub: `{"type":"hello","machine","version","address","features"?}` (the first message, within 10 seconds), `{"type":"open_failed","id","error"}`,
    `{"type":"presence","active"?,"notifies"?,"ttl_ms"?}` (only from persona-link with a compatible parent: whether you are at this computer and its notifications show, as the link comes up and for every line the parent writes; `ttl_ms` how much longer an active one counts, at most 120000; a missing field is false; [link.md](../operations/link.md) "Presence"),
    `{"type":"rang","interaction_id"}` (only from persona-link with a compatible parent: the parent confirmed the notification of this card, as the summary names it; sent only on the link whose summary listed the card: persona-link numbers its links for the parent, and drops a confirmation for an earlier one; a confirmation only wakes the pushes waiting for it and changes no computer's being a desktop);
    `features` lists what this persona-link takes besides streams: `attention` (the "Needs you" summary below). Older persona-link sends none; older managers ignore it.
  - hub → persona-link: `{"type":"endpoints","endpoints":[{"url","kind"}]}` (https candidates only), `{"type":"open","id"}`,
    `{"type":"node","online","error"}`, `{"type":"attention","attention":{…}}` (only to a link whose hello listed `attention`: once right after `endpoints`, then on every change; a computer waiting to be confirmed or marked `trust: "work"` gets an empty summary, which also takes back what it had; while the hub cannot say which computers wait, nothing new is sent to one not known to be a work computer).
    Both sides ignore a `type` they don't know.
  - `attention` is the "Needs you" summary of the manager that carries the computer, a full snapshot each time ([link.md](../operations/link.md) "Needs you"):
    `{"rev","needs_you","more","web_url"?,"items":[{"machine_id","session_id","title","place","kind","detail","muted","notify","interaction_id"?,"since"?,"route"}]}`.
    `needs_you` is the web app's "Needs you" count (muted agents and agents waiting only on the assistant's decision included), `items` at most 20 of them (one per agent, by its oldest card handed to the user, else its oldest card; newest `since` first, then by machine and session id, so past 20 the oldest are cut; `kind` is `permission` / `plan` / `question` / `screen`), `more` the rest;
    `title` and `place` are at most 80 characters and `detail` 60, an ellipsis included;
    `notify` is whether the phone's push rule would push the item: once a card of the agent is the user's (rung, as the phone is pushed; not a question the assistant is still deciding on; a terminal dialog once the screen card made for it is; a card made again after a reconnect or a restart only when it is known to have rung: a screen card read again as the card that rang), and never when `muted`: clients notify on `notify` alone, the first time an item shows with it (which may be after it was listed without it: the assistant handed its question to the user), and `muted` is for showing; `since` is RFC 3339 UTC to the second; `route` is the web app's `/s/<machine>/<session>`, percent-encoded; `web_url` is the hub's https `public_url` (sub-path included), else the `address` of the hello.
    `rev` is a hash of the rest: the same summary has the same `rev`. Nothing needs you: `needs_you: 0`, `items: []`.
  - Close codes: 4001 replaced by a new link from the same machine, 4002 credential revoked, 4003 hello doesn't match the credential, 1001 hub shutting down. Both sides ping every 10 seconds and disconnect after 5 seconds without a pong (configurable).
    When hub.json sets `link.ping_seconds` / `link.ping_timeout_seconds`, `endpoints` also carries `ping_ms`, `ping_timeout_ms` (milliseconds), and persona-link uses them on this link
    (clamped to 50 milliseconds through 10 minutes; ignored unless both are positive). When not set, these two fields aren't sent, and old persona-link doesn't know them either.
- `GET /api/v1/link/stream?id=<id from open>` (WebSocket, same credential, permessage-deflate): binary messages whose content is the RPC byte stream;
  the hub treats it as failed if it doesn't arrive within 15 seconds. When the link drops, its streams drop with it.

## hub ↔ hub (linked hubs, [mesh.md](../server/mesh.md))

- `POST /api/v1/peer/pair` (`Authorization: Bearer jx_…`, the other side's link code): `{hub_id,name,version,fp,tls_port,endpoints,token,center,term}` →
  the same fields (`token` is the link credential given back to the other side; `center` / `term` are the center and term of the code issuer's group: the side using the code joins that group). Invalid / used / expired code: 401; this hub has no TLS: 409.
- `GET /api/v1/peer` (WebSocket, TLS only, a credential with `role: peer`, permessage-deflate): binary messages whose content is the byte stream of the JSON-line RPC from hub ↔ node above:
  - Calls: `hello {hub_id,name,version,epoch}` (once each way), `stream.open {id}` (the stream carries one HTTP/1.1 connection to the other side's peer server),
    `relay {to,from,ttl,method,params}` (`creds.import {tokens:[{id,name,kind,role,created_at,last_seen,hash}]}` → `{added}`: a member hands credentials to the center;
    `creds.revoked {tokens:[{id,name,kind,role,hash}]}` (other fields unused) → `{revoked}`: tells the group's hubs about revoked credentials;
    `pair.code {}` → a pairing code: `personad hub pair` on a member), `unpair {}`;
  - One-way: `rec` (the hub's record: links, `center`, `term`, computers in hub.json), `stream.data` / `stream.ack` / `stream.close`.
  - Close codes: 4011 duplicate link, 4012 unlinked, 4013 can't keep up sending, 1001 hub shutting down. Both sides ping every 10 seconds and disconnect after 5 seconds without a pong (configurable).
- HTTP on a stream always carries `X-Persona-Peer-Ttl` (starts at 8, decremented each hop; at 0 returns `508 mesh_loop`) and is forwarded hop by hop to the target hub:
  - App requests a member forwards to the center: as is (including `Authorization`), plus `X-Persona-Peer-Source: <lan|public> <client address> <tls|plain>` (the member's judgment of the source).
    Can't forward: `503 center_unreachable`; forwarding failed: `502 hub_unreachable`.
  - Node streams the center opens through a member: `GET /api/v1/peer/node`, `Upgrade: persona-node`, `X-Persona-Peer-Node: <member hub_id>/<machine id>`, `X-Persona-Peer-From: <center hub_id>`;
    the member returns `101`, followed by the node's byte stream. A request from a hub that isn't its center gets 403; not in hub.json gets 404; can't open gets 502 (`error` is the reason).
- Admin interface (after signing in to the admin UI, [admin.md](../operations/admin.md)): `GET /api/v1/admin/mesh`, `GET /api/v1/admin/peers`, `POST /api/v1/admin/peers/code`, `POST /api/v1/admin/peers`,
  `POST /api/v1/admin/peers/probe`, `DELETE /api/v1/admin/peers/{hub_id}`, `POST /api/v1/admin/peers/{hub_id}/center`, `GET /api/v1/admin/routes`;
  the same set under `/api/v1/admin/cli/…` is for the command line on the hub machine (loopback + main token).

## hub → connector (kind service, [link.md](../operations/link.md) ("Passive mode"), [mesh.md](../server/mesh.md) ("kind service"))

- The hub connects to `<address>` pinned to the `fp` in the pairing link (optionally via a `socks5://` proxy): `POST /api/v1/connector/pair {code,token,machine,hub_id,hub_name}` once;
  after that `GET /api/v1/connector/info` (every 30 seconds, liveness and RTT) and `GET /api/v1/connector/stream` (WebSocket, the node's byte stream), both with `Authorization: Bearer <credential>`.
  `info` answers `{"machine","version","features"?,"attention_rev"?}`: `features` as in a link's hello, `attention_rev` the `rev` of the summary the connector holds (absent: none). Older connectors answer only the first two; older managers read only those.
- `POST /api/v1/connector/attention` (same credential), body one `attention` object above and nothing after it but white space, the whole body at most 64 KiB → `204`; `400` without a `rev`, with anything else in the body or over the cap, `401` with another credential. The manager posts only to a connector whose `info` listed `attention`:
  on every change, and after an `info` whose `attention_rev` is not the summary's (a post that failed, a connector that restarted). The connector drops the summary when another hub pairs and after 2 minutes without the hub coming in.
  When hub.json sets a heartbeat (`link`), the stream request also carries `X-Persona-Ping: <interval ms> <timeout ms>`, and the connector pings on this stream accordingly; when not set it's omitted, and old connectors don't know it.
- 401: don't dial again for 5 minutes; 429: follow `Retry-After`; 503 `node_unavailable`: show the reason and back off as usual; stream closed with 4002: needs re-pairing, stop trying; 1001: back off as usual.

## Bus (service ↔ hub, `GET /api/v1/bus`)

The hub is meant to become just a channel: the assistant (and later other services) is a separate process that connects out to the hub's bus and stays connected, rather than living inside the hub. The hub knows nothing of any service's business semantics.
By default the hub starts the assistant as its own child process (`personad assistant`); the assistant can also run elsewhere (`docs/assistant/assistant.md` ("Process")).
The channel itself is authentication, handshake, a roster, dispatch by method name, and calls in both directions; the assistant and hub call each other through it; see "Methods the assistant uses" below.

**Identities and tokens**

- One identity per service. Currently there is only one role, `manager` (one manager process, the assistant; ids look like `assistant`, start with a lowercase letter, at most 32 characters). The table keeps a role column so adding other roles later needs no table change; tokens for other roles are rejected at upgrade today (401).
- Tokens start with `jb_` and can only open `/api/v1/bus`: neither device tokens nor the main token can open the bus, and `jb_` can't open App endpoints either (401). The hub stores only the sha256 (table `bus_identities`, migration 0311).
- Only `Authorization: Bearer` is accepted, not `?token=`. Public sources need TLS (otherwise `403 tls_required`); failure counting and `429 rate_limited` are the same as for App endpoints; loopback and LAN aren't counted.
- Creating and revoking are functions inside the hub (`createBusToken`, `revokeBusToken`, in `server/internal/hub/bustokens.go`). Every time the hub starts it creates one for the assistant and passes it via the child process's stdin;
  when the assistant runs elsewhere, create one with `personad hub assistant-token` (`assistant.external` in `docs/operations/config.md`). There's no endpoint or UI.
  Creating again for the same identity replaces the old token: the old one stops working immediately, and connections using it are closed with 4002.
- Member hubs in a linked group don't forward the bus to the center: a service belongs to whichever hub it connects to.
- The managers' roster, installation codes and revocation are described in `docs/assistant/managers.md` (`GET /i/<code>` is the install script and `GET /i/<code>/docker` the one for a container: no credential, and fetching them does not use the code up). Every manager may use every bus method and event: the hub keeps what each reports as its own (`docs/assistant/managers.md` "What the hub keeps of each manager"). An identity with role `manager` is a manager. The roster also records the location it reported at its last handshake and `last_seen` (migration 0419); a new manager exchanges a one-time installation code for a token (`POST /api/v1/bus/join`, no credentials required).

**Managers (`/api/v1/managers`, answered by the hub itself)**

| Method | Path | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/api/v1/managers` | `{managers:[{id, name, online, default?, builtin?, host?, os?, arch?, deploy?, version?, since?, last_seen?, installing?, needs_update?, inbox_needs_you?}], default, bot_conflicts?:[{platform, managers:[id, ...]}]}`: `needs_update` is `true` for an online manager whose `manager.hello` named no `config.own` (a build from before managers read their own `manager.json`: it runs on its built-in defaults, "Handshake" below); conflicts name managers sharing an enabled Feishu bot or bound WeChat account (latest reports, including offline managers; no raw bot identities). `inbox_needs_you` is how many open items of that manager's inbox are under "Needs you" (the listed items' `status` `action`, the ones not triaged yet and the connectors' among them: what `GET /api/v1/inbox?sources=all` lists open with that status for it), an integer ≥ 0 the manager reports itself (`inbox.needs_you`, "Methods the assistant uses" below); it is absent when not known (the manager is offline or being installed, runs a build from before it reported one, or could not read its stored items), which is not 0. Agents waiting for the user are not in it. The default manager first, installations in progress last; `builtin` is the assistant started by the hub, `installing` is the installation code's expiry time. Roster changes (creation, rename, connection, disconnection, deletion, reported bot identities, and a changed `inbox_needs_you`, one second after it changed so that the numbers changing together are one push) push `{"type":"managers"}` to apps that requested `managers` (`?features=` or `client_hello`'s `features`), without entering the event log (apps reread the list after reconnecting) |
| POST | `/api/v1/managers` | `{name}` (1–40 characters) → 201 `{manager, code, expires_at, commands}`: a one-time installation code, valid for 10 minutes and one use; `commands` are the commands that install it, `{service, join, docker?}` (`docs/assistant/managers.md`, install commands) |
| POST | `/api/v1/managers/{id}/code` | A new code for an existing manager, or for one being installed (its code still good, or expired less than 7 days ago: `installing` in the past) → `{code, expires_at, commands}`; the hub's own assistant returns `409 builtin_manager` |
| POST | `/api/v1/managers/{id}/machines` | `{machine_id}` → `{machine_id, manager, from}`: one of the hub's own machines is carried by this manager from now on (`assistant`: back to the carrier); `400 not_movable` for a machine not in the hub's own list, `409 installing`, `404 no_manager` (removed meanwhile), `503 owners_unknown` (the hub could not read who carries which machine yet) |
| POST | `/api/v1/managers/{id}/sources` | `{source: "mail:<account>", from?}` → `{source, manager, from}`: the source moves from `from` (default: the default manager) to this one; `503 assistant_offline` when either is not connected, `404 no_source`, `409 source_exists` / `source_kind`, `502 source_not_released` (both have it now; moving it again releases it), `502 source_in_doubt` (the import did not answer and neither did the question whether it took it), `404 no_manager` (removed meanwhile). See `docs/assistant/managers.md` "Moving a machine or a source" |
| PATCH | `/api/v1/managers/{id}` | `{name?, default?: true}`: rename or set as default; an installation in progress returns `409 installing` |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/managers/{id}` | Revoke (invalidate the code for an installation in progress) → `{ok}`; the default returns `409 default_manager`, the hub's own manager `409 builtin_manager`, a missing one `404 no_manager` |
| POST | `/api/v1/bus/join` | `{code}` → `{id, name, token, hub_id}`; an incorrect, expired or used code returns `401 bad_install_code` (counted per source); plaintext from the public internet `403 tls_required`, which voids the code it carried (it expires at once). A request may carry `builtin: true` (`persona-manager join --builtin`): a code is traded only by the join of its kind, the built-in manager's (`persona-hub manager-code`) only with it and every other only without it (`409 builtin_code` / `409 not_builtin_code`). The built-in manager's code is also refused while the built-in manager is not a bound service here (`409 builtin_not_service`: `assistant.mode` not `service`, or `assistant.external`) and from a public address (`403 builtin_local_only`); a code the hub cannot look up is refused (`503`). None of these refusals spends the code. Only the latest code of a manager works: a new one voids the unused ones before it, a join uses up all of them |

Editing the roster, creating codes and deleting require a full-permission device (read-only devices get 403).

**Per-manager routing (ownership, `docs/assistant/managers.md` ("Ownership"))**

- **Which manager receives the request**: header `X-Persona-Manager: <id>`, or query `?manager=<id>` (for WebSockets and links opened in a browser; the header wins when both are supplied). Omitted means the default manager (`default` in `GET /api/v1/managers`), except for an extension's token, which acts as the manager whose extension it is (the one that recognized the token) and only as it: routes that name no object, merged lists (its manager's only) and an extension API prefix several managers serve go to it, and naming another manager, or another manager's computer, session, pending card or conversation (in the path, the query or the body), gets `403 other_manager`; `GET /api/v1/machines`, `/interactions` and `/sessions` list its manager's only (`docs/assistant/managers.md`, "Ownership"). An id absent from the roster returns `404 no_manager`; one present but disconnected returns `503 assistant_offline`, as when the assistant was offline before. One exception: on `GET /api/v1/sessions` `manager` is a filter, not routing: the header is not read there and a disconnected manager still gets 200 (see "One manager's sessions").
- **For requests tied to an object, the hub resolves ownership itself; specifying a manager does not override it**: `/machines/{mid}/…` belongs to the computer's manager, `/sessions/{mid}/{sid}/…` to the session's (a manager's own chat belongs to the one reporting it, other chats to the computer's), and `POST /interactions/{id}/resolve` or `/choose` to whoever reported that card. Everything else (assistant page, chats, schedules, Inbox, to-dos, knowledge base, model config, extensions and sources, usage…) uses the header / parameter above. When a list item (an Inbox item, an extension) carries `manager`, include it in requests for that item.
- **The `manager` field**: computers (`GET /api/v1/machines`, `machines` pushes), sessions (`GET /api/v1/sessions`, `sessions` / `sessions_delta` pushes) and pending cards (`GET /api/v1/interactions`, `interaction` pushes) each carry top-level `manager` (the manager id). With one manager, responses are unchanged except for this extra field. A manager's own live updates (`ws.broadcast`, "Messages to the App" below) carry it only when they are another manager's than the assistant the hub starts.
- **Merged lists**: without a manager specified, `GET /api/v1/inbox` (`items`), `/api/v1/todos` (`todos`), `/api/v1/extensions` (`extensions`), `/api/v1/plugins` (`plugins`) and `/api/v1/connectors` (`connectors`) query the default and other connected managers in turn, concatenate their lists (default first) and add `manager` to every item; other fields (`as_of`, `triage`, `can_install`…) come from the default manager. With a manager specified, only its list is returned. Managers that do not answer, or answer with something other than a JSON object (`null` included), are omitted; if none answers, the default manager's response is returned unchanged (for example `503 assistant_offline`).
- **Inbox validator**: the merged `GET /api/v1/inbox` (no manager named, not an extension's token) answers a request that sends `If-None-Match` with `ETag: W/"i1-<32 hex digits>"`, a hash of the answer as localized for that request, leaving out the value of its top-level `as_of`. When a tag sent is that one (weak comparison, or `*`), the answer is `304 Not Modified` without a body, still `Cache-Control: no-store`: the list the client has is still the hub's, and the client keeps it with its `as_of`. Only a 200 that every manager answered with a 2xx carries a tag. The validator is the hub's: the managers are asked for their lists without the client's `If-None-Match`. A request without `If-None-Match` gets no `ETag` and the same answer as before; a client with no tag yet sends one no answer has (the web app sends `W/"i1-"`). Each manager lists its items newest first and, among items of the same moment, by id, so the same items always give the same bytes and the same tag (#4739). The hub may give a request the merged inbox it made for the same query, language, role and managers in the last 2 seconds, unless a manager told the apps `{"type":"inbox"}` or a request other than GET or HEAD went to a manager since. Old hubs send no `ETag` and never 304.
- **Inbox delta**: the merged `GET /api/v1/inbox` (no manager named, not an extension's token) with `since=<cursor>` answers only what changed since the list that cursor names (#4740): `{"as_of", "cursor", "delta": true, "items": […], "removed": [{"id", "manager"}], "triage"}`, where `items` are the items added or changed, each whole and stamped with `manager` as in the whole list, and `removed` the items gone from it, for whatever reason (filed more than three days ago or past the newest 200 done, forgotten, dropped). A client applies them by `(manager, id)`; each manager's items stay together in the managers' order, newest first and by id among items of the same moment.
  - **A cursor the hub cannot follow gets the whole list**, as without `since`, plus `cursor` and no `delta`; the client replaces its list. That covers `0` (what apps send before they hold a cursor), a cursor from before a manager restarted, and one past the 16 lists each manager keeps or unused for an hour. Nothing goes wrong: it costs one whole list.
  - **How the hub works it out**: each manager keeps the lists it answered with a cursor (each item's sum of the bytes it was listed with), and the same items listed again get the same cursor. The merged cursor holds each manager's part; it is opaque to clients. The answer is a delta only when every manager could follow its part; otherwise every manager is asked again without one.
