  The assistant's `ask_user` raised with `wait: false` is `resumable` too (#4928): no hook waits on it, the manager's own record of the question claims the card back after a restart (`docs/assistant/assistant.md`, "Asking without holding the turn"). A waiting `ask_user` that lets go of its turn becomes `resumable` while it is up (#7392): the hub is sent the same card again with the flag set, and its history row is marked.
- Measured locally (fake hub + sandboxed node + real `personad hook`): killing the node during a question and starting a new node 2 seconds later, the hook got the phone's answer after 3.1 seconds, and the hub saw only one id.

### When the manager is away (resident nodes)

A resident node (`personad node --attach`: Persona Link, the Mac's launchd node, a service node) outlives its manager connection. While no connection is served (before the first one, and between one ending and the next), it answers `node.sock` itself, in **standby** (`server/internal/node/spool_standby.go`). Standby only listens where nothing else answers: a `node --stdio` that serves by itself (it reached no resident node in time) keeps the socket, and standby takes it once that one is gone (it looks every 5 seconds).

- `hook`: the event is kept in the spool. Two kinds are not kept: a resumed hook (the node it first reached already reported it), and the events a report-only hook does not report anyway.
  - A hook that would wait on the phone (`PermissionRequest`, `Elicitation`) gets `{"retry":true}` while the **hold** lasts: 10 minutes after the manager was last connected for at least a minute, or after the resident node started. It then asks again with the same `attempt` and gets its card if the manager is back within `nodeclient.ResumeWait` (2 minutes); after that it goes to the terminal. So each such hook waits at most 2 minutes, and the hold only decides whether it waits at all. Connections shorter than a minute (a manager that keeps failing) don't renew the hold.
  - Past the hold, and for every other hook, the answer is `{"output":null}`: the terminal decides, as without a manager. A `PreToolUse` of `Bash` or `AskUserQuestion` is never held.
- `ask`: `{"retry":true}` during the hold (the same 2 minutes per call), else `{"status":"unavailable"}`.
- `notify`: kept → `{"sent":false,"queued":true}`. `personad notify` exits 0; with `--strict` it exits 1 because nothing was sent yet, though the notification still goes out later.
- `ping` / `hook.decided`: `{"ok":true,"standby":true}`.
- Anything else (`mcp.*`, `cli.call`, `launcher.env`…) gets `{"away":true}`, which `nodeclient` turns into `ErrNoNode`: callers do what they always did with no node (`personad mcp` redials a call for 15 seconds, as through a hub restart). The request says it understands that with `away_ok: true`; an `mcp.tools` / `mcp.call` without it (an older `personad mcp` that is still running) gets what a node answers when it cannot reach its manager instead: `{"tools":[],"error":…}`, or an error tool result saying the call was not run.
- **The spool** is `~/.persona/node-spool.jsonl` (0600): one entry per line `{id, at, kind: "hook"|"notify", request, tries?}`, oldest first, at most 500 entries or 1 MiB (the oldest go first, and the node logs how many it dropped). It is the resident node's own: only its standby writes it and only its connections replay it, one at a time. A node serving by itself neither keeps nor replays. The spool survives a restart of the resident node.
- **Replay.** Each connection of the resident node replays the spool before it handles new `hook` / `ask` / `notify` requests (they wait, at most 20 seconds, and a report-only hook at most 2, its own limit being 3), in order. It first waits for the session state from the manager, so report-only events of Persona's own sessions are told apart as they are live and a notification keeps its pane's session. When the first try of `state.load` fails (an error, or no answer in 20 seconds), the replay is **held**: new requests stop waiting at once, the spool stays untried, and the node tries `state.load` again on the same connection after 30 seconds, 1, 2 and 4 minutes, then every 4 minutes, merging what it brings under what the connection already has (live hooks get the state from then on too); the replay runs once it comes. New requests never wait past their own limits: when the replay is slower than that, they go first.
  - A replay that runs after new hooks went ahead of it (a held replay, or a hook that waited out its limit) leaves alone what they moved on: kept hook events of a session that had a new hook since are dropped (the manager already heard newer news of it), and a pane a new hook bound is not bound back to the session it had before. A resumed hook (one asking again, such as a permission standby told to retry) does not count as new: it reports nothing itself, so its kept copy is still handed over.
  - A hook entry gets the bookkeeping a live hook gets (turn counters with the original time, pane binding, transcript path) and a `hook.event` with `spool_id` and `spooled_at`. It never creates a card, and SessionStart's herdr restore and the assistant's view repair are not replayed. Managed AskUserQuestion entries also restore their PreToolUse id / hook-attempt pairing and PostToolUse completion, so a terminal answer spooled while the manager was away completes the matching resumed PermissionRequest instead of creating another phone card.
  - A notification goes through the usual `notify` request with `spool_id` (5 seconds at most each).
  - An entry leaves the file once it was handed over: a hook event once written to the connection, a notification once the manager answered. The node takes those out together, in one rewrite of the file every 64 entries and when the pass ends (also when it ends early), so the file is at most 64 entries behind the replay; standby adds an entry by appending to the file. When the connection ends mid-replay, the rest stays for the next one. A notification the manager refused, did not answer in 5 seconds, or could not take now stays too (the rest goes on, so hook events keep their order; once one times out or the manager says the hub is away, the other notifications are not tried in that pass). One that can never be sent (empty, not JSON) is dropped at once.
  - **Retries on the same connection.** The kept notifications are tried again on the same connection after 30 seconds, 1, 2 and 4 minutes, then every 4 minutes while any is left; new requests do not wait for this. One is dropped after 5 failed tries (refused, or not answered in 5 seconds: about 7 minutes of refusals). "Not now" answers do not count, so they only wait: `spool_busy` (the manager still has an earlier try) and `hub_away` (the manager has no connection to the hub, or the link was down before the call went out; both codes in `server/internal/nodeproto`), and neither does a call that times out as its connection drops (the node looks for the close for a quarter of a second).
  - Entries older than a day are dropped unsent. The day counts from when standby took the entry, not from a first refusal: what a notification or hook event says dates from then (a day-old "build finished" is no news), and a refused notification no longer waits for a reconnect to be tried again, so the age only bounds what waits for a manager or a hub that stays away.
  - Repeats: an entry handed over twice (the node stopped between sending it and taking it out of the file, at most 64 entries) is dropped by the manager by `spool_id` (`devices/spooldedupe.go`, in memory per machine). A notification's id is remembered once the hub took it, and also once it went out to the hub and the manager's link dropped before the answer: the hub may have pushed it and does not tell a repeat itself, so it is taken for sent (at most once rather than twice). A hook event written just as the connection drops can still be lost.

## Runtime ↔ node (unix socket `~/.persona/runtime.sock`, or a daemon the node connects to)

A **runtime** is an Agent runtime with no terminal that manages its own sessions (currently DSH, `docs/integrations/dsh.md`). It is not a "host": the host is where the terminal is opened (herdr / Herdr App / Orca,
see "Engines"), and the node recognizes sessions from panes and transcripts; a runtime reports its own sessions and provides its own content, and coexists with the engine this machine picked. How to connect a new runtime,
the SDK and the acceptance checklist are in `docs/integrations/runtimes.md`; this is the wire protocol (`server/internal/node/runtimes.go`).

The runtime connects to the node's `~/.persona/runtime.sock` (0600, so it must be the same system user as the node) over one long-lived connection; the frame format is exactly the same as hub ↔ node (`internal/rpc`:
one JSON per line, request / response / one-way events, both sides can send requests). The hub and App don't know runtimes exist: they see ordinary sessions, items and interaction cards.
**Who owns the socket**: a resident node (`personad node --attach`) opens `runtime.sock` as soon as it starts, shared by every hub connection (`node/runtimehost.go`):
the runtime doesn't have to wait for the hub, the connection doesn't drop while the hub reconnects, and the first session list on the next connection already includes its sessions. Without a resident node, when `--stdio` serves by itself, the socket
exists only for the duration of that hub connection, as before.

**Without a hub**: the runtime can still connect and hello still answers (`hub: false`), and lists are still accepted; content pushed for the phone is dropped (once the hub is back it re-watches from the phone's progress);
`interaction.create` returns the error `code: node_gone`, and the runtime asks again with the same id once the hub is back. The node pushes `runtime.hub` once each time the hub arrives or leaves, so the runtime
doesn't wait for a phone that can't answer (SDK: without a hub, always go to the local UI first). When the node process itself goes away (restart, binary swap), the runtime reconnects: while the socket file still exists it tries every
second; if the file is gone it backs off up to 30 seconds.

runtime → node:

| Message | Description |
| --- | --- |
| request `runtime.hello {runtime, name?, agent?, version?, instance?, launcher?, launcher_model?, launchers?, caps: {start, send, interrupt, rename, close, assistant?, modes?, model?, models?, check?, resume?, archive?, workspaces?}, package?: {name, hash}}` → `{protocol, node_version, hub, features, update?: {name, hash, version}}` | Must be sent first. `instance` identifies this process (the SDK uses one per runtime, unchanged across reconnects): when the same runtime id already has a live connection with a different `instance`, it returns the error `code: runtime_conflict` (another process is configured with the same id and can't connect; the SDK retries every 30 seconds and doesn't take over); when it's the same, this process reconnected and the old connection is closed. Old runtimes without `instance` behave as before (the latest connection wins). `hub` is whether the node is currently connected to a hub (old nodes don't send it; assume yes). `features` are capabilities the node supports beyond the first protocol version: `prefer_running` (when two runtimes list the same session, the one listing it as non-`offline` owns it, so a runtime can list sessions that exist only on disk as `offline`), `resume_argv` (recognizes `resume_argv` in session rows), `handover` (when sending a message returns `code: handover`, hand it to the runtime that takes over; see `session.send` below), `transcript` (recognizes `transcript` in session rows), `launchers` (recognizes hello's `launchers` and the event `runtime.launchers`), `start_params` (`session.start` carries the form's choices), `modes` (`session.modes`), `resume` (`session.start {resume}`), `codex_thread` (recognizes `codex_thread` in session rows), `unlisted_transcripts` (recognizes `unlisted_transcripts` beside `sessions`), `workspaces` (recognizes `caps.workspaces`: the event `runtime.workspaces`, the requests `workspace.prepare` / `workspace.create`, and `workspace_id` in an engine runtime's session rows); daemons get only `prefer_running`, `start_params`. The node drops any events sent before it. `runtime` is the id (`[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*`, e.g. `dsh`), and also the sessions' `space_kind`; `agent` is the Agent its sessions run, defaulting to `runtime` itself; `name` is what the App calls it (`DSH`); such sessions carry `agent_label: name`, so the App needs no release for a new runtime. `caps` declares which operations are supported; for undeclared ones the node returns `unsupported` directly. When `launcher` is non-empty and `caps.start` is set, the node's `launchers.list` gains an entry `{name: launcher, model: launcher_model, source: runtime}`, and new sessions created with it are handed to this runtime. When two runtimes report the same launcher name, only the first to connect provides it (the other logs a line); when it has the same name as a launcher in the login shell, the shell's wins and the runtime's isn't listed. `caps.assistant` (requires start and send): its launcher can run Persona's assistant, and carries `assistant: true` in `launchers.list`; how the node drives it is in `docs/integrations/runtimes.md` ("Assistant").
`launchers` (requires `caps.start`): besides `launcher`, the new-session form also offers these entries. Each is `{name, model?, agent?, models?}`:
  - A runtime that runs multiple Agents (Paseo) has one entry per provider.
  - `agent` is the Agent this entry starts: with `claude` the form offers Claude Code's choices, and the App draws it as Claude.
  - `models` are the models `launchers.models` returns and their thinking efforts.
  - Naming rules are the same as for shell launchers; anything beyond 64 entries, or 200 models per entry, is dropped.

`caps.modes`: accepts the phone switching permission mode / thinking effort (`session.modes`). `caps.resume`: can take over a Claude session it doesn't have (`session.start {resume}`). `caps.archive`: archives and restores its sessions with its own reversible archive (`session.archive` / `session.unarchive`). `caps.seen`: keeps an unread mark of its own and clears it when the user saw the session in Persona (`session.seen`). `caps.workspaces` (#6295): it keeps workspaces of its own, which it lists (`runtime.workspaces`), makes worktrees as (`workspace.prepare` / `workspace.create`; the SDK declares it only with both `prepareWorkspace` and `createWorkspace`), and renames and archives (`workspace.rename` / `workspace.archive`, #6297); the node uses them only while the runtime is one of the computer's engines (Paseo) on its own socket, never a daemon's (`docs/integrations/runtimes.md` ("Workspaces")). |
| event `runtime.sessions {sessions: [Session], unlisted_transcripts?: [string]}` | All its sessions, pushed in full on change. `unlisted_transcripts` (the `unlisted_transcripts` feature, #4521): the Claude session ids of sessions of its own that it does not list (archived in the runtime); the node lists those transcripts as sessions not running, under the transcript's id, instead of leaving them out as one-shot `claude -p` runs (`docs/integrations/runtimes.md` ("Runtimes that run Claude Code")); a session whose id is not its transcript's is not named but stays a row of the runtime's, `offline` with `transcript`, so it keeps its id (#4771); at most 2000 (the last ones named), replaced by each push that has the field, an empty list too; a push without it leaves them (a runtime that cannot say yet), and they stand for ten minutes after the runtime disconnects. Fields are a subset of `Session`: `session_id` (`[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]{0,127}`, wider than Claude's uuid; DSH uses `session-<uuid>`), `title`, `cwd`, `status` (`working / blocked / done / idle / offline`; anything else counts as `unknown`), `agent`, `model`, `updated_at`, `last_text`, `rev` (when it changes the App fetches new content), `space_*`, `launcher`, `permission_mode` / `effort` (the modes it's using now; `session.info` reports these too), and still-running sub-Agents and background tasks `subagents` / `background` (`docs/integrations/runtimes.md` ("Sub-Agents and background tasks"): the node writes a sub-Agent's `session_id` as `<session>@<id>`; calls for this id go to the runtime owning the parent session, which also pushes content under this id; a background task's `output_file` is cleared). The node clears hub-computed fields like `machine_id`, `state`, fills in `agent` / `agent_label` / `space_kind`, and marks the source with the same fields as in "Codex sources and capabilities": `source_kind: "runtime"`, `source_instance_id` is the runtime id, `capabilities` = `{read: true, send: caps.send, interrupt: caps.interrupt, approve: true, terminal: false, attach: false, modes, close: caps.close, rename: caps.rename, model: caps.model, rewind: caps.rewind, rewind_code}` (`rename` and `rewind` false on a sub-Agent's row; the row's own `capabilities` may turn `rewind` off and `rewind_code` on, which is otherwise false; `model` on a `<session>@<id>` one; those without `send` declared carry `read_only_reason`; `modes` as in "Codex sources and capabilities": `caps.modes`, not a sub-Agent, and agent `claude` or the runtime's own); the App and hub use them to toggle buttons and guard sending. It's merged into `sessions.list` and `sessions.changed` is pushed immediately. When two connections both report the same id, the one listing it as non-`offline` owns it; if equal, the newer wins (`prefer_running`). A session another of the runtime's sessions started carries `is_subagent` and `parent_session_id` (#4494; the node fills in `root_session_id`, the hub sends no "done" push for it and holds its parent's, `docs/integrations/runtimes.md` ("Sub-Agents and background tasks")); while its `status` is `blocked` the node lists it without them, so a session that needs the user is a row of its own in every client, and names that parent in `asking_parent_session_id` instead (see "Session hierarchy"). A row may say when the session began in `started_at`; the node drops a runtime's own `folded_under`, `folded_as`, `children` and `asking_parent_session_id` (the manager's and the node's to set). `workspace_id` is kept only for an engine runtime with `caps.workspaces` (Paseo; the id of one of its `runtime.workspaces`, so the apps place the session in that catalog row); any other runtime's is cleared, as are `pane_id` and `tab_id`. Fields the node uses and the App never sees: `pane_id` (which pane of this machine's terminal engine the session runs in: for pi in a herdr pane, the node merges it with the engine's pane into one herdr session row; the terminal part of calls goes to the engine and the rest to the runtime, `docs/integrations/pi.md`), `resume_argv` (how a session listed as `offline` is resumed in the terminal engine: when the phone sends a message, the node opens a new tab in the engine, runs it via `personad tab-start`, waits until the runtime lists the session as running again, then sends the message; if the engine is absent it refuses; the `resume_argv` feature), `transcript` (this session's chat is a Claude transcript on this computer; the value is the Claude session id; the `transcript` feature), `codex_thread` (this session's chat is a Codex thread with a rollout on this computer; the value is the thread id: the node does not list the thread again as Codex history, and the thread's sub-Agents carry this session as `parent_session_id`; the `codex_thread` feature, #4495).

**Sessions with `transcript`** (runtimes that run Claude Code, such as Paseo):
  - **What the node handles**: content comes from the transcript; `session.items` / `item` / `image`, watch, `session.info` and sub-Agents all belong to the node, the same as for Claude sessions in a terminal.
    The row's `last_text`, `rev`, "what it's doing" and background tasks also come from the transcript.
  - **What the runtime handles**: status, title, model, modes, sending, cards. It only pushes streaming text; items it pushes are dropped.
  - **Listing**: the transcript's own "not running" row is no longer listed.
  - **Only transcripts the node can find count**: when the first turn has just started and nothing is written yet, or it's in a config directory the node doesn't know, content belongs to the runtime for now.
    Once the file appears, on the next list the node switches to the transcript: an active watch is re-subscribed, `history` changes with it, and the App refetches the whole page.
  - **Limits**: daemons can't carry this field. When the connection drops, its sessions disappear from the list. **The list is only "what to show the App now", not ownership**: a runtime only lists its recent sessions (DSH lists the latest 80 out of thousands), and the node remembers which runtime listed each session (by runtime id, so still the same after reconnect); calls for an old session not on the list still go to it. For a session that has nothing on this machine (no Agent, no transcript), calls like `session.send` / `items` / `watch` first ask the connected runtimes with `session.items {session_id, limit: 1}`, and the one that can answer owns it (one that can't be found isn't asked again for a minute). When it belongs to a runtime that isn't connected, the error is `code: runtime_away` (`delivered: none`); it is never treated as a Claude session and resumed in a terminal |
| event `runtime.launchers {launchers}` | replaces hello's `launchers`: providers were added or removed, or their models are only known now |
| event `runtime.workspaces {workspaces: [{workspace_id, title?, cwd, kind, branch?, space_id?, space_name?, repo_root?, owned?}]}` | requires `caps.workspaces` (the `workspaces` feature): all its workspaces, pushed in full on change, replacing the last list (the SDK says it again to every node it connects to). `workspace_id` follows the session id rule and is what its sessions name in their `workspace_id`; `cwd` is absolute; `kind` is `checkout` (a repository's main checkout), `worktree` (a linked worktree) or `folder` (anything else counts as one); `space_id` / `space_name` are the space its sessions are grouped in; `repo_root` is the repository's main checkout; `owned`: the runtime made the checkout and removes it with the workspace. At most 2000; invalid rows are dropped. While the runtime is one of the computer's engines, these are its rows of `workspaces.list` (below), with or without sessions in them; the node keeps them only while it is connected |
| event `session.items {session_id, items, history, from_seq, to_seq, more_after?}` | new content of a watched session, forwarded as is to the hub (same shape as node → hub `session.items`; continuity rules in "Continuity of items"). A rewatch replay is capped at eight pages; when more remains, its last batch carries `more_after: true` so the App fetches the rest. Sessions it didn't list aren't forwarded |
| event `session.delta {session_id, text}` | the whole paragraph being generated; an empty string means this paragraph ended. Forwarded as is to the hub; the App draws it as streaming output |
| request `interaction.create {interaction, timeout_seconds?}` → `Resolution` | three kinds: question (`question`), plan (`plan`), permission (`permission`), same shape as `Interaction` above. The node fills in `created_at` / `expires_at` (default 30 minutes, same as hooks; `timeout_seconds` can only shorten it), the session title, the directory, and `agent` / `agent_label` (the Agent the runtime runs and its name; not set for runtimes running Claude Code, so the App draws a Claude card), pushes it to the phone via the hub, and blocks until answered. When nobody answers (expired, the phone's "hand back to computer", no hub) it returns `{dismiss: true}`, and the runtime hands over to its own UI. Interactions with a `tool_use_id` are `resumable`: the `id` the runtime gives (or the one the node computes from runtime + session + kind + tool_use_id) stays the same; if the node goes away midway it returns the error `code: node_gone`, and once the runtime connects to the next node it asks again with the same id, and the hub reattaches the original card |
| event `interaction.cancel {id}` | this interaction is gone on the runtime side (tool call cancelled): withdraw the card on the phone |
| request `runtime.package {name}` → `{name, hash, version, files: [{path, data}]}` | auto-update (`docs/integrations/runtimes.md` ("Auto-update")): `package` in hello says what code the runtime runs (package name and hash); when the node carries a package with this name and a different hash, the reply includes `update`, and the runtime fetches the files with this request (`data` is base64), checks the hash itself and swaps them in. Packages live in personad (`internal/runtimepkg`, generated from `integrations/` at build time); daemons can't get them (no `update`, and this request returns `unsupported`); no such package returns `not_found` |
| requests `mcp.tools {assistant?}` → `{tools: [{name, description, input_schema, shell?}]}`, `mcp.call {name, args, session_id, assistant?}` → `ToolResult` | the hub's tools (the phone's `phone_*`, `mail_*`), forwarded to the hub (except `mail_save_attachment`, which the node answers itself and fetches over `mail.attachment`); without a hub `mcp.tools` is empty and `mcp.call` returns an error result. The runtime gives them to its own Agent (DSH: `docs/integrations/dsh.md` ("Phone tools")). `assistant: true` only matters for runtimes that declared `caps.assistant`: `mcp.tools` gains the assistant-only tools and the tools declared by extension command gates; `mcp.call` is handled as an assistant call only when the session belongs to this runtime and is an assistant chat (otherwise as an ordinary call). Gate-declared tools are run by the node itself; their `shell` is the word that runs them directly in a shell (command name, skill script path), which the runtime intercepts in the assistant chat's shell (`docs/integrations/runtimes.md` ("Assistant")) |

node → runtime events: `runtime.hub {connected}`, sent to every runtime when the hub connects / disconnects.

node → runtime requests (sent only on the connection that owns the session; all of the hub's `session.*` calls for these sessions go through here):

| Request | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `session.items` | params and result as in hub → node `session.items` (`before_seq` / `turns` / `limit` / `after_seq` / `from_seq` + `through_seq`); images are always placeholders (`lazy`), with content fetched via `session.image`. `fold_work` is applied by the node on the result (`transcript.FoldWork`); the runtime doesn't deal with it |
| `session.image {session_id, item_id}` → `{mime, data}`, `session.item {session_id, item_id}` → `Item` | raw image data, full text of a truncated item |
| `session.watch {session_id, since_seq, transcript?}` / `session.unwatch` | start / stop pushing this session's new content; with `since_seq > 0`, first replay what comes after it, at most eight pages and with `more_after` on the last when more remains. The node remembers how far each watched session has been pushed, and re-watches from that seq when the runtime lists it after reconnecting. `transcript: true`: the node pushes content from the transcript, and the runtime only pushes streaming text |
| `session.send {session_id, text, images, client_msg_id, assistant?, context?, mode?, memory_dir?}` | send a message (`assistant` and the following fields are only sent for assistant chats on runtimes that declared `caps.assistant`: `docs/integrations/runtimes.md` ("Assistant")). `client_msg_id` is given to the runtime for idempotency (the node itself also dedups on it for 10 minutes), and the node also uses it to recognize this message among items the runtime pushes ("Matching pending messages"); a runtime that knows which item is this message can put `client_msg_id` on the item directly, and the node forwards it as is. An assistant chat's message (`assistant: true`) carries the id it came with too, and none when it came with none (#5225). The runtime returning the error `code: handover` (`data.delivered: "none"`) means it doesn't take this session and has started the program that can run it (a read-only-disk companion process): the node waits for another connection to list the session as non-`offline`, or asks the other runtimes every 2 seconds whether they have it (`session.items {limit: 1}`), and whichever comes first gets the message; if none within 45 seconds, it returns `not_running` and nothing is sent |
| `session.interrupt {session_id}`, `session.rename {session_id, title}`, `session.close {session_id}` | each allowed per `caps`; missing ones return the error `code: unsupported` (text starts with `unsupported`, same as a host lacking a capability). A rename with only `tab_name` succeeds directly (these sessions have no tabs) |
| `session.start {cwd, prompt?, assistant?, launcher?, model?, permission_mode?, effort?, workspace_id?, resume?, shell_launcher?, open_elsewhere?}` → `{session}` | when its launcher was chosen, or when it is this machine's engine; the returned session enters the list immediately. `assistant: true`: the assistant opens a new chat with its launcher (`cwd` is the assistant directory, no `prompt`; the first message follows via `session.send`). Other fields are only included when set; see below |
| `launchers.check {launcher, cwd, prompt}` | optional availability probe when `caps.check` is true. Returns `{ok, agent?, model?, answer?, millis, error?}`. Runs in the runtime's authentication context. The node owns and removes the temporary workspace and preserves native failures without falling back to the shell |
| `launchers.models {launcher, refresh?}` | optional live model catalog request when `caps.models` is true. Returns `{agent, models, locked?}` in the existing launcher-model shape. Errors propagate to the caller. Older runtimes keep their advertised list |
| `session.modes {session_id, permission_mode?, effort?, model?}` | the phone switches permission mode / thinking effort (for runtimes that declared `caps.modes`; values are validated by the node first). `model` requires explicit `caps.model`, otherwise the entire request is refused |
| `session.seen {session_id}` | requires `caps.seen`: the user saw the session in Persona (#6299). The manager sends it to the node for a runtime's session the node lists as `done`, in the background; the node answers it itself for any other session and runtime. Paseo clears its own unread mark (`requiresAttention`) |
| `session.rewind {session_id, prompt, occurrence, prompts_after?, restore}` | requires `caps.rewind`, and for `restore: "code_and_conversation"` the row's own `capabilities.rewind_code` (a row's `capabilities.rewind: false` refuses it). Conversation rewind returns `{prompt, restore, code_restored: false, input_cleared: true}` after verifying the selected message and publishing the new history token; one restoring the files says `code_restored: true`. Refusals carry the existing `rewind_*` codes. The SDK exposes optional `driver.rewind(params)` and refreshes inventory after success |
| `session.archive {session_id}`, `session.unarchive {session_id}` | archive / restore an idle session in the runtime's own archive, without stopping or closing it (for runtimes that declared `caps.archive`; a runtime without it is never asked, and the node answers the manager `native: "unsupported"`). Both must be idempotent: already archived (restored) answers success |
| `workspace.prepare {cwd, repo_root}` → `{checkouts}` | requires `caps.workspaces`: the folder the runtime puts the worktrees of that repository in (`repo_root` its main checkout, physical), absolute. "New worktree…" shows it, and the worktree's own folder name is the only part of the path that can be chosen |
| `workspace.create {cwd, workspace_id?, branch?, create_branch, base?, name?, key}` → `{workspace}` | requires `caps.workspaces` (#6295): a worktree of the repository `cwd` is in, made by the runtime as a workspace of its own, from the workspace named when there is one. `create_branch: false` checks out the existing `branch` as it is; otherwise a new `branch` is cut from `base` (the source checkout's branch, or its commit on a detached HEAD); without `branch` the runtime names the branch, and without `name` the folder. `key` stays the same when the call is retried. `name` is a folder name as Paseo makes one (`[a-z0-9]` runs joined by single hyphens, at most 50 characters, the node's `runtimeFolderName`), and nothing was at `<checkouts>/<name>` when the node asked: the runtime makes the worktree there, not beside it. The node has checked what it checks for a terminal host first (a repository with a commit, a valid branch not checked out in another worktree, a folder that does not exist in the runtime's worktrees folder) and waits within one deadline for the whole create or add, 145 s. The answer is the new workspace's `runtime.workspaces` row, with the folder and branch it actually has; the node lists it at once |
| `workspace.rename {workspace_id, title}` → `{workspace?}`, `workspace.rename {space_id, title}` → `{space_name}` | requires `caps.workspaces` (#6297): a workspace's title ("Rename" on a catalog row, `worktree/rename`), answered with its row as it is now; or the name of the space its sessions are grouped in (`space.rename`, Paseo's project), answered with the name the space shows now, which the hub keys pins by. Neither renames a branch, a folder or a session. The node sends only ids of the runtime's own workspaces and spaces |
| `workspace.archive {workspace_id}` → `{archived_at?}` | requires `caps.workspaces` (#6297): the workspace leaves the runtime's list, its sessions archived with it, and a worktree the runtime made is removed from the disk, its branch kept. Sent only for a worktree the runtime made (`owned`), with no session in it at work and no agent running in its folder: a confirmed `worktree/delete`, after the node has checked the preview's token and what it showed, or a closed Agent's own worktree (`worktree/remove`, #6115). One deadline covers the node's checks and the runtime's archive, 145 s; then the node trusts only the runtime's list and the disk |

Fields `session.start` carries, each only when set:
  - **The form's choices**: `launcher`, `model`, `permission_mode`, `effort`. `workspace_id` is which of its spaces to create in (its sessions' `space_id`), or, for a runtime with `caps.workspaces`, one of its workspaces (`runtime.workspaces`; a workspace it no longer has is refused, `workspace_missing`, rather than the session going elsewhere).
  - **`shell_launcher: true`**: `launcher` is a login-shell launcher; the runtime picks its own one with the same name, or its default if there's none.
  - **`resume`**: the id of the Claude session to take over (`caps.resume`, this machine's engine continuing a session that isn't running). The returned session id must be the same.
  - **`open_elsewhere: true`**: a live claude has this session open. If it isn't the runtime's own, it must refuse with the error code `open_elsewhere`, so two processes don't write at once;
    the node replaces the refusal with a hint saying where it's open.

Terminal calls (`session.keys`, `session.screen.before`, `terminal.watch`) return `unsupported` for runtime sessions, and `session.screen` returns a blank screen;
these sessions have no `pane_id`, and the App doesn't show a terminal for them anyway.

**daemon** (`docs/integrations/daemons.md`, `server/internal/node/daemons.go`): a runtime that is itself a resident service and can't reach the local socket; the node connects to it.

- **How it connects**:
  - The node connects to the daemon's WebSocket endpoint per `daemons.json` next to `runtime.sock`; the request carries `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and the subprotocol `persona-runtime.v1`, and the daemon must answer with this subprotocol.
  - Once connected, one text message is one line as above; the protocol is exactly the same as on the local socket.
- **What the node rewrites in between**:
  - `runtime`, `name`, `launcher` in hello are replaced with the configured values, and `agent` too (if configured); `instance` is set by the node to `daemon:<id>` (when it reconnects the old connection is closed); `caps` keeps only start / send / interrupt / rename / close, no `assistant`.
  - Session ids get the prefix `<id>.`, `space_id` gets `<id>:`, and interaction ids are replaced with stable hashes; the prefixes are removed when replying to the daemon.
  - `pane_id`, `resume_argv`, `agent_label` in session rows are dropped, and `features` doesn't tell it about `resume_argv` and `handover`; when it returns `code: handover` for `session.send`, the node turns it into `not_running` and doesn't hand it to another runtime.
- **What the daemon can't see or use**:
  - When a call's session id lacks its prefix (the node asking "whose session is this"), the node answers `not_found` itself and doesn't send it to the daemon;
  - `mcp.tools` returns empty, `mcp.call` returns `unsupported`.
- **id conflicts**:
  - A runtime on the local socket saying hello with an id from `daemons.json` gets the error `code: runtime_conflict`;
  - when an id is already taken by a connected runtime, the hello of a daemon with the same id also gets `runtime_conflict`; the node then disconnects it and reconnects later.

### Tasks and the chat feed

Tasks dispatched from an assistant chat ([unified-entry.md](../assistant/unified-entry.md)). The assistant hands in a plan with `task_plan`; read-only ones and ones the user chose to remember start directly, and the rest wait for "Start" on the phone.

**Stable task rows (#2878).** The feed endpoint additionally returns `task_cards`, a derived projection, without changing or
removing its original `items` and `plans`. Android and web render a task only as its single row in **In progress**, or in
**Needs you** while it waits on the user (#3387); the chat shows hand-off cards instead of plan/task/receipt/review/report cards (Android's Glass style draws the receipts, reviews, reports, Persona's hand-offs, message cards and `notice` lines in the chat as iOS does, `docs/plans/android-ios-alignment/chats.md` C13). Web, iOS and Android draw one card per Agent a dispatch started or a task took over (#5096, #5110). A card with an Agent opens that Agent's page, and before an Agent is up it opens the task, never the whole tray (#3700).
Clients take the dispatched to-dos from data they already have: a `task` item's `ref`, or a started plan's `tasks[].todo_id`
in plan order (a task without `todo_id` did not start and has no link); no extra field is sent. Plans awaiting Start and acceptance decisions are handled in **Needs you**. Task details and the original audit records remain accessible.

`TaskCard` is `{id,todo_id?,plan_id?,index?,at,updated_at,state,receipt_id?,report_id?}`:

- `id` is `plan:<plan_id>:<index>` for a plan task (zero-based `index`, including zero), stable before and after `todo_id`
  is assigned. A task with no plan uses `todo:<todo_id>`. A reused task is projected only under its current durable plan.
- `at` is the original plan's `created_at`, or the to-do's `created_at` when there is no plan. State changes, reports and
  receipts never move this anchor. `updated_at` includes newer to-do, supervision, progress, session and task-feed changes.
- `state` uses the existing task states: `not_started`, `working`, `needs_you`, `interrupted`, `usage_limit`, `unread`,
  `followup`, `done`, `failed`, `cancelled`; `accepted` specifically means a closed task with an effective accepted
  supervision review. Cancellation, failed starts and automatic completion are not silently relabeled accepted.
- `receipt_id` and `report_id` name the latest corresponding original entries **in this page**, if any. Clients merge them
  with their cached audit entries by task id; absence does not clear previously received evidence. Titles and editable
  planning fields remain in `plans[plan_id].tasks[index]`; live progress and PR links remain on `Todo` and `Session`.
- This is an **upsert page**, not an authoritative removal snapshot. `since` can omit the original plan event; the server
  resolves a task's durable `plan_id` in one batch to retain its identity. `[]` means no task upserts in this page. `null`
  means projection data could not be read; keep the prior state or legacy projection. Old hubs omit the field, and old
  clients continue reading the unchanged events. Remove rows only through the existing task/plan lifecycle, not because
  they were absent from a feed page.
- Clients continue updating the same row from live to-dos and sessions, independently of new feed events. Actual
  `supervision.progress.{kind,step,steps,text,at}` or `Session.plan.{done,total,current}` supplies progress, never elapsed
  time or a guessed percentage. The row words a report as `supervision.progress.line` when the hub sent one, else
  `text` (#3181); the task's details show the report itself, `detail` when present, else `text`, with Markdown rendered. Quiet scheduled-task runs use the existing schedule fields and provenance, not a new
  model call; `Todo.quiet` is notification policy and is not proof that a user-dispatched task is a background turn.
- **Why a stopped task is still open (#3180).** While the task is neither working nor done, and its to-do's `check` is
  current (not older than `reopened_at`) with a `verdict` other than `done` or `unsure`, Android and web write the row's
  text as "Stopped, not done yet · <reason>" (the first part alone when `reason` is empty); an Agent's open question still
  comes first. `task_cards` does not change; clients that don't know `check` draw the row as before.

```jsonc
// TaskPlan
{"id":"plan_…","conversation":"<assistant chat id>","state":"open|started|dismissed","created_at":"...","updated_at":"...",
 "tasks":[{"title":"Fix the login crash","prompt":"The first message to the Agent","machine":"<machine id>","cwd":"/abs/path",
           "launcher":"","model":"","permission":"acceptEdits","readonly":false,"why":"one-line reason",
           "ultracode":true,            // optional (#12): the Claude Code Agent starts with ultracode on; on start, true / false sets it and leaving it out keeps the assistant's choice
           "done_when":["PR merged into master"],"expect_minutes":30,   // acceptance criteria, expected minutes (#3124); required of task_plan since #3822; clients only display them and don't send them back on start
           "goal":"one sentence","out_of_bounds":["do not merge"],"started_why":"…",   // optional (#3822): the brief's goal and bounds, and why the assistant starts it on its own
           "continues":"todo_…","continues_why":"…",   // optional (#3822): the to-do this task takes over from; it keeps that to-do's brief
           "brief":{…},                 // the hub's (#3822): the brief as it will be kept (the to-do's `brief` above), for the card to show before Start; never sent back
           "reuse_todo":"todo_…",       // optional (#5279): the to-do the task runs on instead of a new one (task_plan's per-task `todo_id`); the apps neither send it back nor change it
           "todo_id":"todo_…",          // only present after start
           "owner_started":true,        // the hub's (#4929): the owner tapped Start on the card, as against the hub starting it without asking; never read from task_plan arguments or sent back
           "error":"",                   // why the Agent didn't start
           "error_code":"launcher_missing","error_args":{"where":"terminal","launcher":"…","pane_shell":"bash"}}]}
                                         // optional (#1642): the start's coded refusal and its details, as a session's start_error_code / start_error_args
// An open plan may also carry "suggestion" (RuleSuggestion, below); it is filled in where the apps read the plan and never stored with it.

// RuleSuggestion (#4929, unified-entry.md "A rule after the same answer three times"): the line a card carries once the owner gave
// the same answer to its kind of card for the same scope 3 times within 14 days. Optional on TaskPlan (`suggestion`), on a to-do's
// decision (`ask.suggestion` on GET /api/v1/todos) and on a question a supervisor passed up (`interaction.suggestion`); a client that
// does not know it shows the card as before. Its two actions are POST /api/v1/assistant/rule-suggestions/{id}/always and …/not-now.
{"id":"rs_…",                           // names the kind and scope; what the two actions take
 "kind":"plan_start|standing_authorization|delegate",
 "text":"You approved this 3 times. Always allow merging in /code/example on example-node once checks pass and there are no conflicts?",   // in the request's language (the user's on an event)
 "scope":{"machine_id":"example-node","machine":"Example node","directory":"/code/example",
          "action":"merge","conditions":["ci_green","no_conflicts"],
          "quote":"Merge the PR now? → Yes"},   // action, conditions and quote only for standing_authorization (quote: what the grant would keep as the owner's words, their latest answer); {} for delegate
 "creates":"tasks.trust|standing_authorization|",   // what Always stores; "" for delegate, which stores nothing
 "setting":"agents.delegate",            // only for delegate: the setting to open instead
 "count":3}                              // how many identical answers were counted

// FeedItem: entries the hub inserts into an assistant chat, not in the transcript; clients draw them merged with the transcript by at
{"id":"feed_…","conversation":"…","at":"...","kind":"plan|task|answered|receipt|routed|today|message|inbox_suggestion|review|report|notice|brief","ref":"plan_…, todo_…, a date or an Inbox entry id",
 "body":{…}}
// plan: ref is the plan id, no body; task: ref is the to-do id; body {"wake":"active|resumed"} when the task was made of an Agent
//   it did not start (#5096, the web's hand-off badge): resumed when agent_send with a task resumed a closed Agent, active for an
//   Agent running already (agent_supervise, agent_send with a task, an Agent that became a task when its turn ended, a task
//   moved to this conversation); no body when the task started its Agent
// answered: {"question":"Use Bash","answer":"Approved · don't ask again for this kind",
//           "items":[{"question":"Use Bash\nnpm test\nReason: run the tests","answer":"Approved · don't ask again for this kind"}]}
//   question / answer are the one-line summary shown when collapsed (squashed to one line, cut at 120 characters); old clients and old records from before #1231 only have these two.
//   items are the full content, drawn when expanded: each question paired with its answer, line breaks kept; multi-question cards in card order; unanswered ones say "Not answered",
//   ignored ones "Ignored". Plan approvals carry the plan text and the denial reason / mode after approval; tool approvals carry the tool, summary and reason;
//   screen dialogs carry the selected option and text typed into options; form fields are written "Label: value". 4000 characters per segment, 12000 per entry, at most 20; anything beyond is truncated.
//   Password fields (Field.secret, the screen's secret, MCP form password / writeOnly, names that look like passwords / tokens) are written only as "(filled in, not saved)"; values are never stored.
// receipt: {"title":"…","state":"done|failed|interrupted","summary":"the Agent's last reply (Markdown, cut by lines to about 600 characters, never inside a markup token)","pr":"https://github.com/…/pull/N","machine":"…"}
//   review (#1988), optional on done receipts only: {"state":"checking|awaiting","criteria":3}. criteria is the number of done_when entries (0 is included).
//   Present when the latest to-do is open, has a supervision ledger and its effective state is not needs_user (waiting on the user).
//   checking means the turn ended but task completion has not been established. awaiting is only for an existing pending_review verdict.
//   Reopened accepted / cancelled tasks have an ongoing effective state and qualify. The receipt is written before judgment, without waiting for a model;
//   judgment and supervision signals follow as before. Failed / interrupted receipts omit review.
//   Older clients ignore unknown review states; older receipts omit it. Web labels an open non-pending task as "Persona follows up" and uses "Waiting for Persona's review"
//   only when the linked live to-do is pending_review; once done it shows the existing green completion card without the hint.
//   interrupted (#1516): the Agent's turn was interrupted by a model service error; summary is "The model service errored and was interrupted", error is the original error text; clients draw it in red with "Continue".
//   A turn with no reply, no tool calls and no error (the model service returned 200 with empty content, #2349) is also interrupted, with error "This turn produced no output: …"
//   Interrupted receipts after the fact (#3834, docs/assistant/unified-entry.md "Interrupted receipts after the fact"): "cause":"model_error|rate_limited|auth|model_route|no_output",
//   "resolution":"pending|cancelled|rerouted|resumed|accepted|done" (worked out by the hub on every read; a changed one is sent again as assistant_feed with the same id),
//   "group":"<feed id>" on a receipt that joined an earlier one's batch (same cause, same chat, within 10 minutes; clients don't draw it on its own),
//   and on a batch's first receipt "batch":{"cause","machine"?,"total","pending","resolved","tasks":[{"receipt","todo_id","title","resolution","at"}]}.
//   Clients draw a batch as one card and a handled receipt as a grey line; a receipt without resolution (an older hub) is drawn as before.
// routed: {"text":"…"} (the note sent to the Agent when the supervisor sends work back is also a routed);
//         "interrupted":true when the assistant stopped the Agent's turn first and then told it (agent_interrupt with then, #5112); clients that don't know it show an ordinary line to the task
//         "from":"assistant" when Persona wrote it (agent_send with task, agent_interrupt's then, a rework; #1542): the apps fold it (a line, or the task card's
//         "N instructions sent", docs/assistant/unified-entry.md "Messages to agents") instead of the user's bubble; what the user sent has no from; older clients ignore it
// report: ref is the to-do id; a supervised task's Agent reported to Persona (report_to_supervisor, #5112): {"kind":"question|blocked|done","text":"…","evidence":["…"],"step":2,"steps":5,"later"?:true};
//         progress reports are not written here (only supervision.progress); clients that don't know it skip this entry. `later`: a question the Agent sent with urgent false (#6287): nobody was woken, it is in the briefing's "Can wait" queue (`docs/extensions/bots.md` ("Questions that can wait")); clients that don't know the field draw it as any question
// notice: no ref; a one-line note the hub writes into the chat {"text":"…"} (already written in the hub's language); clients draw it as a centered line of small text, and clients that don't know it skip it.
//         There's only one kind now: after scheduled tasks were skipped because the main chat wasn't set up, once ready, before the first run the main chat gets "Computers and models are set up; scheduled tasks are running again, this time 'Morning briefing'" (#4253)
// review: ref is the to-do id; the supervisor did one acceptance review (#3124): {"title","verdict":"accepted|rework|needs_user|parked|cancelled","round":1,"note":"…",
//         "checks":[{"criterion","met","evidence"}]}; a parked review (#3804) also has "until" (RFC 3339) and "waiting_on", and its note is what the task waits for
//         when the review gave none; "by":"background" when the background supervisor wrote it (#5084; absent for every other review and from a hub before it:
//         such a review took no turn of this conversation, so a client may draw the entry here as its only record); clients that don't know it skip this entry
// message: ref is the Inbox entry id; the AI twin drafted a reply to a message related to the task:
//         {"todo_id","source":"lark|mail|…","account","chat","sender","text":"original words (truncated)","draft":"the draft"}; sending goes through the Inbox send endpoint
// inbox_suggestion (#5932): ref is the Inbox entry id; the conversation the entry was handed to (Hand to AI) handed in a reply or a
//         conclusion with inbox_suggest: {"version","kind":"reply|conclusion","outcome"?:"fyi|done","text","note"?,"recap"?,"title","source",
//         "account"?,"sender"?}, a snapshot never updated. Clients read the entry for its state: the entry's suggestion still this version from
//         this conversation offers Send / Got it (POST /api/v1/inbox/{id}/suggestion with that version); otherwise it was sent, filed or
//         replaced. Not counted in Needs you (the entry is); clients that don't know it skip it
// today: ref is the user's date for that day; {"date":"2026-11-03","done":[{"id","title"}],"waiting":[{"id","title"}],"pending_review":[{"id","title"}],"working":2,
//         "meetings":[{"start","end","title"}],"at_me":[{"name","unread","preview"}],"unread":5} (fields Lark didn't answer for are omitted)
//         pending_review: this chat's open supervised tasks whose supervision state is pending_review, oldest created first (#4889).
//         They appear only here, not in waiting, working or done, regardless of their agents' state. Omitted when empty; older clients ignore it.
//         "failed":[{"kind":"task|routine","id","ref"?,"title","at","why"?,"skipped"?}],"failed_total":3: what hasn't succeeded since 18:00 yesterday (#4124):
//         dispatched tasks from this chat that didn't start (kind task, id is the to-do) and failed / skipped scheduled-task runs (kind routine, id is the scheduled task, ref is that run),
//         newest first, at most 8 entries; failed_total is the total count; why is a short one-line reason. Omitted when empty; old clients ignore it as unknown
// brief: ref is the scheduled task's id (the morning or evening routine with `facts` on); written into the routine's own conversation when a run is sent, whether or not the Lark bot is on
//         (`docs/extensions/bots.md` ("Morning and evening briefings")): the fixed part of that run, as it was when the run started:
//         {"title":"the routine's name","at":"…","hours":12,"waiting_unknown"?:true,
//          "waiting":[{"id":"<card id>","title":"what the card asks (a line, in the hub's language)","from":"who asked","link"?:"<web page>","machine_id"?,"session_id"?,"waited_s":4800,"nudged"?:true}],
//          "failed":[{"kind":"task|routine","id","ref"?,"title","at","why"?,"skipped"?}],"failed_total":3,       // as in today.failed: what didn't go through in the last `hours` hours, newest first, at most 8
//          "done":[{"id":"<to-do id>","title","at"}],"done_total":12,                                           // to-dos closed in that window, newest first, at most 10 (those waiting to be verified are under accept only)
//          "accept":[{"id":"<to-do id>","title","detail"?:"what changed","from"?,"link"?,"waited_s","asked_at":"…","verdict"?:"the verdict line","outcome"?:"done|cannot|decide","recommend"?:"…"}],  // to-dos waiting to be verified, or whose conclusion waits for the owner, the longest waiting first
//          "later"?:[{"id":"<question id>","title":"what was asked (a line)","from"?,"link"?:"<the Agent's chat>","machine_id"?,"session_id"?,"waited_s"}],"later_total"?:3,  // questions Agents left for a briefing (urgent false), the oldest first, at most 10; both left out when the queue is empty; the Handled button posts the id to POST /api/v1/later/{id}/handled
//          "progress":[{"id":"<to-do id>","title","stage"?:"plan|develop|review|merge|deploy|verify","stage_kind"?:"code|general"}],"progress_total":2,  // open to-dos whose Agents are working, the longest open first, at most 8
//          "setup"?:[{"id":"delegate|standing_authorizations|task_trust|triage_decide|triage_auto_continue|triage_wake|leaders|review_sample|independent_review|supervisor_tier",
//                     "setting":"agents.delegate","count":4,"minutes"?:31,"text":"the whole line, in the hub's language","link"?:"<its settings page in the web app>"}]}
//         setup (#5085, `docs/assistant/assistant.md` ("Recommended setup")): which mechanism that is off would have removed how many (`count`) of the last 7 days' asks or
//         background rounds (`minutes`: the time of those rounds, for leaders), with its cost and where it is turned on in `text`. Only on the first briefing of a week,
//         and only when it names something; left out otherwise. Read-only: nothing is turned on, and no route answers it. An app that does not know it skips it.
//         `supervisor_tier` (#5805) is not a mechanism that is off: its line says the background supervisor's reviews held on its current model and that its provider has a
//         lower tier; `count` is the settled acceptances of the last 30 days it was judged on and `setting` the model purpose `assistant.supervise`. An app draws `text` like any other row.
//         `link` is absolute and present only when the hub has a public address; an app links to its own settings page by `id` instead.
//         stage_kind (#3380): also sent on to-dos; general tasks omit the web stage strip, code draws it. Missing or unknown keeps the legacy behavior.
//         waiting_unknown: the cards waiting for an answer were not read yet (the hub had just started), so `waiting` is empty for want of knowing.
//         machine_id / session_id (#2320): the chat a waiting card or a question that can wait came from, which the apps open; left out for a card from no chat, and by a hub from before
//         (the iOS app then opens a waiting card it still has among its pending cards, and otherwise draws the row without a link). The Accept button posts `asked_at` to
//         POST /api/v1/todos/{id}/accept. `accept` has a row for every deployed to-do that waits for the owner, and for every supervised to-do's conclusion (#1226), with or without the Lark bot: the ask is kept whether or not a Lark card went out.
//         `verdict` is the verdict line word for word as the row's Lark card says it, in the bot's language ("done, deployed" for a deployed to-do); `outcome` is set for a conclusion only (decide: needs the owner's
//         decision, and the Accept button takes `recommend`; a decision without `recommend` has nothing to take). A hub from before leaves the three out. A retry of a failed run adds no second item. Clients that don't know the kind skip the entry (iOS builds before #2320 decode it as `unknown`, Android's draw has no branch for it).
```

The live state of task cards and plan cards isn't in the feed: clients read the plan (`task_plan` push) and the to-do + the session state of its attached Agents by `ref` (status rules as in [todos.md](../assistant/todos.md)).
Questions from a task's Agent are interactions as usual; clients draw them at the bottom of the chat by to-do.

## MCP tools (`personad mcp`)

`personad mcp` handles each request separately (a tool waiting on the phone doesn't block other tools). When Claude Code sends `notifications/cancelled` (this turn was stopped), it cancels that call and doesn't answer; the socket to the node hangs up with it, and the hub withdraws its card via `rpc.cancel` (#3525, #2597).

A call that asks for progress (`_meta.progressToken`, which Claude Code always sends) gets `notifications/progress` every minute while it waits (`keepAlive`, #1498). Claude Code ends a stdio MCP call that sends "no response or progress" for 30 minutes (`CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_TOOL_IDLE_TIMEOUT`), and a write approved on the phone waits up to 30 minutes, `ask_user` up to 2 hours: without progress the client gave up first, and the model got its generic abort instead of the hub's timeout reply. The deadlines stay the hub's and the manager's; `personad mcp` itself ends a call only after `CallTimeout` (2 hours 10 minutes, above `ask_user`'s wait, which a test in `assistant` keeps below it).

Every progress notification's params are exactly `{progressToken, progress, message}`; `progress` still counts the one-minute beats and no notification follows cancellation or the final answer. `message` is one of four fixed English strings for the Agent's terminal client (not Persona UI text): `Waiting for your approval` for a pending permission or plan interaction, `Waiting for your answer` for a pending `ask_user` question, `Waiting for the computer` while remote work runs without a user wait, and `Still waiting` for `unknown`, an unrecognized value, no live update, or an older peer on the path. Resolving an interaction removes that card's own entry and publishes the newest still-open kind (or the call's base state), so the next beat changes state even when cards resolve out of order. Direct permission cards use their interaction kind rather than being mistaken for questions. A native LCU permission offering both session and always scopes is still `approval` when its four choices require question-card presentation; a genuine enum question remains `answer`. A confirmed phone call reports `approval` after its `tool_call` is sent and `computer` when the hub's wait for the phone result ends; a hub-owned settings approval uses the same two transitions. A nested LCU elicitation carries the canonical UUID `call_id` through the existing `computer.call` / `computer.elicit` requests only when the target node advertises `mcp_wait_v1`; the manager's live registry binds it to the originating machine and the same card state, with no machine-routing field on either request. An older target gets no correlator, and the manager reports `unknown` only for the duration of that delegated RPC before restoring the preceding state. These updates use `mcp.wait` and the opted-in local lines above; they carry no tool or interaction content and no table or setting retains them.

| Peer combination for a token-bearing call | Terminal wait message |
| --- | --- |
| New MCP process, new originating node, new hub and new manager | The live kind; `Still waiting` until the first update or whenever the kind is unknown |
| Old MCP process | Its legacy single-response behavior and historical lowercase `still waiting`; it never receives local interim lines |
| New MCP process with an old originating node | `Still waiting`; the old node does not forward the opt-in |
| New MCP process and originating node with an old hub | `Still waiting`; without the current hub feature the node generates no correlator |
| New MCP process, originating node and hub with an old manager | `Still waiting`; the old manager publishes no wait events |
| New upstream path delegating to an old target computer node | `Still waiting` during that `computer.call`, then the preceding live state; no nested correlator is sent |
| New upstream path and a capable target computer node | `Waiting for the computer` while it runs, or the live approval / answer kind for a correlated nested card |

An old MCP process here means the actual old binary, not a new process whose upstream peer is old: only the former retains the historical lowercase message. Every mixed combination still executes the tool and returns the same final result.

| Tool | Executed by | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Device `phone_*` tools | phone App | declared by the App via `register_phone` (contacts, calendar, reminders, location, health, photos, clipboard, device info, notifications…); the hub adds `queue_if_offline` to confirmed writes (below) |
| `phone_write_queue_list` / `phone_write_queue_cancel` | hub | inspect retained phone writes / cancel an unsent write, including when all phones are offline |
| `mail_accounts` / `mail_search` / `mail_read` | hub | read-only |
| `mail_save_attachment` | node on the agent's machine | writes a file under `<data dir>/attachments/mail`; the bytes come from the manager over `mail.attachment` (at most 25 MB, only while the mail connector offers the tool to that caller); `mail_read` lists the attachment ids |
| `mail_send` | hub (mail connector) | write: goes through `connector_gate`; by default a `permission` interaction is created before sending, and it sends only after approval on the phone. Bad params are refused directly without a card |
| `github_search` / `github_read` / `github_diff` / `github_checks` | hub (GitHub connector) | read-only, see the next row |
| `github_comment` / `github_review` | hub (GitHub connector) | write: goes through `connector_gate`; by default each one is confirmed on the phone. The card states repo#number "title", the full text and who will see it; approvals start with [Approve] |
| `<connector id>_*` | hub (connector) | only for the assistant, and only for connectors whose status is `ok`. Read-only tools run directly; writes first go through `connector_gate` in the manager's manager.json, which by default creates a `permission` interaction (the card states who will see it), and run only after approval on the phone (`server/internal/connector`) |

### Phone write queue

The hub adds an optional `queue_if_offline: boolean` to the schemas of `phone_calendar_create_event`,
`phone_reminders_create`, `phone_reminders_update`, `phone_reminders_complete`, `phone_reminders_delete`, and
`phone_health_write_sample`. Without true, the existing immediate call and background wake behavior stays unchanged.
With true and no connected device offering the tool, the hub persists a queue entry and immediately returns that record
as JSON text in a successful `ToolResult`. After admission it schedules a best-effort silent push in the background,
using the normal most-recent-device selection and 30-second wake throttle; the reply does not wait for the push or a
connection. Without configured push, this attempt does nothing. A woken phone registers its tools and triggers delivery
as usual. With a connected device the hub calls the tool normally. The hub strips the option
before sending `tool_call`; existing apps need no change, and reads and writes without phone confirmation cannot queue.
The tool must also appear in a retained phone registration before the hub accepts it into the queue. A queued receipt
means the request was accepted for later delivery; it does not mean the change was saved.

The queue belongs to this hub's transport, shared across its computer sessions and devices. An entry contains:

```text
PhoneWrite {
  id: string, tool: string, args: object,
  state: queued | delivering | succeeded | declined | failed | uncertain | cancelled,
  result?: ToolResult,
  created_at: RFC3339, updated_at: RFC3339
}
```

| Operation | Response |
| --- | --- |
| MCP `phone_write_queue_list {id?}` | `{items: [PhoneWrite], pending_count: N}`; an optional ID filters the list, but the count always includes all pending entries |
| MCP `phone_write_queue_cancel {id}` | The cancelled `PhoneWrite`; an already-cancelled ID returns the same record, otherwise an error if missing or no longer queued |
| `GET /api/v1/phone/write-queue?id=<optional id>` | The same list envelope; records in enqueue order, empty `items` if the ID is not retained |
| `POST /api/v1/phone/write-queue/{id}/cancel` | The cancelled record (also for a repeated cancellation); 404 if missing, 409 for any other nonqueued state |

Both HTTP routes use normal hub authentication and require full credentials; answer-only devices and extension tokens
cannot access them. They need no phone connection. Clients can poll the list on connection, foregrounding, and while a
queue view is visible. `pending_count` counts `queued` plus `delivering` and can supply a badge. This API prepares the data for an App queue view; iOS and Android do not yet display that view or badge.

At `register_phone`, the hub schedules a single asynchronous delivery loop. It picks the oldest queued entry whose tool
is currently registered by a connected phone, commits `delivering` before sending, and waits for that phone's result
before taking another entry. The normal phone confirmation remains mandatory. Queue delivery never holds the hub's
global lock while waiting for storage or the phone, and registration never waits for delivery. A disconnected or disabled
tool leaves its entries queued until a capable device registers it again. Each delivery pass reads only queued entries
in enqueue order, at most 100, using the queue's partial index; its idle timer does not load terminal history. The list
API and list tool use a plain SELECT without taking the queue mutation lock or deleting records.

| State | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `queued` | Persisted and not sent; cancellation is still possible |
| `delivering` | Claimed for delivery; awaiting the normal phone confirmation/result |
| `succeeded` | Phone returned a successful result |
| `declined` | Phone explicitly returned `The user declined on the phone.` with `isError: true` |
| `failed` | Phone returned another tool error; the result includes its explanation |
| `uncertain` | Confirmation timed out, the sending connection closed, or the hub restarted while delivery was in progress; never automatically resent |
| `cancelled` | Cancelled before delivery began |

Each send waits up to `phoneConfirmWait` (30 minutes), independent of the original caller's request lifetime. A timeout
or disconnect does not prove the phone made no change, even when a late result arrives after reconnecting; inspect the
actual phone data before submitting another write. Restart recovery changes leftover `delivering` entries to `uncertain`
and preserves queued entries. There is no automatic retry for terminal records.

Deduplication covers only `queued` entries: the same tool and normalized JSON arguments reuse the existing ID (key order
and whitespace are irrelevant). It does not cover already-delivering or terminal entries. The limit is 100 pending
entries (`queued` plus `delivering`), with at most 64 KiB of arguments each. Cleanup runs only on admission and when
recording a delivery result, removing terminal records older than 30 days and keeping the newest 1,000 terminal records.
Reads, cancellations, and startup recovery do not clean up: older records and additional terminal records from
cancellation or recovery remain visible until the next cleanup. The total table remains bounded at 1,100 records.
Stored results are limited to 64 KiB; when a phone returns more, the hub stores an explanation instead of its full result
without changing the outcome state. Pending entries do not expire or get evicted when a queue is full.
See `docs/apple/phone-tools.md`, "Offline write queue", for caller behavior and confirmation details.

## Connector API

Feature `connectors` (in the `features` of `/health` and the WebSocket hello); old hubs don't have this endpoint.

| Method | Path | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/api/v1/imessage` | `{machine, status, error?, guide?:[…], via?, ai}`: status of the Messages connector (which machine it reads is chosen in Settings › Extensions › Messages; if not chosen, manager.json's `imessage.machine`), asked of that Mac on the spot (after granting permission, a refresh shows the new state). Without Full Disk Access, `guide` gives step-by-step instructions to enable it on that Mac, and `via` is how that Mac's node runs (`ssh` / `launchd`; the two are enabled differently). Not set up: 404 `not_configured` |
| PUT | `/api/v1/imessage/settings` | `{ai: bool}`: the "Hand to Persona" switch (stored on the manager, on by default). While on, real chats go into the knowledge base and Inbox, and the assistant has `imessage_*` tools. A successful off response follows any already reserved archive page commits and stops retired pages from writing later; retained data is not deleted. If a reservation cannot finish or be checked within 30 seconds, off remains saved but the request fails so it can be retried. Returns the shape of `GET /api/v1/imessage` (with `ai`) |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/imessage/data` | deletes Messages data stored on the hub: Messages chats and people in the knowledge base (with indexes, references in projects and the timelines they wrote, archive cursors; projects are marked for rewrite), and Messages entries in the Inbox → `{chats, people, posts, items, inbox}` (posts and items are counts of other knowledge records owned by this connector). While "Hand to Persona" is on: 409 `ai_on` (turn it off first, or the next round syncs it back); messages on that Mac are unaffected |
| GET | `/api/v1/imessage/chats?limit=&before=` | that Mac's chats, newest first (the node's `connector.chats`; fields under "hub ↔ node" below). Read-only, not stored, not given to models. No permission 403 `no_permission`, Mac offline 503 `offline`, node too old 409 `node_outdated` |
| GET | `/api/v1/imessage/chats/{id}/messages?limit=&before=` | one page of a chat's messages, oldest first (the node's `connector.older`); an `id` that doesn't look like a chat id (`imessage-<12 hex chars>`) isn't sent to the Mac: 404 `no_chat` |
| GET | `/api/v1/connectors?all=1` | `{"connectors":[{id, name, status, account?, via?, error?, guide?:[…], last_sync?, last_event?, capabilities:[…], hosts?:[…], enabled, archive?, inbox?}]}`: connectors registered on the hub. Without `all=1`, Lark (`lark`) and mail (`mail`) are excluded: Apps before M6 draw every list entry as a row, and these two each have their own row, so they'd appear twice; Apps that pass it draw these two as the original Lark and mail rows themselves (status still read from `/api/v1/lark/status`, `/api/v1/mail/accounts`). `guide` is a one-sentence-per-step fix when something's wrong (how to enable permission on that Mac when the Messages connector lacks it). `status` is `ok` / `not_configured` / `not_signed_in` / `no_permission` / `rate_limited` / `error` / `disabled` (the user turned it off in settings; `enabled` is false); `via` says where the sign-in comes from ("gh sign-in from <machine>"); `error` is one human-readable sentence, without secrets; `capabilities` are drawn from `status` / `tools` / `actions` / `events` / `hosts` / `inbox` / `archive` / `login`; `hosts` are the hostnames of this connector's links (the App uses them to recognize links); `archive` / `inbox` are whether "Save to knowledge base" and "Send to Inbox" are on, only present for connectors with the `archive` / `inbox` capability |
| GET | `/api/v1/connectors/sent?before=&limit=&connector=` | the ledger of what was written as the user through the connectors' gate (`docs/extensions/connectors.md` "Sent as the user"), newest first → `{items: [{id, at, connector, action, target, text, summary, origin, let_through, message_ref?, recalled_at?, can_recall, chat_rule}], next}`. `target`, `origin` and `let_through` are objects (their shapes are in that section); `text` is at most 4000 characters. `can_recall` is whether the message can be taken back now, the answer a recall acts on (its connector is here, signed in and able to, the row has a `message_ref`, the kind of message can be taken back, it is not recalled yet and not too old); a message that ages out before the tap is refused by the recall (409 `too_old`). `recalled_at` is when it was taken back. An app that does not know `can_recall` reads the page as before. `chat_rule` says what the row offers: `{can, exists, id?, reason?}`: `can`: a rule that stops the asking about its chat can be made from it (`POST …/chat-rules` below), from a row taken back too (the rule is for the chat, not the message); `exists`: its chat has a rule of the user's (a hand-written rule before it can still decide otherwise), `id` being the rule's, for `DELETE`; `reason`: why none can be made (`recorded`, `mail`, `review`, `reply`, `route`, `target`, `command`, `unknown`). `let_through` of a write one of those rules let through is `{kind: "rule", rule, user_rule: true}` (for a write the node's Lark gate let through the mark is read by value, since the node does not say which rule it used: it can be missing, or on a write a same-shaped rule of an extension's own gate file let through; `docs/extensions/connectors.md`). A client that does not know `chat_rule` or `user_rule` loses only that: the write still reads as one a rule let through. `limit` defaults to 50, at most 200 (400 below 1); `before` is a row id (400 below 1), the rows older than it; `connector` keeps one connector's. `next` is the `before` for the page after this one, `null` on the last. The user's own full-access devices and the owner on the hub machine only (403 for an answer-only device, a pairing token or an extension's token, whatever its scopes); 503 `no_database` without a database |
| GET | `/api/v1/connectors/sent/chat-rules` | the rules the user made from the ledger ("don't ask again in this chat", `docs/extensions/connectors.md` "Sent as the user", Per-chat rules), newest first → `{rules: [{id, connector, chat, at, row?, summary?}], most}`. `id` is opaque and safe in a path; `connector` is `lark` or `github`; `chat` is a Lark conversation's id or `owner/name#number`; `row` is the ledger row it was made from (the ledger is pruned, the row may be gone) and `summary` that row's one line; `most` is how many rules there can be (500). Same callers as the ledger: the user's own full-access devices and the owner on the hub machine (403 for an answer-only device, a pairing token or an extension's token, whatever its scopes; an extension's token cannot be granted it); 503 `no_database` |
| POST | `/api/v1/connectors/sent/chat-rules` | `{row}` (a ledger row's id, and nothing else: any other field is 400, so no client can say what a rule allows; the manager makes the rule from the row, `connector.ChatRuleFor`): keeps the rule that lets writes into the chat the row went to through without a card → `{rule: {id, connector, chat, at, row, summary}, created}`; a chat that has a rule gets the rule it has (`created: false`). It takes effect at once for the assistant's tools and, for Lark, at the node's next pull (about a minute). A rule made is recorded in the audit (`connector_chat_rule_added`, `docs/extensions/extensions.md`), not one that was there already. Who may: the user's own full-access devices only (403 for the owner's hub token, an answer-only device, a pairing token or an extension's token, whatever its scopes; the owner may read the list and drop a rule). That is a rule of who is trusted, not a wall: a pairing token is redeemed for a full device's token, a full device can add a device (`POST /api/v1/auth/tokens`), and the owner on the hub machine can make a pairing code. 404 `not_found` for a row that is not there; 409 `no_chat_rule` when the row offers none, with `reason` (the same codes as `chat_rule.reason`); 409 `too_many_rules` at 500 rules; 500 `timeout` when the database did not answer in 15 seconds (the rule is not in force; the list says what the manager holds); 503 `no_database` |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/connectors/sent/chat-rules/{id}` | drops the rule with that `id` → `{ok: true}`: the next write into the chat is asked about again (a Lark rule at the node's next pull). 404 `not_found` when there is no such rule; 500 `store_failed` when the rule is off but could not be dropped from the database, each time that is asked (it comes back at the next start unless a later request finishes the drop; the database gets 15 seconds); 503 `no_database`.
