A drop is recorded in the audit (`connector_chat_rule_removed`, `docs/extensions/extensions.md`). Same callers as the list |
| POST | `/api/v1/connectors/sent/{id}/recall` | `{"confirm": true}` → `{ok: true, item}`: takes back the message the ledger's row `id` made (`docs/extensions/connectors.md` "Sent as the user", Recall; GitHub's issue comments, and what the connector of an extension that declares `recall` sent). Who may: the user's own full-access devices only, by hand: 403 `own_device_only` (with the reason) for the owner's master token on the hub machine (which does read the ledger), a pairing token, an answer-only device or an extension's token, whatever its scopes; an extension's token does not get through the hub either. The user's own device is the confirmation: the app asks in its own dialog, once, and sends `confirm: true`; no card is shown on the phone (#1190, what the user does by hand is not gated). A body without `confirm: true` recalls nothing (400 `confirm_required`, at once; a body that is not JSON 400, one over 4 KiB 413). `item` is the row as the ledger has it now (`recalled_at` set, `can_recall` false). The first confirmed request for a row calls the connector; every request that joins its flight receives the same result without another call: 200 with the same `item` on success, or the same real error (including 504 `recall_unknown`, never a generic busy response). Only the executing caller writes the audit record. A request after the flight gets 409 `already_recalled` if the message is gone, or makes a new attempt after failure / unknown. A request waits for at most one recall, about 40 seconds, so **a client's request timeout should be at least 60 seconds**. A recall that took a message back is recorded in the audit (`connector_recall`, `docs/extensions/extensions.md`). A failure is `{error, code}`: 404 `not_found`; 409 `not_recallable` (its connector cannot take that message back, the row has no message id, or the hub cannot tell the row is the extension's own: a send from before its install, or a gate the extension does not alone have), `too_old`, `already_recalled` (with `item`, the row as it is, whoever took it back); 503 `connector_unavailable` (switched off, not signed in, offline, its token refused) and `no_database`; 502 `recall_refused` (the other side refused, or whether the message is gone could not be checked: nothing changed); 504 `recall_unknown` (it may or may not be gone, nothing was recorded, asking again is safe); a failing ledger, or a mark that failed after the message was taken back (asking again finds it gone), a plain 500. An `id` that is not a number from 1 is 400 |
| POST | `/api/v1/connectors/{id}/login` | step-by-step sign-in (for connectors with the `login` capability, `docs/archive/extensions/plan-telegram.md`): `{"step": "", "values": {}}`; an empty `step` starts from the beginning, and later requests carry the previous `step` and the filled fields → `{step?, fields?:[{name, label, secret?, placeholder?}], hint?, error?, done?, account?, kind?, url?, user_code?, interval?}`: what to fill next, or `done`.
| GET | `/api/v1/subscriptions?connector=&extension=` | source subscriptions → `{subscriptions: [Subscription], features: {deliver, generate}}`; `Subscription`, its `state` (`off` / `ok` / `failing` / `not_connected` / `rate_limited` / `needs_recipe`) and `error {code, message}` are in [subscriptions.md](../extensions/subscriptions.md) "API". Every device may read |
| GET | `/api/v1/subscriptions/summary` | the entry rows' counts from cached catalogs only → `{connectors: [{connector, extension, subscribable?, on, failing}]}` |
| GET | `/api/v1/subscriptions/catalog?connector=` | a connector's subscribable sources and tools read now (each tool with its `input_schema`, `subscribable` or `refused {code, message}`), its sources' own recipes and existing subscriptions, `direct {inbox, archive}`. Without `connector`: `{catalogs: [...]}` from earlier reads only, never calling a connector |
| GET | `/api/v1/subscriptions/{id}` | `{subscription, runs}`: the newest 20 runs first, `{at, ms, trigger, new, count, error}` |
| POST | `/api/v1/subscriptions/-/dry-run` | `{id}` or `{connector, source}`, `recipe?` → `{ok, checks, shape, count, maybe_more, weak_dedup, items_path, items, paths, error}` (`items_path`: where the items were read, found when the recipe left it empty; `shape.arrays`: the top-level lists); writes nothing. Full access only (403 `read_only_device`), like every change below |
| POST | `/api/v1/subscriptions` | `{connector, source, recipe?, recipe_origin?, label?}` → 201 `Subscription`, both destinations off; a recipe that fails its checks is 422 with its code and `dry_run`; `recipe_origin: "model"` records a model's draft taken as it was |
| POST | `/api/v1/subscriptions/{id}/generate` | drafts a recipe with the model (purpose `subscription.recipe`): `{revision?}` for a subscription, saved when it passes → `{recipe, note, dry_run, subscription}`; `-` with `{connector, source}` → `{recipe, note, dry_run}`, nothing written. 422 with the check's code, `dry_run` and the draft's `recipe` when it still fails after one more try; 503 `no_model`, 502 `model_failed` ([subscriptions.md](../extensions/subscriptions.md) "Drafting with a model") |
| PUT | `/api/v1/subscriptions/{id}` | `{revision, label?, recipe?, to_inbox?, to_kb?, interval_seconds?, daily_at?, triage_rules?, fallback_tier?}` → `Subscription`; 409 `conflict` with the current `subscription`, 422 `interval_too_short` |
| POST | `/api/v1/subscriptions/{id}/run` | 202 `Subscription`: runs once as soon as its connector's limits allow |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/subscriptions/{id}?data=1` | 204: the subscription with its seen keys and pending items; `data=1` switches it off and has the Inbox and the knowledge base remove what they took first (503 `assistant_offline` while the assistant is away, the subscription left off) |
| POST | `/api/v1/subscriptions/-/ui` | the subscription pages as declarative UI, with an extension page's request and answer (`context`, `state`, `action`, `values` → `{view}` or an action's result). Every device may draw them; an `action` needs full access (403 `read_only_device`) ([subscriptions.md](../extensions/subscriptions.md) "Pages") |
When `kind` is `device_code`, this step has no fields: show `user_code` and have the user enter it at `url`; the App asks again every `interval` seconds with the same `step` (no values) until a different step or `done` comes back (GitHub's device-code sign-in). When `url` already carries the code (an https URL whose query's `user_code` is the step's `user_code`, as Lark's does), the hub also adds `qr` (the same `{size, rows}` as a `qr` step) so the App can show a code to scan with the phone, keeping the code and link for this computer (#5818); a URL that asks for the code to be typed (GitHub's) gets none.
When `kind` is `qr`, likewise no fields and the same polling: `url` is the content to scan with another App (WeChat), and the hub attaches its QR matrix `qr: {size, rows}` (`rows` is one string of `0` / `1` per row, without the quiet zone) for the App to draw; old Apps don't know this `kind` and show only `hint`. A wrong entry (bad verification code) returns the same step with `error`, keeping the form for re-entry; other errors 502. Filled values go only to the connector, never into logs or any response; the session obtained from sign-in is stored encrypted on the hub (`connector_secrets`) |
| GET | `/api/v1/connectors/github/auth` | where the GitHub sign-in comes from: `{source: "machine" \| "device", machine?, machines: [{id, name, state, account?, scopes?, missing?, error?}], scopes?, scopes_known, missing?: [{scope, affects}]}`. `state` is `signed_in` / `not_signed_in` / `no_gh` / `too_old` / `offline` / `error` (the hub asks gh on each online computer on the spot, then asks GitHub whose token it is and what scopes it has; the token never leaves the hub); `missing` lists scopes the token in use lacks and the features affected |
| PUT | `/api/v1/connectors/github/auth` | `{source: "machine", machine: "<id>"}` or `{source: "device"}`: switch the sign-in source, stored in hub settings (overrides manager.json's `github.auth.from_machine`); returns the same as above. Choosing a computer forgets the device-code sign-in token |
| POST | `/api/v1/connectors/{id}/logout` | sign out: the hub deletes the stored credentials and sign-in state, and the assistant clears pending turns and text questions for every channel backed by the connector. Whether the session on the other service also ends depends on the connector: Telegram ends its device session; other connectors usually just make the hub forget its own copy (such as GitHub's device-code sign-in), and authorization has to be revoked on the other service → `{"ok": true}` |
| PUT | `/api/v1/connectors/{id}/settings` | `{"enabled"?: bool, "options"?: {…}, "archive"?: bool, "inbox"?: bool}`: `options` is the connector's own settings (for those with the `options` capability, also included in GET; GitHub's is `{ci, muted_repos, ignore_branches}`, `docs/assistant/inbox.md` ("Noise reduction")); invalid ones 400; stored on the hub and kept across restarts; after a change the Inbox collects a round right away with the new settings. `enabled` is the switch in Settings › Connectors. A disabled connector doesn't run, provides no tools, collects nothing for the Inbox and adds nothing to the knowledge base; its status is `disabled`, and sign-in and sign-out work as usual. The choice is stored in hub settings and kept across restarts; a connector whose switch was never touched is on, except ones like Telegram where the user must enter credentials, which default to off. `archive` is "Save to knowledge base": when off, the hub no longer asks it for archive changes (not a single request), while the Inbox and assistant tools work as usual; `inbox` is "Send to Inbox": when off, nothing new is collected and existing entries stay. Both default to on; changing one on a connector without that capability returns 400; the choice is stored in hub settings → this connector's entry (same as `GET`) |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/connectors/{id}/data` | delete stored data: first turns this connector off (the switch is saved as off, or the next round syncs it back), then deletes its saved knowledge: chats and people, including permitted `archive_sources`, posts, and documents / meetings / events (with indexes, project references, archive cursors and deleted chats' history-import state), and its Inbox entries → `{chats, people, posts, items, inbox}`. Ownership and legacy-data rules: `docs/assistant/knowledge.md` ("Deleting a connector's saved knowledge"). Separate from signing out (`/logout`); the account and messages on the connector's side are unaffected |
| GET | `/api/v1/connectors/{id}/thread?thread=&before=&limit=` | connectors with the `threads` capability: one page of messages of an Inbox thread (the entry's `connector.thread`) → `{chat: {id, name, kind, url?, avatar?, members?, reply?, state?, author?, labels?, branch?, body?, body_format?}, messages: [{id, at, sender: {id?, name, avatar?}, mine?, event?, text?, format?, media?: [{kind, ref?, thumb?, mime?, name?, size?, duration?, width?, height?, emoji?}], reply_to?: {id, from?, text?}, edited?, url?, kind?, review?, code?, check?}], before?}`, oldest first; `before` pages back, and its absence means the start was reached; `limit` defaults to 30, at most 50. `chat.members` is a group's member count / a channel's subscriber count, given only on the first page (without `before`) and omitted when unknown (Telegram: `docs/archive/extensions/plan-telegram.md` ("Members")). A lark-cli page takes `kind` (`dm` / `group`) and `name` from the chat's own record (`im chats get`, read beside the messages and kept an hour; one that is refused is asked for again a minute later): its message list says neither. A direct chat's record has no name, so the page is named for the other person in it. Hubs before this sent `kind: ""`, which the web takes for a chat and the native apps took for a page that is not one (the item's plain text). Not signed in or switched off 409 (`code: unavailable`); the source refused 403 (`code: no_permission`); rate limited 429 (`code: rate_limited`, `error` says how much longer); no such connector 404. An item with no conversation of its own, a source subscription's (its `source` is the subscription's id, its thread `sub:<subscription>:…`, deleted since or not) or a connector's without `threads`, answers 200 with `{chat: {id: <thread>, name: "", kind: "none"}, messages: []}` (#5537): the apps show what the hub collected (the item's `context`) as for any page that is neither a chat nor GitHub's thread, with no error. Hubs before it answered 404 or 409 (`code: conversations_unsupported`, or no code before that): iOS falls back quietly on both, the web on the 404 and notes the 409 without a Retry; `…/media` and `…/thread/reply` still refuse them |
| GET | `/api/v1/connectors/{id}/media?ref=` | the bytes behind `avatar` / `ref` / `thumb` in a page (images, stickers, video thumbnails, avatars), `Content-Type` as is, `Cache-Control: immutable`; the hub stores them in `<hub directory>/cache/connector-media/` (at most 256 MB, oldest deleted first), and many concurrent requests for the same ref ask the connector only once |
| POST | `/api/v1/connectors/{id}/thread/reply` | `{thread, action, text, reply_to?}`: reply in the thread using the action given by the page's `chat.reply` (params `{chat, text, reply_to}`) → `{ok, result}`. Requests from the user's own devices (full device token) run directly without `connector_gate` (#1190); other identities such as pairing tokens still go through the gate, and refusals are 403 (`code: declined`). Rate limited 429 |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/connectors/{id}/archive` | delete stored knowledge base content: first turns off "Save to knowledge base" (saved as off, or the next round archives it back), then performs the same knowledge-base cleanup as `/data` → `{chats, people, posts, items, inbox: 0}`. The connector keeps running; the Inbox and tools are unaffected; connectors without the `archive` capability return 409 |

## Mail API

| Method | Path | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/api/v1/mail/accounts` | `{"accounts":[MailAccount]}` (no passwords) |
| POST | `/api/v1/mail/accounts` | add an account (password / authorization code): saved only after a successful connection test → `{"account"}`; `auth:"oauth2"` always returns 400 |
| GET | `/api/v1/mail/oauth/google/config` | Whether "Sign in with Google" can start on this hub: `{"configured": bool}` (false without `google.client_id`); the apps ask before showing the button and offer Gmail with an app password otherwise (`docs/extensions/mail.md` ("One-time setup: Google Cloud OAuth client")) |
| POST | `/api/v1/mail/oauth/google/start` | Gmail "Sign in with Google": `{"login_hint"?}` → `{"auth_url","callback_scheme","state"}`; the App opens `auth_url` with ASWebAuthenticationSession and waits for the `callback_scheme` callback; without `google.client_id` 400 `{"error","code":"google_not_configured"}`, the error in the client's language saying who sets it up, always containing "not configured" (older Android apps match that phrase) |
| POST | `/api/v1/mail/oauth/google/finish` | `{"state","code"}` from the callback URL (or `{"state","error"}`) → the hub exchanges for a refresh token, verifies IMAP + Gmail API (sending uses Gmail API), then saves → `{"account"}`; signing in again with the same email = update credentials (ID unchanged); state is single-use and expires after 15 minutes |
| GET / PUT | `/api/v1/mail/oauth/microsoft/config` | Outlook sign-in settings: `{configured, client_id?, source?: app\|config, redirect_uri}`; PUT `{client_id}` stores the client ID the user registered in Microsoft Entra (encrypted on the hub; empty string clears it; bad format returns 400) (`docs/extensions/mail.md` ("Outlook: Sign In with Microsoft")) |
| POST | `/api/v1/mail/oauth/microsoft/start` | `{"login_hint"?}` → `{"auth_url","callback_scheme","state"}`; 400 without a client ID |
| POST | `/api/v1/mail/oauth/microsoft/finish` | callback `{state, code}` or `{state, error, error_description}` → `{"account"}`; errors are turned into what to do next (admin consent, IMAP / SMTP AUTH disabled, authorization expired…). Signing in again with the same email = update credentials |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/mail/accounts/{aid}` | |
| POST | `/api/v1/mail/accounts/{aid}/test` | `{"ok":true}` / `{"error"}` |
| GET | `/api/v1/mail/accounts/{aid}/mailboxes` | `{"mailboxes":[{"name","role","unseen","total"}]}`, role ∈ inbox/sent/drafts/trash/archive/junk/"" |
| GET | `/api/v1/mail/messages?account_id=&mailbox=INBOX&limit=50&before_uid=&q=` | `{"messages":[MailSummary],"has_more","next_before_uid"?,"headers_only"?,"uid_validity"?}`; empty `account_id` = merge all accounts' inboxes (newest date first, no `next_before_uid`); if any account fails, return HTTP 502 with code `mail_search_incomplete` and no messages, so older clients cannot mistake a partial page for a complete one. Explicit single-account requests retain their own error and paging behavior. `next_before_uid`: the next page's `before_uid` when `has_more` is true; while a page of local matching (see below) hasn't been fully scanned, `messages` can be empty with `has_more` still true. `headers_only`: the server found nothing for `q` (providers such as 163 don't support keyword search), so results come from matching subject, sender, recipients / cc on the hub, without looking at bodies (`docs/extensions/mail.md` ("Capabilities")). `uid_validity`: the mailbox's UIDVALIDITY for a single-account list; a change means the server reassigned UIDs, so UID-based cursors must be invalidated; omitted when 0 or for a merged multi-account list |
| GET | `/api/v1/mail/messages/{aid}/{uid}?mailbox=INBOX` | `{"message":MailMessage}` |
| GET | `/api/v1/mail/messages/{aid}/{uid}/attachments/{attachment_id}?mailbox=INBOX` | download by account, mailbox, UID and the stable attachment ID from the details; same Bearer authentication as mail reads; supports `Range` / `If-Range`, returning `Accept-Ranges` / `Content-Range`, 206 or 416 |
| POST | `/api/v1/mail/messages/{aid}/{uid}/flags` | `{"mailbox","seen"?,"flagged"?}` |
| POST | `/api/v1/mail/send` | `{"account_id","to":[],"cc":[],"bcc":[],"subject","text","html"?,"in_reply_to"?,"references"?}`; `references` is a space-separated Message-ID string, but a string array is also accepted (old iOS sends this; the hub joins it with spaces) |

The mail details page first reads the body and attachment list, then submits `{"mailbox":"INBOX","seen":true}` via `/flags`. The details GET uses `BODY.PEEK`, preserving old clients' behavior rather than marking messages read automatically. Attachments include a stable `id`, filename, MIME type and decoded size; IDs bind the MIME order, file metadata and decoded content, so attachments with the same name can be distinguished. Downloads also use read-only `BODY.PEEK`, with no dependency on extensions such as BINARY; the server streams decoded content into a temporary file, then returns byte ranges of the decoded content via HTTP Range. Unknown attachments or changed content return 404; an account the manager doesn't have is 404 `mail_account_unknown`, with an `error` that names the account in the request's language (`/test` still answers `{"ok":false,"error"}`).

```jsonc
// MailAccount
{"id":"acc_…","name":"Gmail","email":"me@example.com","provider":"gmail|feishu|imap","auth":"password|oauth2",
 "username":"…","imap_host":"imap.gmail.com","imap_port":993,"smtp_host":"smtp.gmail.com","smtp_port":465,
 "smtp_security":"tls|starttls","status":"ok|error","error":""}
// Extra field on add: password. With provider feishu, the supplied servers are ignored; the hub tries both imap/smtp.larkoffice.com and imap/smtp.feishu.cn (993 / 465, SSL), saving the first pair that signs in successfully (docs/extensions/mail.md ("Lark mail"))
// MailSummary
{"account_id","mailbox","uid":123,"message_id","subject","from":{"name","email"},"to":[{"name","email"}],
 "date","snippet","seen":false,"flagged":false,"has_attachments":false}
// MailMessage = MailSummary + {"cc":[…],"text":"…","html":"…","attachments":[{"id","filename","mime","size"}],
//                               "in_reply_to","references":[…]}
```

## Inbox API

The hub collects Lark, mail and connector data in the background and hands it to the manager (assistant) to aggregate into entries (`docs/assistant/inbox.md` ("Ownership: the manager owns the Inbox"): entries in `server/internal/assistant/inbox.go`, sources in `server/internal/extmgr/inbox.go`). The hub forwards these endpoints to it; when the manager isn't connected they return `503 assistant_offline`.

| Method | Path | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/api/v1/inbox` | `{items:[InboxItem], as_of, triage}`: unhandled entries + the newest 200 of the entries handled in the last 3 days (by `done_at`, then `id`; the rest are on `GET /api/v1/inbox/done`), newest `updated_at` first; excludes `context`. Defaults to Lark and mail only; connector entries (GitHub…) with a `connector` block require `?sources=all`. Old Apps and watches don't pass it, so they don't draw PRs as mail; Android, Mac and new watches pass it (each draws a connector entry from its `connector` block). `triage`: `{state, reason?, waiting, sources?:[{source, name, state, reason, waiting, read_error?, read_reason?}]}`, how many new plugin-connector entries haven't entered the Inbox because they couldn't be triaged (and had no fallback) or weren't reached this round, and why; a source (a mail account as `mail:<account id>`, named by its address) the latest round couldn't read has `read_error` (`timeout` / `rate_limited` / `login_refused` / `failed`) and `read_reason`; when none, `{"state":"ok","waiting":0}` (`docs/assistant/inbox.md` ("AI triage"); old hubs lack it). `as_of` is when this list was read (hub clock, RFC 3339), sent back when handling in bulk by filter (`/bulk`; old hubs lack it). Each entry may also carry event fields (phase one, [inbox.md](../assistant/inbox.md) ("Events and handling chain"); old hubs lack them and old Apps don't recognize them): `status` (unhandled sections `action` / `working` / `fyi` / `noise`, falling back to `tier` when absent), `urgent`, `recap`, `handling`, `suggestion`, `chain` (handling chain, at most the latest 50 entries), `related` |
| GET | `/api/v1/inbox/done` | `?before=&before_id=&limit=&sources=all` → `{items:[InboxItem], next?:{before, before_id}}`: done entries the manager keeps (90 days, `docs/assistant/inbox.md` ("Lifecycle")), newest `done_at` first, ties by `id` descending; entries as in the list. `before` (RFC 3339 `done_at`) and `before_id` start after that entry (pass `next` back as is); without `before`, from the newest. `limit` 1–200, default 50. `next` only when the page is full (the page after may be empty). `sources=all` as in the list. A bad `limit`, a `before` that is not RFC 3339, or `before_id` without `before` is 400. One manager's page: the one named (`X-Persona-Manager`), else the default; items carry `manager` but pages are never merged, so ask each manager and merge by `done_at`. Watches (answer-only devices) can't call it; extensions need `inbox.read`. Old hubs: 404 |
| GET | `/api/v1/inbox/done/days` | `?tz=<IANA zone>&sources=all` → `{tz, days:[{day, count}]}`: how many done entries the manager keeps (the same as `/api/v1/inbox/done` pages) fall on each calendar day in `tz` (`day` is `YYYY-MM-DD`), newest day first; days with none are left out. `tz` is required and must be a zone name the hub knows (`Asia/Shanghai`, `UTC`; not `Local` or an offset), else 400: a day follows the zone's own offset on its date, across daylight saving. `sources=all` as in the list. The apps' Done shows each day's count with it and jumps to a day with `/api/v1/inbox/done?before=<the day's end>` (no `before_id`: the entries done before that moment). One manager's counts, routed as `/api/v1/inbox/done`; watches can't call it; extensions need `inbox.read`. Old hubs: 404 (#2967) |
| GET | `/api/v1/inbox/{id}` | one entry, with `context` (plain text of the chat / email, for AI); mail also carries `reply_target:{uid,version}`. Also answers a done entry of the history (`/done` above) the list no longer has |
| POST | `/api/v1/inbox/{id}/done` | `{done: bool, dismiss?: bool}`: mark handled / reopen; returns the entry. With `dismiss` true, this is "Ignore" (`done_by=dismissed`; old hubs treat it as handled). Reopening also brings back a done entry of the history the list no longer has (as do `/done` with `done:false` and `/bulk` `reopen`); marking one of those handled again is 404 (`missing` in bulk) |
| POST | `/api/v1/inbox/done` | `{done: bool, items:[{id, version?}]}` → `{changed:[InboxItem], unchanged:[id], skipped:[{id, reason}]}`: mark multiple entries at once (mark all handled, all seen / clear all, and their undo), one database write and one `inbox` push. `version` is the entry's `version` from the list: when marking handled, a mismatch (new messages merged in since listing) leaves it unmarked, with `reason=changed` in `skipped`; a missing entry has `reason=missing`; one already in that state goes in `unchanged` without changing `done_at` (retries or simultaneous taps on another device don't write twice). Reopening doesn't compare versions. At most 1000 entries; more returns 413; no `done` returns 400. Only recorded in Persona, not written back as read to the source (`docs/assistant/inbox.md` ("Mark All as Done")); old hubs lack this endpoint (405), so the App falls back to `/{id}/done` per entry. New clients use `/bulk` below; this stays for old Apps |
| POST | `/api/v1/inbox/bulk` | Clear all (`docs/assistant/inbox.md` ("Clean up all")): `{action, items?:[{id, version?}], ids?:[id], filter?, as_of?}` → `{action, changed:[InboxItem], ids:[id], unchanged:[id], skipped:[{id, reason}], undo?:{action:"reopen", ids}}`. `action` is `done` (handled, `done_by=user`) / `dismiss` (ignored, `done_by=dismissed`) / `reopen` (reopen, for undo); clients send only `dismiss` for Clear all, keeping `done` for sections and clients before #5114. **Either** provide `items` / `ids` (`ids` is shorthand without versions; both can be supplied): handle only these, with the same rules as `/done` (version mismatch on marking: `skipped reason=changed`; missing: `missing`; already in that state: `unchanged`); **or** provide `filter` + `as_of`: handle unhandled entries selected by `filter`, using the `as_of` returned by `GET /api/v1/inbox` (or `/refresh`); entries arriving after it, or with new messages merged after it, are left alone (`skipped reason=changed`). `filter`: `{sources?: "all", source?, account?, tier?, kinds?:[]}`, where `source` is lark / mail / connector id, `account` is `feishu` or a mail account id, `tier` is action / fyi / noise / untriaged, and `kinds` is a list of `kind` values; without `sources:"all"`, connector entries are excluded as in the list. Client-side filters such as search use `ids`. `reopen` only accepts `ids`. `ids` lists what changed this time; POSTing `undo` back as is undoes it (reopens only what changed this time). One database write and one `inbox` push for the batch; only recorded in Persona, not written back as read to the source. At most 1000 entries (413); unknown `action`, supplying both or neither of `ids` and `filter`, `filter` without `as_of`, `reopen` with `filter`, or unknown `tier` all return 400. Watches (answer-only devices) can't call it (403); extensions need `inbox.write`. Old hubs lack it (404 / 405): fall back to `/done` (Clear all is recorded there as done) |
| POST | `/api/v1/inbox/merge` | Merge rows by hand (`docs/assistant/inbox.md` ("Merge rows and Add to to-dos")): `{items:[{id, version?}]}`, 2 to 20 → `{item: InboxItem (the survivor, with merged_from), members:[id], skipped:[{id, reason}], undo:{id}}`; fewer than two mergeable left: 409; fewer than two sent: 400. Extensions need `inbox.write`; old hubs lack it (404 / 405): hide the button |
| POST | `/api/v1/inbox/merge/undo` | `{id}` (the survivor) → `{changed:[InboxItem]}`: the members get their rows back; 404 when it has none |
| POST | `/api/v1/inbox/todo` | Add rows to to-dos: `{items:[{id, version?, title?}], due_at? | due_date?}` (the client works the due time out: a moment, or a day for all day) → `{changed:[InboxItem], unchanged, skipped, failed, todos:[{item, todo}], undo?:{items:[{id, todo_id}]}}`; each filed row is `done_by=todo`, a row not filed gets no to-do |
| POST | `/api/v1/inbox/todo/undo` | `{items:[{id, todo_id}]}` → the bulk result: the to-dos are deleted and the rows reopened |
| GET | `/api/v1/inbox/mutes` | `{mutes:[{id, source, source_name, tag, value, name, created_at}]}`: the user's mutes (`tag` is `repo` / `chat` / `sender`, `docs/assistant/inbox.md` ("Muting")). Each entry in the list carries `mutes:[{tag, value, name}]`, saying how it can be muted (old hubs lack it) |
| POST | `/api/v1/inbox/mutes` | `{item_id, tag}` → `{mute, settled}`: mute this entry's value under `tag` (the hub reads it from the entry), settle open entries covered by it in the same source (`settled` count), and settle future arrivals; only one copy of each mute exists |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/inbox/mutes/{id}` | unmute: future entries arrive normally; already settled entries don't return |
| GET | `/api/v1/inbox/policies` | `{policies:[{id, source, source_name, tag, value, name, tier?, twin?, created_at, updated_at}]}`: the user's policies (`docs/assistant/inbox.md` ("Policies")): `tier` is `action` / `fyi` / `noise`, `twin` is `first` / `never`. An entry's policy is the one whose `source` and `tag` + `value` match one of its `mutes` options, `sender` before `chat` before `repo` (old hubs: 404) |
| POST | `/api/v1/inbox/policies` | `{item_id, tag, tier?, twin?}` → `{policy, applied}`: set the policy of this entry's value under `tag` (read from the entry; nonexistent entry 404, unknown tag / tier / twin 400). A policy for the same target is updated; one left with neither `tier` nor `twin` is removed. Open triaged entries it covers get its tier at once (`applied` count) |
| PATCH | `/api/v1/inbox/policies/{id}` | `{tier?, twin?}` → `{policy, applied}`: set both parts as given; neither removes it; unknown id 404 |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/inbox/policies/{id}` | remove a policy: entries keep the tier it gave until new content is triaged again |
| POST | `/api/v1/inbox/{id}/draft` | `{instruction?}` → `{text}`: draft a reply in the user's voice (not sent); `503 model_unavailable` when no model the hub can call directly is set up for drafting |

| POST | `/api/v1/inbox/{id}/task-link/recheck` | Maintenance: rejudge an open event against all open task candidates without starting processing or sending a reply. Preserves eligible links and drafts; saves before supervisor signaling. Returns `{status, method?, item}` (`linked`, `unmatched`, `existing`; `method: "judge"` if called). Bot/app broadcasts return `excluded` or `cleared` (`method: "policy"`): remove only an ineligible task link, without a model, task card or notification. `409` for `disabled`, `closed`, `changed`, `task_closed`; `404` unknown event, `502` model failure, `503` failed read/save. Eligible rejudgment requires the AI twin; policy correction does not. Extension scope `inbox.write`. |
| POST | `/api/v1/inbox/{id}/reply` | `{text, changes?, client_id?, expected_uid?, expected_version?}` (if the assistant connection breaks mid-send: 502 `assistant_in_doubt`, `delivered:"unknown"`; it may already have been sent, and retrying the same one won't send twice): send to the original Lark chat / as a mail reply / as a cloud-document comment (where `doc.reply` points), and mark handled (`done_by=replied`); returns the entry. For cloud documents, `changes:[{ref,field,value}]` changes statuses before commenting; `text` may be empty for status-only changes. With `client_id`, a receipt is saved, and Lark passes it through as upstream `clientId`; without it, `clientId` is computed from the entry id and text (UUIDv5), so retries after a hub restart don't duplicate it either. A Lark entry's same reply is sent only once: replies to the same entry are queued; an entry already handled by reply with the same text returns success directly without sending again. Different text is sent normally. Lark destination: DMs go into the chat; non-empty `lark.thread_kind` replies to `reply_to` within its topic; group @mentions (`kind=mention`) reply quoting `reply_to`; other groups and old data without `reply_to` still send into the chat |
| POST | `/api/v1/inbox/{id}/suggestion` | `{version, action, text?, client_id?}`: act on the current suggestion (submitted by the manager's handling chat, [inbox.md](../assistant/inbox.md) ("AI twin: handling chats and suggestions")): `confirm` (execute as is, or after editing when `text` is supplied) / `reject` (return to the handling chat) / `instruct` (`text` required, return for a new suggestion) → this item. Confirmed replies use the same send-once path as `/reply`, but do not mark done (`handling.state=waiting`). `409 {code:"suggestion_stale", error, item}` when `version` is not current or no suggestion remains; `409 inbox_item_done`; `400`; `403` for answer-only devices except text confirmation of replies or conclusions; `502 assistant_in_doubt` as in `/reply`. Old hubs lack it (404 / 405) |
| POST | `/api/v1/inbox/{id}/handoff` | Hand to AI with write-back ([inbox.md](../assistant/inbox.md) ("Item actions")), in two forms. `{text, client_id?}` sends `text` after a block naming the item to its main conversation (`session.send_once` with `client_id` as the message id; without one, a UUIDv5 of the item and text), or starts the main conversation with it. `{session:{machine_id, session_id}, kind:"agent"|"conversation", title?, client_id?}` without `text` only records a hand-off the client already sent: nothing is sent or woken, processing and done state stay unchanged, and the chain gets `agent` or `handling` with the session link and `via:user`. Both forms record `handoffs` so that conversation may write back with `inbox_suggest` `item`, and answer `{item, session:{machine_id, session_id}}`. The same `client_id` again answers as before without recording or sending again; the record-only form derives a missing id from the item, session and kind. For the sending form, the hub keeps a receipt by `client_id` as for `/reply`, and answers `502 assistant_in_doubt` when the link to the manager breaks mid-request (retrying the same one won't send twice). `400` without text in the sending form, or with text / missing session ids / an invalid kind in the record-only form; `404` for an unknown item. A failed send or start records nothing and is answered as `POST /api/v1/assistant/conversations` answers it (a refusal the node codes `409` with its code, offline `503`, otherwise `502`, a work machine included). Not for answer-only devices (403). Old hubs and managers lack it (404 / 405) |
| POST | `/api/v1/inbox/{id}/doc/status` | `{ref, field, value}`: set this row's status in a cloud document to `value` (must be an option for that column); read the latest value before writing (if someone just changed it, fails with 409); returns the reread entry |
| POST | `/api/v1/inbox/refresh` | collect once immediately, returning the list and `triage` (`?sources=all` as above); new plugin-connector entries enter the list after background triage finishes, without waiting for it. When the collect call itself fails, nothing was read now and it answers `502 {code:"inbox_refresh_failed", error, detail, retryable:true}` instead of the list (`error` a sentence in the request's language, `detail` the collect's error), so a refresh never looks like it worked when it did not; a source that could not be read within a round that did run is still `200`, named in `triage.sources[].read_error`. Older hubs answer `200` with the list as it was |
| PUT | `/api/v1/inbox/{id}/parent` | `{kind, id}` sets this entry's parent (`kind` is `inbox` / `todo` / `session`); `null` or `{}` removes it → this `InboxItem`; missing entry or parent 404, invalid parent 400, would create a cycle 409 ([inbox.md](../assistant/inbox.md)) |
| PUT | `/api/v1/inbox/{id}/folder` | `{folder}`: a `/`-separated path files the entry there by hand (`folder_by: user`), `""` takes it out of every folder, `null` hands it back to the model → this `InboxItem`; missing entry 404, a path that normalizes to nothing 400 ([inbox.md](../assistant/inbox.md) "Folders") |
| GET / PUT | `/api/v1/inbox/folders` | Folder settings and the folders in use: `{enabled, rules, folders: [{path, count, open}]}`; PUT takes `{enabled?, rules?}` and answers the same ([inbox.md](../assistant/inbox.md) "Folders") |
| GET | `/api/v1/inbox/tree/{kind}/{id...}` | a node's trail: `{node, item?, ancestors:[{kind, id, item?}], children:[InboxItem]}`, children ordered by start time; missing entry 404, invalid `kind` / `id` 400 |
| POST | `/api/v1/translate` | `{texts:[string]≤30, target}` → `{texts}`, preserving order; missing model outputs are empty strings. target is BCP 47 (zh-Hans, en, ja…, `docs/apple/ios.md` ("Translation")). Like the Inbox, this belongs to the assistant (forwarded through the hub), using the "Translation" use in model configuration |
| POST | `/api/v1/translate/mail` | `{account_id, uid, mailbox, target}` → `{subject, text, clipped?, model_fingerprint?}`: the assistant asks the hub to read this mail (HTML-only mail becomes text preserving paragraphs and links), then translates it itself; returns the Inbox's existing translation if it used the same model; body at most 12000 characters. An account the manager doesn't have is 404 `mail_account_unknown`, as on the mail routes; other failures to read or translate the mail are 502 |

Mail replies may carry `expected_uid` and/or `expected_version` from the details response. The version binds the account, mailbox, UID in the thread, message identifier and sender. A changed target returns HTTP 409, `code=mail_reply_target_changed`, `delivered=none`, `retryable=false`; nothing was sent this time. The App keeps the draft, loads the latest mail, and after the user confirms the new recipients makes a new request with a new `client_id`. When the network result is unknown, it checks the receipt using the original request, target and `client_id`. Omitting the validation fields preserves old behavior, so existing iOS needs no changes; persistent receipt rules are unchanged.

`InboxItem`: `id`, `source` (lark / mail, or a connector id: github), `kind` (dm / mention / group / bot / mail; connectors define their own: review_requested / mention / team_mention / author / ci_failed / assign), `account` (`feishu` or a mail account id),
`account_name`, `title` (chat name / mail subject), `sender`, `avatar`, `preview` (latest message), `count`, `started_at`, `updated_at`,
`tier` (action / fyi / noise, empty before triage), `summary`, `reason`, `read` (seen elsewhere), `done_at` (the history's order and cursor, `GET /api/v1/inbox/done`), `done_by` (user / dismissed / read / replied; dismissed means the user chose "Ignore"), `version` (what this entry currently contains; changes when new messages merge in; sent back when marking handled in bulk; old hubs lack it),
`lark{account_id,ol_account,feed_id,is_group,is_topic,start_position,read_position,mention_position,at_all,reply_to,thread_kind}` (`account_id`: the Lark gateway account number this chat belongs to; 0 in old records = account 1; `ol_account`: present for a non-default account, the `ol_account` to pass when opening the chat or calling Lark endpoints; `read_position`: this chat's read position in Lark, refreshed on every collection; `reply_to`: id of the last message sent by someone else; `thread_kind`: where it is, empty = in the chat, `topic` = a topic in a topic group, `thread` = a threaded reply in a regular group; these two refresh when new messages are collected and are absent in old data), `conversation{source,id,account?,start_position?,read_position?,mention_position?}` (present in the list: where to open a Lark entry in the messaging source; `source` is the connector id, `account` is the `account` to pass for a non-default account; Apps with this source use it, `docs/extensions/extension-messaging.md` ("Live events and the Inbox")), `mail{account_id,mailbox,uids,message_id,from,direct,thread}`,
`translations{<target language>:{subject,preview}}` (foreign-language mail the hub translates ahead of time, `docs/apple/ios.md` ("Translation")), `doc{url,link,type(docx/doc/sheet/base/other),notice(mention/comment/reply),notice_id,rows:[{ref,table,title,fields:[{name,value}],status:[{field,name,value,options:[{name,color}]}]}],reply{kind(thread/record/cell/doc),label,…},error}`
(`kind=doc`, `docs/assistant/inbox.md` ("Docs: mentions in sheets, bases, and documents")); `agent.changes:[{ref,field,value}]` are status changes the AI twin proposes with its draft;
`connector{thread,label,url,open_url,reply_to,can_reply,rule_tier}`: a connector entry (`docs/assistant/inbox.md` ("Connector: GitHub")); the App draws only this block, without knowing the specific source:
`label` is the row label, `url` opens inside the App, `open_url` is handed to the system (`sms:` and similar), `reply_to` says where a reply goes and who can see it, and `can_reply` false means replies aren't allowed (CI failure).
When the list changes, WebSocket pushes `{"type":"inbox"}` (no content; the App fetches it).

## Lark bot

`/api/v1/bots/feishu` (read status / change credentials, toggles and features), `…/pair` (pairing code), `…/owner` (DELETE unpairs), `…/test` (test message); fields in `docs/extensions/bots.md` ("Configuration and endpoints").

## Knowledge base API

The knowledge base belongs to a manager (the assistant). The hub forwards these endpoints to it as-is (the forwarding in "Bus" above); when it is not connected the hub returns `503 assistant_offline`. Returns `503 kb_disabled` when the manager has disabled the knowledge base, and `503 kb_unavailable` while it is enabled but not ready. A successful list with no entries is `200 {"items":[],"tags":[]}`. Clients distinguish these states from transport failures. `kind` supports `projects`, `chats`, `people`, `docs`, `meetings`, `events`, `recordings` (recordings are read-only here; writes go through "Recording sync" below), `topics` (knowledge points by subject, #3783: the list puts the most points first with the count in `extra`; `detail.points` is `[{id, path?, kind, text, why?, sources?: [{kind, id, day?}], when?}]` with `kind` one of `concept`, `decision`, `practice`, `pitfall`, `fact`, `question`; `PUT` changes `name`, `note`, aliases, tags and `pinned` only; `docs/assistant/knowledge.md` "Topics").

| Method | Path | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/api/v1/kb/{kind}?tag=` | `{items,tags}`; can filter by tag |
| GET | `/api/v1/kb/{kind}/{id}` | `{detail,agents?}`; for a project, can also return related online Agents |
| PUT | `/api/v1/kb/{kind}/{id}` | body is a `kb.Update` (projects also take `unmerge: true`); can update name, tags, importance, summary and project properties; returns `{id}`; fields in [knowledge.md](../assistant/knowledge.md) |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/kb/projects/{id}` | Soft-deletes a project into the knowledge base's trash and unlinks it from its chats, people and items; returns the trash entry `{id, kind, slug, name, deleted_at, unlinked}`; `404` for unknown or merged projects, `403 kb_read_only` when read-only ([knowledge.md](../assistant/knowledge.md) "Deleting a project") |
| GET | `/api/v1/kb-trash` | `{items}`: deleted projects' trash entries, newest first |
| POST | `/api/v1/kb-trash/{id}/restore` | Restores a deleted project and its recorded links; returns the entry; `404` if there is no such entry, `409` if a project with its slug exists again, `403 kb_read_only` when read-only |
| GET | `/api/v1/kb-search?q=&messages=0&kind=` | `{hits}`; includes messages by default, `messages=0` excludes them; `kind` (one of `projects`, `chats`, `people`, `docs`, `meetings`, `events`, `recordings`, `topics`) searches that kind only, as `kb_search` does, with `results=1` too (#3862 phase 6: `recordings` for meetings); another `kind` is a `400`, and a hub from before ignores it and searches every kind |
| GET | `/api/v1/kb/chats/{id}/context` | What the knowledge base knows about a chat: `{chat_id, chat_name, kind, summary, projects:[{name, summary}]}` (top three projects); read-only, used by the extension's `/agent`; 404 if the chat does not exist ([knowledge.md](../assistant/knowledge.md)) |
| GET | `/api/v1/kb/chats/{id}/days/{day}` | All messages of a chat on one day: `{day, messages, prev, next}` (`prev` / `next` are the nearest earlier / later days with messages); 404 if none |
| GET | `/api/v1/kb/selection` | The selection document: what chats and documents bring into the knowledge base and for how many days (the defaults when none was saved; [knowledge.md](../assistant/knowledge.md) "Selection") |
| PUT | `/api/v1/kb/selection` | The whole document, validated: `400` says what is wrong (unknown rule names, an `order` without every rule exactly once, days outside 1–36500, `context` outside 0–200, items without a source, kind or id), `403` from a read-only device; returns the stored document and sends a `kb_selection` event |
| GET | `/api/v1/kb/selection/candidates?source=` | A connector's chats for the per-item picker: `{source, cached?, listed_at, chats:[{id, name, kind, source, bot?, muted?, collapsed?, done?, estimate?, item, read, days?}]}`; `read` is `whole`, `personal` or `none`; `cached` when the history import runs or is stopped and the list comes from its plan; `404` when the connector offers no history |

### Recording sync (#3235)

After transcription, recordings from the phone (including ones the watch sends back to the phone) are synced into the knowledge base's `recordings` through these endpoints ([recording.md](../apple/recording.md), [knowledge.md](../assistant/knowledge.md) ("Recordings")). Only the transcript text is sent, never audio.
Like the other knowledge base endpoints, the hub forwards them as-is to the manager; they need a device token; 503 when the knowledge base is off or the manager is not connected.

| Method | Path | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PUT | `/api/v1/recordings/{id}` | Upload or update a recording (idempotent, see below) |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/recordings/{id}` | Delete: `200 {"deleted": true\|false}` (false means it did not exist); removes the files and index, leaves a tombstone |
| GET | `/api/v1/recordings` | Reconciliation: `{"days":14,"recordings":[{"id","revision","complete","started_at","minutes_state"?,"trimmed_at"?}],"deleted":["<id>"]}` (`days` is `recording_days`; a trimmed recording is listed with `trimmed_at`, see below) |
| POST | `/api/v1/recordings/{id}/minutes` | Make or remake the meeting minutes (below) |
| POST | `/api/v1/recordings/{id}/minutes/todos` | Turn confirmed action items of the minutes into to-dos (below) |
| POST | `/api/v1/recordings/{id}/live` | Append finished sentences while an attended meeting records ("Attending a meeting" below) |
| POST | `/api/v1/recordings/{id}/segments` | Append transcript sentences to an all-day recording ("All-day recordings" below) |
| GET | `/api/v1/recordings/{id}/live` | An attended meeting's live state and its questions (below) |
| POST | `/api/v1/recordings/{id}/ask` | Ask the attending Persona a question during the meeting (below) |

`{id}` is the recording's UUID (case-insensitive, stored lowercase). Each PUT carries the **complete state so far** and overwrites the same record in full, so replays, reordering and transcript completion never create an extra record:

```jsonc
{
  "revision": 3,                              // required, > 0; increases monotonically per recording (suggested: this state's update time, in ms)
  "started_at": "2026-11-05T09:00:00+08:00",  // required, RFC 3339
  "ended_at": "2026-11-05T10:02:13+08:00",    // omitted while still recording
  "duration": 3733.5,                         // seconds recorded so far
  "language": "zh-CN",                        // BCP 47
  "device": "phone",                          // phone | watch: the device that recorded
  "title": "",                                // optional, name given by the user
  "kind": "note",                             // optional: "meeting" or "note" (default "note"); a meeting gets minutes ([meeting-minutes.md](../assistant/meeting-minutes.md)); "day" on a hub with recording_day ("All-day recordings" below)
  "calendar": {"title": "", "attendees": [], "location": ""},  // optional hint from the device's own calendar; no event id
  "attendance": "off",                        // optional: "off" (default), "listener" or "participant" (below)
  "attending_session": {"machine_id": "<machine id>", "session_id": "<session id>"},  // optional: absent = the main chat
  "bookmarks": [{"at": 120.5, "label": ""}],  // at: seconds from the start
  "segments": [{"start": 0, "end": 4.2, "text": "…"}],  // seconds from the start; "echo": true marks Persona's echo (meeting_echo, below)
  "spoken": [{"start": 10, "end": 17.5, "text": "…"}],  // optional, meeting_echo: where Persona spoke and what it said
  "complete": false                           // true only when recording has ended and transcription is fully done; send the parts available before that
}
```

Minutes for a meeting recording ([meeting-minutes.md](../assistant/meeting-minutes.md)):

- `kind` and `calendar` are optional and travel with the full-state upload, so a later upload replaces them. Unknown `kind` is `400`. A client sending neither is unchanged.
- `calendar` keys other than `title`, `attendees` and `location` are ignored; a title or location over 200 characters, more than 100 attendees or one over 100 characters is `400`.
- A recording is a meeting when `kind` is `meeting`, when a `meetings` or `events` item in the knowledge base overlaps a recording of at least 5 minutes, or once the user asked for minutes (`minutes_asked`).
- `GET /api/v1/kb/recordings/{id}` adds to `detail.meta`: `kind`, `calendar` (when sent), `meeting` (`{kind, id, name}` of an overlapping `meetings` or `events` item, when matched), `minutes_state` (`pending`, `ready`, `failed`; absent when not a meeting; also on each recording of `GET /api/v1/recordings`) and `minutes_asked`. Once minutes were written, `detail.minutes` is `{version, revision, generated_at, title, when, where?, attendees?, points:[{text, at, who?}], decisions:[{text, at}], actions:[{id, who?, what, by?, due_date?, at, todo_id?}], open:[{text, at}], partial?, language?, markdown}`, with `at` in seconds from the start, the same clock as `segments[].start`; previous minutes stay while newer ones are `pending` or `failed` (their `revision` is below `meta.revision`). Absent sections and unknown names are omitted, never filled in. `version` increases at every rewrite; `revision` is the recording revision they were made from; `due_date` (`YYYY-MM-DD`) only when the spoken `by` resolves to one date; `markdown` is the same minutes as text with clock times. `language` (`zh-Hans`, `en`, `ja`) is what the minutes and their Markdown's headings are written in: the recording's `language`, else the owner's; absent on minutes from an older hub, which are Chinese (#5906).
- `detail.summary` stays the short summary either way. `kb_get` prints the minutes (`minutes.md`) and each action item's to-do state before the transcript, and `kb_search` matches the minutes text (`kind=recordings` searches the recordings alone).
- `POST /api/v1/recordings/{id}/minutes` (re)generates the minutes, also for a recording that is not a meeting yet (it becomes one): `202 {"state":"pending"}`, `409` when the transcript is not `complete`, `409 transcript_expired` when the recording was trimmed (below), `404` when the recording does not exist. It does not change the transcript or the revision.
- `POST /api/v1/recordings/{id}/minutes/todos` `{"version": 2, "actions": ["a1"]}` creates one ordinary to-do per listed action (title `what`, prefixed `who: ` when named; due `due_date`) and writes its `todo_id` back → `200 {"todos":[Todo],"minutes":Minutes}`. An action with a `todo_id` is not created again, and a retried request creates nothing new. `409 minutes_stale` when `version` is not the current one; `404` no recording, no minutes or an unknown action; `400` empty `actions`; `403` from a device that cannot write to-dos.
- When minutes become ready the manager sends one push (`notify.request`, kind `assistant`, a stable id per recording and `version`; a tap opens the main chat) and the same text, with the recording's web link, to the Lark bot and the channels with pushes on. From #3862 phase 6 the push names the recording: the notification's `recording_id` (`assistantwire.Notification.RecordingID`), which the hub puts at the top level of the push payload and on the WebSocket `notify`, beside `machine_id` and `session_id` (still the main chat), only when it is a UUID. Apps that know it open the meeting's thread; others, and every push from an older manager, open the main chat as before.

- Response `200 {"id","revision","status","attendance"?,"attendance_problem"?}` (the last two below): `stored` was written (a replay of the same revision also overwrites); `stale` the stored revision is higher, nothing written; `expired` the start time is before the retention window, or the recording was trimmed, not stored.
- `410`, `code: recording_deleted`: this recording was deleted (the tombstone stays until the retention window ends); the phone should stop sending it.
- `400`: id is not a UUID, `revision` ≤ 0, missing `started_at`, unknown `device`, or too large (at most 20000 segments, 4 MB of transcript in total).
- Segments are sorted by `start`; empty text is dropped. When `complete` goes from true back to false (re-transcribing in another language) the record is overwritten as usual, and the summary is redone once transcription completes.
- **Persona's echo** (#5905, [meeting-minutes.md](../assistant/meeting-minutes.md) "Persona's echo"), on a hub that lists `meeting_echo`: a meeting's segment may carry `"echo": true` (Persona's own answer as the microphone heard it), and `spoken` lists the stretches Persona spoke in with the answer said in each (`text` absent for one saved before). The hub marks a segment echo when the phone did, or when it overlaps a span (0.5 s more on each side) and its words are the span's (60% of its character bigrams after normalizing; a span without text keeps the old rule, at least half inside). Echo segments are kept (`detail.segments` carries `echo: true`, `transcript.md` marks them `[Persona 回声]`) but left out of the minutes, the summary, the follow-up's seed and `chars`. `spoken` has at most 1000 spans, each text cut to 4000 bytes; one that is not a list or is over the limit, and a malformed span, are ignored, never failing the upload. A phone leaves echo lines out of the upload to a hub without `meeting_echo`.
- The retention window is the assistant setting `recording_days` (default 14, 1–365): `GET /api/v1/assistant` includes the effective value, `PUT /api/v1/assistant {"recording_days": 30}` changes it, and `assistant.recording_days` in `persona_settings` can also read and change it.
  On every pass the manager deletes recordings whose start time is past the retention window, together with their files and index.
  A recording with minutes is trimmed instead (#3780): it keeps `meta.json` (with `trimmed_at`), `minutes.json` and `minutes.md`, loses its transcript, summary and live log, and is deleted by retention only once its start is past a finite `minutes_days` (`GET` / `PUT /api/v1/assistant`, `assistant.minutes_days` in `persona_settings`; forever by default: unset or `0`, otherwise 1–3650, never below `recording_days`; the settings tool also accepts `"forever"`). A trimmed recording stays in reconciliation at its revision with `trimmed_at`, an upload of it is `expired`, `GET /api/v1/kb/recordings/{id}` returns its meta and minutes with no `segments`, and its to-dos can still be confirmed. Tombstones keep the `recording_days` window either way ([meeting-minutes.md](../assistant/meeting-minutes.md) "Privacy").
- Reading: `GET /api/v1/kb/recordings`, `GET /api/v1/kb/recordings/{id}` (`detail.meta` is the fields above except `segments` and `spoken`, with `attendance` and `attending_session` as below, plus `name` and tags; `detail.summary`; `detail.segments`, Persona's echo among them with `echo: true`); `kb-search` finds the full transcript text.

#### Attending a meeting (#2981)

The normative text, with every rule and example, is [meeting-minutes.md](../assistant/meeting-minutes.md) "Attending a meeting"; this is the summary. Only on a hub that lists the `meeting_attendance` feature, which it does only while the default manager names that capability in its `manager.hello`.

- Upload fields: `attendance` (`off` default, `listener`, `participant`) and `attending_session` (`{machine_id, session_id}`; absent, `null` or both ids empty = the main chat, as it is at each batch) travel with the full-state upload like `kind`. They never fail an upload: an unknown role, a role on a recording whose `kind` is not `meeting`, or a half-filled or over-long session is stored as `off`, and the `200` adds `attendance` (in effect) and `attendance_problem` (`unknown_role`, `not_meeting`, `bad_session`). `detail.meta` returns them (`attendance` absent when off, `attending_session` absent for the main chat). An attending recording is uploaded once when it starts, with `segments: []`.
- `POST /api/v1/recordings/{id}/live` `{"from": 12, "segments": [{"start","end","text"}]}` appends finished sentences to the recording's live log by position, append-only: positions below the hub's count are skipped, so retries store nothing twice; a bad sentence is clamped or cut, never refused. `200 {"next","attendance","attending_session"?: {machine_id, session_id, main?},"fed","problem"?}`; `problem` is an open set: `attendee_unavailable`, `attendee_not_allowed`, `live_full`. Errors in order: `503` as above, `413 too_large` (body over 1 MiB), `410 recording_deleted`, `404 recording_not_found` (upload first; a 404 without that code means the route is missing), `403 kb_read_only`, `400` (bad `from`, over 200 segments, a non-numeric time), `409 not_attending`, `409 live_gap` (`{"error","code","next"}`: send from `next`), `413 live_full` (20000 positions or 4 MB). Only sentences said while attending enter the live log. Live sentences feed the attending session in batches (message source `meeting`); they are not the transcript, which the upload still owns.
- `GET /api/v1/recordings/{id}/live` → the same object plus `asks` (oldest first), also on a read-only knowledge base; with `attendance` `off`: `{"attendance":"off","next","fed","asks"}`. `410 recording_deleted`, `404 recording_not_found`. A hub that lists `meeting_conversation` adds `revs` and takes `parts`, one that lists `meeting_live_view` adds `topics` and, with `?from=n`, `lines`, and one that lists `meeting_highlights` adds `highlights` ("Meeting conversation (#3862)" below).
- `POST /api/v1/recordings/{id}/ask` `{"id": "<UUID>", "question"?, "at"?, "live_next"?}`: without `question` (`at` then required) the question is what was said in the 45 s before `at`, every live sentence overlapping them (with `live_next`, once the hub holds that many live positions, waiting at most 15 s). Held at most 20 s: `200 {"ask"}` answered, else `202 {"ask"}` pending (send the same request again; clients wait at least 30 s). `Ask` is `{id, question, question_source: typed|heard, at?, state: pending|answered|failed, answer, lang, speak, sources: [{kind, id, name, when?}], error?, asked_at, answered_at?}`: `answer` is plain text of at most 400 characters (`""` unless answered), `speak` is true for a participant, fixed when asked; `error` is an open set (`model_unavailable`, `model_error`, `model_timeout`, `interrupted`, `nothing_heard`). The same `id` (case-insensitive, returned lowercase) never makes a second answer and is answered from the stored ask before any limit is checked; a `failed` one is tried again; with another `question` or `at` it is `409 op_id_reused`. Errors in order: `503`, `413 too_large` (64 KiB), `410 recording_deleted`, `404 recording_not_found`, `400`, a stored `id`, `403 kb_read_only`, `409 not_attending`, `409 asks_full` (100), `429 ask_busy` (two being answered; no `Retry-After`).
- The answer is one model call (purpose `meeting.answer`) with no tools, whose input until the private-meeting mark exists (#3862 phase 1) contains only this meeting: its title, calendar hint, live lines and earlier asks. Earlier meetings, their projects and their action-item to-do states are disabled together; earlier-meeting material returns with the mark. See meeting-minutes.md "What the hub gives the answering model"; nothing else reaches it.
- `…/live`, `…/ask` and changes to `meeting_attendance_default` take full credentials only (`403 forbidden` otherwise); they are not in `extwire.RouteScopes`.

#### Meeting conversation (#3862)

The normative text, with every rule, limit and error, is [meeting-minutes.md](../assistant/meeting-minutes.md) "Meeting conversation (#3862)"; this is the summary. It ships in phases, each behind a flag the hub lists, like `meeting_attendance`, only while the default manager names that capability in its `manager.hello`: `meeting_conversation` (phase 1), `meeting_live_view` (2), `meeting_highlights` (2b, only beside `meeting_live_view`), `meeting_photos` (3) and `meeting_transcription` (5); phase 4 is `meeting` in the built-in voice extension's `features`, and phase 6 needs no flag. A recording whose upload does not ask for a room keeps "Attending a meeting" above, so phones from before keep working. Every route below takes full credentials only and is not in `extwire.RouteScopes`.

- **Upload fields** (with `kind: meeting`): `room: {"attendance": "off"|"listener"|"participant"}` (the meeting's own room conversation attends in that role; sent on every upload of a meeting, whatever the role, instead of the top-level `attendance` and `attending_session`, which are ignored beside it; once a room meeting, always one), `private` (the meeting's private mark, taken only while the recording has none), `transcription` (`device` by default, or `hub`; the mode of the first upload that names one, kept for the recording; another value names none, and on a `day` or `note` it is ignored), and in hub mode `timeline` (`{roles: [{at, attendance}], speaking: [{start, end, text}]}`, the role changes and Persona's speaking spans so far, each with the answer said in it as in `spoken`, sent whole every time; `speaking` holds only spans that have ended, unlike `spoken`, which may include the one being said; a malformed one, or one over 100 role changes or 1000 spans, is ignored whole). The `200` of a room meeting carries the top-level `attendance` and `room` (the state object below, at least `{"state": "none"}`); a `200` without `room` is an older manager, which never reads the role inside `room` and so feeds nothing. From a manager with `meeting_transcription` the `200` of every meeting upload carries `transcription` (the mode in effect) and, when it is not the mode asked for, `transcription_problem` (`unavailable`, `not_meeting`); a `200` without it is an older manager, and the phone keeps that meeting in `device` mode with no audio socket. The manager keeps the room's role, state and ids, the mark, the follow-up, the mode and the timeline in `recordings/<id>/meeting.json`, never in `meta.json`, which an older manager rewrites and reads on restart to resume feeding. The room and the follow-up are each made once, also across a restart: a pending creation in `meeting.json` with a session id derived from the recording.
- **Shared by `GET …/live` and `detail.meta`**: `private` (absent until chosen), `room` (`{state, machine_id?, session_id?, problem?}`; `state` an open set read as `starting` when unknown: `none`, `starting`, `ready`, `unavailable`, `ended`, `deleted`; `problem` an open set: `runtime_unsupported`, `node_too_old`, `machine_offline`, `start_failed`), `followup` (`{machine_id, session_id}`), and from phase 5 `transcription` (`{mode: "device"}`, or `{mode: "hub", state: live|finishing|final|failed, gaps, problem?, fallback?}` with `gaps` always present; it moves in `revs` when any of those change). A room is `ended` (or stays `none`) at most 6 minutes after the first upload with `ended_at` (12 hours and 3 minutes after the last upload when none carries it), whatever its role or computer did. `GET …/live` also returns `revs` (each part's revision) and takes `?parts=` to read only some parts.
- **Only on `GET …/live`**: from phase 2 (`meeting_live_view`) `lines` (`?from=n`, a whole number of 0 or more, else `400`: the live log's positions from `n`, `[{n, start, end, text, source?}]` (`source` from phase 5, in hub mode: `hub`, or `device` for the fallback), at most 500, `more: true` when there are more; none without `from`), `topics` (always, `[]` before the first: `[{title, state: done|current|open, at?, note?}]`, at most one `current`, at most 20, `title` at most 80 characters, `note` at most 200, `at` seconds from the start; kept in `live.json`, so they go with the transcript) and `topics_at` (RFC 3339, the last change; absent before the first); `?parts=lines` gives the lines only with `from`, `?parts=topics` the topics and `topics_at`, each with its revision; from phase 2b (`meeting_highlights`) `highlights` (always, `[]` before the first: `[{text, at, end}]`, at most 4, the earliest `at` first, `text` at most 80 characters, `at` and `end` in seconds the start of the first and the end of the last of the live log's lines in the minute the point was made in; kept in `live.json`) and `highlights_at`, with `?parts=highlights`; from phase 5 `interim` (`{start, text}`: the latest caption while the meeting records, the role is not `off` and the caption is at most 10 seconds old; `?parts=interim`). The room sets the topics with its meeting tool `meeting_topics_set {topics}` (the whole list; a list over a limit is refused, saying which) and the highlights with `meeting_highlights_set {highlights}` (the whole list of `{text, said_at}`, `said_at` the `H:MM` or `HH:MM` of a batch line, which the hub turns into that minute's `at` and `end`; from phase 2b `meeting_lines` writes `[m:ss · HH:MM]`), and each batch shows it the topics and highlights so far. `detail.meta`, which extension tokens with `kb.read` can read, never carries live lines, topics, highlights or captions. Photos are listed by `GET …/photos`.
- **`…/ask` in a room meeting** is answered by the room conversation: an ask waits for a `starting` room (at most 2 minutes, then the room is `unavailable`), and only a room that is `unavailable` falls back to `meeting.answer`. An ask's `via` is fixed when its first attempt goes out; asking a failed `room` ask again while the room is `unavailable` fails with `room_unavailable`. The request may add `spoken: true` (a question transcribed from a Talk span); `Ask` adds `via` (`room`, `material`), `heard` (`[{start, end, text}]`), `question_source` `spoken` and `error` `no_answer` and `room_unavailable`; `409 meeting_ended` after `409 not_attending` once the room has ended. Each attempt's message to the room is `ask-<id>-<k>`, so asking a failed ask again reaches the room again. In hub mode `POST …/live` is `409 hub_transcribes`, and `…/ask` ignores `live_next` (the hub finishes its sentences up to `at`, waiting at most 15 seconds); while the hub has no sentences (the audio socket down for 30 seconds, one never opened included, or a problem other than `no_interim` for 30 seconds), the manager fills the live log from the upload's segments (`source: device`).

| Method | Path | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PUT | `/api/v1/recordings/{id}/private` | `{"private": bool}` → `{"private"}`: the private mark, which decides only whether this meeting is material for later meetings (only meetings marked `false` are); `409 not_meeting` when the recording is neither `kind: meeting` nor `minutes_asked` |
| POST | `/api/v1/recordings/{id}/just-me` | `{"id", "text"?, "images"?}` → `{"conversation", "client_msg_id"}`: the owner's private question to the main chat, with the meeting as context; a `client_ops` receipt keeps the main chat it went to; its turn pushes nothing with content and is never stored with the recording |
| POST | `/api/v1/recordings/{id}/followup` | `{"id", "text"?, "images"?}` (text or images required) → `{"followup", "created", "client_msg_id"}`: the owner's message to the meeting's follow-up conversation, made with the first one, which carries the meeting as a context block; for any recording with text or minutes (phase 6: a note, or a meeting that never had a room, too); a `client_ops` receipt from the body's `id`, as Just me; `409 meeting_running` while the recording has no `ended_at` (counted as ended 12 hours after its last upload) or its room has not settled |
| POST / GET | `/api/v1/recordings/{id}/photos` | Phase 3 (`meeting_photos`): add a photo `{"id", "at", "mime", "data", "text"?, "caption"?}` (a JPEG or PNG of at most 1 MiB and 4096 pixels on its long side, a body of at most 2 MiB) → `{"photo"}` (`{n, id, at, mime, width, height, text?, caption?, note?, cited, forwarded, added_at}`); the same `id` returns the stored photo, another body under it is `409 op_id_reused`, the `id` of a photo the owner deleted `410 photo_deleted`; then `403 kb_read_only`, `409 not_meeting`, `409 transcript_expired`, `413 photos_full` (50). A photo added while the room attends goes into it (`photo-<id>`, source `meeting`). List them → `{"photos"}`, oldest first, also on a read-only knowledge base |
| GET / DELETE | `/api/v1/recordings/{id}/photos/{n}` | Phase 3: the image, with its `Content-Type`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and `Cache-Control: private, no-store`; remove it → `{"deleted": true}`, `{"deleted": false}` for one the owner deleted before (a photo that went into the room is withdrawn there, `photo-withdrawn-<id>`); `404 photo_not_found`, then for `DELETE` `403 kb_read_only` |
| GET (WebSocket) | `/api/v1/recordings/{id}/audio` | Phase 5: the meeting's audio from the phone in hub mode (PCM16 little-endian, mono, 16 kHz, whole samples, at most 64 KiB a frame, none before `ready`), relayed to the default manager; `Authorization: Bearer` (or `?token=`). Refused before the upgrade only with `403 forbidden` and `503`; the recording's own refusals are the first frame, a fatal `error` (`recording_deleted`, `recording_not_found`, `kb_read_only`, `not_hub`, `transcript_expired`, `transcription_final`). The phone sends `start` (within 10 seconds: `at` the oldest second it holds, the whole `timeline`, whose `speaking` has only spans that have ended; a text frame is at most 8.5 MiB), `seek`, `role`, `speaking` (`on`, `at`, and on `on` the answer's `text`: sent as Persona starts and stops, so the hub holds back sentences that may be its echo until the span closes, then marks Persona's echo by the same rule as `spoken`), `end`; the hub answers `ready` (`from`, `gaps`, `next`: the live log's length), `ack` (stored, not transcribed), `interim`, `line` (the hub's own sentences, never sent again: missed ones through `GET …/live?from=`), `problem` (`upstream_unavailable`, `upstream_failed`, `no_interim`; `code: null` once transcription is back), `error` (an open set, fatal: `bad_frame`, `replaced`, `audio_full` and the refusals). One socket per recording: a new one replaces the one before (`replaced`) |
| PUT | `/api/v1/recordings/{id}/audio?at=` | Phase 5: audio for a gap (`application/octet-stream`, PCM16 16 kHz mono, `at` in seconds), at most 10 MiB → `{"gaps"}`; after the common errors and `403 kb_read_only`: `409 not_hub`, `409 transcript_expired`, `409 transcription_final` (the final pass has started, at the latest 30 minutes after the `complete: true` upload), `413 audio_full` (12 hours of audio) |

- **Conversations**: the room is a guest conversation of kind `meeting` (Claude Code only, no runtime tools, meeting tools only, none of the owner's Claude Code instructions, settings or hooks), with `origin: "meeting"`; the follow-up is a normal Persona conversation with `origin: "meeting_followup"`; both have `origin_ref` the recording id. Message source `meeting` marks the room's header, batches, heard questions and forwarded photos. A message sent into an ended room is `409 meeting_ended`.
- **Event**: `meeting_live` `{recording_id, changed, revs}`, content-free (`revs` are numbers: each changed part's revision, for `lines` the live log's length), at most one a second per recording; clients read only the newer parts (`GET …/live?parts=…`, lines `?from=` their next position, `GET …/photos` for `photos`, which has a revision on `GET …/live` but no field there: `?parts=photos` returns only `{"revs": {"photos": n}}`). Phase 5 adds `transcription` and `interim` (`revs.interim` moves with each caption).
- **Settings** in `GET` / `PUT /api/v1/assistant` (phase 5): `meeting_transcription_default` (`device` until changed, or `hub`; else `400 bad_transcription_mode`), `meeting_glossary` (a list of strings, `[]` by default; trimmed, repeats dropped; more than 200 terms or one over 40 characters is `400 bad_glossary`), `meeting_transcription_extension` (`""` for the built-in voice extension's contribution, or `<extension id>/<contribution id>` naming an installed `transcription` contribution, else `400 bad_transcription_extension`), and the read-only `meeting_transcription_ready` (ignored on `PUT`). Changing them takes full credentials (`403 forbidden`); `persona_settings` changes only the default, after a confirmation card.
- **Minutes** items may cite a photo (`photo`, phase 3); in hub mode `detail.segments` items carry `source` (`hub`, `device`; a `source` the phone uploads is ignored); a phone segment fills in where the hub's sentences, taken together, cover no more than half of it, and every check of whether a recording has text counts that transcript, without Persona's echo. Hub-mode minutes wait for the final pass (the stored audio at 4×; at most 45 minutes after `complete`), and the hub deletes the meeting's audio once the minutes from the final transcript are written.
- **Voice** (phase 4, `meeting` in the built-in voice extension's `features`): protocol 2 `start` with `mode: "meeting"`, `recording_id` and the room as `target`, checked by the extension with `GET …/live` (the hub's token): a room that is not that recording's or not `ready` is the fatal `not_meeting_room`; and `talk` frames (`{"type": "talk", "on": bool}`); audio only between them, in either transcription mode (the extension feeds the upstream silence outside them and drops the app's audio there). Any other call bound to a room is the fatal `meeting_room`. The user-speech gate always holds for a meeting call: its `speech_gate` neither turns it off nor brings Send Anyway. Details in [voice.md](../assistant/voice.md) "Meeting calls".
- **Talk about this meeting** (phase 6, no flag): **Talk about this meeting** on any recording's detail writes into the follow-up through `…/followup`, by text or by a protocol 2 call bound to it; `kind` on `GET /api/v1/kb-search` and on the voice `search_knowledge` tool (`recordings` for meetings); the minutes push carries `recording_id` ("Recording sync" above).
- **Extension point** (phase 5): `transcription` (version 1, `runtime.http`), with `GET /transcription/{cid}/info` and a `GET /transcription/{cid}/ws` job socket on the extension's own socket, dialed only by the manager; the built-in voice extension contributes `gpt-live` (for a GPT-Live `live`-dialect upstream; with none its `setup` is `live_upstream`), and hub mode uses another only when `meeting_transcription_extension` names it. The job's `start.language` is a hint, never a lock: every word is written in the language it was said in, mixed sentences mixed, never translated. Besides `ready`, `interim`, `sentence`, `ack`, `warning`, `error` and `done`, the extension sends `flushed` (after a `flush`), `window` (replay) and `usage` (billed seconds, diagnostics): frames of the job, not of the phone's socket.

#### All-day recordings (#4741)

The normative text, with every rule and error, is [day-recap.md](../assistant/day-recap.md); this is the summary. Only on a hub that lists the `recording_day` feature, which it does only while the default manager names that capability in its `manager.hello`.

- **The recording**: one per local day (stopping and starting again the same day continue it), `kind: "day"` with `day` (`YYYY-MM-DD`, required), `tz` (the day's IANA zone; the owner's when absent), `part` (1–99, default 1) and `coverage` (`{"to", "gaps": [{"from", "to", "reason"}]}`: seconds since `started_at` transcribed and appended so far, and the time with no text and why: `paused`, `interrupted`, `stopped`, `pending`, `lost`, `erased`; the hub mends it and never refuses it for order or overlap). Its `segments[].start` / `end` and `bookmarks[].at` are wall-clock seconds since `started_at`, pauses included. `calendar` and the attending and room fields are ignored on it; `kind` never changes to or from `day` (`409 kind_changed`). It is never a meeting: no calendar match, no minutes, no attending, no short summary.
- **Created and repaired by `PUT`**, which keeps its full-replacement meaning and sets the recording's base (its revision) and the hub's count `next` (the segments it carried, empty ones included). Its `200` adds `base` and `next`, its `revision` is the stored one, and `stale` is not success for a day recording (send again above it). Over the limits it is `413 day_full`.
- **Grown by `POST /api/v1/recordings/{id}/segments`** `{"base", "revision", "from", "segments" (at most 500), "duration"?, "ended_at"?, "title"?, "bookmarks"?, "coverage"?, "complete"?}`: appends by position like `…/live` (positions below `next` are skipped, so retries store nothing twice); the other fields apply only when present and only from a request whose `revision` is at least the stored one. `200 {"id", "revision", "next", "status"}` (`stored`, `expired`). Errors in order: `503`, `413 too_large` (body over 1 MiB), `410 recording_deleted`, `404 recording_not_found`, `403 kb_read_only`, `400`, then `expired`, `409 not_day`, `409 base_changed` (`{"error", "code", "base", "next"}`), `409 segments_gap` (`{"error", "code", "next"}`), `413 day_full` (`{"error", "code", "next"}`: past 20000 positions or 4 MiB of text, nothing stored: the phone continues in the next `part`, a storage partition with the same `day`, `tz` and `started_at`). Full credentials only.
- **Reconciliation** lists a day recording with `kind`, `day`, `part`, `next` and `base` (always present, `0` when lost: send a `PUT`), `recap_state`, `recap_final` and `recap_final_at`.
