- **Reading**: `detail.meta` adds `kind`, `day`, `tz`, `part`, `coverage`, `next`, `base`, `recap_state` (absent until a recap is due, then `pending`, `ready`, `failed`), `recap_final` and `recap_final_at`; `detail.recap` is `{version, revision, generated_at, day, covers: {from, to}, final, final_reason?: complete|cutoff, summary, timeline: [{from, to, kind: meeting|outside, title, meeting?: {kind, id, name}, points: [{text, at, who?}]}], actions: [{id, who?, what, by?, due_date?, at, todo_id?}], gaps?, partial?, language?, markdown}`, times in seconds since `started_at`; `language` as for minutes (the recap's text and its Markdown's headings); `detail.summary` is the recap's `summary`. `POST …/minutes` (re)writes the recap and `POST …/minutes/todos` confirms its actions (`200 {"todos", "recap"}`); neither makes it a meeting.
- **When**: the hub notes each finished hour of text once as it arrives (notes in `recap_notes.json`, kept per chunk while its lines are unchanged) and merges them into a recap that is due once a day at the recap time (30 minutes before the evening routine's time, 21:00 by default, in the owner's time zone) for each day recording overlapping the owner's today with text the newest recap did not read, when the recording becomes `complete`, 6 hours after a day that never completed (and 30 minutes after its last upload), on `POST …/minutes`, and at once after a `PUT` that set a new base while a recap exists or is due (until it is rewritten, entries overlapping `erased` gaps, items whose line is gone, and the summary are withdrawn). Due recaps are persisted and retried, never re-armed by new text. One push a day, at the recap time (or with the first recap after it); the evening routine's facts carry today's recaps to the model only.
- **Retention**: the transcript and `recap_notes.json` follow `recording_days`; `recap.json` and `recap.md` survive trimming like minutes and follow `minutes_days`.
- **Watch ↔ phone** (no hub involvement; normative in day-recap.md "Watch to phone"): audio in chunks of about 10 s with a per-recording `seq` (a 4-byte header length, the JSON header, the audio) by `sendMessageData` while reachable, else queued at once by `transferFile` (oversized chunks stay with it), never more than 5 minutes behind for audio recorded while reachable (a backlog drains as the system delivers files); pauses, interruptions, losses, erases and the day's close as numbered control events; each kept on the watch until the phone acknowledges it (`{"recording", "acks", "events"}`); erase and delete as durable wall-clock tombstones applied before deduplication; phone audio gone at the earliest of 3 days after the first final recap, 7 days after the day and `recording_days`, unacknowledged watch audio after `recordingDayKeepDays`. The phone's application context says what it can take: `recordingDay` (`1`, the contract's version, once the user agreed; `0` before; absent on an older phone), `recordingDayHub` (whether its hub lists `recording_day`) and `recordingDayKeepDays` (`min(7, recording_days)`).

## Messaging source API (`/api/v1/messaging`)

Sources from the `messaging` extension point (the first is Lark): `GET /api/v1/messaging` lists sources; `/api/v1/messaging/{source}/…` handles chats, messages, sending and so on. After authentication, the hub forwards to the extension and validates responses against the schema. Specification in [extension-messaging.md](../extensions/extension-messaging.md); `/api/v1/lark` below is the legacy API from before migration, kept until Mac, Android and web finish migrating (#2138).

## Lark API (Lark gateway)

These routes aren't the hub's own code: #1571 (3c) removed the hub's direct connection to the Lark gateway, and `server/internal/lark` now contains only the `lark` config (the manager's manager.json). `/api/v1/lark/…` is provided by the Lark plugin's `api` contribution; `lark` is a prefix being migrated out of the hub (`migratablePrefixes`, `server/internal/extmgr/extension_api.go`), and the plugin's contribution takes precedence. The hub authenticates first, removes `Authorization` and `token`, adds `X-Persona-Device` / `X-Persona-Role`, then forwards as is to the plugin, which asks the Lark gateway ([extensions.md](../extensions/extensions.md) ("App endpoints")). Without a plugin providing them, these routes return 404. Below is the endpoint contract plugins must follow; "hub" mostly means the plugin the hub forwards to. The hub wraps plugin-declared `receipts` with send receipts.

All routes below accept the query parameter `ol_account=<Lark gateway account number>`: which Lark account this request uses (invalid returns 400). Without it, the plugin's default account is used, decided by the plugin's own Lark gateway config: the hub doesn't hand manager.json's `lark.account` to the plugin; it is only used for the assistant's Inbox (`server/internal/lark/config.go`, `docs/extensions/feishu.md` ("Multiple accounts")). Media URLs for other accounts already carry it.

On a Lark gateway error, the plugin returns 502 `{"error"}`; when the gateway itself lost its Lark sign-in (`AUTH_*`), it returns `{"error","code":"lark_not_logged_in"}`, which the App uses to prompt the user to sign in to Lark again in the gateway. `/raw/…` is an exception: it forwards the gateway's own response as is.

| Method | Path | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/api/v1/lark/accounts` | `{"accounts":[{"id","name"?,"avatar"?,"tenant"?,"user_id"?,"signed_in","primary"?,"unread","quarantined"?}],"default"}`: Lark accounts signed in on the gateway (in gateway order; `signed_in` is false for quarantined accounts) and the default account number. Old gateways without an account list return only the default account; old hubs lack this route (404), so the App shows no account switching |
| GET | `/api/v1/lark/status` | `{"configured","connected","name","error","last_event_at"}`: Settings › Connectors › Lark. configured comes from the plugin's own Lark gateway config (before 3c it meant "hub.json has lark"); connected asks the gateway's `/accounts` on every request; last_event_at is the latest live event (Unix seconds) |
| GET | `/api/v1/lark/message-display` | `{"account_id","anti_recall","show_edit_history"}`: display settings of the selected Lark account; returns only these two switches and the actual user ID, no script / auto-send config |
| POST | `/api/v1/lark/message-display` | `{"account_id","key","value","expected"}`: key is `anti_recall` or `show_edit_history`, value/expected are booleans; full device permissions, body ≤1 KiB, unknown fields rejected; a restricted PATCH through the gateway preserves other fields. Account / old-value conflicts 409, unauthorized 403, old service without endpoint 404; expired sign-in 502 + `lark_not_logged_in`. Success returns the same structure as GET and pushes a `lark` event with `settings_changed=true`; unknown results aren't retried automatically |
| GET | `/api/v1/lark/encryption` | native encryption status `{accountId,configured,locked,unifiedPassword}`. Requires separate native encryption authorization; no keys or credentials returned, `Cache-Control: no-store`. The plugin declares `lark_native_encryption` in its `api` `features`, and the hub merges it into its features; upstream without the native endpoint returns 426 + `lark_gateway_upgrade_required`, missing separate authorization returns 403 + `VAULT_NATIVE_NOT_AUTHORIZED` |
| POST | `/api/v1/lark/encryption/unlock` | `{account_id,password}` → same as above. Full write permission only; validates against the actual Lark account, sharing the web's password-attempt limit; the password isn't stored |
| POST | `/api/v1/lark/conversations/{id}/encryption/covers` | `{account_id}` → `{lines:[string]}`; candidate historical cover text uses the same rules as the gateway web UI |
| POST | `/api/v1/lark/conversations/{id}/encryption/prepare` | `{account_id,text,cover}` → `{accountId,feedId,messages:[{text}]}`. Only generates ciphertext with cover text, without sending; rejects identity mismatch, unauthorized, locked, or missing recipient public keys |
| POST | `/api/v1/lark/conversations/{id}/encrypted-messages` | `{account_id,ciphertext,client_id,reply_id?}` → `{ok,message_id?}`. Requires a stable UUID, accepts only the OLK2/OLK3 wire shape, and revalidates native authorization and the actual account; upstream writes carry `expectedSenderId`. Segments are sent in order, and only the last can quote a message; each segment gets a separate dedup receipt. All native-encryption responses are `no-store`; failures never fall back to the plain-text endpoint; protocol and limits in [Encrypted messages](../extensions/lark-encryption.md) |
| GET | `/api/v1/lark/conversations?scope=&cursor=&limit=` | `{"conversations":[LarkConversation],"next_cursor"}`; scope: `chats` (default, Lark "Messages": excludes completed / folded chats and filters by label display rules), `unread`, `done` (completed), `label:<id>`, `inbox`, `mentions`, `muted`, `p2p`, `group`, `thread`, `later` |
| GET | `/api/v1/lark/pinned` | all pinned chats (keeps reading the pinned head of inbox + done, merges and dedups, then sorts by pin time); pagination anomalies return an error rather than treating a truncated set as success |
| GET | `/conversations`, `/pinned` above with `account_bound=1` | additionally returns the actual selected `account_id`; an empty collection is `[]`; intermediary caching prohibited. May carry expected `account_id`; identity changes before / after the request or an expected-account mismatch return 409 `lark_account_changed` with no chat data. Not signed in still uses `lark_not_logged_in`; old calls omit the parameter and keep the original contract |
| GET | `/api/v1/lark/conversations/{id}/pins?account_id=&cursor=&limit=` | in-chat Pin list: `{account_id,items:[{id,message_id,message?:LarkMessage,operator_name?,created_at}],next_cursor,total}`. limit defaults to 50, max 100. Preserves upstream pagination fully; repeated / missing cursors return errors. This read clears the gateway's unread Pin marker, so home-page prefetching is prohibited |
| GET | `/api/v1/lark/conversations/{id}/pin-messages/{message}?account_id=&topic=` | locate a Pin: `{account_id,target:{message,root?,page}}`, with page in the same shape as chat / topic pagination. A regular message returns an around window; a reply returns the topic root and a reply window containing the target (at most 20×100 entries). Target not found returns 409 `lark_pin_no_position`; the client keeps the current window |
| POST | `/api/v1/lark/conversations/{id}/pins` | `{account_id,message_id,pin_id?,remove}` → `{account_id,pinned}`. remove=true requires the corresponding pin_id; before writing, verifies message feed, capabilities, Pin ownership and actual account. An unknown result returns `lark_pin_result_unknown`, requiring a reread to confirm, not an automatic retry. All three Pin APIs are `no-store`; account switch returns 409 `lark_account_changed` without data; old gateway routes return 426 `lark_gateway_upgrade_required`, missing original messages `lark_pin_not_found` |
| GET | `/api/v1/lark/labels` | `{"labels":[{"id","name","count"}]}` |
| GET | `/api/v1/lark/unread-count` | `{"count"}`: "Unread N" (excludes muted chats) |
| GET | `/api/v1/lark/flags` | flags: `{"conversations":[LarkConversation],"messages":[{"feed_id","chat_name","chat_avatar","flagged_at","message":LarkMessage}]}` |
| GET | `/api/v1/lark/conversations/{id}/labels` | `{"label_ids":[…],"labels":[{"id","name"}]}` (labels this chat belongs to / available labels) |
| POST | `/api/v1/lark/conversations/{id}/settings` | `{"done"?,"pinned"?,"flagged"?,"muted"?,"label_ids"?}` → gateway `PATCH settings` (isArchived / isShortcut / isFlagged / isMuted / labelIds; labelIds is the full set) |
| POST | `/api/v1/lark/conversations/{id}/unread` | `{"unread":true}` marks unread / `false` clears unread |
| GET | `/api/v1/lark/conversations/{id}/messages?before=&after=&around=&limit=&topic=` | `{"messages":[LarkMessage],"has_older","has_newer","older_cursor","newer_cursor"}`, oldest→newest; no cursor = latest page; `around=<read position+1>` opens from the first unread message; `topic=1` fetches a topic group's topic list (backward paging only) |
| GET | `/api/v1/lark/messages/{id}/thread?before=&limit=` | messages in a topic / reply thread, same format as above; supports only backward paging with `before`, reading the latest page without a cursor; no `after`, since upstream provides no forward pagination or cursor; see [Topic pagination limits](../extensions/feishu.md#话题分页限制h06) |
| POST | `/api/v1/lark/conversations/{id}/messages` | `{"text","client_id"?,"mentions"?}` sends as the user, returning `{"ok":true,"message_id"?}`. `client_id` is an App-generated UUID passed as is to the gateway's `clientId` and stored with a receipt on the hub: resending the same message with the same id sends only one; missing or non-UUID values are generated by the hub. `mentions` is `[{"user_id","name"}]` (at most 100; exceeding the limit or missing `user_id` / `name` returns 400); `text` must contain literal `@name`; the hub doesn't rewrite text and passes it as is to the gateway's `mentions`; @everyone is `{"user_id":"all","name":"所有人"}` ("everyone") |
| POST | `/api/v1/lark/messages/{id}/replies` | `{"text","thread"?,"client_id"?,"mentions"?}` replies to this message as the user, returning `{"ok":true,"message_id"?}`. `thread=false` (default) quotes it in the original chat; `thread=true` sends into its topic (a top-level message in a regular group becomes the root of a new topic; in a topic group it goes into its topic). Proxies gateway `POST /messages/{id}/replies`, passing `client_id` as is as `clientId` and saving a receipt; `mentions` as in the previous row. The target may be a root message or a reply in a topic; upstream resolves topic ownership. Empty `text` returns 400 |
| GET | `/api/v1/lark/conversations/{id}/members?q=&limit=` | members for @mentions: `{"members":[{"user_id","name","avatar"?}]}`. Empty `q` lists members; non-empty searches names / group nicknames / pinyin; `limit` defaults to 50, at most 200; `name` prefers the group nickname, falling back to display name |
| POST | `/api/v1/lark/conversations/{id}/images` | `{"client_id","name","mime","data"}`; data is base64, decoded size at most 7.5 MiB; image format validated; returns `{"message_id"}` |
| POST | `/api/v1/lark/conversations/{id}/files?client_id=&name=&mime=` | raw `application/octet-stream` bytes, Content-Length required, 1 byte to 100 MiB; returns `{"message_id"}`; streamed through the hub |
| POST | `/api/v1/lark/conversations/{id}/read` | `{"position","badge_count"?,"message_ids"?}`: report viewed messages (highest position, that message's badge_count, and unread message ids sent by others in between); only sent after messages actually appear on screen |
| POST | `/api/v1/lark/conversations/{id}/read-states` | `{"message_ids":[…]}` (at most 100; more returns 400): read receipts for these messages, returning `{"states":[{"message_id","read_count","unread_count"}]}`. Messages the gateway provided no receipt for (still sending, unknown) don't appear in `states`; when old hubs lack this route, the App shows no receipts |
| GET | `/api/v1/lark/media/{key}?size=` | images / stickers / avatars / videos / files forwarded as is (`size` returns a thumbnail when a multiple of 24 and ≤624) |
| GET | `/api/v1/lark/messages/{id}/media/{key}` | message-scoped media (as above) |
| GET | `/api/v1/lark/emojis` | `{"emojis":{"<lowercase key>":{"label","url"}}}`, including skin-tone variant keys; cached by the hub for a day |
| POST | `/api/v1/lark/messages/{id}/card-actions/{actionId}` | press a card callback button as the user (body passed as is to the gateway) |
| GET / POST | `/api/v1/lark/raw/{path...}` | read-only proxy for gateway `/agent/v1/<path>`, forwarding queries and allowed read-only POSTs; not a general write endpoint |
| GET | `/api/v1/lark/reactions/quick` | `{keys}`: quick reactions |
| POST | `/api/v1/lark/messages/{id}/reactions` | `{key,remove?}`: add or remove a reaction, returning `{ok:true}` |
| GET | `/api/v1/lark/users/{id}?feed_id=` | user profile, upstream JSON forwarded as is |
| POST | `/api/v1/lark/users/{id}/chat` | open a DM, returning `{feed_id}` |
| GET | `/api/v1/lark/messages/{id}/url-preview?url=` | link preview within a message, upstream JSON forwarded as is |
| POST | `/api/v1/lark/documents/comments` | `{url, content, mentions?:[{user_id,name}], quote?, block_id?, client_id}`: post a new document comment as the user (#1290). Without `quote`, a whole-document comment; with `quote` (and its containing block `block_id`), a comment on that body passage. Each @mentioned person in `content` is written as `@name`, as in messages. Returns `{ok, threads, anchored?}`: `threads` is all threads read back after writing (same shape as `documents/comments`; null if unreadable, but the comment was sent); a comment on a passage also carries `anchored` (`false`: the containing block couldn't be found, so the passage is quoted in a whole-document comment instead). Body anchors use the gateway's inline comments; the plugin finds the block by `quote` in the document JSON (if the App knows `block_id`, it sends it directly). These routes exist only when the plugin declares `lark_doc_comments`; writes from the user's own device bypass the AI gate; recorded in receipts (receipt id derived from `client_id`, so retries with the same id don't send twice) |
| POST | `/api/v1/lark/documents/comments/{thread}/replies` | `{url, content, mentions?, client_id}`: reply to this comment thread, returning `{ok, threads}` |
| POST | `/api/v1/lark/documents/comments/{thread}/resolve` | `{url, resolved}`: mark resolved (`true`) or reopen (`false`), returning `{ok, threads}`; invalid content 400 `comment_invalid`, this document doesn't support such comments 400 `comment_unsupported` |
| GET | `/api/v1/lark/documents/people?url=&q=` | `{members:[{user_id,name,avatar?}]}`: candidates for @mentions in comments, searched by name (same shape as group `members`) |
| GET | `/api/v1/lark/moments/posts/{id}` | single-post content, upstream JSON forwarded as is |
| GET | `/api/v1/lark/moments/posts/{id}/comments` | single-post comments, upstream JSON forwarded as is |

The optional `client_id` for Lark sends, threaded replies and Inbox replies can be used directly for retries, with no extra request header required. The hub derives an internal receipt UUID from the operation kind and original ID, reusing Postgres `client_ops`; the same ID with the same target and params returns the original HTTP status and response body without sending again, even if the Inbox entry changed or the hub restarted. Reusing an ID with different params, target or authenticated device returns `409 {"code":"op_id_reused"}`. Recorded upstream errors are also returned as is, to avoid duplicate sends when the result is uncertain; execution not yet finished returns `202 {"state":"pending"}`, and execution left over after a restart without a result returns `202 {"state":"unknown"}`, which clients must verify. Receipts use the `client_ops` retention policy. When a request carries both `client_id` and `X-Persona-Op-Id`, the receipt derived from `client_id` wins.

Threaded replies use the separate operation kind `lark_thread_reply` with the same receipt rules. Before sending, Android persistently saves the topic draft and original request; on `202` or a lost receipt it stays pending confirmation, and submits the same target, text and `client_id` again to check the original result, never generating a new ID to resend. `ok:true` means upstream accepted it; the topic list is then reread.

Old clients without `client_id` keep the original behavior: the upstream client generates IDs for Lark chat sends, and the hub generates a stable ID per entry for Inbox Lark replies. HTTP response shapes are unchanged; no WebSocket events are added.

```jsonc
// LarkConversation
{"id":"<feedId>","name","avatar":"/api/v1/lark/media/…","is_group","is_topic","unread","marked_unread","at_me","at_all","muted",
 "pinned","flagged","done","tags":["外部"|"公开"|"会议"|"机器人"|"AI"…],"preview","preview_sender","is_mine","updated_at", // gateway tag values: External | Public | Meeting | Bot | AI
 "read_position","mention_position"}
// LarkMessage
{"id","position","sender_id","sender_name","sender_avatar","sender_type":"user|bot","is_mine",
 "type":"TEXT|POST|IMAGE|CARD|SYSTEM|FILE|MEDIA|STICKER|MERGE_FORWARD…","text":"plain-text preview","created_at",
 "recalled","retained"?,"edited","reply_count","thread_reply_count","badge_count","at_me","is_read",
 "parts":[MessagePart],                       // gateway content as is (see below); media URLs rewritten to /api/v1/lark/
 "olk"?:{…},                                 // encrypted projection: status, public cover text, authorized decrypted body, key distribution info
 "edit_history"?:[{"edited_at","text","parts"?,"olk"?}],
 "reply_to":{"id","sender_name","text","recalled","retained"?,"parts","olk"?},
 "reactions":[{"key":"THUMBSUP","count":2,"mine":true,"users":["Example member A","Example member B"]}]}
// MessagePart (the gateway's MessagePart; field names unchanged)
{"kind":"text|at|link|image|file|code|emotion|media|card|docs|interactive|table",
 "text","url","refId","metadata":{…}}   // the card's entire element tree is in metadata.body / header; rich-text block ancestors are in metadata.blocks
```

Sending attachments requires full device permissions (unavailable to answer-only devices) and uses the Lark gateway account bound to the plugin; callers can't override the account. The plugin declares `lark_attachments`, which the hub merges into hello/health features.
`client_id` must be a UUID and stay the same across retries of the same message; message reads also preserve optional `client_id`, `local_state`, used to remove late echoes after send timeouts. `local:` and pending/failed copies don't count as send confirmation.

Media rewrite rules: throughout parts JSON, `"/api/media/` → `"/api/v1/lark/media/`, `"/api/messages/` → `"/api/v1/lark/messages/`
(including messages nested inside merged-forward cards).

`retained=true` means the gateway retained the recalled original content, not that permissions are restored; display still keeps `recalled`, and this must not enable replies, reactions or card writes. Neither display switch deletes server-retained data or restricts existing message-read permissions; when settings are off / unknown, clients hide recalled originals and edit-history entry points. OLK projections in history, quotes and forwards use current authorization; when locked, only public content is shown and decrypted bodies are cleared from the phone cache.

## Personal Agent source status

The hub has no personal Agent sources of its own; all sources come from `agent_sources` of running extensions (`docs/extensions/extensions.md` ("Personal Agent sources")).
With no such extension running, `GET /api/v1/agents` returns `{"sources":[]}` and `GET /api/v1/agents/sessions` returns `{"sessions":[]}`, both HTTP 200.
With sources, `GET /api/v1/agents` has one entry per source: `{"sources":[{"source":"<contribution id>","enabled","error"?,"setup"?,"providers":[…],"accounts":[…]}]}`;
the Lark plugin picks its own source id; keeping the same id across upgrades keeps session ids unchanged.
`setup` explains why the source is reachable but has nothing to list yet; clients turn it into a notice when the session list is empty:
`missing` (the backend doesn't support personal Agents, such as a gateway without agent-bridge), `disabled` (supported but not enabled, such as agent-bridge being off on the gateway),
`no_accounts` (enabled but no accounts connected yet); these states mean the source has no sessions. Other failures (such as unreachable, or an extension still waiting for its own settings) go in `error`, from `agentsrc.status` or from the last failed `agentsrc.sessions`, and clients show them when the session list is empty. When other sources list sessions, the web and the Apple apps show the same lines as a notice above the list (#3098, #3216). Without `source`, listing, paging, counting and searching skip a failing source when other sources exist or when it has not listed since it was registered, and answer 200; a lone source that has listed before returns its error, so clients keep the rows they have. With `source`, the source's error is returned.

## Personal Agent list preferences

`GET /api/v1/agents/prefs` / `PUT /api/v1/agents/prefs` (replaces the whole set), stored in the hub's settings table (key `agents.prefs`), shared by web and iOS:

```json
{"pins":["<sessionId>"],
 "view":{"group":"date|provider|none","sort":"updated|unread|name","show":"all|unread|sendable","providers":["grok_bot"]},
 "sections":[{"id":"s1","name":"Work"}],
 "assign":{"<sessionId>":"s1"},
 "hidden":{"<sessionId>":1762500000000},
 "updatedAt":"…"}
```

- Omitted fields = defaults (group by date, sort by latest update, show all, all sources). `pins` is ordered and deduplicated; `assign` entries pointing to missing sections are dropped.
- `hidden` is what the user removed from the list (session id → when, ms). It changes only through `POST …/hide` / `…/unhide` below: a PUT keeps the stored set whatever it carries, so an app that does not know the field cannot bring removed conversations back by saving its pins.

### Removing a personal Agent from the list

The conversation belongs to its source (the Lark gateway through its extension), which can't delete or archive one, and the hub pulls the list from it again every minute. So removing is Persona's own: the extension manager (`server/internal/agents/hidden.go`) keeps the id in `hidden`, and leaves it out of `GET /api/v1/agents/sessions` (whole list, pages and counts, its unread included) until the source reports a message after the removal (`rankTimeMs` past the stored time). Then it is back by itself, like a deleted Agent session that is used again.

| Request | Response | Permission |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/v1/agents/sessions/{id}/hide` | `{"ok":true,"hidden":true}`; a conversation no source lists 404 | full |
| `POST /api/v1/agents/sessions/{id}/unhide` | `{"ok":true,"hidden":false}` | full |
| `GET /api/v1/agents/hidden` | `{"sessions":[Session]}`: the removed ones the sources still list and that got nothing new since | full |

Each write broadcasts `{"type":"agents"}` (the list) and `{"type":"agents.prefs"}`. Extension tokens can't use these routes. The web offers **Remove from list** in a personal Agent row's ⋯ and right-click menu (with Undo in the toast), and a folded **Removed (N)** section with **Restore** at the end of `/a`. iOS / Mac offer it in the row's long-press menu on the personal agents page (no swipe actions there), with the same Undo and a folded **Removed (N)** at the end of that page (#138); `hidden` in `GET /agents/prefs` is decoded but not used to filter, the list already comes filtered.

The web shows a prefs change at once and then PUTs it. When the PUT fails (other than a 404 / 405 from a hub without the route, where the change stays in localStorage only), it puts back the value from before unless a later change came, shows "Couldn't save the list settings: …", and reads `GET /agents/prefs` again once its PUTs are done, so a change the hub did not store never looks saved (#1880).
- Pinned sessions always appear in "Pinned" at the top, followed by custom sections, then groups from `view.group`.
- After a successful PUT, broadcasts `{"type":"agents.prefs"}`, and other clients GET again. When an old hub lacks this endpoint (404), clients store preferences only locally.

## Tags in messages (parsed by clients)

| Tag | Written by | Meaning / display |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<attached_images>` one path per line `</attached_images>` | node (images sent from the phone), Android composer (photos it uploaded) | images attached to the message; square thumbnails above the bubble. Only lines starting with `/` or `~` are photos. For Claude Code the node adds a `path:<path>` line after each path (Claude Code turns a line that is only an image path into `[Image #n]` and drops it, so its transcript keeps only the `path:` lines; nodes before #4361 wrote `path: <path>`, and readers take both); `path:` lines are for the agent and never shown |
| `<persona-context kind="context\|edit\|doc\|instructions" title="…" url="…">text</persona-context>` | phone (text selected in a link card), hub (Lark /agent instructions and context) | not written by the user: all blocks gather into one "Context · N items" row beside the bubble (with one block, "Context · title"), collapsed by default; expanding shows a title list, each opening the body and link. Attributes may be in any order or omitted (`url` is often absent); attributes a reader has no field for are kept and never drawn, so a block can carry ids for the model (the subscription pages' Set Up with the assistant, docs/extensions/subscriptions.md "Pages"); only text outside the tags is user-written |
| Rename (#3182): tags are moving from `<persona-context>` to `<persona-context>`, with attributes unchanged | | readers (hub, node, web, Android, Apple, DSH) accept both names, with mixed opening / closing tags allowed; closing tags of either name are stripped from block bodies. Attribute-free live snapshots and run instructions already write only `<persona-context>` (written and stripped by the same node, never seen by the App); blocks with attributes (hub templates, the three clients) still write `<persona-context>`, to switch once Apps that recognize the new name are widespread: old Apps only recognize `persona-context` and show an entire `<persona-context …>` block as body text |
| `<persona-context kind="workspace" title="…" url="" machine="<machine id>" cwd="<folder>" branch="…">` | web and the iPhone/iPad shell composer (a workspace picked in the assistant's @ menu, #5594 / #2599) | shown like the other blocks. Before the assistant gets it, the manager replaces the block (same tag, `branch` dropped) with where to dispatch by default, knowledge-base projects and recent Agents in that folder (docs/assistant/assistant.md "Workspace mentions"); a block naming an unknown computer is passed on as written |
| `<persona-context kind="skill" title="…" url="" ref="<opaque id>">source and description</persona-context>` | Web Assistant and Agents composer | an explicit selection, only recognized among leading context blocks; never inferred from `@name`, email, file paths or quoted/later prose. The current manager and node resolve `ref` against the target environment's catalog, never a client path or display name. Draft/queue/outbox/history keep this text. Old clients display it as an ordinary context; old messages need no new fields. Node-generated `kind="skill-instructions"` carries Claude's exact-file reading adapter and is hidden by Web transcript/queue readers, not restored as a user selection. |
| `<persona-context kind="forward" title="…" url="persona://session/…?at=…" msg="…" role="…" author="…" chat="…" project="…" machine="…" time="…">` | iOS (Forward on a message, #3807; several at once, #3838), web (#3899) | the user forwarded a message (or several, one block each) from another chat: a card at the top of the user's bubble that opens the original; see "Forwarded messages" below |
| `<cross-session-message from-name="…">…</cross-session-message>` | Claude Code (cross-session messages) | a left-side "From name" card, body rendered as Markdown |

### Quote and comment blocks at the start of messages (web and iOS, #2427, #2437, #151)

Web "Quote" and "Comment" use no tags or structured fields: on send they become `> ` blocks at the start of the message (`withQuoteBlock` in `web/src/lib/drafts.ts`, `web/src/lib/comments.ts`); the assistant and Agents on computers read them as text, and other clients that don't recognize them simply see `>` lines.
At most one quote block starts a message (the quoted words; for a task card, the first line is `任务「标题」（todo id: …）`, meaning `Task “title” (todo id: …)`), followed by any number of comment blocks, separated by blank lines, and finally the user's typed text:

```text
> Quoted words                  ← quote block (optional)

> Comment 1                     ← comment on selected text: number, original text (nested in another `> `), blank line, comment
> Selected text:
> > The selected lines
>
> State the source clearly here

> Code comment 2                ← code comment: number, location, optional Side / Diff / Truncated, fenced code, comment
> File: src/app.ts:12-14        ← path relative to the session directory (original path if outside it); line numbers are from the new file, with `Side: old` when only deleted lines are selected
> Diff: staged                  ← absent for comments on files; staged | unstaged | commit <first 8 chars>; a session review's (#151): uncommitted | branch since <base> | since <base> (Git's short hash); code lines carry `+`, `-`, space, and the fence uses `diff`
> Truncated: the first 60 of 80 lines
> ```ts
> const a = 1;
> ```
>
> Why not use a constant?

> Element comment 3             ← an element picked in a dev server preview (docs/web/preview.md): number, page, selector, optional Component (with its source) or Source, Text, Truncated, the element's HTML, comment
> Page: http://localhost:5173/settings
> Element: main > form > button.save
> Component: SaveButton (src/settings/SaveButton.tsx:14)
> Text: Save changes
> ```html
> <button class="save">Save changes</button>
> ```
>
> Make it the primary color

The user's typed text
```

Limits: comments up to 4000 characters, attached code up to 60 lines (extra lines are counted in `Truncated` but not included); the fence has one more backtick than the longest run in the code. Numbers follow the order of comments above the input, starting at 1.
On reading back, web only recognizes blocks after the first block whose first line is `Comment N` / `Code comment N` / `Element comment N` (`splitQuotes`), so ordinary `> ` quotes are unaffected; editing a sent message puts comments back above the input. The iOS app writes and reads the same blocks (`MessageComments`) and draws them as cards in sent bubbles; both are checked against `spec/fixtures/comments`.

### Message source (#2125)

`Item.source` is optional authorship metadata, independent of the runtime's `role`. New automated input keeps the model's existing user role and the legacy `injected` / `from` fields. Clients must not render any nonempty source kind as a user bubble, count it in user-only navigation or statistics, or match it to a user's pending send. Unknown kinds get a generic source label; they do not fall back to a user identity.

```json
{"kind":"conversation","conversation_id":"<sending conversation id>","title":"Research"}
```

| `source.kind` | Meaning | Optional fields |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `conversation` | Input from `conversation_send` or `conversation_new` | `conversation_id` is the sending session's stable id; `title` is its title at send time |
| `patrol` | A repeating scheduled run, including daily routines and interval patrols | `title` is the scheduled task title; `conversation_id` is the originating conversation when recorded; `push: "asked"` marks a run whose normal completion stays quiet |
| `followup` | A one-shot scheduled follow-up, wake, or usage-limit continuation | `title` and originating `conversation_id` when recorded; `push: "asked"` as for `patrol` |
| `supervision` | A supervision dispatch | Existing `injected.level` and turn-folding behavior still apply |
| `meeting` | A batch from a recorded meeting this session attends: live sentences, questions and answers since the last batch, the end of the meeting (#2981, [meeting-minutes.md](../assistant/meeting-minutes.md) "Feeding the attending session") | `title` is the meeting's name; no `conversation_id` |

The manager persists explicit provenance in the native transcript with a leading context block, rendered by `shared/message_source.md`:

```text
<persona-context kind="message-source" title="">
{"kind":"conversation","conversation_id":"<sending conversation id>","title":"Research"}
</persona-context>
```

The original content follows the block. JSON is HTML-escaped when written so a title cannot close the block. This is metadata, not a selectable Context card: clients exclude `kind="message-source"` from Context groups. The block survives history reads, full-item reads, paging, subscription backlog and process restarts without depending on the 24-hour echo cache or a database migration. Queued relays retain their sender id/title in the existing persisted relay JSON; dispatch reconstructs the same source after restart. Scheduled runs receive a source whether they address an existing chat, reuse their own chat, or start a new one.

For compatibility, prefer explicit `source`, then persisted source context, then existing `injected`: `followup.daily|interval` maps to `patrol`, other followup states to `followup`, and `system.supervise` to `supervision`. `from` still names a native peer and is not converted into a conversation id. With no metadata, only the complete canonical relay context (`assistant/relay.md`, matching sender and reply ids, recognized relay tool and numeric hop limits) supplies a conversation id/title; an emoji, title, or ordinary user sentence never does. Existing generated task templates remain the narrow fallback for old transcripts. A message with `client_msg_id` is never text-inferred. New user starts and app sends protect pasted source blocks or complete templates with an outer `message-source` block containing `{"author":"user"}`; this internal sentinel produces no source and prevents nested metadata or legacy recognition, even before the echo id arrives. Explicit source fields supplied by app input are removed.

### Forwarded messages (#3807)

A message forwarded from one chat to another goes out as the user's own message in the target chat: a
`<persona-context kind="forward">` block that carries the original, then the note the user typed (with no note, a fixed
"Please look at the forwarded message above." in the sender's language). It is sent through
`POST /api/v1/sessions/{mid}/{sid}/messages` like any message, or as a new Agent's first message; there is no forward
endpoint, and nothing is written to the original chat. Only chats of the same hub are offered.

```text
<persona-context kind="forward" title="Forwarded from Claude · Network tests" url="persona://session/<machine id>/<session id>?at=<item id>" msg="<item id>" role="agent" author="Claude" chat="Network tests" project="weather › tests" machine="MacBook Pro" time="2026-11-11T10:24:00+08:00">
Retries live in `RetryPolicy.swift`: 3 tries.
</persona-context>

Make the photo upload use the same retries
```

| Attribute | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `title` | "Forwarded from {author} · {chat}" in the sender's language: what a reader that does not know `forward` shows, and the title the hub takes for a chat that starts with it |
| `url` | `persona://session/<machine id>/<session id>?at=<item id>`, the item id percent-encoded: the original, which clients open at that message |
| `msg` | The original item id |
| `role` | Whose message it was: `user` (the user's own), `persona`, `agent`, or `other` (a relayed or scheduled message, another session's Claude) |
| `author` | Who wrote it, by name; for the user's own, "Me" in the sender's language |
| `chat` | The original chat's title |
| `project` | The Agent's project (`space › tab`); absent for Persona's chats |
| `machine` | The computer's name (not its id); absent for Persona's chats |
| `time` | When the original was written, ISO 8601 with the sender's offset |

The attributes are written in this order after `kind`, `title`, `url` and `msg`; values escape `&`, `"`, `<` and `>`,
and readers keep attributes they do not know. The text is the original as the chat shows it: without message-source
metadata, photo notes or file tags; quote and forward blocks it opened with become `> ` lines led by their heading;
files sent with it are named, not copied; at most 20,000 characters, then a line saying it was cut. It goes through the
usual closing-tag removal. Photos the user sent with their own message go with the forward as the new message's images.

Clients draw the block as a card at the top of the user's bubble (the heading, the computer and time, the first lines
of the original) that opens the original chat at that message; a reader that does not know `forward` folds it like the
other context blocks ("Context · title"). Persona's CLAUDE.md says how to read it, and that `agent_read` and
`conversation_read` read the original chat from the ids in `url`. Shared cases: `spec/fixtures/forward`.

**Several at once (#3838).** Messages picked together go as one message with one block per message, in the original
chat's order (not the order they were picked), one per line, then a blank line and the note; with no note, "Please look
at the forwarded messages above.". Nothing new is written into a block. Each is cut at the smaller of 20,000 characters
and 60,000 divided by how many go (rounded down), and at most 30 go at once; the user's own photos go along up to the
box's limit, the earlier messages' first. Readers show forward blocks that sit next to each other and whose `url` names
the same session as one card: the chat, then each message with its author, time and first lines, each opening the
original at that message. Another session's forward or any other block starts a new card. Shared cases:
`spec/fixtures/forward/several.json`.

## Messages injected by Persona

The hub sends some model-facing messages into chats as "user input" (#2360, #2358). In the transcript they have `role:"user", kind:"text"`, just like the user's typed words,
but aren't user-written: **clients don't draw them as user bubbles or show the instructions for the model inside them**. The runtime role stays unchanged; generated content carries the source context above.
The hub preserves explicit provenance and recognizes legacy generated lines by template (`prompts.ParseInjected`, tested against rendering), adding `injected` to the item. Pagination (`/items`), pushes (`items` events and subscription backlog),
and `/items/{iid}/full` all carry the metadata. Old messages and those written by old nodes keep the narrow template fallback. A line the App sends with its own `client_msg_id` is never recognized as injected.

```jsonc
"injected": {
  "kind": "task_notice|followup|system",
  "state": "…",            // see the table below
  "title": "Remove the extension list from README", // task name / scheduled task title / what a wake-up is waiting for / the inbox item's title; may be empty
  "machine": "<computer name>",  // task_notice only: which computer the Agent is on (name; may be empty)
  "todo_id": "td_…",        // task_notice only: when the hub can identify the task (still open, unique title); may be empty, in which case the client looks for a task card in the same chat by title
  "line": "Task 'Remove the extension list from README' is done", // one human-readable sentence, displayed directly
  "detail": "…"             // followup once / daily / interval only: the task's own instructions (what the user wrote in the scheduled task), which can be shown collapsed; empty otherwise
}
```

| Source (template) | Start of text | `kind` | `state` | `line` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A quiet task dispatched from the main chat has a result (`assistant/task_notice.md`) | `🔔 任务「标题」做完了（电脑）` ("Task 'title' is done (computer)"), with `（这是 Persona 的任务通知，……` ("This is a Persona task notification, …") on the second or third line | `task_notice` | `done` / `needs` / `interrupted` / `failed` | Task "x" is done / waiting for you / interrupted / couldn't start |
| A scheduled task or follow-up is due (`assistant/task_run.md`) | `⏰ 标题（你之前安排的跟进）` / `（定时任务）` / `（定时任务，每 30 分钟）` ("title (a follow-up you scheduled)" / "(scheduled task)" / "(scheduled task, every 30 minutes)") | `followup` | `once` / `daily` / `interval` | Follow-up "x" is due / Scheduled task "x" starts running |
| Wake an Agent that is waiting (`agents/wake.md`, Agents chats) | `⏰（Persona 叫醒你，第 N 次）` ("Persona wakes you, attempt N") | `followup` | `wake` | Persona woke it: check whether "what it's waiting for" is ready |
| Continue an Agent once its subscription usage limit reset (`agents/limit_continue.md`, Agents chats, #1710; only the hub marks it) | `⏰（Persona 叫你接着做）订阅的用量额度已经重置了` ("Persona asks you to go on: the subscription's usage limit has reset") | `followup` | `limit_continue` | Usage limit reset: Persona told it to go on |
| A node restart lost background tasks (`assistant/lost_tasks.md`) | `⚠️ 运行你的 node 刚重启过` ("The node running you just restarted") | `system` | `lost_tasks` | The node restarted; N background tasks stopped |
| A supervision message in the main chat (`assistant/supervise.md`, #3124) | `📋 督办：你派出去的任务有 N 个要你处理` ("Supervision: N tasks you dispatched need your attention"), with `这是 Persona 的督办消息` ("This is a Persona supervision message") on the second line | `system` | `supervise` | Supervision: N dispatched tasks need attention |
| News of an inbox item for a chat it was handed to (`inbox/handoff_note.md`, #1194; [inbox.md](../assistant/inbox.md) "Item actions") | `📥 收件箱事件「标题」有了下文` ("Inbox item 'title' has news"), with `这是 Persona 的收件箱通知` ("This is a Persona inbox notice") on the second line | `system` | `inbox` | Inbox: an update on "title" |
| How a question a conversation asked without waiting ended (`assistant/ask_later.md`, #4928, #6421; [assistant.md](../assistant/assistant.md) "Asking without holding the turn") | `🔔 你 <time> 用 ask_user 问过用户（wait: false，当时没有等回答）：` ("You asked the user with ask_user at <time>, without waiting"), ending with `（这是 Persona 的通知，不是用户在这里发的消息。）` ("This is a Persona notice, not a message the user sent here") | `system` | `ask_answered` / `ask_expired` / `ask_closed` | You answered: "answers" (`title`: the answers, joined with " · " and clipped to 60 characters) / The question timed out unanswered / The question was closed without an answer |

**Display** (the same on every client):

- Draw a lightweight centered system notice: icon + `line`, not a right-side user bubble, without exposing the original text. Tapping `task_notice` opens the task (`todo_id`, otherwise find a task card / to-do in this chat by `title`; untappable if neither is found);
  once / daily / interval `followup` can be opened to read `detail`; the rest aren't tappable.
- If a card for the same task (receipt, task card) is already above it in the main chat, this line can merge into the card instead of being drawn separately; never repeat the Agent's last words (already on the card).
- Doesn't count as user-sent: isn't treated as a turn start when matching pending bubbles (`client_msg_id` / text matching), and isn't counted in "what you said" statistics. Chat list previews, search results and copying "the user's words" use `line`, not the original text.
- A task notification still queued for sending already uses only `任务「x」的通知` ("Notification for task 'x'") in the `queued` field of `sessions`.

**Supervision turns** (#1988): `injected.state = supervise` additionally carries `level: info|triage|user`, read from the exact `<persona-supervision level="…" />` line in the generated message. Missing level on older supervision messages means triage. Info is progress-only and does not dispatch a main-chat turn. Web defaults an entire triage turn to one muted, expandable record; original input, tool trace and replies remain inspectable in that record. User-level turns remain visible. A successful `supervision_finish` result with `visibility:user`, `notify_user`, `ask_user`, or user-facing `task_review` promotes the whole turn; failed calls do not. A pending ask_user remains visible while waiting for the user's answer. `fold.supervision_user:true` carries successful promotion across server-side work folding. Native clients must implement this turn-level behavior separately; merely drawing the input as a system line does not hide its reply.

**When an old hub has no `injected`**, recognize by text (only lines with `role:"user", kind:"text"` and no `client_msg_id`; strip leading whitespace and `<persona-context>` snapshot blocks first):

- `task_notice`: the first line matches `^🔔 任务「(.+)」(做完了|在等用户|被模型服务出错打断了|没开起来)(?:（(.+)）)?$` (task title, done / waiting for the user / interrupted by a model service error / couldn't start, optional computer), and the full text contains `这是 Persona 的任务通知` ("This is a Persona task notification").
  Group 2 maps to `done` / `needs` / `interrupted` / `failed`; group 3 is `machine`.
- `followup`: the first line matches `^⏰ (.+)（(你之前安排的跟进|定时任务(?:，每 [^）]+)?)）$`: `你之前安排的跟进` ("a follow-up you scheduled") is `once`, `定时任务，每 …` ("scheduled task, every …") is `interval`, `定时任务` ("scheduled task") is `daily`;
  `detail` is the body after the first blank line (remove the trailing instruction paragraph starting with `（知识库`, "(knowledge base"). A first line starting with `⏰（Persona 叫醒你，第` ("Persona wakes you, attempt") is `wake`; `title` is the text inside `在等「…」` ("waiting for '…'").
- `system`: starts with `⚠️ 运行你的 node 刚重启过` ("The node running you just restarted"); the count of lines starting with `- ` is the number of stopped tasks. Supervision messages and inbox notices are only sent by new hubs that write them, and always carry `injected` when sent; how a question asked without waiting ended (`ask_later`) is marked by the hub on every item it sends, old ones included. None of these are in the shared fixtures, and clients don't need to recognize them themselves.
- Anything unrecognized stays a user bubble (better to miss recognition than hide the user's words).
- Shared fixtures: `spec/fixtures/injected/cases.json` (Go test `TestParseInjected` generates them from templates; `UPDATE_GOLDEN=1` rewrites them): `input.text` → `expected` (`null` means not recognized); all clients run their fallback recognition against these fixtures.

Other "not user-written" messages retain their own shapes: inter-chat input now additionally carries `source.kind="conversation"` as above; background for resuming the old main chat (`<persona-context title="接上旧主对话">`, "Resume the old main chat")
is gathered as "Context" by the tags above; background-task notifications use `kind:"notice"` + `task`; `/model`, compaction and similar notices use `kind:"notice"`.



### Workspace catalog lineage (#1399)

Each `workspaces.list` / `GET /api/v1/workspaces` workspace may carry `parent_source_id` and `index` (host order). A parent identity is `(machine_id, source, parent_source_id)`, never the globally qualified workspace `id` or its directory. Optional `project_id`, `project_name`, `project_path` and `is_main` describe the host project separately: multiple root workspaces share one project ID, while a cross-project child still follows its explicit workspace parent. Project IDs are scoped to machine and source, and names are labels. Optional `head`, `unread`, `sidebar_status` and `workspace_kind` preserve host-owned sidebar presentation; they are not inferred Agent capabilities. Optional `owned` (an engine runtime's rows only, #6297) marks a worktree the runtime made and removes with its workspace: the web offers Delete worktree on a Paseo row only with it. The node preserves the host's user-visible title in `title` without changing session names or pin identities. Missing fields remain compatible with old nodes and clients. Existing discovery snapshots preserve these fields as part of their JSON; no new table is required. Workspace containers are independent of Agent sessions, including empty parents and multiple distinct workspaces in one directory.

`POST /machines/{mid}/worktree/prepare` advertises `choose_parent: true` when the host can select a sidebar parent independently of the Git source. Only then may the client send `parent_workspace_id` to `worktree/create`; `workspace_id` still names the repository/base checkout. Both IDs belong to that machine and host. Orca validates the selected parent before creating anything and returns `parent_workspace_id` with the result. Omission retains the original source-as-parent behavior; clients must not offer independent parent selection on older nodes that ignore unknown request fields. An explicit `workspace_id` in an Orca session start must still exist and contain `cwd`; a stale choice is refused instead of falling back to another workspace.

`POST /machines/{mid}/worktree/rename` is a full-device node action: `{workspace_id, name, kind?, locale?}` changes a listed worktree's display name through its host (its refusals in `locale`, which the hub fills in). It does not rename its branch, directory or Agents. The name is a trimmed single line of at most 80 characters. Orca uses `worktree.set` with only `displayName`; Paseo sets the workspace's title (runtime ↔ node `workspace.rename`, #6297); Agent tab names use `terminal.rename` instead. Missing or foreign targets are refused.


### Orca worktree composer and removal

Advanced worktree routes are full-device node adapters. The Hub validates named fields, applies authorization and forwards requests; creation retains the existing `X-Persona-Op-Id` receipt. It does not choose repositories, inspect Git, or decide removal safety.

Probe `POST /api/v1/machines/{mid}/worktree/prepare` with `{workspace_id,kind:"orca",composer:true}`. Only a response containing `composer` enables advanced creation; old nodes may ignore the probe flag and return legacy metadata. Legacy explicit `{workspace_id,branch,path,kind?,parent_workspace_id?}` and generated `{workspace_id,auto_name:true,kind?,parent_workspace_id?}` creation retain their existing semantics. Never send an advanced mutation to a node that did not advertise it.

The advanced prepare response retains `root`, `repoName`, `branch`, `path`, `choose_parent` and `automatic_name`, and adds `composer:{project,base_ref,refs,presets,capabilities}`. Presets are `{id,name?,directories:string[]}`. Adapter capabilities are `create`, `source.github`, `sparse_presets`, `branch_override`, and optionally `folder_parent`. These names describe this adapter, not Orca runtime capability names. The adapter requires the runtime's `worktree.open-existing-branch.v2-request.v1`; folder parents additionally require `worktree.set.folder-parent.v1`, and `branch_override` requires `worktree.create.exact-name.v1`. Prepare reads actual repository metadata, refs and sparse presets; unsupported RPCs fail rather than fabricating choices. GitHub source queries can still fail independently because of provider configuration or authentication.

Advanced `worktree/create` takes `{workspace_id,kind:"orca",composer:true,name?,branch_override?,base_ref?,parent_workspace_id?,no_parent?,note?,sparse_preset_id?,source_id?,source_url?,locale?}`. `auto_name:true` is accepted but unnecessary. Omitted name generates a name, with final naming and checkout placement owned by Orca. Legacy `branch` and `path` conflict with composer mode. The source workspace chooses the repository; the visual parent is independent and can belong to another local project. Omitted parent defaults to the source; `no_parent:true` conflicts with an explicit parent. The default Git base is the project's base, independently of the parent. Reusing a free local branch preserves its tip and sends `open-existing-v2` so a directory collision cannot select a different branch. A new explicit branch sends `create-exact`, refusing a collision rather than silently selecting a suffixed branch. A PR source cannot also reuse an existing branch. Results contain actual `{workspace_id,parent_workspace_id?,path,branch,tab_id?,pane?,terminal?}`; never reconstruct the returned path from a requested name.

`worktree/source` takes `{workspace_id,kind:"orca",query?,locale?}` and returns `{items:[{type,number,title,url,branchName?,baseRefName?,isCrossRepository?}],errors?,warning?}`. This adapter exposes GitHub issues and PRs only. Creation uses `source_id:"issue:<number>"` or `"pr:<number>"` with the exact returned `source_url`; the node revalidates the selected item and resolves PR checkout/push refs through Orca. `worktree/preset` takes `{workspace_id,kind:"orca",name,directories,locale?}`, with directories as newline-separated repository-relative paths, and returns the runtime's `{preset:{id,name?,directories}}`.

An unchanged creation intent retains one receipt UUID, body, connection owner and target across retries and dialog reopening. An unknown or pending receipt never authorizes a new create ID. Inspect `/api/v1/ops/{id}` or replay the exact original request with its original ID. The Hub preserves unknown outcomes and does not repeat the node call. Workspace creation and optional Agent launch are separate stages.

`POST /api/v1/machines/{mid}/worktree/delete` previews with `{workspace_id,kind:"orca",preview:true,locale?}` and returns `{workspace_id,kind,host_id:"local",instance_id,path,branch,dirty,folder,preview_token}`. Confirm with `{workspace_id,kind:"orca",preview_token,force?:true,delete_branch?:true,locale?}`. A token binds the exact node, local runtime instance, repository, branch, path, workspace kind, parent, checkout and Git-directory filesystem identity, HEAD and reviewed dirty content. Confirmation expires after ten minutes. Main or unknown-main workspaces, Git main checkouts, parents with children, ambiguous/missing/nonlocal identities and incomplete catalogs are refused. Confirmation re-resolves the target and rereads dirty state; changed content requires another preview even when `force` is true. Branches are kept unless explicitly requested otherwise. Raw `force` never waives archive-hook failure or unverified terminal-stop safety.

For `kind:"herdr"`, the same preview-confirm-reconcile route accepts `close_only:true` for workspace closure.
The preview returns `kind:"herdr"`, `host_id:"local"`, an empty `instance_id`, and `close_only:true` with `folder:true`.
Every confirmation and reconciliation repeats the same `close_only` flag. Closing keeps the checkout, files and
branches and accepts main checkouts and missing directories. A close token cannot authorize checkout deletion.
Omitting `close_only` removes a verified linked checkout through native `worktree.remove`. Its preview binds the
native workspace, socket instance, pane membership, checkout/Git-directory identity, branch, HEAD and reviewed dirty
contents. `force:true` acknowledges the previewed uncommitted files. `delete_branch:true` requests safe merged-branch
cleanup after observed checkout removal. The native catalog and checkout disappearance establish completion.
A dispatched token supports read-only reconciliation and retains the ten-minute confirmation and 24-hour reconciliation
windows. The web checks `worktree/status` before offering herdr checkout deletion. Closing remains available for a main
checkout.

Removal requires runtime `worktree.remove-branch-policy.v1` and `worktree.archive-failure-blocking.v1`; folder unregister also requires `folder-workspace.unique-id-mutation.v1`. Folder workspace keys use `folderWorkspace.delete` with `requireUniqueId:true`; folder-project children use host-qualified `worktree.rm`. Neither recursively deletes the user's folder. Git removal sends `runHooks:true`, `waitForBackgroundRemoval:true` and explicit branch policy without hook/PTY waivers.

Deletion returns `{workspace_id,removed,state,branch_deleted?}`. Only `removed:true,state:"removed"` is completion: the runtime result must agree with catalog absence and checkout disappearance (folder unregister checks catalog absence). Background acceptance returns `removing`; transport uncertainty returns `unknown`; reconciliation may return `present`. Use `{workspace_id,kind:"orca",preview_token,reconcile:true}` on the same route for read-only reconciliation; it never repeats removal. A dispatched token is consumed for mutation and retained for reconciliation for up to 24 hours. Node restart invalidates tokens; refresh the authoritative inventory and review the outcome before a fresh deletion attempt. Runtime refusals, including archive failures, remain errors. Orca does not currently accept an expected workspace instance or dirty fingerprint in `worktree.rm`, so checks protect stale confirmations but do not form an atomic transaction with concurrent external filesystem/runtime changes.

The advanced adapter supports only workspaces owned by the local Orca execution host. SSH, paired runtimes and cross-store parents are unavailable here. Runtime versions alone never imply support. All adapter error text has en, zh-Hans and ja resources under `worktree-composer`.

For `kind:"paseo"` (#6297) the same preview-confirm-reconcile route deletes a worktree Paseo made (`owned` in its
`runtime.workspaces` row): a main checkout, a folder and a worktree Paseo did not make are refused at the preview, and
so is `close_only`; so is a row whose folder is gone, one git no longer knows as a worktree (its record in the repository
pruned) and a folder inside a worktree, each with its own reason. Neither the preview nor the confirmation goes on while
work could be lost: a session in the workspace starting, working, waiting for the user or in a state Paseo does not say,
or an Agent of any engine running in the folder (a herdr one that went there); idle, done and stopped sessions are what
the archive ends, as the preview showed. The preview returns `kind:"paseo"`, `host_id:"local"`, the bridge's instance
as `instance_id`, `folder:false`, and binds the runtime process, the workspace's identity (its id, folder, kind, `owned`
and repository: a new title or project name is the same workspace), its sessions (the archive ends them), the checkout
and Git-directory identity, branch, HEAD and reviewed dirty contents. One deadline, 145 s, covers the confirmation's
checks and Paseo's archive; past it the outcome is `unknown` and reconciliation tells. Confirmation has Paseo archive the
workspace (runtime ↔ node `workspace.archive`); Paseo removes the folder whatever is in it, so `force:true` is still
required for previewed changes. Completion is the workspace gone from the runtime's list and its folder gone; a
workspace archived with its folder left is `unknown`. `delete_branch:true` uses Git's safe branch deletion after
that; the branch is kept otherwise. Reconciliation reads the list and the disk, Paseo connected or not.

### Codex speed settings

Session rows may include `service_tier` (acknowledged native value, omitted while unknown) and
`service_tiers: [{id, name, description?}]` (native model choices plus `default` for Standard).
A standalone `service_tier` request to the session modes endpoint calls `session.speed {session_id, service_tier}`.
Only writable Codex app-server threads with advertised tiers support this request. Native errors are returned, and
older nodes return `node_outdated`. Speed changes apply to subsequent turns independently of reasoning effort.

For a new Persona conversation, the launcher model list also carries each model's native `serviceTiers` as
`service_tiers`. While the default manager names `assistant_start_service_tier` in `manager.hello`, the hub lists that
feature and the web can send an advertised `service_tier` with `POST /api/v1/assistant/conversations`; choosing another
manager disarms the pre-start draft. The node applies the tier through the same acknowledged `thread/settings/update`
after opening or adopting the thread and before its first `turn/start`; effort remains independent. Omission sends no
settings update and preserves the native default. An old hub receives no such field from this web client, an old manager
gets 501 `assistant_service_tier_manager_outdated` before relaying an explicit one, and a node without
`assistant_service_tier` refuses a nonempty value with 409 `node_outdated` instead of silently starting Standard.
Resumed sends and non-Codex starts return coded 409 refusals; a native refusal returns
`assistant_service_tier_refused`, stops the unused new process and persists no conversation before the first turn.
New Agent starts do not take a speed setting.
